nodes.label: AgentControllerSession
nodes.rationale: Sessions that share a resource but use different session ids each get their own run loop, thread binding, mode, model and state, while their stored threads and resource-scoped memory belong to the shared resource.

nodes.label: MastraClient.getAgentController()
nodes.rationale: Takes the registration key, which can differ from the controller's own id.

nodes.label: MastraClient.listAgentControllers()
nodes.rationale: Each entry's id is the key the controller is registered under in new Mastra({ agentControllers }), not the controller's own id.

nodes.label: OtherAgentControllerEvent
nodes.rationale: Because OtherAgentControllerEvent.type is string, comparing event.type to a literal does not narrow the union; callers must narrow with isKnownAgentControllerEvent first.

nodes.label: Session (in-process)
nodes.rationale: A process that owns the controller uses the in-process Session instead of the HTTP-backed AgentControllerSession.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.create()
nodes.rationale: Sessions are get-or-create on the server, so calling create() with the same sessionId resumes the existing conversation instead of forking it.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.followUp()
nodes.rationale: Sends immediately when the session is idle, otherwise queues for after the active run completes.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.listMessages()
nodes.rationale: Used to close the message gap after a reconnect.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.respondToToolSuspension()
nodes.rationale: The resumeData shape depends on the suspended tool: string or string[] for ask_user, "Yes"/"No" for request_access, and a PlanResume for submit_plan.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: The reply arrives as message_* events on the subscription, not as the return value of the call.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.sendNotification()
nodes.rationale: The agent's delivery policy decides whether the notification wakes an idle thread immediately or is held and summarised for later; notifications are delivered as agent signals on messages rather than as controller events.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.state()
nodes.rationale: Used for initial UI hydration and for re-syncing after a reconnect, since the server does not replay events missed while disconnected.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.subscribe()
nodes.rationale: The promise resolves once the stream is established and rejects when it cannot connect, so a rejected call leaves nothing running in the background; reconnect only governs re-establishing a stream that drops after it was established. idleTimeoutMs defaults to 60000 and is reset by 25-second server heartbeats, so only a silent half-open connection trips it.

nodes.label: AgentControllerSession.switchModel()
nodes.rationale: Persists the model as the current model for the active thread, independently of mode changes.

nodes.label: agent.abortThreadStream()
nodes.rationale: Aborting preserves queued input by default; clearPendingSignals:true drops the queue too.

nodes.label: result.accepted promise
nodes.rationale: Resolves when Mastra decides what to do (wake, deliver, persist, discard, blocked), not when a run finishes.

nodes.label: AgentController Session
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Agent methods and manages the thread subscription; most applications use the Agent methods directly.

nodes.label: agent.cancelQueuedMessages()
nodes.rationale: Removes queued input without stopping the active run; cancellation is best-effort across processes and doesn't revoke accepted input.

nodes.label: ifActive.behavior
nodes.rationale: Applications usually keep the defaults (deliver to the active run); override only for a different result.

nodes.label: ifIdle.behavior
nodes.rationale: Applications usually keep the defaults (wake a new run); override only for a different result.

nodes.label: result.persisted promise
nodes.rationale: Used to wait for a storage write; set only when the action is persist.

nodes.label: agent.queueMessage()
nodes.rationale: Used when the current answer should finish before the agent sees the next message; queued input waits for the active run to finish, then starts a new run.

nodes.label: agent.queueSignal()
nodes.rationale: Queues typed context with the same behavior as queueMessage but keeps the signal's type, tagName, and attributes.

nodes.label: agent.sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: Returns right away; await result.accepted to wait for Mastra's routing decision and catch routing failures.

nodes.label: agent.sendNotificationSignal()
nodes.rationale: Used when an event needs a durable inbox record, delivery policy, and later reading; can merge related pending events.

nodes.label: agent.sendSignal()
nodes.rationale: Adds context from the application (e.g. background job result); delivers by default, transient:true applies context only to the current request.

nodes.label: agent.sendStateSignal()
nodes.rationale: For named context that changes over time; sends a full snapshot or a description of what changed instead of adding a chat message.

nodes.label: transient signal option
nodes.rationale: Applies context only to the current request; Mastra doesn't store it, and transient signals can't be state signals.

nodes.label: subscription.abort()
nodes.rationale: Requests cancellation of the active run; pending signals survive unless clearPendingSignals:true is passed.

nodes.label: hideSignals option
nodes.rationale: Filters signal chunks for one subscriber only; doesn't change model context, stored messages, shared broadcasts, or other subscribers, and isn't a security boundary.

nodes.label: processDataStream()
nodes.rationale: Passes output to onChunk and continues listening after the answer finishes.

nodes.label: reconnect option
nodes.rationale: For long-lived subscriptions; resubscribes when the transport closes, retrying indefinitely with a one-second delay by default.

nodes.label: sendToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Sends the approval decision when a run pauses for tool approval; the existing subscription receives output when the run resumes.

nodes.label: subscribeThreadEvents()
nodes.rationale: Used separately to observe queue counts.

nodes.label: subscribeToThread()
nodes.rationale: Subscribe once to receive output across runs on the same thread; the subscription stays open between runs.

nodes.label: thread-history chunk
nodes.rationale: Carries the newest page of stored messages in oldest-first order; has an empty runId because its messages can span several runs.

nodes.label: thread-run-status chunk
nodes.rationale: Identifies the run's outcome independently of its output; an idle thread alone doesn't indicate success.

nodes.label: subscription.unsubscribe()
nodes.rationale: Closes the subscription without aborting, so the run continues and you can subscribe again later.

nodes.label: withInitialHistory option
nodes.rationale: Lets the application show the conversation so far before displaying new output; requires memory.

nodes.label: withRunStatus option
nodes.rationale: Opt-in so existing subscriptions don't receive run-status chunks by default.

nodes.label: SSE heartbeats
nodes.rationale: Periodic heartbeat frames keep browsers, proxies, and load balancers from closing an idle connection before the next signal or model chunk arrives.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Supports request cancellation using the standard Node.js AbortSignal API, useful for canceling in-flight requests or cleaning up stale network calls.

nodes.label: MastraClient
nodes.rationale: Initialized with a baseUrl and exposes a type-safe interface for calling agents, tools, and workflows.

nodes.label: createTool() (client tools)
nodes.rationale: Client-side tools let custom functions execute on the client when the agent requests them.

nodes.label: observe helper
nodes.rationale: Always available: when no tracing context is active, span runs the function directly and log is a no-op, so no null-checking is needed.

nodes.label: toModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Because client tools execute locally, the mapping runs on the client after execute completes; both transformed output and raw result are sent to the server so the raw result stays available for storage and application logic.

nodes.label: Client Tools
nodes.rationale: Let agents trigger browser-side functionality such as DOM manipulation or local storage access, executing tools in the user's environment rather than on the server.

nodes.label: CORS requests with credentials
nodes.rationale: Requires a concrete Access-Control-Allow-Origin (not *) and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, or the browser blocks the call before it reaches Mastra.

nodes.label: credentials: 'include'
nodes.rationale: Ensures each request carries session cookies when the UI and Mastra API are on different origins, avoiding 401 responses after browser sign-in.

nodes.label: Dynamic Workflows
nodes.rationale: Persisted workflow definitions are validated and registered with the running Mastra instance; durable storage requires a storage adapter supporting the workflowDefinitions domain.

nodes.label: Mastra Client SDK
nodes.rationale: Provides a concise and type-safe interface for interacting with a Mastra Server from browser environments using the native fetch API.

nodes.label: workflowDefinitions storage domain
nodes.rationale: Without this storage domain, Core can register a workflow in memory, but the server's dynamic-workflow API cannot preserve it across restarts.

nodes.label: approveToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Use when rendering the resumed chunks from the approval response.

nodes.label: declineToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Optional reason tells the model why the call was rejected; default is 'Tool call was not approved by the user'.

nodes.label: initialHistoryPagination
nodes.rationale: Only describes the initial subscription page for the current agent, resource, thread, and withInitialHistory value; not changed by live output or setMessages().

nodes.label: listSuspendedRuns()
nodes.rationale: Discovery is backed by storage, so it works after a server restart and across server instances.

nodes.label: processDataStream()
nodes.rationale: Reads the subscription stream until the connection closes or the request is aborted.

nodes.label: reconnect
nodes.rationale: true retries indefinitely with a one-second delay; 4xx other than 408/429 or 501 stops reconnecting and rejects with that error.

nodes.label: resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Continues execution after a suspension point, such as a workflow suspend within an agent.

nodes.label: resumeStreamUntilIdle()
nodes.rationale: Resumes a suspended agent stream with custom data and keeps the stream open until every background task completes.

nodes.label: sendToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Use with subscribeToThread() when resumed chunks should arrive through the existing thread subscription instead of a separate continuation stream.

nodes.label: streamUntilIdle()
nodes.rationale: Keeps the stream open until every background task dispatched during the run completes; server re-enters the agentic loop on each task completion.

nodes.label: useChat
nodes.rationale: agentVersionId is passed through requestContext to pin the chat to a specific agent version.

nodes.label: withRunStatus
nodes.rationale: useChat enables this for its thread subscription; callback types include these chunks only when requested.

nodes.label: aggregateSpans
nodes.rationale: Counts spans at any depth, such as nested agent runs that trace aggregation misses; token and cost measures belong to the span that recorded the usage and aren't added to parent spans.

nodes.label: aggregateTraces
nodes.rationale: Groups traces selected by a time range and optional predicate, returning one row per group or per group and non-empty time bucket when interval is set; check capabilities.traceAggregate before calling.

nodes.label: createFeedback
nodes.rationale: Feedback methods go through the target Mastra runtime and its configured observability storage; they don't call the hosted Mastra Platform Feedback API.

nodes.label: deleteFeedback
nodes.rationale: Deletion is idempotent, so missing ids are ignored; optional organizationId and resourceId restrict each deletion to records with matching scope fields.

nodes.label: deleteScores
nodes.rationale: Deletion is idempotent, so missing ids are ignored; optional organizationId and resourceId restrict each deletion to records with matching scope fields.

nodes.label: deleteTraces
nodes.rationale: Deletes traces and their associated spans, metrics, logs, scores and feedback; signals not linked to a trace are preserved.

nodes.label: getObservabilityCapabilities
nodes.rationale: Capability flags (spanQuery, spanAggregate, traceAggregate, threadQueryRows, aggregateTimeToFirstMeasures) must be checked before using optional query and aggregation features; older adapters return 501.

nodes.label: getTraceQueryFields
nodes.rationale: Returns canonical query fields and observed top-level string metadata fields for one predicate scope, including value kind, supported operators and whether value suggestions are available.

nodes.label: getTraceQueryValues
nodes.rationale: Call only after selecting a field with valueSuggestions: true; suggestions are bounded and advisory, and the client doesn't retry either discovery request.

nodes.label: listTracesLight
nodes.rationale: Returns the same rows as a trace list without input, output and attributes payloads, carrying short previews instead, so a list can render preview columns without transferring the whole payload; fetch the full record only when a row is opened.

nodes.label: querySpans
nodes.rationale: Returns completed span summaries across traces; requires a positive ISO timestamp range over span start time and supports cursor pagination.

nodes.label: queryTraces
nodes.rationale: Finds completed logical traces using trace fields and conditions over related spans; every query requires an ISO timestamp range and supports keyset, numbered-page and delta-polling modes (one mode per request).

nodes.label: queryTraceThreads
nodes.rationale: Returns thread summaries from completed traces; traces without a thread ID aren't included, and exactly one time selector must be chosen.

nodes.label: Feedback
nodes.rationale: Human-in-the-loop signals such as ratings, thumbs, comments and corrections linked to traces and spans.

nodes.label: MastraClient
nodes.rationale: When server auth is enabled, the client must attach a valid JWT in the Authorization header to reach protected routes.

nodes.label: MastraJwtAuth
nodes.rationale: Lightweight auth mechanism: verifies incoming requests against a shared JWT secret and plugs into the Mastra server via the `auth` option.

nodes.label: A2AAgent
nodes.rationale: Wraps a remote A2A agent so a parent Mastra agent can delegate work to it as a subagent; falls back to non-streaming generate when the remote card does not advertise streaming.

nodes.label: MastraClient.getA2A()
nodes.rationale: Use the client SDK when application code needs to call an A2A-enabled Mastra endpoint directly, rather than delegating through a parent agent.

nodes.label: MastraClient.getA2AV1()
nodes.rationale: Opts into the A2A v1.0 wire protocol and adds the tasks/list operation; sends A2A-Version: 1.0 automatically.

nodes.label: resubscribeTask()
nodes.rationale: Recovers live updates for an in-progress task after a stream disconnect.

nodes.label: verifyAgentCard hook
nodes.rationale: Enforces expected providers, endpoints, certificate-bound identities or signed cards before a parent agent delegates to a remote agent.

nodes.label: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol
nodes.rationale: Open protocol for delegating work across network, framework, vendor and language boundaries while the remote agent keeps its tools, prompts, memory and infrastructure private.

nodes.label: A2A agent card
nodes.rationale: Discovery document served from a well-known URL that describes the remote agent and carries the execution URL for A2A JSON-RPC requests.

nodes.label: A2A agent card signing
nodes.rationale: Lets clients verify a discovered card came from a trusted publisher and was not changed in transit; client verification is opt-in and unsigned cards still return unchanged.

nodes.label: A2A human-in-the-loop (input-required)
nodes.rationale: Maps Mastra agent suspension to the A2A input-required task state in both directions so tool approvals and suspend() calls can be resumed with the same taskId.

nodes.label: A2A push notifications
nodes.rationale: Used when a client cannot keep a stream open or a long-running task should update a callback URL after the original request ends; delivery is best-effort and configs are in-memory.

nodes.label: @mastra/codemod CLI
nodes.rationale: Automates each migration step (client-msg-function-args, client-sdk-types, client-offset-limit, client-get-memory-thread, client-to-ai-sdk-format).

nodes.label: agent.generate()
nodes.rationale: messages is now the first argument, matching @mastra/core/agent syntax.

nodes.label: getMemoryThread()
nodes.rationale: Parameter structure changed to an object to align the API across memory methods.

nodes.label: agent.network()
nodes.rationale: messages is now the first argument, matching @mastra/core/agent syntax.

nodes.label: workflow.runById()
nodes.rationale: Now returns a unified WorkflowState with metadata and processed execution state, and accepts fields/withNestedWorkflows options for performance optimization.

nodes.label: runExecutionResult()
nodes.rationale: Removed along with the /execution-result endpoints because runById() now returns the same unified WorkflowState.

nodes.label: agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: messages is now the first argument, matching @mastra/core/agent syntax.

nodes.label: streamVNext / resumeStreamVNext / observeStreamVNext
nodes.rationale: The experimental VNext methods became the standard implementation with updated event structures and return types.

nodes.label: useChat hook
nodes.rationale: Internally converts a provided threadId into the memory option, so component code needs no changes.

nodes.label: Get* to List* type rename
nodes.rationale: Aligns type names with the method naming convention.

nodes.label: memory option
nodes.rationale: Replaces the removed threadId and resourceId options with a cleaner memory configuration API across @mastra/client-js and @mastra/react; also supports thread metadata when creating new threads.

nodes.label: Network memory methods
nodes.rationale: Removed to simplify the memory API by dropping specialized network memory functionality in favor of regular memory APIs.

nodes.label: page/perPage pagination
nodes.rationale: Replaces offset/limit to match page-based web pagination.

nodes.label: Watch-related types
nodes.rationale: Removed because the watch API was replaced by streaming.

nodes.label: Client SDK v1 Migration
nodes.rationale: Client SDK changes align with server-side API updates, including utility renames, updated pagination, and type naming conventions.

nodes.label: editor.agent.update()
nodes.rationale: Creates an inactive draft and does not assign activeVersionId; publishing requires passing status: 'published' and activeVersionId explicitly.

nodes.label: editor.prompt.update()
nodes.rationale: Creates an inactive draft and does not assign activeVersionId, matching the stored-agent REST PATCH behaviour.

nodes.label: mastra.getAgentById()
nodes.rationale: Without a selector it returns the registered code-defined agent; status or versionId selectors apply a stored override.

nodes.label: getStoredAgent()
nodes.rationale: The returned resource includes methods for updates, deletion, dependents, export and version management.

nodes.label: activeVersionId
nodes.rationale: The resource record stores activeVersionId while individual snapshots carry no lifecycle status, so published resolution is driven by the record.

nodes.label: Code source (source: 'code')
nodes.rationale: Active overrides are serialized as deterministic JSON under <codePath>/agents/<encodedAgentId>.json (default ./mastra/editor) so Git history can serve as the version store; the history scan reads up to 50 recent commits and skips consecutive commits whose parsed JSON snapshot is unchanged.

nodes.label: Draft version
nodes.rationale: A draft is the latest snapshot when it differs from activeVersionId, or when no active version exists; creating a draft doesn't change what published requests resolve to.

nodes.label: Historical version
nodes.rationale: Restoring a historical version copies its configuration into a new inactive draft rather than reactivating the old snapshot.

nodes.label: Stored-agent REST API
nodes.rationale: The PATCH route creates an inactive draft unless autoPublish is enabled, and POST /stored/agents/:id/versions/:versionId/activate publishes it, keeping REST and SDK semantics aligned.

nodes.label: Sub-agent versioning
nodes.rationale: Version overrides propagate through supervisor-agent delegation in request context; entries merge by agent ID with precedence direct invocation > request body or existing request context > Mastra instance default.

nodes.label: Editor Versioning
nodes.rationale: Database-backed resources use draft and publish operations, while code-backed agent overrides use deterministic files and Git history.

nodes.label: AdminOnlyWorkosAuth
nodes.rationale: Subclassing MastraAuthWorkos and overriding authorizeUser() is the documented way to apply stricter, custom authorization rules.

nodes.label: authorizeUser()
nodes.rationale: Default authorization grants access to any authenticated WorkOS user; the check succeeds when the resolved user object contains both a Mastra user ID and a WorkOS user ID.

nodes.label: createMastraClient()
nodes.rationale: When auth is enabled, all MastraClient requests must include a valid WorkOS access token prefixed with Bearer in the Authorization header.

nodes.label: fetchMemberships option
nodes.rationale: When false, Mastra skips the extra WorkOS listOrganizationMemberships() call on each authenticated request; set true when using MastraFGAWorkos so FGA checks can resolve the correct organization membership ID.

nodes.label: trustJwtClaims option
nodes.rationale: Useful when the JWT template already includes the exact FGA context Mastra needs, letting Mastra fall back to verified claims when a bearer token isn't meant to round-trip through workos.userManagement.getUser().

nodes.label: abortRun(runId)
nodes.rationale: Use abortRun() to stop a run without a per-call abortSignal; cancelling the response body or client-wide abortSignal only disconnects the observer from durable execution.

nodes.label: cancelQueuedMessages()
nodes.rationale: Cancels selected pending signals without stopping the active run; SDK accepts only signal IDs, not queueOwnerId.

nodes.label: clearPendingSignals
nodes.rationale: Clear-on-abort affects the receiving server's local queues and is forwarded to the active owner; it is not a global queue clear.

nodes.label: Shared PubSub Backend
nodes.rationale: Server publishes all requested IDs through its shared PubSub backend so other subscribed instances can remove matching pending input; propagation is best-effort and asynchronous.

nodes.label: Schedule lifecycle hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks live at the Mastra level as a single flat bundle so they apply to both code-defined and stored agents; each context carries agentId for branching.

nodes.label: Mastra Code /schedules command
nodes.rationale: Session scoped: schedules live only in the Mastra Code process that created them, nothing is written to storage, and each fire is sent with agent.sendSignal().

nodes.label: mastra.schedules
nodes.rationale: The canonical create, read, update, and delete surface for both agent and workflow schedules.

nodes.label: Agent schedule tools
nodes.rationale: Because a schedule can run a script on every fire, create/resume/run need the same approval as running a shell command unless YOLO mode is on.

nodes.label: Storage adapter
nodes.rationale: Schedules require a storage adapter that implements the schedules domain.

nodes.label: Cron cadence
nodes.rationale: Validated at create/update time; timezone is settable so fire times don't depend on the host's locale.

nodes.label: Schedules
nodes.rationale: Persisted so they survive restarts and redeploys; publication is best-effort and skipped occurrences are not replayed.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: The delivery mechanism behind threaded schedules.

nodes.label: Workflow schedules
nodes.rationale: Schedules created through mastra.schedules are independent of the declarative schedule field on createWorkflow.

nodes.label: MastraAuthAuth0
nodes.rationale: Verifies Auth0-issued JWT tokens and integrates with the Mastra server via the auth option.

nodes.label: MastraClient (Auth0)
nodes.rationale: Must include a valid Auth0 access token in the Authorization header when auth is enabled.

nodes.label: MastraAuthClerk
nodes.rationale: Verifies incoming requests using Clerk's authentication system and integrates with the Mastra server via the auth option.

nodes.label: MastraClient (Clerk)
nodes.rationale: Must include a valid Clerk access token in the Authorization header when auth is enabled.

nodes.label: MastraAuthFirebase
nodes.rationale: Verifies Firebase ID tokens and integrates with the Mastra server via the auth option; reads env vars when no constructor options are given.

nodes.label: MastraClient (Firebase)
nodes.rationale: Must include a valid Firebase ID token in the Authorization header when auth is enabled.

nodes.label: MastraAuthSupabase
nodes.rationale: Verifies incoming requests using Supabase's authentication system and integrates with the Mastra server via the auth option.

nodes.label: MastraClient (Supabase)
nodes.rationale: Must include a valid Supabase access token in the Authorization header when auth is enabled.

nodes.label: Firestore user_access collection
nodes.rationale: Presence of a document keyed by user UID determines whether a user is authorized by default.

nodes.label: mastra-client-js Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill entry point that routes agents to per-topic reference documents for @mastra/client-js v1.59.0 instead of relying on training data.

nodes.label: Agent.sendNotificationSignal()
nodes.rationale: Server-side API for durable notification records.

nodes.label: queueMessage()
nodes.rationale: If the thread is active, Mastra starts a new run after the current run completes; if the thread is idle, Mastra starts a run immediately.

nodes.label: queueSignal()
nodes.rationale: Follows the same ordering as queueMessage(), but keeps the signal's type, tagName, and attributes.

nodes.label: sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: Use with subscribeToThread() so the client can render the stream that wakes from, or receives the message.

nodes.label: sendSignal()
nodes.rationale: Use this for system-generated context such as reactive reminders or notification-shaped context that doesn't need inbox storage; for user-authored input prefer sendMessage() or queueMessage().

nodes.label: ArcadeToolProvider
nodes.rationale: Registered with an Arcade API key to expose a catalog of tools with built-in authentication.

nodes.label: ComposioToolProvider
nodes.rationale: Registered with a Composio API key to expose its tool catalog in Editor without adding each tool in code.

nodes.label: mastra.getEditor()
nodes.rationale: Provides programmatic access to everything available in Studio for scripting bulk updates or seeding stored configurations.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Lets Editor data use a separate backend from application data via the editor storage domain.

nodes.label: MastraEditor
nodes.rationale: Added to the Mastra instance via the editor option to enable Studio-owned agent fields.

nodes.label: MCP Clients
nodes.rationale: Reusable clients created in Studio that expose tools from local stdio or remote HTTP servers, with per-agent tool filters.

nodes.label: Prompt Blocks
nodes.rationale: Saved reusable instruction text shared across agents so a policy change is published once instead of editing each agent.

nodes.label: Versioning
nodes.rationale: Draft and published versions let collaborators test changes while the live agent keeps serving the published version.

nodes.label: toAISdkStream()
nodes.rationale: Keeps the existing AI SDK v5/default behavior; version selects the AI SDK stream contract to emit. Useful for building custom streaming endpoints outside Mastra's provided route helpers.

nodes.label: createStoredAgent()
nodes.rationale: Publishes the initial version immediately by default; autoPublish:false creates an unpublished draft for review before activateVersion(). Editors with the code source always publish because saving writes to the file system.

nodes.label: Durable stored agents
nodes.rationale: Only serializable options are accepted; durable cache and pubsub are inherited from the server's Mastra instance, so durability is process-local without distributed cache/pubsub, and automatic recovery is configured in code via recovery.durableAgents.

nodes.label: Stored agents
nodes.rationale: Agent configurations stored in a database, created/updated/deleted at runtime; they reference primitives by key which are resolved from the Mastra registry at instantiation, and memory is configured inline as SerializedMemoryConfig.

nodes.label: listMemoryThreads
nodes.rationale: When agentId is omitted and storage is configured on the server, threads are retrieved using storage directly, which is useful when multiple agents share the same threads (e.g. workflows with multiple agent steps).

nodes.label: updateWorkingMemory
nodes.rationale: By default the call replaces the whole record; for schema-based resource-scoped working memory, mode 'merge' deep-merges only the provided fields atomically, and the server returns 400 if the storage adapter doesn't support atomic merges (currently only @mastra/pg).

nodes.label: Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Working memory lets agents keep persistent information about users across interactions and can be scoped to a specific thread or across all threads for a resource (user).

nodes.label: toAISdkMessages()
nodes.rationale: Keeps the existing AI SDK v5/default behavior; pass version: 'v6' when the app is typed against AI SDK v6 useChat() message types, or 'v7' for v7.

nodes.label: thread.clone
nodes.rationale: Clone supports options such as newThreadId, title, metadata, messageLimit and messageFilter (startDate/endDate) to copy a thread with a subset of its messages.

nodes.label: thread.listMessages
nodes.rationale: Metadata filters match shallow scalar values only (string, finite number, boolean, null) with AND semantics; arbitrary metadata filters may scan candidate messages, so performance depends on the server storage backend.

nodes.label: conversations.items.list()
nodes.rationale: Returns up to 1000 items in a single response, so has_more is currently always false.

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API Conversations surface
nodes.rationale: Gives the conversation-management side of Mastra Agents as a Responses API; stored Responses calls return conversation_id, which in Mastra is the raw memory threadId. Currently experimental.

nodes.label: approveToolCallGenerate()
nodes.rationale: Non-streaming counterpart used with generate().

nodes.label: declineToolCallGenerate()
nodes.rationale: Non-streaming counterpart used with generate().

nodes.label: stream()
nodes.rationale: Cancelling the response body aborts the underlying HTTP request and stops any pending client tool executions and follow-up requests.

nodes.label: abortSignal
nodes.rationale: Allows cancelling a stream from outside the response body; available on streamUntilIdle(), resumeStream(), resumeStreamUntilIdle(), approveToolCall(), declineToolCall(), generate(), and generateLegacy().

nodes.label: Metric analytics HTTP routes (aggregate, breakdown, timeseries, percentiles)
nodes.norm_label: metric analytics http routes (aggregate, breakdown, timeseries, percentiles)

nodes.label: Google Cloud Spanner observability storage
nodes.rationale: Implements metric queries only when disableMetrics is false; metrics are disabled by default.

nodes.label: listMetrics(args)
nodes.rationale: The client SDK does not expose a raw listMetrics() method; raw metric records are listed via the observability store or the GET /api/observability/metrics route.

nodes.label: MetricDistinctColumn
nodes.rationale: Required when aggregation is count_distinct; supported columns are a fixed enumerated list.

nodes.label: comparePeriod
nodes.rationale: previous_period uses the duration of filters.timestamp to derive the comparison window.

nodes.label: Delta mode (listMetrics)
nodes.rationale: Supports incremental polling via after/limit; a backend that doesn't support delta polling returns an unsupported-operation error.

nodes.label: Observability store
nodes.rationale: The base observability storage implementation throws *_NOT_IMPLEMENTED errors for raw listing, analytics, and discovery methods, so a configured observability domain can exist while its backend does not implement metric queries.

nodes.label: Page mode (listMetrics)
nodes.rationale: Default mode; supports pagination and orderBy, which are not allowed in delta mode.

nodes.label: responses.create
nodes.rationale: Use previous_response_id to continue from a previous stored response, or conversation_id to target a known thread directly.

nodes.label: Conversation
nodes.rationale: Stored responses return conversation_id, which in Mastra is the raw memory threadId.

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API
nodes.rationale: An OpenAI-compatible, agent-backed adapter over Mastra agents, memory and storage; agent_id selects the agent and model can override the agent's configured model for a single request. Currently experimental.

nodes.label: subscribeToThread()
nodes.rationale: Use this to render output from a thread that may be started or continued by sendMessage(), queueMessage(), sendSignal(), or server-side notification dispatch. withInitialHistory delivers stored messages as a first thread-history chunk; finished runs aren't replayed after it, so completed answers don't stream again on reconnect.

nodes.label: useChat()
nodes.rationale: Exposes the hasMore flag from the first history page as initialHistoryPagination so callers can offer loading older messages without another history request.

nodes.label: createDatasetExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Creates an experiment without starting a run; dataset version is pinned at creation time. Idempotent on a caller-supplied id so a retried workflow converges on the same experiment.

nodes.label: finalizeExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Server computes succeeded/failed/skipped counts from persisted rows; idempotent, returning the stored record if already completed.

nodes.label: runExperimentItem()
nodes.rationale: Upserts on (experimentId, itemId, attempt) so retried activities converge on a single row; scorer precedence is experiment > item > dataset.

nodes.label: submitExperimentResult()
nodes.rationale: For pure ingestion: re-submitting the same (experimentId, itemId, attempt) key updates the existing row instead of duplicating; a different attempt records a deliberate repeated trial.

nodes.label: MastraClient
nodes.rationale: Type-safe interface for interacting with a Mastra Server from a client environment.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Imported from @mastra/client-js; can also be passed as a plain Record<string, any>.

nodes.label: Client SDK error handling
nodes.rationale: All API methods can throw errors that callers catch and handle.

nodes.label: Agent Builder
nodes.rationale: Recommended instead of Editor when collaborators need to create and manage fully stored agents in a browser rather than start from code-defined agents.

nodes.label: Editor
nodes.rationale: Acts like a CMS for Mastra agents so collaborators can change instructions and tools in Studio without touching the codebase, and test changes before publishing.

nodes.label: Agent schedules
nodes.rationale: Persisted agent schedules managed over the /api/schedules routes.

nodes.label: Observability capability flags
nodes.rationale: Capabilities are checked before showing a feature because the configured observability store may not support each API; gated fields return 501 before storage runs.

nodes.label: Span selection (direct span predicate)
nodes.rationale: Span operations share a direct span predicate without nested spans clauses, unlike trace operations.

nodes.label: Trace selection (timeRange + where)
nodes.rationale: The same selection returns the same traces from either API, and aggregation counts exactly the traces that a query would list, so a selection can be reused between query and aggregate operations.

nodes.label: purgeDatasetItem()
nodes.rationale: Scrubs item content from history and linked results while preserving version history, counters and review status; idempotent and irreversible, and later item updates are rejected.

nodes.label: deleteDatasetExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Deletes observability traces first, then the experiment and its result records; if trace deletion fails for any other reason the promise rejects and the experiment is kept, though some traces may already be removed.

nodes.label: deleteExperiment()
nodes.rationale: For experiments orphaned by dataset deletion; a tenancy-scoped request that doesn't match the experiment returns success without deleting it.

nodes.label: getTraces()
nodes.rationale: Returns paginated root spans only; use getTrace() for complete traces with all spans.

nodes.label: aggregateSpans()
nodes.rationale: Trace aggregation only sees each trace's root span, so span aggregation exists to count every matching span at any depth, including agent runs nested inside workflows.

nodes.label: aggregateTraces()
nodes.rationale: Use for counts and measures, since trace queries cannot request counts or measures.

nodes.label: mastra api trace aggregate / span query / span aggregate
nodes.norm_label: mastra api trace aggregate / span query / span aggregate

nodes.label: agent_run span type
nodes.rationale: Filtering to agent_run gives latency as the caller of each agent sees it, since time to first chunk is measured from the run's start.

nodes.label: cost object (coverage, unit)
nodes.rationale: Coverage below 1 signals that cost.sum understates the group's spend, because partly priced calls lower coverage even though their known cost is included.

nodes.label: Group filtering (having, orderBy, limit)
nodes.rationale: having, orderBy and limit operate on groups using measures over the whole time range even when interval is set, so every returned group includes its full series of non-empty buckets.

nodes.label: model_generation span type
nodes.rationale: Model calls record usage on model_generation spans, so token totals per agent are obtained by selecting model_generation spans and grouping by the calling agent.

nodes.label: model_inference span type
nodes.rationale: Filtering to model_inference gives per-provider-call time to first token.

nodes.label: Time buckets
nodes.rationale: Buckets without traces are omitted rather than returned as zero rows; clients fill gaps when drawing charts.

nodes.label: Time to first token and chunk measures
nodes.norm_label: time to first token and chunk measures
nodes.rationale: timeToFirstChunk is measured from the agent run's start so it includes work done before the first model call (input processors, memory recall), while timeToFirstToken is the model call's own time to first token; traces without a value are skipped rather than counted as 0.

nodes.label: Token and cost measures
nodes.rationale: Averages divide by the number of usage-bearing (or priced) traces rather than by count, so traces that recorded no usage do not dilute the average; both sum and avg are null when no such traces exist.

nodes.label: Trace-query discovery
nodes.rationale: Discovery lets clients build field and value autocomplete without scanning trace payloads or copying the query grammar into the client.

nodes.label: Trusted tenant scope
nodes.rationale: The scope is supplied outside the query document and ANDed into every scan, so a caller's organizationId predicate can only narrow the tenant's own traces and never widen it.

nodes.label: AgentController Session Notification Route
nodes.rationale: Durable records over HTTP go through this route, which forwards to sendNotificationSignal().

nodes.label: client.getAgent().sendSignal()
nodes.rationale: Bypasses inbox storage, so use it only when the event needs no record, retries, or later reading.

nodes.label: createNotificationInboxTool()
nodes.rationale: Gives the agent the inbox tool so it can inspect records without exposing storage APIs.

nodes.label: decide()
nodes.rationale: Runs at receipt and again at delivery for records whose first decision deferred them or scheduled a summary; must be kept side-effect free because the stored schedule fixes when and how they deliver.

nodes.label: Notification Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Reads due records, groups summaries by agentId, resourceId, and threadId, and emits signals through the thread runtime.

nodes.label: MAX_NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS
nodes.rationale: After five failed attempts the record moves to failed and stops being due.

nodes.label: sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: Use for user input rather than notification events.

nodes.label: agent.sendNotificationSignal()
nodes.rationale: Canonical way to create durable notification records; returns the record and the policy decision.

nodes.label: sendSignal({ type: 'notification' })
nodes.rationale: Sends event context without creating an inbox record or providing its retries.

nodes.label: Storage Adapter (notifications domain)
nodes.rationale: Without a storage adapter with the notifications domain, sendNotificationSignal() throws instead of silently dropping the record.

nodes.label: Workflow Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Only apps that defer or summarize a notification create the lazy dispatch schedule and activate the workflow scheduler with it.

nodes.label: Coalescing (dedupeKey / coalesceKey)
nodes.rationale: dedupeKey identifies one event that may arrive more than once; coalesceKey groups related events into one pending record. Merging only considers records on the same thread, source, kind, agent, and resource that are still pending.

nodes.label: Delivery Policy
nodes.rationale: Decides whether to send the event immediately, summarize it with other events, or leave it for later; source rules run before priority rules so a noisy source can be summarized while everything else delivers.

nodes.label: Notification Inbox
nodes.rationale: Durable inbox separate from the conversation's messages so the event remains available even if the agent is busy when it arrives.

nodes.label: Notification Record
nodes.rationale: Stored record includes routing, priority, status, delivery attempts, and the original payload; the model receives an XML element built from summary and attributes, not payload automatically.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.rationale: Use notifications for events that need a durable inbox and delivery behavior; use sendMessage() for user input, a state signal for changing application context, or a transient reactive signal for context needed by one model request.

nodes.label: State Signal
nodes.rationale: Use for changing application context.

nodes.label: Notification Summaries
nodes.rationale: Summaries keep a busy thread from receiving a burst of individual notifications; a summarized record stays pending because a summary tells the model that records exist without marking them delivered.

nodes.label: Thread Stream
nodes.rationale: The subscription receives both the summary and the full notification as thread stream chunks.

nodes.label: Transient Reactive Signal
nodes.rationale: Use for context needed by one model request.

nodes.label: restoreVersion()
nodes.rationale: Restores by creating a new version with the same configuration rather than mutating history.

nodes.label: resumeSchedule()
nodes.rationale: Next fire time is recomputed from now so a long-paused schedule doesn't fire a backlog.

nodes.label: runSchedule()
nodes.rationale: Fires a schedule once immediately without changing its cron cadence.

nodes.label: getExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Does not require a dataset reference; datasetId is null for experiments orphaned by dataset deletion.

nodes.label: deleteTraces()
nodes.rationale: Cascades deletion to trace-linked observability signals.

nodes.label: getAgentController()
nodes.rationale: Retrieved by the registration key, which can differ from the controller id; .session(sessionId) returns a session client requiring await session.create().

nodes.label: mastra api trace query
nodes.rationale: Without an explicit --url, observability commands default to https://observability.mastra.ai even when a local server is running.

nodes.label: ClickhouseStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Delta polling is best effort because its delta index and trace records use separate materialized-view tables; the delta index retains two days of events and does not backfill historical rows.

nodes.label: getTrace()
nodes.rationale: Query responses do not include the related spans that matched the predicate, so the full trace must be loaded separately.

nodes.label: listTracesLight()
nodes.rationale: Its numbered-page-to-delta-polling workflow is replaced by using the numbered response's deltaCursor.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Stops trace queries after 15 seconds by default and returns 504; configurable via observability.traceQueryTimeoutMs.

nodes.label: queryTraces()
nodes.rationale: Lists selected traces, adding ordering and pagination to trace selection; the SDK, CLI, and HTTP endpoint all accept the same request.

nodes.label: Context identifiers (runId, sessionId, userId, organizationId)
nodes.rationale: Trace-scope predicates read the current root span; span-scope predicates bind to one related current span, so a run recorded only on a child span is found through spans.some.

nodes.label: Delta polling
nodes.rationale: Not a durable change feed and does not guarantee delivery of every matching trace; cursors bind the selection, ordering, and authorization state.

nodes.label: Entity lineage fields (entityType, entityId, entityVersionId, rootEntityVersionId)
nodes.norm_label: entity lineage fields (entitytype, entityid, entityversionid, rootentityversionid)
nodes.rationale: Version fields let one clause qualify the same span by its entity lineage.

nodes.label: metadata.<key> paths
nodes.rationale: Prefer canonical trace fields such as resourceId, threadId, or environment because they use dedicated storage columns; metadata.<key> remains for when the metadata object value is specifically needed.

nodes.label: model and provider span fields
nodes.rationale: Fall back to attributes.model/attributes.provider exported by older @mastra/observability versions so existing filters keep matching older spans; trace results omit them because a trace can match through one span while other spans used a different model.

nodes.label: outcome field
nodes.rationale: Separate from status, which only reads whether the span recorded an error; a missing outcome means not recorded, never success.

nodes.label: Pagination modes (keyset, numbered, delta)
nodes.rationale: The three modes are mutually exclusive; page, pagination, and delta mode must not be combined.

nodes.label: Query limits
nodes.rationale: The planner rejects a query before storage execution when it exceeds any limit.

nodes.label: Trace query request fields
nodes.rationale: Unknown fields are rejected; requests cannot select a projection, declare joins, request counts or measures, or control authorization.

nodes.label: Span properties (durationMs, startedAt, endedAt)
nodes.rationale: Span startedAt/endedAt conditions filter related spans independently of the top-level root timeRange.

nodes.label: spans.some / spans.none clauses
nodes.rationale: Every condition inside one clause applies to the same current span, so a matching name on one span and an error on another do not satisfy the predicate.

nodes.label: status field
nodes.rationale: Derived success/error outcome; use error when only testing whether error details are present.

nodes.label: stopReasonContext
nodes.rationale: Returned only; cannot be filtered, grouped, or sorted.

nodes.label: Store capability features and capabilities
nodes.rationale: Stores advertise support through feature flags reported as server capabilities; against an older store results omit the field and a predicate or sort on it returns 501 before storage runs.

nodes.label: tags field
nodes.rationale: A list of strings on the root span, so it uses collection operators instead of scalar in/notIn; available in trace predicates only.

nodes.label: matches / notMatches text operators
nodes.rationale: Whole-word contiguous phrase matching only; substring, wildcard, regular-expression, and fuzzy matching are not supported and there is no cross-field search.

nodes.label: timeToFirstTokenMs
nodes.rationale: Measures from the start of the provider request to the first streamed chunk, deliberately excluding work Mastra does before calling the model such as input processors; stored in its own column and omitted from stored attributes.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.rationale: Exposes the full agent loop, tools, and memory; AgentController layers session runtime defaults on top of it.

nodes.label: AgentController
nodes.rationale: Provides opinionated defaults for an ongoing session where the agent acts as a collaborator rather than a one-shot endpoint; use the Agent class directly for full control or request-response calls.

nodes.label: Channel adapters
nodes.rationale: Each external chat thread maps to one controller Session and Mastra thread.

nodes.label: createCodingAgent()
nodes.rationale: Returns a standard Agent that already has a workspace, task tracking, and retries for transient model errors, which are the defaults Mastra Code runs on.

nodes.label: controller.createSession()
nodes.rationale: Get-or-create by session id so the same controller can host many Sessions without storing a current Session on the controller.

nodes.label: session.displayState
nodes.rationale: Provides a reduced complete render snapshot for UIs; the client surface has no equivalent.

nodes.label: session.listMessages()
nodes.rationale: Paged form returns pagination metadata; the numeric form remains for the newest message window as an array.

nodes.label: MastraClient (@mastra/client-js)
nodes.rationale: Browser UIs run in a different process, so they reach the same session over the controller's HTTP routes.

nodes.label: session.model.switch()
nodes.rationale: Model selection is stored as the thread's current model and remains active when the Session changes modes.

nodes.label: session.mode.switch()
nodes.rationale: Modes change the instructions and tools used by the shared backing agent without replacing the Session or thread.

nodes.label: onSessionStart
nodes.rationale: Channel sessions are created by the controller rather than by user code, so this is where their model and memory settings are configured; it runs once per session.

nodes.label: onStaleToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Approval gates live in memory, so every approval answered after a restart is stale; this hook settles the attempt the user answered instead of dropping it.

nodes.label: session.permissions
nodes.rationale: Permission policies decide whether a tool is allowed, denied, or sent to the UI for approval; permission denies take precedence over a mode's availableTools allowlist.

nodes.label: resolveSession
nodes.rationale: Replaces built-in session creation and runs before any session exists so a host can refuse a request; onSessionStart swallows errors and therefore cannot refuse.

nodes.label: session.respondToToolSuspension()
nodes.rationale: Interactive tools use resumable tool suspensions rather than approval gates.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: An isolated live runtime per user/task so sessions with different ids have separate event buses, run loops, state, mode and model selections, and thread bindings.

nodes.label: session.subscribe()
nodes.rationale: Subscriptions are isolated by Session so events from another Session on the same controller are not delivered.

nodes.label: session.state
nodes.rationale: Treated as live Session data unless the host explicitly persists and restores it.

nodes.label: Subagents
nodes.rationale: Forked subagents preserve the parent prompt prefix and require memory on the controller; regular subagents run with constrained toolsets.

nodes.label: submit_plan tool
nodes.rationale: Takes a plan file path rather than plan text, so it needs a writable filesystem such as a workspace filesystem.

nodes.label: Thread
nodes.rationale: Stored conversation that can survive controller and process recreation when storage is configured, unlike live Session state.

nodes.label: session.thread.transferOwnership()
nodes.rationale: Transfers are serialized within one process; hosts needing durable cross-process compare-and-set should commit in their own storage first and mirror the owner.

nodes.label: Mastra Code
nodes.rationale: Flagship AgentController implementation: a coding agent with multi-model support, persistent conversations, and plan-then-execute workflows.

nodes.label: Mastra Factory
nodes.rationale: Flagship AgentController implementation: a coding agent with multi-model support, persistent conversations, and plan-then-execute workflows.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Observer and reflector model choices are independent so a host can change the main model without rewriting automatic role settings.

nodes.label: resumeBackgroundTask()
nodes.rationale: Passing options.suspendedAt lets the server reject stale answers with 409 if the task resumed or suspended again since it was read.

nodes.label: run.cancel()
nodes.rationale: Stops running steps and prevents subsequent steps; steps checking abortSignal can clean up resources such as timeouts and network requests.

nodes.label: workflow.createRun()
nodes.rationale: The resourceId parameter associates a run with a specific resource (user, tenant) and is persisted so runs can be filtered and queried later.

nodes.label: getDynamicWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Returns an instance for definition management only; execution goes through getWorkflow(id).createRun() like any other workflow.

nodes.label: listWorkflowRunCounts()
nodes.rationale: Counts are computed server-side and keyed by the workflow's registry key (which can differ from the workflow's own id); the server may cache counts for a few seconds and older servers return 404.

nodes.label: run.resume()
nodes.rationale: forEachIndex (zero-based) lets a suspended .foreach() step resume one iteration at a time; untargeted iterations remain suspended.

nodes.label: resumeSchedule()
nodes.rationale: The next fire time is recomputed from now so a long-paused schedule doesn't fire a backlog.

nodes.label: workflow.runById()
nodes.rationale: The fields option limits which optional fields are returned for performance; metadata fields and status are always included, and withNestedWorkflows skips expensive nested workflow data.

nodes.label: runSchedule()
nodes.rationale: Fires a schedule once immediately without changing its cron cadence.

nodes.label: run.start()
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget start that returns immediately; useful for long-running workflows where results are polled later via runById().

nodes.label: run.startAsync()
nodes.rationale: Awaits completion and returns the full workflow output; initialState must match the workflow's stateSchema.

nodes.label: upsertDynamicWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: The server validates, persists and live-registers the definition; nested helper workflows that don't exist yet are passed via dependencies so the bundle is validated and registered as a unit.

nodes.label: approveNetworkToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Network approval uses snapshots to capture execution state, so a storage provider must be enabled.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Creates a conversational flow where users provide the required information naturally instead of through explicit resume calls.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Required by .network() to store task history and by automatic resumption to track suspended tools across messages.

nodes.label: .network()
nodes.rationale: Uses memory to store task history and determine when a task is complete.

nodes.label: resumeNetwork()
nodes.rationale: Manual resumption gives full control over resume timing and data, suited to custom UIs with approval buttons.

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: Lets the network extract resume data from the user's message during automatic resumption.

nodes.label: structuredOutput
nodes.rationale: Returns typed, validated results; objectStream exposes partial objects as they generate.

nodes.label: Agent.network()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: the network primitive will be removed in a future major release; use supervisor agents with agent.stream() or agent.generate() instead.

nodes.label: chatRoute()
nodes.rationale: Forwards the incoming request's AbortSignal to agent.stream() so a client disconnect aborts in-flight generation; use a custom API route with consumeStream() if generation should continue after disconnect.

nodes.label: networkRoute()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated along with agent networks; migrate to supervisor agents with agent.stream() or agent.generate().

nodes.label: Agent.generate()
nodes.rationale: Non-streaming replacement for .network().

nodes.label: Agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: Streaming replacement for .network().

nodes.label: isTaskComplete
nodes.rationale: Task completion scorers validate whether the task is complete; failed scorer feedback is included in context.

nodes.label: maxSteps
nodes.rationale: Limits how many iterations the supervisor can take, replacing the implicit iteration limit in .network().

nodes.label: messageFilter
nodes.rationale: Controls what conversation context is shared with subagents, e.g. removing sensitive data.

nodes.label: .network()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated and will be removed in a future release; development now focuses on supervisor agents.

nodes.label: onDelegationComplete
nodes.rationale: Called after a delegation finishes; can bail out of the supervisor loop or return feedback saved to memory.

nodes.label: onDelegationStart
nodes.rationale: Called before the supervisor delegates; can modify the prompt, limit steps, or reject the delegation.

nodes.label: onIterationComplete
nodes.rationale: Called after each supervisor loop iteration to log progress, provide feedback, or stop early.

nodes.label: Routing agent
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favor of supervisor agents, which provide the same multi-agent coordination through a simpler API that improves control and debugging.

nodes.label: Storage provider
nodes.rationale: Required for network approval because snapshots capture execution state.

nodes.label: Supervisor agents
nodes.rationale: Replacement for deprecated agent networks; same multi-agent coordination with a simpler API.

nodes.label: getParams()
nodes.rationale: Normalizes URL/query/body extraction because frameworks expose these values differently.

nodes.label: MastraServer (abstract class)
nodes.rationale: Provides the foundation for all adapters: handles route registration logic, parameter validation, and other shared functionality so adapters only implement framework-specific parts.

nodes.label: registerAuthMiddleware()
nodes.rationale: Should skip registration entirely when authentication is not configured on the Mastra instance.

nodes.label: registerContextMiddleware()
nodes.rationale: Runs first and attaches Mastra context to every incoming request because route handlers need access to the Mastra instance, tools, and other context to function.

nodes.label: stream()
nodes.rationale: Reads from the agent stream and optionally applies redaction to hide sensitive data before writing chunks in SSE or newline-delimited JSON format.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is a good production default because it works well for transactional runtime state and is widely available as a managed service.

nodes.label: storage.prune()
nodes.rationale: Called from a scheduler or maintenance job to enforce retention policies.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Default storage for snapshots.

nodes.label: Agent-level storage
nodes.rationale: Configured on a Memory instance and overrides instance-level storage for that agent's memory data only, for an isolated memory boundary or different backend.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Persistence layer for the Mastra runtime so memory, workflow state, observability data, eval results, schedules, and long-running agent state survive restarts.

nodes.label: Repository file storage (code source)
nodes.rationale: Keeping overrides as JSON files alongside application code lets developers review them in pull requests and deploy them with the application, with Git providing review and version history.

nodes.label: Agent editor configuration field
nodes.rationale: TypeScript defines starting values that collaborators can override; when a field is handed to Editor, Studio owns that field exclusively and it must be omitted from the agent config.

nodes.label: Project tools
nodes.rationale: Project tools must be implemented and registered in the Mastra project by a developer; collaborators cannot implement new tools in Studio.

nodes.label: Editor versioning (draft and published)
nodes.rationale: Saving creates a draft while the live agent keeps serving the published version, so changes can be tested before going live.

nodes.label: AI Elements component library
nodes.rationale: The ai-elements command runs shadcn add against the AI Elements registry, which currently publishes Radix UI components only; installing into a Base UI project produces TypeScript errors.

nodes.label: src/app/api/chat/route.ts
nodes.rationale: POST streams the agent response in AI SDK format; GET fetches message history from memory so the UI can be hydrated on reload.

nodes.label: createNextRouteHandler
nodes.rationale: Exposes Mastra's full HTTP API (agents, tools, workflows, memory, custom API routes, MCP, A2A) through the same Next.js deployment via a catch-all route.

nodes.label: mastra instance (src/mastra/index.ts)
nodes.rationale: When running Studio alongside Next.js, the storage URL must be an absolute path because relative paths resolve based on each process's working directory, which differs between next dev and mastra dev.

nodes.label: agentConfig()
nodes.rationale: `model` is the only required field; the build fails when an agent directory doesn't provide a model, while other capabilities come from sibling files or have defaults.

nodes.label: instructions.ts
nodes.rationale: Allows the always-on prompt to be computed in TypeScript; wins over instructions.md when both exist.

nodes.label: memory.ts
nodes.rationale: Configures persistent memory without crowding runtime options.

nodes.label: workspace.ts
nodes.rationale: Configures files and sandbox behavior separately from model settings.

nodes.label: Discovery Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Discovery is source-based and conservative: it skips symlinks, test files, and non-agent directories, and file-routes workflows and singleton project files only when they have a default export.

nodes.label: File-Based Agent
nodes.rationale: After discovery a file-based agent runs as a normal Agent, so the Agent API, Studio, workflows, and application code all use the same runtime as a code-defined agent.

nodes.label: config.ts Precedence Rules
nodes.rationale: Dynamic config.instructions beats the instructions file, static config.instructions loses to it, instructions.ts beats instructions.md; function-valued config.tools/config.skills cause discovered tools/skills to be ignored, while object values merge with config winning on collisions.

nodes.label: config.ts (file-based agent)
nodes.rationale: Keep config.ts focused on runtime options; adjacent concerns live in sibling files when they benefit from their own location (readable markdown prompts, typed tool modules, load-on-demand skills, separate memory/workspace/processor config).

nodes.label: instructions.md
nodes.rationale: Keeps the always-on prompt readable as markdown.

nodes.label: processors/
nodes.rationale: Separates input and output processing pipelines.

nodes.label: skills/
nodes.rationale: Keeps load-on-demand procedures separate from always-on instructions.

nodes.label: subagents/
nodes.rationale: Gives each specialist child agent its own directory; file-based subagents require a non-empty description because the parent model uses it for delegation routing.

nodes.label: tools/
nodes.rationale: Gives each callable action its own typed module.

nodes.label: addFeedback()
nodes.rationale: addFeedback() is optional on the observability entrypoint, so callers must check that the active observability implementation supports it before calling it.

nodes.label: CorrelationContext
nodes.rationale: Live span or trace context lets feedback be emitted without rehydrating the target from storage.

nodes.label: createFeedback()
nodes.rationale: Storage-level calls write directly to the store, so the caller must include timestamp; the HTTP/client SDK route sets timestamp server-side and generates feedbackId when omitted.

nodes.label: deleteFeedback()
nodes.rationale: On ClickHouse, deletion uses lightweight deletes on the main feedback events table to remove rows from reads without guaranteeing immediate physical removal, so open-source deployments must configure an observability retention period to physically purge them.

nodes.label: MastraStorageExporter
nodes.rationale: Must be configured when adding feedback by ID after execution, including when MastraPlatformExporter handles remote export.

nodes.label: updateFeedbackReviewStatus()
nodes.rationale: Retries the pending delete; throws a not-found error if the retry succeeds, or saves the new status and throws the delete's error if it fails again.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext
nodes.rationale: Current observability domain implementation; the legacy ObservabilityStorageClickhouse class remains supported for projects that haven't migrated.

nodes.label: Observability feedback HTTP routes
nodes.rationale: These routes belong to a Mastra runtime and use its configured observability storage; they are separate from the unversioned Mastra Platform Feedback API, which doesn't provide a feedback creation route.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Composite storage lets you mix adapters per domain when the adapter packages export the corresponding domain classes.

nodes.label: applyRetention()
nodes.rationale: Lets deployments update TTL configuration without running the full initialization path.

nodes.label: prune()
nodes.rationale: Deletes in bounded, batched chunks (each batch its own transaction) so it never takes a long lock or bloats the transaction log; runs are resumable and cancellable; it never runs a VACUUM.

nodes.label: PruneOptions
nodes.rationale: maxBatches, maxRows, pauseMs and signal bound each run so a large backlog drains over several maintenance windows without starving live traffic.

nodes.label: PruneResult
nodes.rationale: done:false signals eligible rows remain so the caller can call prune() again on the next tick.

nodes.label: RetentionConfig
nodes.rationale: Fully typed: domain keys must exist and their table keys must be declared retention-eligible, so unknown domains or tables produce compile errors.

nodes.label: TableRetentionPolicy
nodes.rationale: batchSize bounds lock duration and WAL growth on large tables by making each batch its own transaction.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Native TTL
nodes.rationale: ClickHouse observability storage uses native table TTLs instead of prune(); deletion requests are retained for the longest finite signal retention plus 30 days so erasure keeps being enforced after signal rows expire.

nodes.label: Growth Tables
nodes.rationale: Retention covers only tables that accumulate rows unbounded as a side effect of normal operation; user-authored artifacts and config grow with user intent and are edited or deleted explicitly, so they're not valid retention keys.

nodes.label: MongoDB TTL Indexes
nodes.rationale: TTL is simpler and zero-maintenance for fixed retention periods; prune() gives more control over deletion timing, rate capping, and resumable/cancellable cleanup.

nodes.label: Reclaiming Disk Space
nodes.rationale: prune() deletes rows but doesn't shrink the database file; freed pages go on a freelist for reuse, which prevents unbounded file growth for most users, and handing space back to the OS is a separate concern Mastra doesn't manage.

nodes.label: Age-Based Storage Retention
nodes.rationale: Storage grows without bound by default, so retention is opt-in and age-based; unconfigured data is kept forever so behavior doesn't change until you opt in.

nodes.label: maxRetainedTasks
nodes.rationale: Caps every task the in-memory store still holds so a client running many short tasks cannot grow memory without bound.

nodes.label: MCPTaskStoreAdmin
nodes.rationale: A custom store must implement it (list, updateByKey, cancelByKey) for Studio to list tasks.

nodes.label: tasks.recover
nodes.rationale: Only applies to tasks kept in Mastra storage; workflow tasks ignore it.

nodes.label: tasks option
nodes.rationale: Lets a tool, workflow or agent answer tools/call with a task so the result outlives the request and is not limited by HTTP timeouts.

nodes.label: Agent graph entry
nodes.rationale: Only retries and metadata persist; function-valued options such as onFinish and function-valued toolChoice are rejected when a code-defined workflow is stored.

nodes.label: DynamicWorkflowGraph
nodes.rationale: Schemas use JSON Schema rather than Zod so the definition can round-trip through JSON; Mastra converts each schema to Zod when it registers the workflow.

nodes.label: Mapping graph entry
nodes.rationale: Mapping entries must be top-level graph entries; they can't be placed inside parallel, conditional, foreach, or loop containers.

nodes.label: JSON predicate DSL
nodes.rationale: Missing paths don't throw; path-based operators return false when the path can't be resolved, so exists/notExists distinguish a missing value from a falsy value.

nodes.label: Sleep / sleepUntil graph entry
nodes.rationale: Stored definitions require literal duration/date values; use a code-defined workflow when the duration or date must be calculated at runtime.

nodes.label: CompositeFilesystem
nodes.rationale: Use manual composition when another part of the application needs the composite as a filesystem provider; the mounts option performs the same routing setup with less configuration for normal sandbox mounting.

nodes.label: LocalSandbox
nodes.rationale: LocalSandbox creates a symlink inside its workingDirectory instead of using FUSE for mounts.

nodes.label: mastra_workspace_apply_patch
nodes.rationale: Opt-in only: it must be enabled with its own entry in tools, and the top-level tools.enabled does not turn it on. The tool checks every change in the patch before it writes any file.

nodes.label: prepareQuery()
nodes.rationale: prepareQuery exposes the client for hover, definition, implementation, and other direct queries; the file must be closed before releasing the lease, both in a finally block, because a leaked lease can prevent an idle client from being evicted when maxOpenClients is set.

nodes.label: Containment
nodes.rationale: Containment applies to filesystem operations including file tools and search indexing, but does not restrict shell commands.

nodes.label: Filesystem resolver
nodes.rationale: A resolver lets storage vary by request, user, role, or tenant; write tools stay registered because the provider is not known until the request runs, so the provider rejects writes at runtime.

nodes.label: Mounts
nodes.rationale: Mounts are a better fit than passing file contents between tool calls when programs expect a directory tree or need to process large or binary files.

nodes.label: File-tool and command-tool policies
nodes.rationale: File-tool and command-tool policies are independent: requiring approval for write_file does not stop the agent from using execute_command to write the same mounted path, so command tools must be disabled if files must only be accessed through file tools.

nodes.label: Custom language servers
nodes.rationale: Custom definitions are merged with built-in definitions; a custom definition with the same id replaces the built-in one.

nodes.label: LSP inspection
nodes.rationale: A language server can identify a symbol's type, declaration, implementations, and diagnostics because it understands the language and project structure; LSP complements read_file, grep, and search rather than replacing them.

nodes.label: lsp.root
nodes.rationale: Mastra normally finds a project root per file by walking upward for the server's project markers and falls back to lsp.root when no marker is found; restrict it to a trusted project because LocalFilesystem containment and allowedPaths do not constrain LSP inspection.

nodes.label: maxOpenClients
nodes.rationale: Limits the language-server clients retained for one configuration; when the limit is reached Mastra closes the least recently used client that has no active query lease. Omitting it leaves retained clients unlimited; Mastra Code uses a default limit of 4.

nodes.label: packageRunner
nodes.rationale: Package-runner fallback is disabled by default because it may install software or hang in some project layouts.

nodes.label: refundCorrectnessScorer
nodes.rationale: Correctness is binary: 1 means every requirement is satisfied and no prohibited claims appear; 0 means at least one criterion failed. A fractional score such as 0.8 would obscure that distinction.

nodes.label: Eval Loop
nodes.rationale: LLMs are stochastic and users ask unanticipated questions, so vibes alone cannot tell whether a change improved quality; a systematic loop provides evidence to improve the agent, try a different model, and catch regressions.

nodes.label: Golden Dataset
nodes.rationale: Keep the dataset small enough to read the results manually; add cases when gaps are discovered.

nodes.label: LLM Judge
nodes.rationale: Choose a different model from the agent, ideally from another provider; keep the judge fixed when comparing changes, and review its judgments because it can make mistakes too.

nodes.label: mastra.shutdown()
nodes.rationale: Stops runs still executing after its drain window without further writes and releases their claims, so the next boot recovers them without waiting for claims to lapse.

nodes.label: recover()
nodes.rationale: force: true takes over a run still held by a hung execution; without force it throws DURABLE_AGENT_RUN_ACTIVE for a live run.

nodes.label: recoverActiveRuns()
nodes.rationale: Manual recovery entry point for finer control such as scheduled recovery; returns each run's outcome and does not re-check skipped runs.

nodes.label: recoverAllDurableAgents()
nodes.rationale: Called by the deployer on boot when recovery.durableAgents is 'auto'; returns counts and schedules eligible ownership re-checks itself.

nodes.label: shouldPersistSnapshot option
nodes.rationale: A custom predicate replaces the default policy; one that includes 'running' keeps crash-recovery checkpoints without enabling automatic recovery (e.g. when calling recoverActiveRuns() behind a leader election).

nodes.label: Automatic Recovery
nodes.rationale: recovery.durableAgents: 'auto' is the only automatic recovery path for durable agent runs, which are excluded from the generic boot-time restart of active workflow runs.

nodes.label: Crash Recovery
nodes.rationale: Recovery re-runs the agentic loop from the last persisted snapshot, which can reissue LLM calls (with real cost) and re-execute tool calls, so tools must be idempotent or deduplicate external side effects.

nodes.label: Manual Recovery
nodes.rationale: Reads the same running checkpoints as automatic recovery, so with recovery off a run that crashes before reaching a shutdown step boundary has no checkpoint and is not found.

nodes.label: Run Fencing
nodes.rationale: When the workflows store supports run fencing, each write is checked against the claim in the same operation, so writes from an execution that lost the run are rejected; without it the claim is only a PubSub lease and a taken-over run can end with the old execution's output.

nodes.label: Run Ownership
nodes.rationale: Every stream/generate/resume/recover call claims the run and renews the claim every 5 seconds; a claim lapses 15 seconds after its last renewal so a crashed process's run becomes recoverable quickly while two executions cannot drive the same run.

nodes.label: Snapshot Persistence
nodes.rationale: pending, paused, and suspended snapshots are always persisted because resume() and tool approval read them; per-step running checkpoints exist solely to make in-flight runs recoverable after a crash, so they are skipped when recovery is off until shutdown.

nodes.label: Tool Approval (human-in-the-loop)
nodes.rationale: When a tool call requires approval the workflow suspends and emits onSuspended, waiting for the caller to resume with resume(); suspended snapshots are always persisted so this works without configuration.

nodes.label: createTool()
nodes.rationale: Lets agents trigger browser-side functionality such as DOM manipulation or local storage access, enabling tool execution in the user's environment rather than on the server.

nodes.label: MastraClient.upsertDynamicWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: A successful upsert validates the complete definition and registers it with the running Mastra instance; calling again with the same id replaces the stored definition and live workflow registration.

nodes.label: Mastra client
nodes.rationale: The Mastra Client SDK provides a concise, type-safe interface for interacting with a Mastra Server from the client environment; it is designed for browser environments and uses the native fetch API.

nodes.label: hideSignals option
nodes.rationale: Filters signal chunks for one subscriber only; it is not a security boundary and doesn't change model context or stored messages.

nodes.label: reconnect option
nodes.rationale: Long-lived subscriptions resubscribe on transport close, retrying indefinitely with a one-second delay by default; 4xx other than 408/429 and 501 stop retrying.

nodes.label: subscribeToThread()
nodes.rationale: Subscribe before sending input so output from the start of the run is received.

nodes.label: thread-history chunk
nodes.rationale: Carries the newest page of stored messages oldest-first; has an empty runId because its messages can span several runs.

nodes.label: thread-run-status chunk
nodes.rationale: Identifies a run's outcome independently of its output; a run outcome doesn't close the thread subscription.

nodes.label: withInitialHistory option
