nodes.rationale: Lets an application show the conversation so far before displaying new output; requires memory.

nodes.label: withRunStatus option
nodes.rationale: Opt-in so existing subscriptions don't receive run outcome chunks by default.

nodes.label: subscribeThreadEvents()
nodes.rationale: Use separately to observe queue counts.

nodes.label: Studio Models panel
nodes.rationale: Model panel edits change the running server's in-memory agent and are lost on restart; function-valued model lists are read-only because they can vary by request context.

nodes.label: ClickhouseStore
nodes.rationale: Long-standing class backing every domain with the legacy observability adapter; new projects should prefer ClickhouseStoreVNext.

nodes.label: ClickhouseStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Backs memory, workflows, and observability domains with ClickHouse and uses the vNext observability adapter automatically, avoiding manual composite wiring.

nodes.label: MastraStorageExporter
nodes.rationale: Automatically selects the insert-only strategy when ClickHouse is the observability backend.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouse
nodes.rationale: Original legacy observability adapter retained for projects not yet migrated to the vNext schema.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext
nodes.rationale: Current observability domain implementation using an insert-only schema backed by ReplacingMergeTree, optimized for trace/log/metric/score/feedback volume.

nodes.label: ClickHouse
nodes.rationale: Recommended production observability backend: columnar compression and insert-only strategy give highest write throughput.

nodes.label: Insert-Only Strategy
nodes.rationale: Writes completed spans in batches without per-span updates, giving the highest write throughput.

nodes.label: Replication Configuration
nodes.rationale: Opt-in replicated table configuration for self-managed multi-replica clusters; not for ClickHouse Cloud because Cloud rewrites MergeTree to SharedMergeTree server-side.

nodes.label: Retention TTL
nodes.rationale: Applied only when the retention option is passed; Mastra configures no default retention TTL.

nodes.label: createBuilderAgent()
nodes.rationale: The @mastra/editor/ee subpath is gated by the Mastra Enterprise Edition license at runtime; the returned agent is registered under agents on the Mastra instance and the key name is conventional.

nodes.label: EditorAgentNamespace
nodes.rationale: applyStoredOverrides returns a fork with overrides applied and leaves the input agent unchanged, so callers must use the returned Agent; it is called internally by mastra.getAgent().

nodes.label: EditorScorerNamespace
nodes.rationale: scorer.resolve returns null for preset types or when instructions or model configuration are missing, since only llm-judge definitions can be built into a runnable MastraScorer.

nodes.label: MastraEditor class
nodes.rationale: Passed to the Mastra constructor to turn on editor features (prompt blocks, agent code override, versioning, tool providers); the 'source' option chooses whether overrides live in the storage backend ('db') or as per-agent JSON files on disk ('code'), and when source is omitted the editor uses configured database storage even though getSource() returns undefined.

nodes.label: createCompletenessScorer()
nodes.rationale: Takes no options and has no scale option: the score is always covered_elements / total_input_elements between 0 and 1, so completeness is comparable across runs.

nodes.label: createContentSimilarityScorer()
nodes.rationale: ignoreCase and ignoreWhitespace default to true only when no options object is passed; passing an options object makes omitted values false, so explicit configuration is never silently overridden.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Used to point storage at an externally hosted libSQL database since the platform no longer hosts one.

nodes.label: MastraPlatformExporter
nodes.rationale: Sends observability events to Mastra platform when MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN is set.

nodes.label: MastraStorageExporter
nodes.rationale: Persists observability events to Mastra Storage for Studio.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.rationale: Replaces logger-based tracing with explicit exporters.

nodes.label: PinoLogger
nodes.rationale: Legacy logger-based tracing approach used before the Observability class.

nodes.label: SensitiveDataFilter
nodes.rationale: Redacts passwords, tokens, and keys from span data before export.

nodes.label: Cloud Store
nodes.rationale: Managed libSQL database backed by Turso that must be exported and migrated to a self-hosted database.

nodes.label: Mastra Cloud
nodes.rationale: Legacy single-project product being replaced by the Mastra platform.

nodes.label: Mastra Platform
nodes.rationale: Replaces Mastra Cloud with separate Studio and Server products, CLI-driven deploys, and a new observability system.

nodes.label: TaskSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: The task list is stored under the task state type in the thread-scoped threadState storage domain, which is the source of truth, and projected onto the tasks agent state-signal lane by the processor, so it survives observational-memory truncation without invalidating the prompt cache.

nodes.label: task_update tool
nodes.rationale: Setting a task to in_progress automatically demotes any other in_progress task to pending, enforcing a single active task.

nodes.label: task_write tool
nodes.rationale: Each call replaces the entire task list; omitted IDs reuse a previous unambiguous match so IDs stay stable across rewrites.

nodes.label: threadState storage domain
nodes.rationale: The task list is persisted in the thread-scoped threadState domain and projected onto the state-signal lane so it survives observational-memory truncation.

nodes.label: TaskSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Recommended setup because it bundles all four task tools and the TaskStateProcessor in a single registration.

nodes.label: .branch()
nodes.rationale: All steps in a branch need the same inputSchema and outputSchema because branching requires consistent schemas so workflows can follow different paths.

nodes.label: Nested workflow
nodes.rationale: Better parallelism: with concurrency N, multiple items run their full pipelines simultaneously. Chained .foreach().foreach() processes all items through step 1, waits, then all through step 2, while nested workflows let each item progress independently.

nodes.label: A2AAgent
nodes.rationale: Wraps a remote A2A agent so a parent Mastra agent can delegate work to it as a subagent; falls back to the non-streaming generate path when the remote card doesn't advertise streaming.

nodes.label: resumeGenerate() / resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Sends follow-up input or credentials back to a remote task that reached input-required or auth-required, using the original taskId.

nodes.label: verifyAgentCard hook
nodes.rationale: Lets a parent agent validate a remote agent before delegating work to it, enforcing expected providers, endpoints, certificate-bound identities, or signed cards.

nodes.label: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol v0.3.0
nodes.rationale: An open protocol for delegating work to agents across network, framework, vendor, and language boundaries, letting a remote agent keep its tools, prompts, memory, workflows, and infrastructure private.

nodes.label: A2A agent card
nodes.rationale: Used for discovery: a JSON document served from a well-known URL that describes the remote agent and includes the execution URL accepting A2A JSON-RPC requests.

nodes.label: Signed agent cards
nodes.rationale: Lets clients verify that a discovered card came from a trusted publisher and wasn't changed in transit; client verification is opt-in and unsigned cards still return unchanged.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop (input-required task state)
nodes.rationale: A2A models HITL work with the input-required task state; Mastra maps its agent suspension model to this state in both directions.

nodes.label: A2A push notifications
nodes.rationale: Used when a client can't keep a stream open or a long-running task should update a callback URL after the original request ends; delivery is best-effort.

nodes.label: Agent-to-Agent (A2A)
nodes.rationale: Used to expose or consume remote agents across service, framework, vendor, and language boundaries.

nodes.label: Connections
nodes.rationale: Choose a connection type based on which system owns the agent runtime and what you need to exchange.

nodes.label: createScorer
nodes.rationale: Unified factory so custom scorers can be built from either native JavaScript functions or LLM-based prompt objects for each evaluation step; at least a generateScore step must be provided.

nodes.label: generateLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Legacy model adapters bypass error processors and use the AI SDK's separate maxRetries default of 2, so coordinated processor retries require the current generation API.

nodes.label: StreamErrorRetryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Keeps retryUnknownErrors disabled by default so authentication, invalid-request and context-length errors fail immediately, and bounds Retry-After values to 30_000 ms by default.

nodes.label: generateScore Step
nodes.rationale: Mastra forwards the judge's number without clamping or normalizing, so the prompt is the only thing defining the score scale; endpoints and middle values must be named explicitly.

nodes.label: Judge configuration
nodes.rationale: The judge only runs for steps defined as prompt objects; function-only scorers never call the judge, so any score or reason must be produced by the functions themselves.

nodes.label: createMultiTurnJudgeScorer()
nodes.rationale: Grades every assistant turn together against one plain-English criterion, scoring 1 or 0.

nodes.label: extractAgentResponseMessages()
nodes.rationale: Returns the text of each assistant message in order so custom scorers can grade a whole transcript.

nodes.label: inputs Array
nodes.rationale: Each input is sent sequentially on the same thread and scorers see the accumulated output, giving one whole-conversation score.

nodes.label: Agent Memory for Cross-turn Recall
nodes.rationale: Recall requires both a resource and a thread because Mastra memory scopes messages by resource and thread; without memory each input runs in isolation.

nodes.label: Multi-turn Evals
nodes.rationale: Multi-turn evals exist to test behavior that emerges across a conversation: memory recall, follow-up questions, tool-call sequences, and multi-step workflows.

nodes.label: Scorer Compatibility with inputs
nodes.rationale: Accumulated output only helps if the scorer reads all of it; prebuilt LLM judges read a single assistant message so they grade only the last turn.

nodes.label: turns Per-turn Assertions
nodes.rationale: The inputs form can hide per-turn failures (an includes check passes if any turn mentions the term), so turns exists when correctness depends on individual turns.

nodes.label: Agent Controller client (client-js)
nodes.rationale: Browser UIs run in a different process, so they reach the same session over the controller's HTTP routes instead of holding the Session object.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: An isolated live runtime per user/task so that event buses, run loops, state, mode and model selections are not shared across concurrent work.

nodes.label: session.displayState.get()
nodes.rationale: Provides a complete render snapshot for UIs; the client surface has no equivalent.

nodes.label: session.model.switch()
nodes.rationale: Model selection is stored as the thread's current model and remains active when the Session changes modes; switching modes doesn't change the model.

nodes.label: session.om.observer
nodes.rationale: Automatic role selection lets a host change the main model without rewriting automatic observer/reflector role settings.

nodes.label: session.permissions
nodes.rationale: Permission denies take precedence over the mode's availableTools allowlist.

nodes.label: session.respondToToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Grants such as always_allow_category are scoped to the gate's thread and are not durable process-level permissions.

nodes.label: session.state
nodes.rationale: Treated as live Session data unless the host explicitly persists and restores it.

nodes.label: session.subagents.model
nodes.rationale: Selections are written to thread settings, and an agent-type selection takes precedence over the Session's default subagent model.

nodes.label: session.subscribe()
nodes.rationale: Subscriptions are isolated by Session so events from another Session on the same controller are not delivered to this listener.

nodes.label: toolCategoryResolver
nodes.rationale: Maps custom tools to categories so category-level permission policies can apply to them.

nodes.label: ClickHouse
nodes.rationale: Recommended target for observability when PostgreSQL trace volume outgrows the deployment, reached via composite storage.

nodes.label: PostgresStore.close()
nodes.rationale: Destroys the pool only if Mastra created it; a caller-provided pool is left open.

nodes.label: PostgresStore.init()
nodes.rationale: Called automatically when storage is passed to Mastra; must be called explicitly when storage is used directly, otherwise tables are not created and operations fail.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: Production-ready PostgreSQL storage; when a pg.Pool is supplied Mastra does not create or close the pool, so the caller owns its lifecycle. disableInit exists for CI/CD pipelines where migrations run separately.

nodes.label: brin index
nodes.rationale: Very small storage; best for large tables with natural ordering and range queries.

nodes.label: btree index
nodes.rationale: Default index method; best for range queries, sorting and general purpose use.

nodes.label: gin index
nodes.rationale: Large storage; fast for contains queries over JSONB, arrays and full-text search.

nodes.label: recover()
nodes.rationale: Recovery restarts from the persisted durable-agentic-loop checkpoint and does not guarantee exactly-once execution, so tool side effects must be idempotent.

nodes.label: durable-agentic-loop checkpoint
nodes.rationale: The nested execution row alone is not sufficient for recovery; the persisted durable-agentic-loop checkpoint is required.

nodes.label: config.ts
nodes.rationale: config.workspace wins over workspace.ts, including when set to undefined.

nodes.label: workspace.ts
nodes.rationale: Add workspace.ts only when the default local directory is not enough (different filesystem root, different sandbox provider, workspace search, or sharing one workspace across agents).

nodes.label: server.drainTimeout
nodes.rationale: Increase when rolling deploys need long-running agent turns or workflow steps to finish; the HTTP drain and workflow drain run one after the other, so plan for twice this value plus 5 seconds of cleanup below the platform grace period. Setting 0 skips both drains.

nodes.label: server.handleShutdownSignals
nodes.rationale: Set to false to manage signals yourself; without a handler Node's default behavior terminates immediately with no drain, and during mastra dev the built-in handlers release storage resources between hot reloads (e.g. DuckDB file locks).

nodes.label: workspace
nodes.rationale: Gives agents a persistent environment for storing files and executing commands; agents inherit the global workspace on the Mastra class unless they have their own.

nodes.label: FilesystemProvider
nodes.rationale: The built-in 'local' filesystem provider is auto-registered; external providers (e.g. S3 or GCS) are supplied via MastraEditorConfig.filesystems and createFilesystem(config) is called at workspace hydration time using the provider id from the stored StorageWorkspaceRef.

nodes.label: ProcessorProvider
nodes.rationale: Serves two purposes: discovery (info, configSchema, availablePhases let the UI render configuration forms) and runtime (createProcessor(config) is called during agent hydration to instantiate processors from stored configuration).

nodes.label: editor.prompt Namespace
nodes.rationale: update() creates a new draft when content changes.

nodes.label: createSandbox
nodes.rationale: Called at workspace hydration time to create a runtime WorkspaceSandbox instance from stored config.

nodes.label: SandboxProvider
nodes.rationale: Interface a package implements to register a sandbox with MastraEditor; the editor calls createSandbox at workspace hydration time using the provider id as lookup key.

nodes.label: StorageWorkspaceRef
nodes.rationale: Discriminated union to attach a workspace to a stored agent: reference by id, inline snapshot, or provider-built workspace.

nodes.label: StorageBrowserConfig
nodes.rationale: Defined in @mastra/core/storage; provider must match a BrowserProvider.id registered on MastraEditor.browsers.

nodes.label: StorageBrowserRef
nodes.rationale: Browsers are always inlined; a { type: 'id' } variant isn't available.

nodes.label: StorageFilesystemConfig
nodes.rationale: provider must match an id registered on MastraEditor.filesystems (built-in: local).

nodes.label: StorageSandboxConfig
nodes.rationale: provider must match an id registered on MastraEditor.sandboxes (built-in: local).

nodes.label: StorageWorkspaceSnapshotType
nodes.rationale: Defined in @mastra/core/storage; serialized workspace configuration embedded under inline refs.

nodes.label: createContextPrecisionScorer()
nodes.rationale: Uses Mean Average Precision so that relevant context placed earlier in the sequence is rewarded, reflecting that early relevant context is more valuable to the model than later relevant context.

nodes.label: createContextRecallScorer()
nodes.rationale: Requires a ground-truth reference answer and returns a score of 0 rather than throwing when groundTruth is absent, so labeled-dataset CI runs degrade gracefully instead of failing.

nodes.label: Mean Average Precision (MAP)
nodes.rationale: MAP = (Σ Precision@k) / R, computed only at positions where relevant items appear, so it captures both relevance and ranking position.

nodes.label: buildBasePrompt()
nodes.rationale: Provides the behavioral prompt Mastra Code uses (repository exploration, edits, commands, commits) for building the instructions passed to createCodingAgent().

nodes.label: createCodingAgent()
nodes.rationale: Builds a coding Agent with the essential defaults a coding agent always needs (local workspace, task signal provider when memory is configured, network-retry error processors, goal judge prompt) so only model and instructions are required; the defaults match the ones Mastra Code runs on, but the product prompt, modes and tools are deliberately not included.

nodes.label: CyberRefusalHandler
nodes.rationale: Retries once when an OpenAI or Anthropic cybersecurity safeguard refuses a step, which often happens to ordinary coding work; it runs in both the error lane (OpenAI refusals are API errors) and the output lane (Anthropic refusals finish the step).

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Configuring memory is what enables the default TaskSignalProvider and is required for goals, which need a memory-backed thread.

nodes.label: PrefillErrorHandler
nodes.rationale: Included for provider compatibility: repairs errors caused by the shape of the message history.

nodes.label: ProviderHistoryCompat
nodes.rationale: Included for provider compatibility: repairs errors caused by the shape of the message history, such as a provider rejecting a conversation that ends with an assistant message.

nodes.label: setObjective()
nodes.rationale: The goal objective is per thread and set with setObjective(), while the goal config carries the judge and run budget.

nodes.label: StreamErrorRetryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Default retry policies: unknown errors retry twice after 3000ms, ECONNRESET retries twice with exponential backoff capped at 30000ms, bad-request retries once after 2000ms; specific policies take precedence over the unknown-error policy.

nodes.label: TaskSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Only added when memory is configured because it needs a memory-backed thread to persist the task list; it is merged into (not replacing) user-supplied signal providers so task tracking is not dropped by custom providers.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.rationale: The default workspace runs commands on the host machine with the permissions of the application process, so an isolated sandbox must be supplied for untrusted work.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Ask decision models fixed-option questions about application state and return typed answers; registered classifiers are retrievable via getClassifier()/getClassifierById().

nodes.label: IDeployer
nodes.rationale: Deployment provider for publishing applications to cloud platforms.

nodes.label: events
nodes.rationale: Internal pub/sub event handler map used by Mastra's workflow engine; most users won't need it.

nodes.label: MastraModelGateway
nodes.rationale: Gateways handle provider-specific authentication, URL construction and model resolution, enabling custom or self-hosted LLM providers.

nodes.label: idGenerator
nodes.rationale: Custom ID generator receiving IdGeneratorContext (idType, source, entityId, threadId, resourceId, role, stepType) so IDs can be shaped by what is being created; defaults to crypto.randomUUID().

nodes.label: IMastraLogger
nodes.rationale: Defaults to ConsoleLogger at INFO in development and WARN in production; can be set to false to disable logging entirely.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: Central configuration object: top-level registries (agents, tools, memory, processors, scorers, vectors, workflows, etc.) exist so reusable instances can be shared across multiple agents rather than configured per agent.

nodes.label: MCPServerBase
nodes.rationale: Exposes Mastra tools, agents, workflows and resources to MCP-compatible clients.

nodes.label: MastraMemory
nodes.rationale: Gives agents coherence across interactions via message history, working memory and semantic recall; the top-level registry is for reusable instances shared across agents.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.rationale: Tracing captures model interactions, agent execution paths, tool calls and workflow steps for monitoring and debugging.

nodes.label: Processor
nodes.rationale: Run at specific points in the agent execution pipeline to modify inputs before the model or outputs before they are returned, e.g. guardrails, prompt-injection detection, moderation.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: Used internally by Mastra for workflow event processing and component communication; defaults to EventEmitterPubSub.

nodes.label: Scorer
nodes.rationale: Provide quantifiable metrics for measuring agent quality using model-graded, rule-based and statistical methods.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Persistence backend used by memory, workflows, traces and background tasks.

nodes.label: MastraVector
nodes.rationale: Vector stores for semantic search and embeddings used in RAG pipelines and similarity search.

nodes.label: Workflow
nodes.rationale: Used for tasks that involve multiple steps with a specific execution order, giving control over how data flows between steps.

nodes.label: backgroundTasks
nodes.rationale: enabled is a feature-availability switch only: it does not opt any tool into background dispatch, tools must opt in at the tool or agent layer. Requires a configured storage backend because tasks are persisted.

nodes.label: OtelBridge.executeInContext
nodes.rationale: Runs async work inside the OTEL context of a Mastra span so OTEL-instrumented code inside the function gets correct parent relationships.

nodes.label: OtelBridge.flush
nodes.rationale: Global providers are resolved at flush time so a LoggerProvider registered after bridge construction is flushed too; neither this method nor forceFlush waits for batches the OTEL SDK has already started exporting, so sdk.shutdown() should also be called before process exit.

nodes.label: NodeSDK
nodes.rationale: Installs a context manager automatically; without a context manager spans are still exported but Mastra root spans cannot read the active span and start new traces instead of joining the outer trace.

nodes.label: OtelBridge.onLogEvent
nodes.rationale: Trace correlation resolved in order: (1) log's spanId with a stored OTEL span context, (2) log's traceId+spanId attached to the log record's SpanContext, (3) whatever OTEL context is currently active. Silent no-op if no LoggerProvider is registered globally.

nodes.label: OtelBridge
nodes.rationale: Experimental bridge providing bidirectional integration: creates native OTEL spans for Mastra operations, inherits context from active OTEL spans, and forwards Mastra log events to the global OTEL LoggerProvider under the originating span's context so trace-log correlation works automatically.

nodes.label: OtelBridge.shutdown
nodes.rationale: Ends spans that weren't properly closed, then flushes providers so those spans are exported.

nodes.label: OTEL TracerProvider
nodes.rationale: Must be registered globally (or passed to the bridge) for Mastra spans to be exported; without one agents and workflows still run but no Mastra spans are exported through OpenTelemetry.

nodes.label: MemoryInputFilter
nodes.rationale: When a stored message and an input message share an ID, the stored copy keeps its text, reasoning, provider metadata, and createdAt, so a client can't change a stored message by sending a different copy of it.

nodes.label: MessageHistory
nodes.rationale: System messages are filtered out because they shouldn't be stored in the database; incomplete tool calls are filtered out before persistence.

nodes.label: SignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Signal providers aren't processors by default; providers that need to intercept agent execution return processors from getInputProcessors()/getOutputProcessors(), and providers exposing agent-callable tools return them from getTools(). The framework prevents overlapping poll cycles: if poll() takes longer than pollInterval, the next cycle is skipped.

nodes.label: WebhookSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Concrete signal provider for push-based event delivery: routes incoming webhook payloads to subscribed agent threads by matching the payload against a configurable resource ID extractor.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Composes storage domains from different providers so different databases can serve different purposes (e.g. LibSQL for memory, PostgreSQL for workflows). Observability data can quickly overwhelm general-purpose databases, so ClickHouse is recommended for production observability while other data stays in the primary database.

nodes.label: LocalProcessManager
nodes.rationale: Processes run as child processes on the local machine using child_process.spawn; when native isolation is enabled they are also wrapped with the same isolation backend.

nodes.label: LocalSandbox
nodes.rationale: Executes commands on the local system; auto-starts on first command execution to avoid requiring explicit init, and defaults workingDirectory to .sandbox/ in process.cwd() for isolation from seatbelt profiles.

nodes.label: NativeSandboxConfig
nodes.rationale: Network access is blocked by default (allowNetwork: false) so sandboxed commands cannot reach the network unless explicitly opted in.

nodes.label: Bubblewrap isolation backend (Linux)
nodes.rationale: /tmp is a private in-sandbox tmpfs so writes never reach the host; the generated policy exposes only selected system paths.

nodes.label: Environment isolation
nodes.rationale: By default only PATH is included so commands can run without accidental exposure of API keys and secrets.

nodes.label: Git Bash shell on Windows
nodes.rationale: executeCommand quotes args for a POSIX shell, so on native Windows without isolation commands run through Git Bash; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=* are set so switches like /F and Windows paths reach native tools unchanged.

nodes.label: Seatbelt isolation backend (macOS)
nodes.rationale: Profiles are written to a separate .sandbox-profiles/ folder so sandboxed processes cannot read or modify their own security profiles; profile filenames are hashed from workspace path plus config to prevent collisions across concurrent sandboxes.

nodes.label: AgentBrowser
nodes.rationale: Built on Playwright and finds page elements through accessibility information, making it suited to general web automation and scraping.

nodes.label: BrowserViewer
nodes.rationale: A CLI provider that launches Chrome and passes its CDP URL to CLI tools, for workspace agents that control browsers through shell commands.

nodes.label: FirecrawlBrowser
nodes.rationale: Runs AgentBrowser tools in hosted Firecrawl Browser Sandbox sessions so browsers need not run on your own infrastructure.

nodes.label: StagehandBrowser
nodes.rationale: Uses AI to find page elements, which works better than fixed selectors for complex interactions described in natural language.

nodes.label: Browser Session Recording
nodes.rationale: Recordings use Motion-JPEG AVI so they don't require ffmpeg; only one recording can be active per process.

nodes.label: Browser Screencast
nodes.rationale: Requires WebSocket packages that are not included by default because they are incompatible with serverless environments like Cloudflare Workers; when absent, screencast is disabled but all other browser functionality works.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: A language model writes prose that must be parsed back into a decision; a classifier avoids the parsing entirely by sending state plus a fixed set of typed questions to a decision model and returning one typed answer per question.

nodes.label: createClassifierScorer()
nodes.rationale: Projects a classifier answer into a score for the eval pipeline.

nodes.label: decide()
nodes.rationale: Sends the state once with every question attached, so adding another question does not add a round trip.

nodes.label: MastraDecisionModel
nodes.rationale: Wraps a decision model when provider output needs normalization before the classifier validates it; the classifier wraps a raw AI SDK decision model automatically.

nodes.label: ModelSelectionProcessor
nodes.rationale: Classifies the incoming request and can downgrade the agent to a cheaper model; minProbability requires a confident answer before switching.

nodes.label: .classifier() workflow step
nodes.rationale: Classifies the workflow input before .branch() routes on the answer.

nodes.label: Decision model
nodes.rationale: A model built to answer typed questions; it is not the agent's language model and the constructor does not accept a 'provider/model' string.

nodes.label: Evals
nodes.rationale: Evals measure whether outputs are good over time, while a classifier makes one decision at runtime that the application acts on.

nodes.label: Mastra instance classifier registration
nodes.rationale: Registering classifiers on the Mastra instance shares them across the application and lets workflows reference them by ID.

nodes.label: Question types (choice, score, boolean)
nodes.rationale: Each question should ask for one judgment; a question weighing several factors produces an answer you can't route on, so factors are asked separately and combined in code where thresholds can be retuned without rewriting a prompt.

nodes.label: mapUserToResourceId
nodes.rationale: Use a canonical identifier from the verified provider as display names and other mutable profile fields aren't suitable ownership keys.

nodes.label: CopilotChat
nodes.rationale: Renders an inline, full-height chat; CopilotSidebar and CopilotPopup are drop-in alternatives sharing the same props and provider.

nodes.label: @copilotkit/runtime
nodes.rationale: Must be excluded from the deployment bundle: it contains dependencies that aren't compatible with bundling and cause 500 errors if included. Not an issue with mastra dev, which doesn't bundle.

nodes.label: createChannel
nodes.rationale: Takes an array of adapters, so a single long-running process can serve several messaging platforms at once.

nodes.label: registerCopilotKit
nodes.rationale: Exposes Mastra agents as an AG-UI endpoint in a CopilotKit-compatible format; by default exposes every agent registered on the Mastra instance and the frontend selects one with the agent prop.

nodes.label: Slack Adapter
nodes.rationale: Runs over Socket Mode, opening an outbound WebSocket to Slack so no public URL or tunnel is required during development.

nodes.label: useAgent
nodes.rationale: agent.state is reactive, so components re-render automatically as the agent's working memory streams to the client.

nodes.label: useComponent
nodes.rationale: Registers a React component so the agent can call it as a tool, rendered inline with typed props defined by a Zod schema.

nodes.label: useFrontendTool
nodes.rationale: The handler runs in the browser when the agent calls the tool, letting the agent act on the application.

nodes.label: useHumanInTheLoop
nodes.rationale: The agent's run stays suspended until the render function's respond callback is called, enabling approve/edit/reject before continuing.

nodes.label: useRenderTool
nodes.rationale: Render-only (does not execute the tool); called repeatedly as Mastra streams tool-call arguments so the UI paints progressively.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.rationale: The generated OpenUI system prompt is injected into the agent's instructions so the agent knows how to use the OpenUI component library.

nodes.label: A2UI (Agent-to-UI)
nodes.rationale: Declarative tier: the agent emits a structured spec and the frontend composes it from a registered catalog; suits the long tail of secondary interactions where breadth matters more than pixel-perfection.

nodes.label: AG-UI Protocol
nodes.rationale: The agent receives ordinary AG-UI input and emits ordinary AG-UI events, so the same Mastra agent runs unchanged across every channel.

nodes.label: CopilotKit Channels SDK
nodes.rationale: Keeps a deliberate credential split: you keep agent logic, model credentials, tools and the channel process, while CopilotKit Intelligence holds platform credentials, message delivery, registration, health and reconnects.

nodes.label: CopilotKit
nodes.rationale: Provides React components to integrate customizable AI copilots with bidirectional state synchronization and interactive UIs.

nodes.label: Generative UI Spectrum
nodes.rationale: A single axis from author-controlled to agent-invented; position on the axis is a trade-off between predictability and breadth.

nodes.label: MCP Apps
nodes.rationale: Open-ended tier: the UI is invented elsewhere (an MCP server) and sandboxed in the app; trades determinism for novelty and is the most experimental point on the spectrum.

nodes.label: Compaction
nodes.rationale: Compaction is a blunt fallback: it adds latency and a single summary must represent everything before it, so repeated summaries can flatten chronology or lose details. Prefer Observational Memory for long-running conversations.

nodes.label: Filesystems
nodes.rationale: Choose a filesystem when the source of truth is a set of files the agent may need to list, read, or update; choose standalone RAG when retrieval is the main requirement and content does not need to behave like files.

nodes.label: Workflow Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Serializable representation of complete execution state, the key mechanism enabling suspend and resume.

nodes.label: suspendSchema
nodes.rationale: Lets you attach custom metadata stored in the snapshot and available on resume.

nodes.label: initialState
nodes.rationale: Passed when starting a workflow run to set starting values; should match the structure defined in the workflow's stateSchema.

nodes.label: stateSchema
nodes.rationale: The workflow's stateSchema is the master schema containing all possible state values, while each step declares only the subset it needs.

nodes.label: suspend
nodes.rationale: State automatically persists across suspend and resume cycles, so all state updates made before suspension are preserved.

nodes.label: Nested Workflows
nodes.rationale: State propagates from parent to child, so changes made by the parent before calling a nested workflow are visible to steps inside it.

nodes.label: Step Input/Output vs State
nodes.rationale: Step input/output flows sequentially between steps, while state is a shared store readable and updatable by all steps and persisting across the whole run.

nodes.label: Workflow state
nodes.rationale: Lets steps share values without threading them through every step's inputSchema and outputSchema; useful for tracking progress, accumulating results, or sharing configuration across the entire workflow.

nodes.label: GithubSignals
nodes.rationale: Polls subscribed PRs and sends notification signals to the agent thread when relevant activity occurs; each subscription is stored in the thread's metadata, so the thread must already exist.

nodes.label: GithubSignals.startPollingForThread()
nodes.rationale: Must be called for each persisted thread subscription after a process restart to resume polling.

nodes.label: GithubSignals.subscribeThreadToPR()
nodes.rationale: Syncs the PR immediately, stores the subscription, and starts polling every five minutes; a thread has one current subscription, so subscribing to another PR replaces the existing one.

nodes.label: review subscription mode
nodes.rationale: Use when the thread only needs code revisions, authorized latest PR comments, and observable review-thread-state updates; CI and merge-conflict changes are saved without notifying.

nodes.label: working subscription mode
nodes.rationale: Follows all actionable PR activity detected by the provider; it is the default when mode is omitted and for stored subscriptions without a valid mode.

nodes.label: observe()
nodes.rationale: Reconnects to an existing run after a network disconnection; idleTimeoutMs and isAlive are opt-in to avoid waiting forever when the producing process dies.

nodes.label: RedisServerCache
nodes.rationale: Shared server cache required for evented agents on cross-process PubSub so events are numbered and offsets work.

nodes.label: resume()
nodes.rationale: Waits up to 5 seconds for another execution holding the run, then throws DURABLE_AGENT_EXECUTION_CONFLICT to avoid concurrent execution.

nodes.label: closeOnSuspend
nodes.rationale: Useful for callers such as AG-UI or A2A that need the stream to end at the suspension boundary.

nodes.label: in-process run registry
nodes.rationale: Closure-based options live on the in-process run registry; cross-process resumes lose them and degrade to serialized JSON-safe shadows.

nodes.label: Client Tool
nodes.rationale: Client-side tools allow custom functions to execute on the client side when the agent requests them.

nodes.label: StoredAgent
nodes.rationale: Stored agents are agent configurations stored in a database that can be created, updated, and deleted at runtime, referencing primitives by key resolved from the Mastra registry.

nodes.label: BlobStoreProvider
nodes.rationale: The editor registers no built-in blob store provider; when no provider ID is given it falls back to the configured storage backend's blobs domain, and external providers (e.g. S3) are supplied via MastraEditorConfig.blobStores.

nodes.label: BrowserProvider
nodes.rationale: No built-in browser providers exist; the editor calls createBrowser(config) at agent hydration time using the provider id from the stored StorageBrowserRef as the lookup key, and for a static browser config the resulting instance is cached alongside the agent.

nodes.label: AgentScorerConfig
nodes.rationale: Separates agent-level scorers (raw output) from trajectory scorers (pre-extracted Trajectory object).

nodes.label: EvalTurn
nodes.rationale: Per-turn gates/scorers evaluate only that turn's input and output so a later-turn regression can't be hidden by an earlier turn.

nodes.label: runEvals
nodes.rationale: Target should be resolved from the Mastra instance (mastra.getAgent/getWorkflow) rather than imported directly, otherwise registry lookups during execution fail, scores aren't persisted, and trace-based trajectory extraction is unavailable.

nodes.label: ScorerEntry
nodes.rationale: A number threshold implies a minimum; { min, max } supports range checks for scorers where a high score is bad (e.g. hallucination).

nodes.label: TrajectoryExpectation
nodes.rationale: Overrides the static defaults in scorer constructors.

nodes.label: WorkflowScorerConfig
nodes.rationale: Allows scorers at workflow, individual step, and trajectory levels.

nodes.label: createTool execute(inputData, context)
nodes.rationale: Tool inputs and execution context are now passed independently as separate parameters.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Renamed from RuntimeContext to identify the class as request-specific data.

nodes.label: Tool context namespaces
nodes.rationale: Namespaces organize agent-, workflow-, and MCP-specific properties under a clearer API surface.

nodes.label: Agent.generate()
nodes.rationale: Non-streaming response generation from an agent with enhanced capabilities; accepts messages plus optional generation options.

nodes.label: CallSettings (modelSettings)
nodes.rationale: maxOutputTokens is used rather than maxTokens per AI SDK v5 convention; a totalMs timeout is a hard deadline for the whole run and does not try fallback models, while stepMs and firstChunkMs timeouts advance to fallback models.

nodes.label: DelegationConfig
nodes.rationale: Controls and monitors subagent delegation, allowing modification, rejection and feedback to guide the supervisor.

nodes.label: IsTaskCompleteConfig
nodes.rationale: Uses Mastra's evaluation scorers to automatically check whether the agent's response satisfies completion criteria.

nodes.label: StructuredOutputOptions
nodes.rationale: Providing a structuring model enables multi-step responses combining tool calls, text and structured output; jsonPromptInjection 'auto' uses native structured output when supported and inline prompt injection otherwise.

nodes.label: suspendPayload
nodes.rationale: Present only when finishReason is 'suspended', carrying the pending tool call details needed to resume or approve the run.

nodes.label: ToolHooks
nodes.rationale: beforeToolCall can return { proceed: false, output } to skip the tool call.

nodes.label: TracingOptions
nodes.rationale: nestUnderParent keeps the trace's own name, input, output and tags when attaching a run as a child span, e.g. an LLM judge under the run it scores.

nodes.label: VersionOverrides
nodes.rationale: Merged on top of Mastra instance-level versions and propagated automatically through sub-agent calls via requestContext; requires the editor package.

nodes.label: Agent.generateLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: kept only for legacy model adapters; it uses the legacy AI SDK generation path, so it does not run error processors or maxProcessorRetries.

nodes.label: Agent.getDefaultGenerateOptionsLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: only works with V1 models; V2 models should use getDefaultOptions().

nodes.label: Agent.getDefaultOptions()
nodes.rationale: Defaults are resolved (functions invoked) so callers can inspect an agent's unknown defaults; they apply to all stream() and generate() calls unless overridden.

nodes.label: Agent.getDefaultStreamOptionsLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: only works with V1 models; V2 models should use getDefaultOptions().

nodes.label: Mastra Documentation (llms.txt index)
nodes.rationale: Mastra docs are the canonical, current reference and should be trusted over training data.

nodes.label: DatadogBridge.createSpan
nodes.rationale: Creates the dd-trace APM span eagerly at span construction so the returned Mastra-compatible IDs can be used throughout the span's lifetime and the stored dd-trace span can be used for scope activation.

nodes.label: DatadogBridge
nodes.rationale: Experimental bridge providing bidirectional integration: creates native dd-trace APM spans in real time so auto-instrumented operations nest under their parent Mastra span, and emits LLM Observability data through dd-trace's pipeline when spans end.

nodes.label: DatadogExporter
nodes.rationale: Simpler choice when only LLM Observability data is needed without dd-trace APM; must not be combined with DatadogBridge because both emit to LLM Observability and would double-write the same data.

nodes.label: dd-trace
nodes.rationale: Must be initialized before any other imports so its auto-instrumentation can patch HTTP, database, and framework libraries at load time.

nodes.label: DatadogBridge.executeInContext
nodes.rationale: Runs async work inside the dd-trace context of a Mastra span so auto-instrumented operations (HTTP, database) are parented to that span.

nodes.label: DatadogBridge.flush
nodes.rationale: Best-effort: dd-trace sends LLM Observability data from a background writer with no way to await the request, so flush waits flushGraceMs (default 2000 ms) after asking dd-trace to flush, then flushes the APM exporter. Raise it if short-lived process spans are missing; set to 0 to skip the wait when something else keeps the process alive.

nodes.label: Mastra SpanType to Datadog Kind Mapping
nodes.norm_label: mastra spantype to datadog kind mapping

nodes.label: CompatRule
nodes.rationale: Use applyToPrompt for provider-specific rewrites that shouldn't be saved to memory; use fix with errorPatterns only when repaired history must persist and the provider can't be stopped from rejecting up front.

nodes.label: ProviderHistoryCompat
nodes.rationale: Use it when an agent may switch between model providers or reuse message history across providers; it also handles providers that reject fields emitted by another provider. Preemptive rewrites are prompt-scoped so persisted history keeps original IDs and content.

nodes.label: RegexFilterProcessor
nodes.rationale: Uses regex pattern matching only — no LLM calls are made — and can be applied to input, output, or both phases.

nodes.label: RegexRedactionDetail
nodes.rationale: Values are left out by default because an audit trail that copies the data it protects widens the exposure it was added to narrow.

nodes.label: anthropic-tool-id-format rule
nodes.rationale: Anthropic enforces ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ on tool_use.id; sanitizing in the outbound prompt prevents the rejection while leaving persisted history untouched.

nodes.label: ensure-user-first-turn rule
nodes.rationale: Bedrock and Gemini reject conversations whose first non-system turn is the assistant's; runs last so it sees the prompt after other rules dropped emptied turns.

nodes.label: openai-orphan-item-id rule
nodes.rationale: Drops the Responses itemId so the message replays by value instead of as an unsatisfiable item_reference.

nodes.label: CostGuardProcessor (deprecated alias)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a deprecated alias for the same class, including the 'token-cost-control' processor id, so existing imports keep working.

nodes.label: TokenCostControl
nodes.rationale: Cost data is persisted asynchronously via buffered exporters, so maxCost is treated as an approximate threshold that fast-running agents may exceed; cost is attributed only via the entityType 'agent' metric filter, so model calls outside an agent run are not counted.

nodes.label: TokenLimiterProcessor
nodes.rationale: In best-fit and contiguous trim modes the prompt is measured after earlier prompt processors have transformed it, so only tokens that actually reach the model are counted; trimming is transient so stored messages are never modified.

nodes.label: ToolCallFilter
nodes.rationale: Register the limiter after prompt-shrinking processors such as ToolCallFilter to count the prompt the model actually receives.

nodes.label: TripWire
nodes.rationale: Thrown when no valid LLM request can be formed: no non-system messages, system messages alone exceed the limit, or no message fits the remaining budget.

nodes.label: ToolCallFilter
nodes.rationale: Filtering happens in processLLMRequest after the message list is converted to a model prompt, and changes are transient: stored messages, memory and UI history keep their original tool calls and results.

nodes.label: Observability storage (getMetricAggregate / getMetricBreakdown)
nodes.rationale: All scopes require observability storage with getMetricAggregate support; without it the Mastra instance throws at registration time, and query failures are handled fail-open.

nodes.label: mastra dev
nodes.rationale: Changes in src/mastra/ automatically restart the development server, so no manual restart is needed while building.

nodes.label: File-based Agents
nodes.rationale: The file system becomes a direct representation of the project structure so humans and coding agents can understand how the project fits together without tracing code wiring; discovery only runs through mastra dev or mastra build.

nodes.label: mastra CLI
nodes.rationale: Gives a coding agent a feedback loop for testing updates and inspecting results across agents, workflows, tools, memory, evals, traces, and logs.

nodes.label: Mastra Skills
nodes.rationale: AI models may not have up-to-date knowledge of Mastra's APIs, so the skill gives coding agents implementation guidance and instructions for fetching the latest docs.

nodes.label: backgroundTasks option
nodes.rationale: Subagent invocations are dispatched as tool calls, so long-running delegations can run as background tasks without blocking the parent's response.

nodes.label: Agent.streamUntilIdle()
nodes.rationale: Used instead of stream() for background subagents so the stream stays open until subagents complete and the parent can respond to their results.

nodes.label: Subagent cancellation via abortSignal
nodes.rationale: The parent's abortSignal is forwarded to delegated subagents so in-flight runs cancel at their next step instead of running to completion.

nodes.label: Agent instructions and subagent descriptions
nodes.rationale: The parent uses subagent descriptions to make delegation decisions, so instructions must list available resources, coordination behavior, and success criteria.

nodes.label: Subagents
nodes.rationale: Specialized agents a parent agent delegates tasks to; the parent uses its instructions and each subagent's description to decide when and how to delegate, then synthesizes results.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Used in examples because it stores data locally in a memory.db file.

nodes.label: recall tool
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent recover source details compressed by the summary, including exact wording, tool output, and chronology.

nodes.label: shareTokenBudget
nodes.rationale: Pools the message-history and observation budgets so history can expand into unused observation space while the observation log is small.

nodes.label: Reflections
nodes.rationale: Reflections don't accumulate as a separate ever-growing layer: each reflection rewrites the entire observation log, condensing older information more aggressively while keeping recent detail, so memory stays bounded around the reflection threshold.

nodes.label: Retrieval mode
nodes.rationale: Normal OM compresses messages into observations and loses the original wording; retrieval mode keeps each observation group linked to the raw messages that produced it so the agent can recall source details.

nodes.label: Supported Storage Adapters
nodes.rationale: OM requires a storage provider; only @mastra/pg, @mastra/libsql, @mastra/mysql, @mastra/mongodb, @mastra/convex and @mastra/oracledb are currently supported.

nodes.label: Three-tier memory system
nodes.rationale: Recent messages give exact history for the current task, observations log what the Observer has seen, and reflections condense observations when memory becomes too long.

nodes.label: Workflow.agent() shorthand
nodes.rationale: Records a declarative entry in the workflow graph rather than an opaque step, so workflows built this way can be persisted as dynamic workflows.

nodes.label: createStep()
nodes.rationale: Composes agents or tools directly as workflow steps when the invocation doesn't need to be modified.

nodes.label: structuredOutput option
nodes.rationale: Sets the step's outputSchema to the provided schema, enabling type-safe chaining to subsequent steps.

nodes.label: Workflow.tool() shorthand
nodes.rationale: Like .agent(), records a declarative entry so the workflow can be persisted as a dynamic workflow.

nodes.label: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Validates the definition before it changes storage or the live workflow registry.

nodes.label: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflows()
nodes.rationale: Validates a bundle of interdependent definitions as a unit and determines registration order from dependencies; if validation fails none are registered.

nodes.label: Dynamic Workflows
nodes.rationale: Definitions are JSON data with no JavaScript closures, so anything that produces JSON (HTTP client, LLM, visual editor, custom tooling) can author a workflow without changing application code or redeploying.

nodes.label: workflowDefinitions storage domain
nodes.rationale: Stored definitions use this domain so Mastra can load active definitions on startup and register them in dependency order, surviving process restarts.

nodes.label: MastraAuthWorkos
nodes.rationale: Set fetchMemberships: true to load WorkOS organization memberships during authentication so FGA checks can resolve the correct organization membership ID; when false, Mastra skips the extra listOrganizationMemberships() call on each authenticated request.

nodes.label: trustJwtClaims
nodes.rationale: Useful when the JWT template already includes the exact FGA context Mastra needs (organizationMembershipId, tenant IDs, service-principal identifiers); Mastra can fall back to those verified claims if a bearer token isn't meant to round-trip through workos.userManagement.getUser().

nodes.label: AgentController Session
nodes.rationale: Durable records over HTTP go through the AgentController Session notification route, which forwards to sendNotificationSignal().

nodes.label: client.getAgent().sendSignal()
nodes.rationale: Bypasses inbox storage, so it should only be used when the event needs no record, retries, or later reading.

nodes.label: createNotificationInboxTool()
nodes.rationale: Gives the agent the inbox tool so it can inspect records without exposing storage APIs.

nodes.label: Notification dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Reads due records, groups summaries by agentId, resourceId, and threadId, and emits signals through the thread runtime; scheduled dispatch runs through the workflow scheduler and is enabled by default.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Notification records require a storage adapter with the notifications domain (libSQL, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB); without it sendNotificationSignal() throws instead of silently dropping the record.

nodes.label: MAX_NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS
nodes.rationale: After five failed attempts the record moves to failed and stops being due; a hold leaves it pending without counting an attempt so another dispatcher can pick it up.

nodes.label: agent.sendNotificationSignal()
nodes.rationale: Canonical way to create durable notification records; returns the record and the policy decision.

nodes.label: sendSignal({ type: 'notification' })
nodes.rationale: Sends event context without creating an inbox record or providing its retries.

nodes.label: coalesceKey
nodes.rationale: Groups related events into one pending record (coalescing); merging only considers records on the same thread, source, kind, agent, and resource that are still pending.

nodes.label: dedupeKey
nodes.rationale: Identifies one event that may arrive more than once so it can merge into an existing pending record.

nodes.label: Notification delivery policy
nodes.rationale: Decides whether to send the event immediately, summarize it with other events, or leave it for later; source rules run before priority rules so a noisy source can be summarized while everything else delivers.

nodes.label: Notification record
nodes.rationale: Stored in a durable inbox separate from the conversation's messages, so the event remains available even if the agent is busy when it arrives.

nodes.label: Notification summary
nodes.rationale: Keeps a busy thread from receiving a burst of individual notifications; a summarized record stays pending because a summary tells the model that records exist without marking them delivered.

nodes.label: Notification inbox
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent list, read, search, markSeen, dismiss, and archive records; reading can inject the full signal and mark the record seen, preventing duplicate delivery later.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.rationale: Deliver external events through a durable inbox.

nodes.label: RedisStore.close()
nodes.rationale: Should be called on application shutdown to close the Redis connection.

nodes.label: RedisStore.init()
nodes.rationale: Called automatically when storage is passed to Mastra; must be called explicitly when storage is used directly.

nodes.label: RedisStore
nodes.rationale: High-performance storage over direct node-redis connections; supports standalone Redis and Sentinel via a custom client, but not Redis Cluster because several operations touch keys that hash to different slots and Cluster rejects them with CROSSSLOT.

nodes.label: Redis Cluster
nodes.rationale: Not supported: RedisStore accepts only a standalone client, and several operations read or write keys that hash to different slots, which Cluster rejects with a CROSSSLOT error.

nodes.label: Redis Sentinel
nodes.rationale: High-availability deployments are supported by connecting a custom client before passing it to RedisStore.

nodes.label: SpannerStore.dangerouslyClearAll()
nodes.rationale: Spanner has no TRUNCATE, so clearing issues DELETE WHERE TRUE.

nodes.label: SpannerStore.init()
nodes.rationale: Spanner does not allow concurrent schema changes, so init() runs each domain's setup sequentially.

nodes.label: listSchedules()
nodes.rationale: Backed by the STORED generated column mastra_schedules.target_workflow_id so the workflowId filter can use a regular secondary index instead of a JSON_VALUE scan.

nodes.label: listTraces()
nodes.rationale: Spanner lacks JSON containment, so metadata and scope filters compile to per-key JSON_VALUE equality checks and tags filters to EXISTS over JSON_QUERY_ARRAY; deeply nested structural matches expressible with Postgres' @> operator are not supported.

nodes.label: listWorkflowRuns()
nodes.rationale: Backed by the STORED generated column mastra_workflow_snapshot.snapshotStatus so the status filter can use a regular secondary index instead of a JSON_VALUE scan; falls back to JSON_VALUE when the column is absent.

nodes.label: SpannerStore
nodes.rationale: Horizontally high-capacity, strongly consistent backend targeting the GoogleSQL dialect; the adapter creates required tables on first use, so credentials need schema-change permission unless init() runs once with elevated credentials.

nodes.label: DuckDBStore
nodes.rationale: CommonJS does not support top-level await, so the DuckDBStore import and domains option must be removed; observability data then goes to default LibSQL storage.

nodes.label: MastraModule
nodes.rationale: Registers a catch-all controller (@All('*')); if imported before app modules it can intercept unrelated routes and return 404s, so it should be imported last or mounted under a dedicated prefix.

nodes.label: MastraService
nodes.rationale: Injectable wrapper with convenience methods for common operations.

nodes.label: MASTRA injection token
nodes.rationale: Used when the Mastra instance is needed directly, e.g. to access storage, memory, or other core APIs.

nodes.label: SvelteKit Chat Route (src/routes/api/chat/+server.ts)
nodes.rationale: POST streams the agent response in AI SDK format; GET fetches message history from memory so the UI can be hydrated on reload.

nodes.label: SvelteKit Page Load (src/routes/+page.ts)
nodes.rationale: load() runs alongside +page.svelte so the GET handler is called to hydrate initial messages.

nodes.label: MastraError
nodes.rationale: Standard serialization omits result, so result must be read explicitly to access scorer artifacts or raw failed output.

nodes.label: MastraScorer
nodes.rationale: Base class for all scorers; most users should use createScorer to create instances rather than instantiating MastraScorer directly.

nodes.label: ScorerJudgeExecution
nodes.rationale: status describes the outcome of the logical prompt-step execution, not the quality of the evaluated response.

nodes.label: ScorerJudgeResults
nodes.rationale: Describes one scorer run's judge model calls; aggregate usage, latency and cost should be queried through Mastra metrics instead.

nodes.label: ScorerRunError
nodes.rationale: A failed scorer stage rejects the .run() promise; ScorerRunError exposes completed stages and partial results so callers can inspect artifacts from a failed run.

nodes.label: ScorerRunResultSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Holds completed stage outputs and judge execution evidence; omitted when neither is available.

nodes.label: listMetrics()
nodes.rationale: The client doesn't expose a raw listMetrics() method; use the observability store or the GET /api/observability/metrics route to list raw metric records.

nodes.label: MetricDistinctColumn
nodes.rationale: Required when aggregation is count_distinct.

nodes.label: Observability store
nodes.rationale: getStore('observability') returns undefined when the storage configuration doesn't provide the observability domain, so in-process queries must guard against a missing store.

nodes.label: Observability.clear
nodes.rationale: Clears all instances without shutting them down.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.rationale: Registry class managing named observability instances, a default instance, and runtime config selection.

nodes.label: Vector Store Prompts
nodes.rationale: Prompts are required in the agent's instructions to specify valid filter operators and syntax for each vector store implementation.

nodes.label: isWorkflowTaskContext()
nodes.rationale: Used by a custom store's cancel and expiry to detect a workflow task's context and cancel the underlying run via createRun({ runId }) then run.cancel().

nodes.label: Task limits
nodes.rationale: Without Mastra background tasks tasks live in memory, so a multi-instance deployment must route every tasks/* request to the creating instance via the Mcp-Name header.

nodes.label: Recovery after a crash
nodes.rationale: recover: true re-runs execute from the start once, so it should only be enabled for tools that are safe to repeat; the default recover: false fails the task instead of running execute twice.

nodes.label: Tasks across instances
nodes.rationale: Tasks are kept in Mastra storage so any instance sharing that storage can answer tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel and run the task; a local file store is only shared by instances on the same host, so a reachable database is recommended.

nodes.label: Task tracing
nodes.rationale: The root span is written as soon as the task starts because a trace without its root drops out of trace lists; spans record a hash of the task id (mcpTaskKey) rather than the id itself.

nodes.label: Workflow tasks (run_<key>)
nodes.rationale: A run starts once under the tools/call that creates the task with a run id of its own; the task id is never the run id, so a task can follow a run across instances and resumes.

nodes.label: bookDelivery
nodes.rationale: A tool can suspend more than once by changing the phase in its payload; each round is a separate request, so put the state the next round needs in the payload and branch on it.

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: resumeSchema becomes the form the caller fills in, so it must describe a flat object of primitives (strings, numbers, booleans, enums).

nodes.label: toolActions.add()
nodes.rationale: Named toolActions because tools() is the method returning the registered tool registry.

nodes.label: MCP Prompts
nodes.rationale: Prompts are reusable templates or workflows that MCP servers expose to clients; they can accept arguments and include resource context, standardizing LLM interactions.

nodes.label: custom chunk
nodes.rationale: Carries provider-specific content blocks that do not map to any standardized chunk type.

nodes.label: data-user-message-cancelled chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitted only after the input has been removed, confirming removal rather than a cancellation request; remains transient and is not saved to history.

nodes.label: data-user-message-pending chunk
nodes.rationale: Transient projection so subscribers can show accepted input immediately, then reconcile with the delivered data-user-message chunk by data.id; not saved to conversation history.

nodes.label: object chunk
nodes.rationale: Used for streaming structured object generation; typically skipped in some execution contexts.

nodes.label: raw chunk
nodes.rationale: Unrecognized provider content is emitted as raw chunks rather than discarded; raw chunks only appear when includeRawChunks is enabled.

nodes.label: reasoning-signature chunk
nodes.rationale: Carries metadata about the model's internal reasoning process (effort level, approach) rather than the reasoning content itself.

nodes.label: response-metadata chunk
nodes.rationale: Used internally for state tracking and does not affect message assembly.

nodes.label: step-output chunk
nodes.rationale: Similar to tool-output but specifically for individual workflow steps, used primarily for usage tracking.

nodes.label: tool-output chunk
nodes.rationale: Often wraps other chunk types (like finish chunks) to provide nested execution context for usage tracking.

nodes.label: tripwire chunk
nodes.rationale: Acts as a safety mechanism: the stream is forcibly terminated when a processor blocks content, preventing harmful or inappropriate content from being streamed.

nodes.label: Voice events
nodes.rationale: Events are useful for building interactive UIs that respond to conversation state; not all events are supported by all providers and non-real-time providers emit few of them.

nodes.label: processLLMRequest()
nodes.rationale: Changes returned from this hook are transient and do not persist back to MessageList, memory, UI history, or future provider calls, making it suitable for provider compatibility rewrites.

nodes.label: ResponseCache
nodes.rationale: Caching is implemented as an input processor rather than an agent-level option to keep the API surface small while Mastra collects feedback.

nodes.label: Schedule delivery guarantees
nodes.rationale: Publication is best-effort; skipped occurrences aren't replayed, while later recurring fires can continue.

nodes.label: Threadless schedule
nodes.rationale: Simplest mode; suits status checks, reports, and other work that doesn't need conversation context.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: Let you send input to an agent's thread at any time, including while the agent is working; by default Mastra delivers it to the active run or starts a run when the thread is idle, so you don't need to check whether the agent is running before sending.

nodes.label: Running across processes
nodes.rationale: When your app runs on several processes, a shared backend is needed so signals reach the process running the thread.

nodes.label: Signal providers
nodes.rationale: Connect polling sources or webhooks to agents.

nodes.label: State signals
nodes.rationale: Keep named, thread-scoped context across turns.

nodes.label: Thread events reference
nodes.rationale: Observe queued messages with subscribeThreadEvents().

nodes.label: registerTaskContext()
nodes.rationale: The manager keeps tool executors in process memory, so after a restart the caller of resume() must re-register the executor closure first.

nodes.label: POST /api/background-tasks/:backgroundTaskId/resume
nodes.rationale: Returns 409 Conflict when the task has resumed or suspended again since the supplied suspendedAt, preventing stale answers.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Lets a task pause for human approvals, webhooks, or data that arrives later; releases the concurrency slot so other tasks can run.

nodes.label: onNoSlot: 'queue'
nodes.rationale: The queue lives in the memory of the process that called resume(); to survive restarts the resume data must be persisted and resume() called again.

nodes.label: metadata.suspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Lets a chat that reloads the thread still show the open request; the entry is removed when the task resumes or is cancelled.

nodes.label: createCodingAgent()
nodes.rationale: Build a standard agent with a workspace, task tracking, and retries already configured.

nodes.label: Harness
nodes.rationale: A harness lets an agent pursue long-running, complex goals while keeping its work durable, visible, and steerable; capabilities can be adopted individually or combined as needed.

nodes.label: AgentController
nodes.rationale: Host isolated sessions around a shared agent runtime, each with its own run controls.

nodes.label: Background Tasks
nodes.rationale: Finish work asynchronously and return its result to the agent.

nodes.label: Durable Agents
nodes.rationale: Persist run state and let clients reconnect to its stream.

nodes.label: Goals
nodes.rationale: Evaluate a thread-scoped objective until it's complete or reaches its run budget.

nodes.label: Schedules
nodes.rationale: Start isolated runs or send prompts into an existing thread on a cron schedule.

nodes.label: Signal Providers
nodes.rationale: Track subscriptions and forward matching external events to agent threads.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: Deliver input now or hold it for the next turn.

nodes.label: Mastra Code /schedules
nodes.rationale: These schedules live only in the Mastra Code process that created them; nothing is written to storage.

nodes.label: Threaded schedule
nodes.rationale: The prompt joins the agent's conversation by sending a signal into the specified thread.

nodes.label: asUserTurn()
nodes.rationale: Wraps each user message in a <turn> tag with speaker id, name, and role because the message body is the one place that survives into history and back into context.

nodes.label: Multi-user threads
nodes.rationale: A single thread shared by multiple users, each with their own name and functional role, carrying speaker identity in the message body so the agent can tell users apart while reading from one shared thread.

nodes.label: Message history
nodes.rationale: Sufficient alone for short conversations or when a verbatim record of who said what is needed; user tags in history carry attribution.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Preferred over working memory for multi-user threads when storage supports it: it extracts facts automatically, scales to any number of participants, and needs no template upkeep.

nodes.label: Request Context
nodes.rationale: Used to read the verified user from the auth layer and build the <turn> tag on the server, so a client cannot choose its own author_id and impersonate another user.

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.rationale: Used when OM isn't an option or when a structured, deterministic participants list is needed; default template assumes one user per thread so a custom participants template is required.

nodes.label: Scheduled Workflows
nodes.rationale: The scheduler dispatches due runs by publishing to the workflow topic.

nodes.label: Inngest Workflows
nodes.rationale: Serverless-native and holds cron state, so it is the recommended path for cron fires on functions-as-a-service platforms.

nodes.label: mastra.schedules service
nodes.rationale: Used to create schedules imperatively at runtime instead of declaratively in code.

nodes.label: Built-in Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Uses a setInterval tick loop polling the schedules table, so it assumes a long-lived host process.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Fastest path for local development because it doesn't require running a separate database server.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Routes domains to different backends when one database isn't the right fit for every domain.

nodes.label: Storage domains
nodes.rationale: A domain owns one type of runtime data and a storage adapter implements one or more domains, allowing per-domain backend routing.

nodes.label: Instance-level storage
nodes.rationale: Shared by agents, workflows, observability, evals, schedules, and other runtime features registered on the same Mastra instance.

nodes.label: schedules domain
nodes.rationale: Stores schedule definitions and fire history; requires an adapter that implements the schedules domain.

nodes.label: workflows domain
nodes.rationale: Stores durable snapshots that must be available when a run resumes, so a reliable persistent database is recommended.

nodes.label: Workflows Table (Snapshots)
nodes.rationale: When suspend() is called on a workflow its state is saved; when resume() is called that state is rehydrated.

nodes.label: auth_header URL parameter
nodes.rationale: Lets an external host hand over a token to open an authenticated Studio session; the token is kept in memory only and never written to local storage.

nodes.label: GET /api/auth/capabilities
nodes.rationale: Studio detects available login methods and current user info/permissions from this endpoint.

nodes.label: roleMapping
nodes.rationale: Maps roles already defined by an external identity provider to Mastra permissions.

nodes.label: server.auth
nodes.rationale: Setting it both displays a Studio login screen and requires authentication for all built-in and custom API routes.

nodes.label: Role-based access control
nodes.rationale: Separate from authentication: server.auth handles who the user is, while server.rbac handles what they can do.

nodes.label: Studio auth
nodes.rationale: One configuration secures both the Studio UI and API routes; without authentication Studio and all API routes are publicly accessible.

nodes.label: Mastra Enterprise Edition license
nodes.rationale: Studio sign-in with a third-party provider, RBAC, and FGA require an EE license in production; Simple Auth, JWT, and API route auth do not.

nodes.label: ChannelProvider
nodes.rationale: A provider owns the full integration lifecycle: app provisioning with OAuth, webhook routing with event handling, adapter creation and agent wiring, and credential management.

nodes.label: channels() helper
nodes.rationale: Returns a resolver backed by the Mastra platform so connections added after boot become usable without a redeploy.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Use it when the application needs a typed choice, numeric score, or boolean probability without parsing generated text; the classifier only returns evaluation results and the application decides how to use them.

nodes.label: EvaluationModelResult
nodes.rationale: Deprecated alias for DecisionModelResult, to be removed in a future release.

nodes.label: MastraDecisionModel
nodes.rationale: Pass a custom wrapper when provider output needs normalization before validation; transformResult() runs after the provider call and before Classifier validates the response.

nodes.label: MastraEvaluationModel
nodes.rationale: Deprecated alias for MastraDecisionModel, to be removed in a future release.

nodes.label: RefusalAnswer
nodes.rationale: A decision model can refuse a question, for example when a safety policy prevents it from answering; the refusal has no choice, score, or probability so callers must check type before reading numeric fields.

nodes.label: baseUrl
nodes.rationale: The platform cannot reach http://localhost:4111, so local development requires a tunnel (cloudflared or ngrok) pointed at by baseUrl so events reach the local dev process.

nodes.label: SensitiveDataFilter
nodes.rationale: Redacts sensitive data like passwords, tokens and keys from span output.

nodes.label: Studio Traces view
nodes.rationale: Tracing filters out low-level framework details so traces stay focused and readable.

nodes.label: createRun()
nodes.rationale: Required to create a run instance when resuming with only a runId.

nodes.label: resume()
nodes.rationale: Can be called from anywhere (HTTP endpoint, event handler, timer) to restart a suspended workflow from the step where it paused.

nodes.label: sleep()
nodes.rationale: Pauses at the workflow level and sets status to waiting, unlike suspend() which pauses within a step.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Pauses execution within a specific step and sets status to suspended, saving state as a snapshot.

nodes.label: suspendData
nodes.rationale: Automatically populated on resume with the exact data passed to suspend(), maintaining context about why the workflow was suspended.

nodes.label: Firestore
nodes.rationale: Default authorization uses a Firestore user_access collection keyed by user UID; presence of a document determines whether a user is authorized.

nodes.label: createLinqAdapter()
nodes.rationale: Takes apiKey and signingSecret directly; the Linq adapter can fetch thread history, so the default threadContext behavior works.

nodes.label: createRedisState()
nodes.rationale: A shared state adapter makes dedup keys visible across instances, so at-least-once retries aren't re-handled after a restart or on serverless where the retry lands on a different instance.

nodes.label: iMessage Agent
nodes.rationale: Uses toolDisplay: 'text' because iMessage has no interactive cards for Approve and Deny actions, and threadContext: { maxMessages: 0 } with Photon to skip the platform history lookup the adapter can't perform.

nodes.label: Linq iMessage adapter
nodes.rationale: Hosted iMessage, RCS, and SMS API; webhook-driven with tapback reactions and media mapped in both directions.

nodes.label: Photon iMessage adapter
nodes.rationale: Hosted or self-hosted iMessage service supporting webhooks and a gateway listener that streams messages over an open connection.

nodes.label: Duplicate deliveries
nodes.rationale: Photon and Linq deliver at least once, so Chat SDK drops repeats using the channel state adapter; Mastra's default keeps dedup keys in memory, which only covers a single long-running server.

nodes.label: Gateway listener
nodes.rationale: Mastra starts the listener during initialization and reconnects it if it drops, so no cron job or extra route is needed on a long-running server; serverless platforms should prefer webhooks because a gateway needs a process that stays alive.

nodes.label: Read receipts
nodes.rationale: Mastra skips inbound messages with neither text nor attachments so the agent doesn't answer its own reply in a loop.

nodes.label: iMessage Webhook Route
nodes.rationale: Mastra derives the webhook path and the platform value on requestContext from the adapter key, so the key must be imessage.

nodes.label: ring_clip tool
nodes.rationale: visibleToModel defaults to false because most models accept images but few accept video; video input also counts toward the context window for every second of footage.

nodes.label: ring_snapshot tool
nodes.rationale: Fetches a still image for an event and passes it to the model; if Ring has no image right after the event it uses the most recent image before it. visibleToModel defaults to true because most models accept images.
