nodes.label: RingSignals
nodes.rationale: Each RingSignals instance adds its own /ring routes, so multiple instances need distinct routePrefix values and their own Ring developer apps; otherwise only the first instance's routes are registered.

nodes.label: Ring account linking
nodes.rationale: Linking is configured in two places in order: the Ring Developer Console and ring.com; tokens are saved in the channels store and refreshed before they expire.

nodes.label: Ring media links
nodes.rationale: Ring doesn't give out shareable media links and downloads need account tokens, so with baseUrl set the tools return a signed link to the user's own server, which fetches the media and passes it on without storing it.

nodes.label: Ring thread routing
nodes.rationale: By default each Ring device gets its own thread with threadId equal to the device ID and resourceId equal to the agent ID; target can be a function to route per event or return undefined to drop the event.

nodes.label: Ring Partner API
nodes.rationale: Doesn't expose lights, sirens, locks, or two-way talk, and devices with end-to-end encryption aren't available.

nodes.label: Nuxt Chat Route (server/api/chat.ts)
nodes.rationale: POST streams the agent response in AI SDK format; GET fetches message history from memory so the UI can be hydrated on reload.

nodes.label: recoverActiveRuns()
nodes.rationale: The concurrency limit bounds waiting, not live executions; timed-out attempts continue in the background and their eventual outcome does not change the returned results.

nodes.label: Mastra.getGatewayById()
nodes.rationale: Useful when you need to find a gateway by its intrinsic id rather than its registration key, e.g. for gateway versioning ('gateway-v1', 'gateway-v2'), when registration keys are unknown, or to identify gateways across different Mastra instances.

nodes.label: createSummarizationScorer
nodes.rationale: Final score is the lower of the alignment and coverage axes: a summary can't pass by being faithful but empty, or by being thorough but wrong.

nodes.label: Coverage axis
nodes.rationale: The coverage step runs as a separate model call that never receives the source text; a judge that could see the source would answer questions from it rather than from the summary, hiding the omissions this axis exists to measure.

nodes.label: ConsoleExporter
nodes.rationale: Outputs trace events to the console for debugging and development.

nodes.label: DatadogBridge
nodes.rationale: Use instead of the exporter when dd-trace APM auto-instrumentation must be correctly parented under Mastra spans.

nodes.label: DatadogExporter
nodes.rationale: Sends tracing data to Datadog's LLM Observability product for monitoring and analytics; data is sent after execution completes so it does not participate in dd-trace's live scope.

nodes.label: DatadogExporter.flush
nodes.rationale: Flush is best-effort because dd-trace sends LLM Observability data from a background writer with no way to await the request, so it waits flushGraceMs (default 2000 ms); set to 0 to skip the wait when something else keeps the process alive.

nodes.label: BaseObservabilityInstance
nodes.rationale: Base class for custom ObservabilityInstance implementations.

nodes.label: BaseObservabilityInstance.startSpan
nodes.rationale: Creates the root span of a trace if no parent is provided.

nodes.label: @mastra/core/evals
nodes.rationale: Legacy evals code was removed from @mastra/core; the new evals/scorers API lives here.

nodes.label: createScorer()
nodes.rationale: Scorers now require an id field instead of name; name becomes optional, aligning scorers with other Mastra entities.

nodes.label: getScorerById()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getScorerByName() to align with the broader API pattern of using id for entity identification.

nodes.label: listScoresByScorerId()
nodes.rationale: Score storage APIs renamed to the listScoresBy* pattern to align with broader storage API naming conventions.

nodes.label: listScorers()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getScorers() to align with the API convention where plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: @mastra/evals/scorers/prebuilt
nodes.rationale: Consolidates the separate scorers/llm and scorers/code paths into a single import path for clearer organization.

nodes.label: runEvals()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from runExperiment() to identify that it runs evaluations.

nodes.label: page/perPage pagination
nodes.rationale: Pagination aligns list operations across the API and prevents accidental loading of large datasets; perPage: false preserves the ability to fetch all records.

nodes.label: CodeModeTransport
nodes.rationale: The default transport uses stdio JSON-RPC over the workspace sandbox process API; transports declaring requiresSandbox: false (IsolatedVmCodeModeTransport, QuickJsCodeModeTransport) run without a sandbox.

nodes.label: createCodeMode()
nodes.rationale: Returns both the tool and the generated instructions so the tool and its matching instructions stay together; generated code runs in a workspace sandbox while each external_* call runs the real tool on the host with validation, request context and tracing.

nodes.label: createCodeModeInstructions()
nodes.rationale: Tool ids are sanitized into valid TypeScript function names, and conflicting sanitized names throw an error.

nodes.label: createCodeModeTool()
nodes.rationale: Use when you only need the tool and want to manage instructions separately; most agents should use createCodeMode() so the tool and matching instructions stay together.

nodes.label: authenticate()
nodes.rationale: Concurrent calls for the same server join the pending flow, different servers authenticate independently, and valid stored tokens reconnect without opening a browser.

nodes.label: createOAuthCallbackServer
nodes.rationale: Creates a one-shot loopback server that validates the OAuth `state` parameter before resolving with the code; because it uses plain HTTP it is only suitable for local loopback redirects, so HTTPS web apps must host their own callback endpoint.

nodes.label: createSimpleTokenProvider
nodes.rationale: Provided for testing or when a valid access token already exists.

nodes.label: DatabaseOAuthStorage
nodes.rationale: Example implementation for persistent token storage across sessions.

nodes.label: getCallbackUrlCandidates
nodes.rationale: Lists every URL the callback helper may bind (sequential fallback ports) so all of them can be listed as redirect_uris in pre-registration or metadata documents.

nodes.label: MastraMCPServerDefinition
nodes.rationale: Transport type is detected from the provided parameters: command selects Stdio, url selects Streamable HTTP.

nodes.label: MCPOAuthClientProvider
nodes.rationale: The provider never registers a client at runtime: give it either clientInformation for a client pre-registered with the authorization server, or a Client ID Metadata Document URL as clientMetadataUrl.

nodes.label: OAuthStorage
nodes.rationale: Backend only needs a key-value contract; the provider stores the latest token set, one entry per authorization-server issuer, discovery state and the PKCE verifier under string keys.

nodes.label: MCP tasks
nodes.rationale: A call that returned a task is never retried, because a retry would start a second task.

nodes.label: allowedHosts
nodes.rationale: Matching is port-agnostic: localhost:3000 in the list allows any port on localhost. Write IPv6 addresses with brackets ([::1]).

nodes.label: allowedOrigins
nodes.rationale: Only the hostname is compared, so https://app.example.com:8443 allows every scheme and port on app.example.com. Requests without an Origin header pass because non-browser MCP clients don't send one.

nodes.label: createIntrospectionValidator
nodes.rationale: Implements RFC 7662 token introspection for production token validation.

nodes.label: enableDnsRebindingProtection
nodes.rationale: A check only runs when its list is non-empty; a rejected request receives a 403 JSON-RPC error.

nodes.label: startHTTP()
nodes.rationale: Every request is self-contained: there is no session to create or resume, so startHTTP works in serverless environments (Supabase Edge Functions, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, AWS Lambda, Deno Deploy).

nodes.label: authorize
nodes.rationale: Runs on every events/poll, events/stream open and webhook subscribe/refresh; used to restrict events because FGA does not apply to them.

nodes.label: match filter
nodes.rationale: match filters on the arguments the client chooses, so it does not control who can subscribe; authorize is needed to restrict callers.

nodes.label: poll source
nodes.rationale: A type with a poll source cannot also be pushed, so delivery cannot add 'push' to it.

nodes.label: eventsOptions.webhook
nodes.rationale: Without it the server does not advertise webhook delivery or answer events/subscribe.

nodes.label: Migration: AI SDK v4 to v5
nodes.norm_label: migration: ai sdk v4 to v5

nodes.label: createBackgroundWorkSignalProcessor()
nodes.rationale: The background runtime stays responsible for execution, persistence, retries, reconciliation and continuation; the processor only retains caller-scoped notification access.

nodes.label: errorProcessors
nodes.rationale: Error processors stop at the first one that returns { retry: true }, so relative order decides which repair runs. Defaults place repairs ahead of the retrying processor so a broad matcher cannot claim a request the repairs could have fixed and resend it unchanged.

nodes.label: onViolation callback
nodes.rationale: Fires on both abort() (block strategy) and warnings (warn strategy) so alerting/logging side effects do not affect the processor's main logic; errors thrown inside it are caught to protect the pipeline.

nodes.label: PrefillErrorHandler
nodes.rationale: Auto-injected and requires no configuration; handles the Anthropic assistant-message-prefill error automatically.

nodes.label: ProviderHistoryCompat
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the outbound request only, so persisted history keeps original tool-call IDs while call/result pairing survives.

nodes.label: StreamErrorRetryProcessor
nodes.rationale: The default instance retries only transient failures: connection resets, retryable OpenAI stream errors, and errors the provider marks as retryable.

nodes.label: ToolCallFilter
nodes.rationale: The filter only affects the LLM input; filtered messages are still saved to memory.

nodes.label: ToolSearchProcessor
nodes.rationale: Gives the agent search_tools and load_tool meta-tools instead of providing all tools upfront, reducing context token usage.

nodes.label: Background work notifications
nodes.rationale: Notifications are process-local and best-effort; if the originating run ended or the signal cannot be delivered, the authoritative result is preserved without recreating the run or retrying the notification.

nodes.label: DOWNLOAD_ASSETS_FAILED error
nodes.rationale: If nothing recovers the download the turn does not fail: the attachment is replaced by a text placeholder and the URL is recorded under metadata.mastra.unavailableAttachments so later turns skip re-downloading.

nodes.label: context.mcp.log()
nodes.rationale: Only controls what the MCP client receives; the Mastra logger and observability are unaffected.

nodes.label: toolActions.notifyListChanged()
nodes.rationale: Exists for tool availability changes made outside the registry, such as authorization changes.

nodes.label: subscriptions/listen stream
nodes.rationale: Notifications that outlive a request are delivered on the subscriptions/listen stream a client keeps open, so they only reach clients while that stream is served by a running instance.

nodes.label: Mastra Registry Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Keeps the Mastra instance tool registry consistent with runtime toolActions.add/remove, matching automatic registration at startup.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Voice Provider
nodes.rationale: Edge-optimized speech synthesis for low-latency applications.

nodes.label: Sarvam Voice Provider
nodes.rationale: Specialized in Indic languages and accents.

nodes.label: Speechify Voice Provider
nodes.rationale: Text-to-speech optimized for readability and accessibility.

nodes.label: Text-to-Speech (TTS)
nodes.rationale: TTS is a core component of any voice application; combined with STT it forms the foundation of voice interaction systems, while newer STS models enable real-time interaction at high cost.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Enables conversational resumption: the agent detects suspended tools from message history on the next user message and extracts resumeData from the user's natural-language reply.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Required for automatic resumption: memory tracks suspended tools across messages and threads.

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: Tells the agent what data structure to extract from the user's message for automatic resumption.

nodes.label: resumeStream
nodes.rationale: Manual resumption path used for programmatic control, webhooks, button clicks and external triggers.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Lets a tool pause during execute() when it discovers it needs additional user input; preferred over a tool without execute when the tool needs a structured answer and also runs inside a subagent, since subagents can't run client tools but suspension propagates through the supervisor. Does not throw, so code after await suspend() still runs before the tool pauses.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.rationale: Use agents when the task is open-ended and the steps aren't known in advance; for predetermined multi-step processes with explicit control flow, use workflows instead.

nodes.label: createTool()
nodes.rationale: Plain object tool definitions silently fail to execute, so tools must be defined via createTool() with id, description, inputSchema and execute().

nodes.label: .generate()
nodes.rationale: Returns the full response after all tool calls and steps complete.

nodes.label: mastra.getAgentById()
nodes.rationale: Ensures the agent has access to shared services such as instance-level storage, logging and the agent registry; a directly imported agent lacks those.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: Registering an agent in the Mastra instance gives it access to shared resources such as memory, logging and observability.

nodes.label: .stream()
nodes.rationale: Delivers tokens in real time via textStream while toolCalls, toolResults, steps and usage resolve when the stream finishes.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: With memory configured, agents retain conversation history.

nodes.label: Model router
nodes.rationale: Using provider/model string format lets Mastra automatically look up the provider's environment variable, so no provider import is needed.

nodes.label: resume()
nodes.rationale: Continues a workflow after receiving human input, resuming from the step where it was paused.

nodes.label: suspendPayload
nodes.rationale: Accessed by identifying the suspended step so the user can see the reason and what is needed to resume.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop
nodes.rationale: Works like pausing with suspend(), but the suspend payload provides context or guidance to the user on how to continue; suited to manual approvals, rejections, gated decisions, or any step requiring human oversight.

nodes.label: Multi-turn human input
nodes.rationale: Each step defines resumeSchema and suspendSchema; each step must be resumed in sequence with a separate resume() call, managing multi-step approvals with consistent UI feedback.

nodes.label: Workflows
nodes.rationale: Use workflows for predetermined, multi-step processes with explicit control flow.

nodes.label: abort(reason, options)
nodes.rationale: Retry replays the step with the abort reason appended verbatim as a system reminder, keeping the previous request as its prefix so provider prompt caching is preserved.

nodes.label: maxProcessorRetries
nodes.rationale: Unset by default, which disables processInputStep/processOutputStep retries; error processors have a separate budget of 3 retries when errorProcessors resolve to a non-empty list.

nodes.label: tripwire stream chunk
nodes.rationale: Carries processorId, reason and structured metadata so downstream consumers can branch on categories like pii, quality or moderation.

nodes.label: authenticateToken()
nodes.rationale: CompositeAuth silently catches errors thrown by a provider's authenticateToken so one failing provider cannot block authentication.

nodes.label: authorizeUser()
nodes.rationale: Authorization does not catch errors: a throwing authorizeUser stops checking remaining providers and fails the request with 500, so providers should return false to deny access or defer to the next provider.

nodes.label: CompositeAuth
nodes.rationale: Combines multiple authentication providers into a single handler, trying each in order until one succeeds, so API keys and OAuth tokens can coexist and providers can be migrated or rolled out gradually without breaking existing clients. Provider order matters for performance, so the most common method should be placed first.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.rationale: Used to connect agents to external tools and resources, or expose Mastra capabilities to MCP-compatible systems.

nodes.label: notScorable()
nodes.rationale: Items returning notScorable() are excluded from gate and threshold averages because there is no numeric evidence.

nodes.label: Gates
nodes.rationale: Gates are scorers that must average 1.0 across data items; they are hard requirements that block a run, separating must-pass checks from nice-to-have tracked metrics.

nodes.label: Thresholds
nodes.rationale: A max threshold is used for scorers where a high score is bad (hallucination, toxicity); min/max bands are used when the score should fall within a range.

nodes.label: Verdicts
nodes.rationale: A single verdict signal (passed, scored, failed) lets CI consume eval outcomes without writing custom assertion logic.

nodes.label: Quick Checks
nodes.rationale: Quick Checks are a natural fit as gates because they return binary 1/0 scores.

nodes.label: server.apiPrefix
nodes.rationale: Generated servers pass apiPrefix to the Hono adapter's prefix option, but middleware paths are registered unchanged so they must explicitly include the configured prefix.

nodes.label: CompositeAuth
nodes.rationale: Resource-ID mapping requirement applies to the provider that authenticated the request; a provider without a mapper keeps its existing behavior.

nodes.label: getAuthenticatedUser
nodes.rationale: Lets middleware resolve the authenticated user from the configured auth provider without changing the default route auth flow.

nodes.label: mapUserToResourceId
nodes.rationale: Simplest way to scope memory and threads to the authenticated user; without a mapper authentication does not enable user isolation.

nodes.label: MASTRA_RESOURCE_ID_KEY
nodes.rationale: Server-set resource ID takes precedence over client-provided ?resourceId so cross-resource access returns 403.

nodes.label: MASTRA_THREAD_ID_KEY
nodes.rationale: Overrides the client-provided thread ID to restrict operations to a thread validated through other means.

nodes.label: mastra build
nodes.rationale: Generates a Hono-based HTTP server in the .mastra directory.

nodes.label: Authorization (User Isolation)
nodes.rationale: Without server-enforced resource scoping, authenticated callers can list threads across resources and access their messages and working memory.

nodes.label: Server Middleware
nodes.rationale: Middleware runs before or after an API route handler for authentication, logging, injecting request-specific context, or CORS; user middleware never runs on routes declared public with requiresAuth: false so it cannot block endpoints the framework needs to keep reachable.

nodes.label: Block Built-in Route Groups
nodes.rationale: Mastra provides no configuration option to remove or allowlist built-in routes, so middleware returns a response without calling next() to make route groups unavailable.

nodes.label: Hono
nodes.rationale: Mastra uses Hono as its underlying HTTP server framework.

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API
nodes.rationale: Agent-backed adapters over Mastra agents, memory, and storage, so requests run through the selected Mastra agent instead of acting as a raw provider proxy; currently experimental.

nodes.label: OpenAPI Specification
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI and Swagger endpoints are disabled in production by default.

nodes.label: Mastra Server
nodes.rationale: Mastra runs as an HTTP server exposing agents, workflows, and other functionality as API endpoints, handling routing, middleware, authentication, and streaming.

nodes.label: Stream Data Redaction
nodes.rationale: The HTTP layer redacts system prompts, tool definitions, API keys, and similar data from each streamed chunk before sending to clients; enabled by default.

nodes.label: mastra.getAgent()
nodes.rationale: Resolve the target via mastra.getAgent()/getWorkflow() rather than importing directly: a directly imported agent has no Mastra instance attached, so registry lookups fail, scores aren't persisted, and trajectory scoring is unavailable.

nodes.label: runEvals
nodes.rationale: runEvals processes multiple test cases through an agent or workflow and returns aggregate scores for CI assertions.

nodes.label: Running Scorers in CI
nodes.rationale: Running scorers in CI provides quantifiable metrics for measuring agent quality over time.

nodes.label: groundTruth
nodes.rationale: groundTruth is supplied per data item for scorer validation.

nodes.label: Workflow .parallel()
nodes.rationale: Provides the control-flow structure for running multiple agents in parallel in a council pattern.

nodes.label: Supervisor agents
nodes.rationale: Defines subagents through the agents property and coordinates them with stream() or generate(), with delegation hooks, message filtering, and memory isolation.

nodes.label: Council pattern
nodes.rationale: Keeps the problem shared across independent agents and synthesizes outputs; intentionally duplicates effort, so it costs more and is slower.

nodes.label: Handoffs pattern
nodes.rationale: Ownership moves to the next specialist instead of reporting back through a coordinator; the tradeoff is that context transfer becomes more important.

nodes.label: Multi-agent system
nodes.rationale: Distributes a task across multiple agents so each component gets the right context, tools, and responsibilities; start with one agent and add more only when structure clearly improves quality, speed, or reliability.

nodes.label: Workflows pattern
nodes.rationale: Control logic lives in the workflow itself, giving predictability and auditability at the cost of adaptivity when the task changes mid-run.

nodes.label: Supervisor pattern
nodes.rationale: A parent agent that coordinates subagents is often called a supervisor; it is one approach to building multi-agent systems in Mastra.

nodes.label: mastra_workspace_computer_screenshot
nodes.rationale: Captures the desktop as a PNG and returns it to the model as native media.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.rationale: Registers computer tools only when a statically configured sandbox supports the computer capability; resolver-backed sandboxes don't register them because the workspace can't inspect the resolved sandbox's capabilities when it builds the tool list.

nodes.label: Computer Capability
nodes.rationale: Sandboxes running a desktop environment can expose screenshot, mouse, and keyboard control; only statically configured sandboxes that declare the capability get the tools registered.

nodes.label: Custom adapters
nodes.rationale: Create a custom adapter when the prebuilt server adapters (Hono, Express, Fastify, Koa) don't support your framework or you have specific request/response handling requirements.

nodes.label: memory domain
nodes.rationale: Reads and writes rows during every remembered agent call, so a transactional database is recommended.

nodes.label: MastraMessageContentV2
nodes.rationale: Designed to align closely with the AI SDK UIMessage message shape.

nodes.label: Resources Table
nodes.rationale: Each resource represents a user or entity, allowing working memory to persist across all conversation threads for that user.

nodes.label: Retention-Eligible Tables
nodes.rationale: Anchor columns are chosen so maxAge matches the meaning of the data: append-only logs use creation time, live state uses last activity, and jobs or runs use completion time so in-flight work isn't pruned.

nodes.label: mastra build --studio
nodes.rationale: Produces a .mastra/output/studio folder so the Mastra server can serve Studio, leaving only one service to deploy and manage.

nodes.label: MASTRA_STUDIO_BASE_PATH
nodes.rationale: Updates the HTML base URL and static asset routing so standalone Studio works correctly under a subpath.

nodes.label: mastra studio command
nodes.rationale: Serves a standalone static UI that connects to an already-running Mastra server, unlike mastra dev which runs both Studio and an API.

nodes.label: Standalone Studio SPA
nodes.rationale: Built Studio assets can't be deployed directly to a CDN because the UI relies on runtime configuration; a Vite build replaces %%PLACEHOLDER%% values with environment variables first.

nodes.label: Studio deployment
nodes.rationale: Studio is a React SPA that runs in the browser and connects to a running Mastra server, so it can be hosted by the platform, alongside the server, or as a standalone SPA.

nodes.label: authorizeUser
nodes.rationale: Default implementation checks the isAdmin column in the users table in the public schema.

nodes.label: AppResources
nodes.rationale: A map of ui:// URIs to app resource configurations, each defining an interactive HTML UI served via the MCP Apps extension (SEP-1865).

nodes.label: executeTool()
nodes.rationale: Runs a tool without a protocol client, which is how the Mastra REST route POST /api/mcp/:serverId/tools/:toolId/execute and Studio invoke tools.

nodes.label: getToolListInfo()
nodes.rationale: It's a read-only list, useful for debugging purposes.

nodes.label: MCPServer
nodes.rationale: This API exists specifically for exposing Mastra tools and agents to external MCP clients; if tools or agents are only used inside a Mastra application, an MCP server is not needed.

nodes.label: MCPServerToolResultOptions
nodes.rationale: modelOutput defaults to false now but becomes true in the next major version, so clients parsing raw JSON text of tools that define toModelOutput should set modelOutput: false to keep current behavior.

nodes.label: Access upstream services safely (MCP authentication guide)
nodes.norm_label: access upstream services safely (mcp authentication guide)

nodes.label: DuckDBConnection
nodes.rationale: Exported for sharing a single underlying database across multiple Mastra storage instances.

nodes.label: DuckDBStore
nodes.rationale: Embedded, file-based OLAP observability store for local development; not recommended for production because it runs in-process and fails on ephemeral filesystems.

nodes.label: Event-Sourced Strategy
nodes.rationale: Buffers spans in memory and writes completed events in batches, appropriate for development-scale traffic.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Ideal for local development; file storage does not work on serverless platforms with ephemeral file systems, so Turso or another database engine is recommended there. In-memory storage resets when the process changes and is only suitable for development.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: When storage is passed to the Mastra class, init() is called automatically to create the core schema.

nodes.label: src/pages/api/chat.ts
nodes.rationale: The POST route streams the agent's response in AI SDK format, while the GET route fetches message history from memory so the UI can be hydrated when the client reloads.

nodes.label: MastraServer (Hono adapter)
nodes.rationale: Exposes Mastra agents as HTTP endpoints without writing the routing yourself or running a separate Mastra server.

nodes.label: Session.getTokenUsage()
nodes.rationale: The executing run saves usage to its own thread as each step finishes; sessions that only subscribe display the saved total without counting replayed steps again.

nodes.label: SessionIdentity
nodes.rationale: id and ownerId are stable for the life of the process-local host and do not change when the resource ID is switched.

nodes.label: Session.sendMessage()
nodes.rationale: The session creates a thread first when no thread is active; author metadata persists under content.metadata.signal.author.

nodes.label: SessionThread
nodes.rationale: Conversation settings (mode, model, thinking level, token usage, pending runs, ownership) are restored from the active thread when the session creates or switches threads; the live session and its event bus do not persist.

nodes.label: SessionThread.clone()
nodes.rationale: Clones use the cloning Session host for both metadata.ownerId and metadata.createdBy.

nodes.label: SessionThread.create()
nodes.rationale: For a session created with createInitialThread: false, explicit mode/model/thread-preference selections made before first binding seed the first new thread; after a conversation is bound, new threads use controller defaults.

nodes.label: SessionThread.delete()
nodes.rationale: Deleting the active thread also clears the current binding.

nodes.label: SessionThread.ensureId()
nodes.rationale: Concurrent calls share one thread; intended for sessions created with createInitialThread: false.

nodes.label: SessionThread.transferOwnership()
nodes.rationale: Transfers are serialized within one process; storage-backed apps needing durable cross-process compare-and-set should perform it in their own store first and mirror the result here. Runs snapshot ownership at start, so a transfer becomes visible on the next run.

nodes.label: Session.respondToToolSuspension()
nodes.rationale: An addressed resume uses the source thread's mode, model and thread-owned preferences without selecting that thread or replacing the active thread's subscription, so tool state callbacks stay bound to the source.

nodes.label: SessionSuspensions
nodes.rationale: Parked tool prompts remain available for later resume, including after a process restart via a full address.

nodes.label: SessionThread.switch()
nodes.rationale: Switching away cancels a running local execution only when this session initiated it; a session listening to another session's run detaches without cancelling it.

nodes.label: session.om.observer.model()
nodes.rationale: Selection intent ('auto' vs explicit ID) is kept separate from the effective concrete model ID.

nodes.label: session.om.observer.modelId()
nodes.rationale: If the auto resolver returns no model or throws, the role falls back to its concrete omConfig model so a role always has a usable model.

nodes.label: session.om.observer.switchModel({ modelId })
nodes.rationale: Automatic selection clears the role's stale concrete model ID so the role follows the active main model rather than a leftover pin.

nodes.label: om_model_changed event
nodes.rationale: Contains the effective concrete modelId rather than the selection intent.

nodes.label: omConfig.resolveAutoModelId
nodes.rationale: Called with the role, current main model ID and read-only session state to turn an 'auto' selection into a concrete model ID.

nodes.label: Agent.listSuspendedRuns()
nodes.rationale: Uses workflow snapshot storage so suspended-run discovery survives server restarts and works across multiple server instances; snapshots are only persisted while a run awaits input, so suspended runs are the only runs discoverable from storage.

nodes.label: Dataset class
nodes.rationale: Obtained via DatasetsManager so that dataset resolution and tenancy scoping are applied; the public constructor skips that lookup and scoping.

nodes.label: dataset.startExperimentAsync()
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget start returns immediately with a 'pending' status; use synchronous startExperiment() when the caller needs the returned summary, and note that with persistence.experiments set to 'none' no experiment record, progress updates, or item results are persisted.

nodes.label: dataset.submitExperimentResult()
nodes.rationale: Submissions are upserts keyed by (experimentId, itemId, attempt) so a retried worker converges on a single row instead of duplicating results; submissions to an experiment that has a target throw EXPERIMENT_HAS_TARGET to prevent two writers racing on the same rows, and score persistence is best-effort so it never fails the submission.

nodes.label: ModelByInputTokens
nodes.rationale: Selects the model for the smallest threshold covering the actual input size, so cheap models handle small Observer/Reflector inputs and stronger models handle large ones.

nodes.label: ObservationalMemoryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Needs a Memory instance for loading and persisting messages, so the engine can be plugged into agent input/output processor chains.

nodes.label: ObservationalMemory.observe()
nodes.rationale: force: true bypasses the observation threshold for that call only and is not saved to the record's config, so a one-off forced observation does not change future behavior.

nodes.label: recall tool
nodes.rationale: Registered automatically when retrieval is truthy so the agent can page back to raw messages behind lossy observation groups.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Observer and reflector model choices are independent so each role can be tuned or left automatic.

nodes.label: Async buffering
nodes.rationale: Pre-computes observations in the background as the conversation grows so buffered observations activate instantly when the threshold is hit, avoiding a mid-conversation pause.

nodes.label: Automatic Model Selection
nodes.rationale: An automatic Observer or Reflector follows the active main model provider, using that provider's built-in low-cost OM model when configured; the effective model is resolved when the role runs so changing the main model doesn't rewrite the saved automatic selection.

nodes.label: Failure Policy
nodes.rationale: 'continue' keeps the failed input pending, reports the failure through OM diagnostics and lets the main agent turn continue, but has no backstop for a sustained outage.

nodes.label: activateAfterIdle
nodes.rationale: Uses a provider-aware prompt cache TTL when set to auto.

nodes.label: blockAfter
nodes.rationale: Safety net for when background buffering can't keep up.

nodes.label: Continuation Hints
nodes.rationale: Agents that drive their own control flow generally want suggestedResponse disabled so memory does not compete for what the agent says next.

nodes.label: observeAttachments
nodes.rationale: Useful when the Observer model is text-only while the main agent uses a multimodal model.

nodes.label: ObserveHooks
nodes.rationale: Lets apps account for OM model spend without wrapping the observer/reflector models in middleware.

nodes.label: Retrieval (recall tool)
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent look up the raw message history behind its observations.

nodes.label: Memory Scope
nodes.rationale: Thread scope works much better than resource scope for prompt caching and agent understanding; resource scope is deprecated.

nodes.label: shareTokenBudget
nodes.rationale: Maximizes context usage through flexible allocation between messages and observations.

nodes.label: Temporal Markers
nodes.rationale: Shown to the observer so it can anchor observations to when events occurred.

nodes.label: Token Estimate Metadata Cache
nodes.rationale: Persists token payload estimates so repeated counting can reuse prior token estimation work.

nodes.label: createFaithfulnessScorer
nodes.rationale: Extracts claims from the output and verifies them against context so RAG responses can be checked for support by retrieved information; when context is omitted the scorer falls back to tool-call results in the run output.

nodes.label: createHallucinationScorer
nodes.rationale: Measures hallucination by identifying direct contradictions and unsupported claims between context and output; getContext takes priority over static context for live scoring where context (e.g. tool results) is only available at run time.

nodes.label: defineSchedule
nodes.rationale: Re-exported from @mastra/core/agent so file-based agents need one import path.

nodes.label: Handler Execution Mode
nodes.rationale: Use it when the prompt depends on current state, when some fires should be skipped, or when the run needs channel delivery context. Handlers are functions, so they are resolved in-process at fire time rather than persisted.

nodes.label: Markdown Schedules
nodes.rationale: Prompt mode with more room to write: frontmatter holds cron/timezone and the body is the prompt.

nodes.label: Prompt Execution Mode
nodes.rationale: Runs the owning agent with a fixed message; threaded fires send a wake signal and return without waiting, threadless fires await agent.generate.

nodes.label: Schedule Registration and Lifecycle Sync
nodes.rationale: The sync writes only what changed and deliberately leaves status alone so pausing through the API survives a redeploy; it only removes rows for agents registered in the current process.

nodes.label: Schedule Identity (path-derived id)
nodes.rationale: The id is stable across builds, which is what lets Mastra tell an edited schedule from a new one.

nodes.label: File-Based Agent Schedules
nodes.rationale: Declaring a schedule file is enough to start the scheduler; a scheduled agent needs no runtime registration code.

nodes.label: Mastra Storage
nodes.rationale: Schedules are persisted rows and in-memory store rows do not survive a restart, so storage is required.

nodes.label: auth configuration
nodes.rationale: Promoted from experimental_auth to stable, reflecting that the auth API is production-ready.

nodes.label: Config type
nodes.rationale: The main @mastra/core index now only exports Mastra and Config.

nodes.label: Mastra class
nodes.rationale: Restructured to restrict top-level imports and replace direct property access with getter methods.

nodes.label: getById / get primitive APIs
nodes.rationale: Each primitive has both a get (registry key) and a getById (intrinsic ID) function.

nodes.label: Intrinsic tool IDs
nodes.rationale: Auto-registered tools use the tool's intrinsic id instead of the configuration object key to prevent collisions when multiple agents/MCP servers have tools with the same key.

nodes.label: list<primitive> APIs
nodes.rationale: get* functions returning all instances of a primitive renamed to list* to better reflect their purpose.

nodes.label: Subpath imports
nodes.rationale: Improves tree-shaking and reduces bundle size by allowing bundlers to eliminate unused code.

nodes.label: @mastra/ai-sdk/ui
nodes.rationale: AI SDK format conversion moved to dedicated utility functions here to improve tree-shaking by separating UI-specific conversion code.

nodes.label: Memory class
nodes.rationale: Memory configuration now requires explicit parameters and defaults were updated for better performance and predictability.

nodes.label: Memory options
nodes.rationale: Defaults changed to more reasonable values based on usage patterns, improving performance and reducing unexpected LLM API calls.

nodes.label: options.readOnly
nodes.rationale: Moved inside options to align readOnly with other memory configuration options like lastMessages and semanticRecall.

nodes.label: Memory.recall()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from query(); returns a simpler { messages: MastraDBMessage[] } format and better describes the action of retrieving messages.

nodes.label: semanticRecall
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default; topK increased 2 to 4 and messageRange changed to {before:1, after:1} based on RAG research for better accuracy with only slightly more messages.

nodes.label: workingMemory
nodes.rationale: text-stream mode removed; only tool-call mode is supported because the streaming mode was less reliable.

nodes.label: controllerHostUrl
nodes.rationale: Replaces the removed environment parameter for specifying a custom Pinecone controller host.

nodes.label: listVectors
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getVectors to align with the API convention where plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: Required id Property
nodes.rationale: Unique identifier used for tracking and managing vector store instances within Mastra.

nodes.label: LeaseProvider
nodes.rationale: Distributed leasing contract kept separate from event delivery (PubSub): the signals layer uses it to elect a single owner across processes for a resource (usually a thread key) so only one process wakes and runs the agent stream while others route follow-up work to it. Leasing requires real lock coordination (atomic Redis SET/Lua or an in-memory map), so backends without it fall back to a no-op always-win provider that preserves single-process behavior.

nodes.label: RedisStreamsPubSub
nodes.rationale: Backed by Redis Streams for cross-process/host delivery with persistence, consumer groups and redelivery; it is a pull transport (XREADGROUP) so Mastra runs an orchestration worker to read on its behalf. It also implements LeaseProvider, which is what lets signals elect a single owner per resource across instances in distributed and serverless deployments.

nodes.label: Signals Runtime
nodes.rationale: Without a shared lease each instance would start its own competing run, so signals rely on RedisStreamsPubSub's LeaseProvider for serverless and multi-instance deployments.

nodes.label: createGraphRAGTool()
nodes.rationale: Uses the GraphRAG system under the hood so retrieval finds relevant content through both direct similarity and connected relationships; the graph is built from the text field of each result's metadata, so chunk text must be stored under metadata.text when upserting.

nodes.label: VectorStoreResolver
nodes.rationale: A resolver function allows dynamic vector store selection for multi-tenant applications where the store is chosen from request context; when provided, vectorStoreName becomes optional.

nodes.label: MCP Resources
nodes.rationale: Resources expose server data that clients can read and use as context for LLM interactions, identified by unique URIs and containing text or binary data.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: Combines separate input (STT) and output (TTS) providers so one voice object can mix providers, e.g. OpenAI for speech-to-text and ElevenLabs for text-to-speech.

nodes.label: listeningModel
nodes.rationale: All listeningModel parameters are optional; defaults come from the specific voice provider.

nodes.label: Speech-to-Text (STT)
nodes.rationale: STT lets voice-enabled applications respond to human speech, supporting hands-free interaction, accessibility for users with disabilities, and a more natural interface.

nodes.label: AI SDK Model Providers
nodes.rationale: AI SDK models can be used directly with CompositeVoice without installing separate Mastra provider packages.

nodes.label: abort
nodes.rationale: Passing retry: true feeds the reason back to the LLM as feedback for the same step; retries only run when maxProcessorRetries is configured.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: content is a structured object, never a plain string; content.parts is the primary text source and content.content is a flattened string kept only for backward compatibility.

nodes.label: MessageList
nodes.rationale: messageList is the canonical way to add, remove or reorder messages because messages is always derived from it; returning a different MessageList instance is an error.

nodes.label: OutputProcessor
nodes.rationale: Type alias requiring at least one of processOutputStream, processOutputStep, or processOutputResult.

nodes.label: processOutputStep
nodes.rationale: Runs after each LLM response in the agentic loop, before tool execution, rather than once at the end, so guardrails can trigger retries per step.

nodes.label: writer.custom
nodes.rationale: The only way for a processor to emit content outside of normal text and tool chunks.

nodes.label: processInputStep
nodes.rationale: System messages are reset to their original values at the start of each step, so modifications made in processInputStep only affect the current step, not subsequent steps.

nodes.label: processOutputResult
nodes.rationale: Runs once at the end of the run, unlike processOutputStep which runs at every step.

nodes.label: Processor State
nodes.rationale: Per-processor and per-request isolation prevents state leaking between processors, requests, or users, while sharing across methods within a request enables cross-method coordination.

nodes.label: voice.connect()
nodes.rationale: Realtime providers must be connected before using speak/send.

nodes.label: GeminiLiveVoice
nodes.rationale: Live API requires GOOGLE_API_KEY; Vertex AI requires project/location and service account credentials.

nodes.label: InworldRealtimeVoice
nodes.rationale: Inworld's wire protocol is the OpenAI Realtime GA spec, so event names match @mastra/voice-openai-realtime; the model is configured via the initial session.update rather than the WebSocket URL.

nodes.label: NovaSonicVoice
nodes.rationale: Authenticates through the standard AWS credential provider chain; pass credentials to override.

nodes.label: EnsureFinalResponseProcessor
nodes.rationale: Appends a reactive signal instead of modifying system messages, which preserves prompt caching.

nodes.label: prepareStep()
nodes.rationale: Shorthand for processInputStep() that does not require creating a class; Mastra internally wraps it in a processor.

nodes.label: Transient Signal
nodes.rationale: Not retaining the signal avoids copies piling up and the model imitating its own past reminders, and keeps a stable prompt cache prefix across turns.

nodes.label: Mastra Guides
nodes.rationale: Explains how Mastra features work together, covering design decisions, runtime behavior, and applicable patterns.

nodes.label: Schedule lifecycle hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks live at the Mastra level so they apply to both code-defined and stored agents.

nodes.label: cron expression
nodes.rationale: Validated at workflow construction time; timezone should be set explicitly in production so fire times don't depend on server locale.

nodes.label: Evented Execution Engine
nodes.rationale: Used when MASTRA_WORKERS is set so every process in a split-worker deployment runs scheduled workflows the same way.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKERS environment variable
nodes.rationale: Only the environment variable triggers the engine switch because createWorkflow runs before Mastra reads its workers option.

nodes.label: schedule field
nodes.rationale: Declared on createWorkflow so the scheduler reads it straight off the workflow at Mastra boot, avoiding a separate register-schedule call.

nodes.label: agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: For a one-off request; it can use Memory but doesn't give a subscription that follows later runs on the same thread.

nodes.label: AgentController Session
nodes.rationale: Manages the thread and subscription for you when building long-running assistants and coding agents on AgentController.

nodes.label: client.getAgent()
nodes.rationale: The client returns the subscription stream and leaves run ownership on the server.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Stores thread history so the same conversation is available across runs and process restarts; accepts any supported storage adapter.

nodes.label: delegation option
nodes.rationale: Configured in defaultOptions or per-call to intercept, modify, or reject delegations as they happen.

nodes.label: enableResultReferences
nodes.rationale: Lets a later delegation reuse an earlier subagent result verbatim via reference IDs, avoiding token cost and detail loss from restating results in the prompt.

nodes.label: hookErrorStrategy
nodes.rationale: Defaults to continuing the delegation when a hook throws; set to 'throw' to fail the delegation instead.

nodes.label: includeSubAgentToolResultsInModelContext
nodes.rationale: Keeps nested tool arguments and outputs out of the parent model context by default, while still exposing them to app code and UI.

nodes.label: messageFilter
nodes.rationale: Controls which parent conversation messages are shared with a subagent, e.g. to remove sensitive data or limit context size.

nodes.label: onDelegationComplete hook
nodes.rationale: Lets you inspect results, bail the parent loop, save feedback for the next turn, or replace the tool result text the parent model sees immediately.

nodes.label: onDelegationStart hook
nodes.rationale: Can allow, reject, rewrite the prompt, set the subagent iteration budget, or attach thread metadata before delegation.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Each delegation receives a shallow copy of the parent's request context excluding run-scoped identity keys, so subagent changes don't affect the parent.

nodes.label: bail()
nodes.rationale: Exits early with a successful result, returning the payload as step output and ending workflow execution.

nodes.label: getStepResultAsync()
nodes.rationale: Resolves to null if the step has not completed successfully, allowing inspection of previous step results.

nodes.label: onError callback
nodes.rationale: Called only on failure or tripwire status for centralized error alerting and tracking.

nodes.label: onFinish callback
nodes.rationale: Called on any completion status for centralized logging or alerting when the result is not awaited, such as background or fire-and-forget workflows.

nodes.label: stream()
nodes.rationale: Lets you monitor workflows for errors by iterating emitted chunks.

nodes.label: bail()
nodes.rationale: Stops workflow execution at a step without triggering an error when a human explicitly rejects an action; the workflow completes with success status and later logic is skipped.

nodes.label: Conditional branching
nodes.rationale: Creates alternative workflow paths based on the success or failure of previous steps.

nodes.label: Workflow result status
nodes.rationale: Result object carries status, result, error, and per-step results so callers can branch on success, failed, suspended, paused, or tripwire.

nodes.label: retries
nodes.rationale: Step-level retry count that overrides the workflow-level retry configuration for that specific step.

nodes.label: retryConfig
nodes.rationale: Workflow-level retry configuration applied to all steps for transient failures.

nodes.label: cloneWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Reuses workflow logic but tracks it separately under a new ID so each clone runs independently and appears distinctly in logs and observability tools.

nodes.label: createWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Composes steps into an execution flow; steps are added with .then() and the workflow is completed with .commit().

nodes.label: getWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Preferred over a direct import because it provides access to the Mastra instance configuration (logger, telemetry, storage, agents, vector stores) and full TypeScript type inference for input/output schemas.

nodes.label: getWorkflowById()
nodes.rationale: Retrieves workflows by their id property but does not provide the same level of type inference as getWorkflow().

nodes.label: Workflow runners
nodes.rationale: Workflows use the built-in execution engine by default, while managed infrastructure is available through runners such as Inngest.

nodes.label: exportSchemas
nodes.rationale: Generates Oracle DDL without connecting to a database, useful when schema changes are reviewed or applied outside application startup.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: When OracleStore is passed to Mastra, init() is called automatically before storage operations run.

nodes.label: OraclePoolManager
nodes.rationale: Shared Oracle pool manager used to share one Oracle pool between OracleStore and OracleVector.

nodes.label: OracleStore
nodes.rationale: Implements Mastra's composite storage interface so one OracleStore instance can back memory, workflow snapshots, observability, scores, scorer definitions, MCP client metadata, and agent registry data. Repeatable migrations are idempotent and reconcile tables/indexes on startup so new domain indexes apply without application code changes.

nodes.label: OracleVector
nodes.rationale: Sharing one OraclePoolManager between OracleStore and OracleVector lets both share a single Oracle connection lifecycle.

nodes.label: Inline experiment task
nodes.rationale: Receives the item's metadata so each row can drive its own thread without changing the agent or any scorer.

nodes.label: runEvals
nodes.rationale: Accepts targetOptions forwarded to agent.generate(), so a single memory thread/resource can be shared across every data item.

nodes.label: targetOptions
nodes.rationale: Global per runEvals call; no per-item override on RunEvalsDataItem is available today.

nodes.label: dataset.createExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on a caller-supplied id so durable orchestrators can retry creation safely; the dataset version is pinned at creation.

nodes.label: ExperimentEvent / onEvent observer
nodes.rationale: Observer calls are awaited serially to apply backpressure and keep event sequence values aligned with delivery order while item execution stays concurrent.

nodes.label: ExperimentSummary
nodes.rationale: Status and counts describe execution only; scores must be inspected to assess output quality.

nodes.label: dataset.finalizeExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Server computes succeeded/failed/skipped counts from persisted rows so callers keep no completion bookkeeping; idempotent and terminal.

nodes.label: itemTimeout / maxRetries
nodes.rationale: Retries use exponential backoff; abort errors are never retried.

nodes.label: Lifecycle hooks (beforeAll/beforeEach/afterEach/afterAll)
nodes.rationale: Teardown failures are logged rather than propagated because discarding a real result over untidy cleanup would lose the data the experiment was run to collect.

nodes.label: persistence option
nodes.rationale: Experiment and score record persistence can be disabled independently; it does not disable storage used by the target such as memory or observability.

nodes.label: dataset.runExperimentItem()
nodes.rationale: Lets a caller-driven orchestrator own the loop while Mastra executes the target and scorers; results upsert on (experimentId, itemId, attempt).

nodes.label: dataset.startExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Blocks until all items finish; use startExperimentAsync for fire-and-forget execution.

nodes.label: dataset.startExperimentAsync()
nodes.rationale: Runs the experiment in the background for long-running datasets; completion is polled via getExperiment.

nodes.label: dataset.submitExperimentResult()
nodes.rationale: Ingests externally executed and scored results; rejected for experiments created with a target so two writers can't race on the same rows.

nodes.label: unmockedToolPolicy
nodes.rationale: Set to 'deny' to block every tool call without a mock, preventing live side effects; item value overrides experiment value.

nodes.label: RequestContext.MastraMemory
nodes.rationale: Pre-seeding RequestContext with MastraMemory is not supported because thread resolution reads args.memory.thread and MastraMemory is populated by prepare-memory-step after thread resolution.

nodes.label: Observational memory (thread scope)
nodes.rationale: Thread-scoped observational memory reads from a record that must already exist, so the thread must be created before the eval runs.

nodes.label: Experiment scorers
nodes.rationale: Exactly one scorer source is used per item in precedence order (experiment, item, dataset, none); sources are never merged and an explicit empty array prevents fallback.

nodes.label: Tool mocks
nodes.rationale: Static mocks attached to dataset items make side-effecting tool calls deterministic; supported for agent targets only.

nodes.label: MastraStorageExporter
nodes.rationale: Traces from this exporter cannot be persisted to Upstash because Upstash storage does not support the observability domain.

nodes.label: UpstashStore
nodes.rationale: Serverless-friendly Redis-compatible store; pay-as-you-go pricing can be unexpectedly expensive because agent conversations generate a high volume of Redis commands, so a fixed pricing plan is recommended. Does not support the observability domain.

nodes.label: Composite storage
nodes.rationale: Used to route observability data to a supported provider when Upstash is the primary store.

nodes.label: Mastra Studio
nodes.rationale: Studio observability features will not work with Upstash as the only storage provider.

nodes.label: Mastra Config (src/mastra/index.ts)
nodes.rationale: chatRoute() creates an API route the React frontend can call for AI SDK-compatible chat responses used with useChat().

nodes.label: session.permissions
nodes.rationale: Permission rules are distinct from in-memory grants: grants reset with the live session, and rules are not durable unless the host restores the corresponding session state.

nodes.label: session.permissions.setForTool({ toolName, policy })
nodes.rationale: Per-tool policies take precedence over category policies.

nodes.label: Session grants
nodes.rationale: In-memory tool grants that reset with the live session, unlike persisted permission rules.

nodes.label: ActorSignal
nodes.rationale: Identifies a call made by a trusted non-user actor; actor.permissions is an untrusted self-asserted hint, so providers should resolve authoritative grants from a trusted source keyed by agentId.

nodes.label: FGADeniedError
nodes.rationale: Thrown by require and requireActor to deny; Mastra surfaces it as an HTTP 403.

nodes.label: FGARouteResolver
nodes.rationale: Derives resource type, resource ID, and permission from the route, parsed params, and request context.

nodes.label: IFGAProvider
nodes.rationale: Implement it to connect Mastra to an FGA backend such as WorkOS Authorization; FGA requires a Mastra Enterprise Edition license in production but works without one in development.

nodes.label: Mastra.getMCPServer()
nodes.rationale: Retrieves an MCP server by its registry key; use getMCPServerById() for the intrinsic id. Registry keys and intrinsic server IDs remain distinct, and registering another server under an occupied registry key keeps the existing instance.

nodes.label: MCPServer
nodes.rationale: Implements MCPServerBase for the MCP 2026-07-28 protocol and sets mcpVersion to 2.

nodes.label: mastra auth tokens create
nodes.rationale: Creates an API token for headless CI deploys.

nodes.label: Mastra CLI
nodes.rationale: CLI-driven deploys replace auto-deploy on push.

nodes.label: mastra deploy
nodes.rationale: Unified command for deploying to multiple environments.

nodes.label: .mastra-project.json
nodes.rationale: Created on first deploy to link the local project to the platform; should be committed to the repository.

nodes.label: mastra server deploy
nodes.rationale: Creates a separate deployment with a stable API URL, env var management, and custom domain support.

nodes.label: mastra studio deploy
nodes.rationale: Builds the project and uploads the artifact before deploying Studio.

nodes.label: browserStateProcessor (example)
nodes.rationale: Decides between delta and snapshot using lastSnapshot and contextWindow.hasSnapshot, returning a fresh snapshot when the active window no longer contains one.

nodes.label: computeStateSignal()
nodes.rationale: Called once per model input step after processInputStep() and before the model request is finalized; returns undefined when nothing changed.

nodes.label: sendStateSignal()
nodes.rationale: Skips an update and returns { skipped: true, reason: 'unchanged' } when both cacheKey and mode match the tracked values; requires Memory and an existing thread (it can't create a missing thread).

nodes.label: timeTravel()
nodes.rationale: Re-executes a workflow from any specific step using stored snapshot data or custom context, useful for debugging, testing, and recovering from errors without re-running the whole workflow.

nodes.label: Delta
nodes.rationale: Description of what changed; the producer is responsible for comparing and combining values.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Full description of current state; send a fresh snapshot if the old one has left the model's context or a delta may be insufficient.

nodes.label: State lane
nodes.rationale: The named slot identified by a state id; start with a snapshot, then send deltas while the model still has the snapshot it needs.

nodes.label: State signal
nodes.rationale: Keeps the model informed about something that changes over time under a stable name on a thread; updates provide context rather than chat messages. State signals can't be transient because Mastra rebuilds tracking metadata from persisted history, so a delivery-only signal would break deduplication.

nodes.label: time travel context
nodes.rationale: Lets you specify the state of previous steps when time traveling.

nodes.label: WORKFLOW_TIME_TRAVEL_ALREADY_CLAIMED
nodes.rationale: Time travel atomically claims the run before executing so only one call proceeds at a time.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.rationale: External events that need a durable inbox record and delivery policy belong in notifications rather than state signals.

nodes.label: Transient reactive signal
nodes.rationale: Use when context only matters for one model request.

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.rationale: Can move out of the system prompt and into a working-memory state signal with useStateSignals: true.

nodes.label: ClassifierProcessor
nodes.rationale: The classifier provides evidence (probabilities, choices, scores) while onResult owns application policy; abort reasons are always the caller-supplied string so provider-generated text never leaks into the abort message.

nodes.label: ClassifierProcessorDecision
nodes.rationale: Emitted after each classifier call, including failed calls, so callers can write an audit record.

nodes.label: ModerationProcessor
nodes.rationale: Hybrid input/output processor using an LLM to detect inappropriate content. bufferSize buffering is recommended for production streaming because it makes far fewer LLM calls and catches content split across chunks; lastMessageOnly avoids an extra LLM call for each earlier message in long conversations.

nodes.label: PIIDetector
nodes.rationale: Hybrid processor for privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA) with multiple redaction methods; lastMessageOnly avoids one LLM call per earlier message in long threads.

nodes.label: computeStateSignal
nodes.rationale: State signals can't be transient because the deduplication tracking is rebuilt from persisted history.

nodes.label: isRetryableOpenAIResponsesStreamError
nodes.rationale: Never retries a credential or quota refusal, even when the chunk reports retry guidance.

nodes.label: StreamErrorRetryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Added last to every agent's default errorProcessors so that processors which repair a request (ProviderHistoryCompat, PrefillErrorHandler, UnsupportedFileHandler) get their chance before this one retries it unchanged; the default instance does not retry unknown errors or replay HTTP 400 responses the repair processors could not fix.

nodes.label: CachingPubSub
nodes.rationale: Wraps any PubSub and records every published event per topic in a cache so a late-connecting or reconnecting subscriber can replay missed events before continuing with live events; used to build resumable streams on transports that keep no history (e.g. EventEmitterPubSub), while transports that already persist events (e.g. RedisStreamsPubSub) don't need it.

nodes.label: withCaching
nodes.rationale: Convenience wrapper that constructs a CachingPubSub; reads better when wrapping inline.

nodes.label: EventEmitterPubSub
nodes.rationale: Default PubSub implementation; delivers events in-process via a Node.js EventEmitter so it needs no external service. Because it is in-process, events are not persisted or shared across processes, so it should be wrapped in CachingPubSub when replay for resumable streams is needed.

nodes.label: ChromaConfig
nodes.rationale: Supports advanced metadata filtering and content-based document filtering with operator expressions.

nodes.label: DatabaseConfig
nodes.rationale: Designed to be extensible via an index signature so new vector databases can add their own configuration block without breaking existing tools.

nodes.label: MongoDBConfig
nodes.rationale: numCandidates improves recall at the cost of query latency; defaults to 20 x topK capped at 10,000.

nodes.label: PgVectorConfig
nodes.rationale: ef and probes trade accuracy/recall against speed; minScore filters out low-quality results.

nodes.label: PineconeConfig
nodes.rationale: Namespace enables multi-tenancy and environment isolation; sparseVector enables hybrid search combining dense and sparse embeddings for keyword-based queries.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Allows databaseConfig and vectorStoreName to be overridden at runtime per request.

nodes.label: TurbopufferConfig
nodes.rationale: Strong consistency guarantees read-your-writes at higher latency; eventual offers lower latency but recently written data may not be visible.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Allows databaseConfig overrides at runtime based on context.

nodes.label: Hybrid Vector Search
nodes.rationale: Merges semantic search with structured filtering criteria in a single query.

nodes.label: Metadata Filtering
nodes.rationale: Combining vector similarity search with metadata filters (hybrid vector search) narrows the search space when documents come from different sources, time periods, or attributes.

nodes.label: Re-ranking
nodes.rationale: Initial vector similarity search can miss detailed relevance; re-ranking is more computationally expensive but more accurate because it considers word order, exact matches, and cross-attention between query and documents.

nodes.label: Vector Query Tool
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent decide at runtime what to retrieve, combining semantic search with optional filtering and reranking based on its understanding of the user's needs.

nodes.label: Storing Embeddings in a Vector Database
nodes.norm_label: storing embeddings in a vector database

nodes.label: AgentThreadEvent
nodes.rationale: The only event type emitted today is queue-count-changed; composite thread state, message lifecycle, run and approval events are not emitted as public thread events.

nodes.label: subscribeThreadEvents()
nodes.rationale: A narrow event surface for queue counts, separate from subscribeToThread(), which streams agent output. Counts are local to the runtime and include messages submitted by other Sessions or Agents sharing the same runtime and PubSub instance.

nodes.label: context.mcp.progress()
nodes.rationale: No-op when the caller did not include a progressToken in the request _meta.

nodes.label: DatadogExporter
nodes.rationale: Gives spans their own IDs, so a link between two Mastra spans does not resolve in that backend.

nodes.label: SentryExporter
nodes.rationale: Gives spans their own IDs, so a link between two Mastra spans does not resolve in that backend.

nodes.label: MCP_SERVER_REQUEST Span
nodes.rationale: A standalone MCPServer with no mastra instance produces no spans.

nodes.label: W3C traceparent / tracestate
nodes.rationale: Read from request _meta first, then HTTP headers, so both Mastra and non-Mastra callers can be linked.

nodes.label: AttachmentUploader
nodes.rationale: Uploads base64 attachments to external storage and replaces them with URL references before messages are persisted, to avoid storage provider record size limits.

nodes.label: MemoryInputFilter
nodes.rationale: Runs first by default so MessageHistory, SemanticRecall, and Observational Memory receive only the new input they need; trims client-echoed history before memory loaders run.

nodes.label: MessageHistory processor
nodes.rationale: Added to both input and output processors so it fetches recent messages before the LLM and persists new messages after the model responds.

nodes.label: SemanticRecall processor
nodes.rationale: Requires a vector store plus an embedder unless the vector store generates embeddings itself; performs vector similarity search on input and creates embeddings on output.

nodes.label: WorkingMemory processor
nodes.rationale: Input-only processor; requires a storage adapter to be configured and performs no output processing.

nodes.label: PrefillErrorHandler
nodes.rationale: Reacts to the API rejection itself instead of re-checking whether the conversation currently ends with an assistant message, making it resilient when the provider rejects for prefill semantics even if the trailing message shape was already transformed upstream. Only acts on the first retry attempt so it needs no configuration.

nodes.label: maxProcessorRetries
nodes.rationale: Without a configured cap, retries requested by input and output processors are treated as aborts; the safety cap of 3 covers only error-processor retries from processAPIError.

nodes.label: processDataParts
nodes.rationale: Defaults to off so processors don't accidentally process tool telemetry or their own output.

nodes.label: ReasoningTransformer
nodes.rationale: Transforms reasoning parts to thinking parts at each step, useful when switching between model providers.

nodes.label: Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Default execution order is designed to be safe by default: if an output guardrail calls abort(), memory processors never run and no messages are saved.

nodes.label: Processor
nodes.rationale: Default span names describe how Mastra ran a processor rather than what it does, which is unhelpful for processors a user did not configure as such; spanType/spanName/spanAttributes let built-ins and user processors declare their subsystem instead.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: CompositeVoice forwards connect() options to the configured real-time provider and throws if none is configured.

nodes.label: voice.connect()
nodes.rationale: connect() waits for both the WebSocket to open and the server to create a session, rejecting on handshake failure or silent timeout, so failures surface as rejected promises rather than only error events.

nodes.label: connectTimeoutMs
nodes.rationale: Set in the constructor rather than connect() because it applies only to connection setup, not to an established session; default 15000ms.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: CompositeVoice delegates listen() to the configured input provider, which may be a Mastra provider or an AI SDK transcription model.

nodes.label: voice.listen()
nodes.rationale: Realtime providers emit 'writing' events instead of returning text, so callers must register a listener rather than await a return value.

nodes.label: Workspace.destroy()
nodes.rationale: Closes workspace-owned resources in order: language servers, browsers, sandbox providers, filesystem providers; LocalFilesystem.destroy() does not delete files on disk.

nodes.label: Workspace.init()
nodes.rationale: Optional in most cases: sandbox auto-starts on first executeCommand, filesystem may auto-create directories; required only for autoIndexPaths indexing.

nodes.label: Workspace.stop()
nodes.rationale: Stopping is not teardown: filesystem, search index and skills remain available and the next sandbox operation restarts the sandbox.

nodes.label: Mastra Templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-built project structures that provide working examples, best practices, educational resources and quickstarts so projects can be bootstrapped faster than building from scratch.

nodes.label: MastraClient.getA2A()
nodes.rationale: Use the client SDK when application code needs to call an A2A-enabled Mastra endpoint directly; uses v0.3 by default.

nodes.label: MastraClient.getA2AV1()
nodes.rationale: Opts into the A2A v1.0 wire protocol and sends the A2A-Version: 1.0 header automatically.

nodes.label: listTasks()
nodes.rationale: Operation added by the direct v1.0 client.

nodes.label: resubscribeTask()
nodes.rationale: Receives live updates for an in-progress task after a stream disconnects.

nodes.label: sendMessageStream()
nodes.rationale: Receives task status and artifact updates over Server-Sent Events.

nodes.label: @mastra/core/a2a/v1
nodes.rationale: Holds v1.0 protocol types and codecs; the existing @mastra/core/a2a/client export remains on v0.3.

nodes.label: notScorable()
nodes.rationale: A scorer that judges refund handling has nothing to say about a run where no refund was requested; notScorable lets the scorer inspect run input/output before skipping.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Verifies the caller; kept separate from delegated access and application authorization because each answers a different question.

nodes.label: Regression Check
nodes.rationale: Use a script when continuous integration should block a release automatically; keep Studio as the place to inspect and compare answers.

nodes.label: AgentControllerRequestContext
nodes.rationale: Every run snapshots the thread owner at start, so a mid-run ownership change applies to the next run rather than the active one.

nodes.label: ChannelSessionRejectedError
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes an intentional refusal from a failure so a broken bot doesn't look like a silent one; carries the original error as its cause.

nodes.label: controller.createSession()
nodes.rationale: Get-or-create by session id so hosts can resume an existing conversation instead of forking it.

nodes.label: resolveSession
nodes.rationale: Replaces built-in session creation and runs before any session exists so a host can refuse a request; throwing refuses before the controller creates a session or calls the model.

nodes.label: session.listMessages()
nodes.rationale: limit is a deprecated alias for perPage; paged callers using orderBy, filter, or include must use perPage.

nodes.label: session.thread.transferOwnership()
nodes.rationale: Transfers are serialized within one process; hosts needing durable cross-process compare-and-set should commit in their own storage first, then mirror the owner onto the active thread.

nodes.label: Thread
nodes.rationale: Stored conversation that survives controller and process recreation when storage is configured, unlike live Session state.

nodes.label: AgentController
nodes.rationale: Shared host for one or more Session instances: the controller supplies shared agents, configuration, storage, workspaces and services, while per-conversation state lives on the Session.

nodes.label: AgentControllerMode
nodes.rationale: Mode tools and additionalTools are mutually exclusive; an empty availableTools array hides every tool in that mode.

nodes.label: AgentController.createSession()
nodes.rationale: createInitialThread defaults to true; set it to false to start a session without a thread so unused sessions leave no empty thread behind.

nodes.label: AgentController.deleteSession()
nodes.rationale: Tears down the live session only; persisted threads and messages are not deleted.

nodes.label: AgentController.destroy()
nodes.rationale: Stops controller-owned interval handlers only; it does not destroy Sessions created by the controller.

nodes.label: AgentController.generateThreadTitle()
nodes.rationale: Passing sessionId borrows a live session's agent and request context so no new Session is created.

nodes.label: AgentController.getDefaultMode()
nodes.rationale: Resolution order: defaultModeId match, then first mode with default/metadata.default true, then first configured mode; an unmatched defaultModeId throws.

nodes.label: AgentController.init()
nodes.rationale: Workspaces initialize lazily when used; repeated calls reuse the same initialization promise.

nodes.label: AgentController.initStorage()
nodes.rationale: Lets direct storage queries run without provisioning a workspace or starting the full controller runtime.

nodes.label: AgentController.listActiveThreadRuns()
nodes.rationale: Comes from in-process run tracking, so it covers only runs started by the current process and never creates or touches a session.

nodes.label: AgentController.listAvailableModels()
nodes.rationale: Results are cached briefly and sorted with usage data when modelUseCountProvider is configured.

nodes.label: AgentControllerOMConfig
nodes.rationale: Concrete defaultObserverModelId/defaultReflectorModelId act as fallbacks when automatic resolution returns no model or throws.

nodes.label: AgentController.onSessionCreated()
nodes.rationale: Blocking listeners let the host prepare session state before the caller can start a run; a blocking listener must not call createSession() for the same id or it deadlocks on its own hydration.

nodes.label: AgentController.queryThreads()
nodes.rationale: Reads stored threads without creating a Session or provisioning its workspace; forked subagent threads are excluded unless includeForkedSubagents is true.

nodes.label: AgentController.resolveWorkspace()
nodes.rationale: Sessions resolve their workspace at creation, dynamic factories included, so this returns that instance and only falls back to the factory for a session created without one.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.rationale: A workspace is optional; sessions without one still support threads, state and agent runs but have no workspace tools unless the mode's agent has its own workspace.

nodes.label: Session.getWorkspace()
nodes.rationale: Preserves session-level overrides and returns undefined when neither the session nor the controller configures a workspace; callers must check before use.

nodes.label: _background per-call override
nodes.rationale: The override only modifies tools already opted in, keeping deterministic foreground-only tools (calculators, lookups, schema validators) from being silently dispatched as tasks.

nodes.label: abort()
nodes.rationale: Pending signals survive an abort unless clearPendingSignals is true.

nodes.label: unsubscribe()
nodes.rationale: Closes the subscription without aborting so the run continues and can be resubscribed later.

nodes.label: Thread stream
nodes.rationale: Subscribe to the stream first, then send input whenever it becomes available, so the subscription is already open when the input starts a run.

nodes.label: SSE heartbeats
nodes.rationale: Periodic heartbeat frames keep browsers, proxies, and load balancers from closing idle connections; used together with client-side reconnect logic.

nodes.label: PubSub backend
nodes.rationale: Outcome recovery is bounded by the PubSub backend's retention, not by the history page size.

nodes.label: Prompt blocks
nodes.rationale: A shared saved instruction text lets one policy update propagate to every agent that references its published version instead of editing each agent.

nodes.label: Display Conditions
nodes.rationale: Conditions control whether a block is included based on request-context values; blocks without conditions are always included.

nodes.label: prompt_block_ref
nodes.rationale: Referenced blocks resolve at runtime; a missing or unpublished reference is omitted from final instructions.

nodes.label: Template Values
nodes.rationale: Templates resolve values from request context at runtime; unresolved placeholders without a fallback remain unchanged.
