nodes.label: listActiveWorkflowRuns()
nodes.rationale: Identifies active runs, which have a status of running or waiting.

nodes.label: restart()
nodes.rationale: Resumes execution from the last active step when a run loses connection to the server; refuses to take over a run whose storage lease has not expired.

nodes.label: restartAllActiveWorkflowRuns()
nodes.rationale: Restarts all active runs of a workflow concurrently up to recovery.workflowConcurrency (default 5) without manually looping through each run.

nodes.label: resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Returns a new ReadableStream to observe workflow events after a stream is closed or interrupted.

nodes.label: run.start()
nodes.rationale: Waits for all steps to complete before returning the final result.

nodes.label: run.stream()
nodes.rationale: Emits events during execution so you can monitor progress or trigger actions as steps complete.

nodes.label: AssistantChatTransport
nodes.rationale: Points the frontend at the standalone Mastra server's stream endpoint instead of the default local /api/chat route.

nodes.label: chatRoute
nodes.rationale: Makes all agents available in AI SDK-compatible formats, e.g. weatherAgent at /chat/weatherAgent.

nodes.label: Assistant UI
nodes.rationale: TypeScript/React chat library built on shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS for building enterprise-grade chat experiences quickly.

nodes.label: Standalone Mastra Server
nodes.rationale: Runs on http://localhost:4111 by default; the frontend connects to its API endpoints rather than embedding Mastra in Next.js routes.

nodes.label: Slack app manifest
nodes.rationale: Manifest-based app creation is the fastest path when adding the agent to your own workspace; it does not cover the platform OAuth flow where other workspaces install the agent.

nodes.label: Slack Connect shared channels
nodes.rationale: Adding the bot to a shared or external channel grants those participants access to the agent and its tools and data, so exposure must be confirmed first.

nodes.label: Server authentication exemption
nodes.rationale: Slack cannot send a bearer token, so Mastra registers the channel webhook as a public route and verifies each request with the Slack signing secret instead, keeping the rest of the API protected.

nodes.label: ElasticSearchStore
nodes.rationale: Shares connection configuration with ElasticSearchVector so a single cluster and client can serve both agent memory and semantic recall.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: On startup Mastra calls storage.init() and creates its tables and indexes in Neon.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: Setting disableInit: true prevents the runtime process from creating or changing the pgvector extension, tables and indexes; the direct unpooled connection is used for setup.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: Supports initialization through a transaction-pooled connection; disableInit lets schema be created during deployment with the direct connection while runtime uses the pooled connection.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres
nodes.rationale: Neon is a managed PostgreSQL service and does not require a separate Mastra storage package; Mastra connects to it through PostgresStore using the Node.js pg driver.

nodes.label: @mastra/redis
nodes.rationale: Use @mastra/redis for Redis deployments that use the official redis client; the packages are tested independently against their respective servers.

nodes.label: ValkeyStore
nodes.rationale: Use it when your deployment runs Valkey or needs GLIDE features such as native Valkey configuration and authentication.

nodes.label: MastraServer (Express adapter)
nodes.rationale: Exposes Mastra agents as HTTP endpoints without writing the routing yourself or running a separate Mastra server.

nodes.label: Browser Scope
nodes.rationale: 'shared' is cost-efficient for non-conflicting tasks; 'thread' provides full isolation for concurrent users.

nodes.label: EventEmitterPubSub
nodes.rationale: Default PubSub; only reaches runs in the same process, so multi-process abort requires a shared backend.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager
nodes.rationale: Not instantiated directly; accessed from a Mastra instance via mastra.datasets.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.deleteExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Deletes the experiment's observability traces first, then the experiment and its result records; unsupported observability storage leaves traces in place and logs a warning.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.getExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Works across all datasets without needing a dataset reference first, unlike dataset.getExperiment().

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.deleteExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Doesn't require the experiment to remain associated with a dataset, so it can delete orphaned experiments whose datasetId was cleared when the dataset was deleted. When organizationId or projectId is provided, deletion is scoped to those values and a tenancy mismatch is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: dataset.deleteExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Use dataset.deleteExperiment() when you have a Dataset instance; use mastra.datasets.deleteExperiment() to delete by experiment ID without a dataset reference, including experiments orphaned by dataset deletion. Trace deletion cascades to spans, metrics, logs, scores and feedback linked by trace ID; unsupported observability storage leaves traces in place and logs a warning.

nodes.label: dataset.finalizeExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Mastra computes final counts server-side from persisted result rows so the caller never tracks completion bookkeeping. Counts are per item (succeeded + failed + skipped === totalItems) even when items have multiple attempts. Finalization is idempotent, and an already-failed experiment is returned unchanged and stays failed.

nodes.label: Conditional Tool Sets
nodes.rationale: Matching variants are shallow-merged at runtime based on request-context values.

nodes.label: Tool Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Later records replace earlier records with the same ID; a collision replaces the complete earlier tool rather than merging fields.

nodes.label: Stored MCP Clients
nodes.rationale: @mastra/mcp is an optional peer dependency of @mastra/editor; install it before configuring stored MCP clients.

nodes.label: Editor Tool Configuration
nodes.rationale: Editor stores tool selections as part of an agent version, combining registered, MCP, integration, and tool-provider tools.

nodes.label: createBiasScorer()
nodes.rationale: Scores bias as (biased_opinions / total_opinions) * scale, with higher scores indicating more bias; opinions are extracted first so factual claims are excluded and cited opinions included.

nodes.label: filterRun()
nodes.rationale: Trims what a scorer sees but still produces a score, unlike notScorable which skips scoring entirely.

nodes.label: notScorable()
nodes.rationale: Declares the run has nothing for this scorer to evaluate; remaining steps are skipped so the judge is never called and averages, gates and thresholds only include runs the scorer actually evaluated.

nodes.label: NotScorable
nodes.rationale: Opaque value recognized by the scorer pipeline; must be returned directly from a step, not wrapped in another object.

nodes.label: Workflow.foreach()
nodes.rationale: If you need to run multiple operations per item, use a nested workflow as the step; this keeps all operations for each item together and is cleaner than chaining multiple .foreach() calls.

nodes.label: getStepResultAsync()
nodes.rationale: Replaces the deprecated getStepResult(), which returns the same value synchronously.

nodes.label: mapVariable()
nodes.rationale: Provides a declarative object syntax for .map() as an alternative to writing a mapping function, extracting fields from step outputs or workflow input.

nodes.label: Workflow.tool()
nodes.rationale: Unlike wrapping a tool with createStep(), .tool() records a declarative entry in the workflow graph, making the workflow portable: the same graph can be serialized and persisted as a dynamic workflow.

nodes.label: createWorkflowStateReader()
nodes.rationale: Creates a reader object with methods bound to one WorkflowState so callers can inspect suspended runs and resume labels without parsing raw workflow snapshots.

nodes.label: getWorkflowSuspendedStep()
nodes.rationale: When multiple steps are suspended, ordering follows the order stored in suspendedPaths.

nodes.label: Workflow class
nodes.rationale: autoRestartActiveRuns is set to false for durable agent workflows because their recovery is owned by the opt-in recovery.durableAgents: 'auto' path, and for workflows whose side effects must not be re-driven by a blanket restart.

nodes.label: workflow-step-progress event
nodes.rationale: Emitted after each foreach iteration completes so real-time progress can be tracked without waiting for the entire foreach to finish.

nodes.label: agentInstructions()
nodes.rationale: Types the export without changing it.

nodes.label: instructions.ts
nodes.rationale: Use instructions.ts when the prompt needs code, for example when it is built from shared constants or resolved per request.

nodes.label: skills/ directory
nodes.rationale: Conditional, large, or action-oriented guidance belongs in skills/ so the model uses it only when relevant.

nodes.label: tools/ directory
nodes.rationale: Conditional, large, or action-oriented guidance belongs in tools/ so the model uses it only when relevant.

nodes.label: instructions.md
nodes.rationale: Instructions are always in context, so keep them for stable behavior that applies to every request; move anything conditional, large, or action-oriented into tools/ or skills/, which the model uses only when relevant.

nodes.label: Input Processors (processors/input/)
nodes.rationale: Files under processors/input/ run before messages reach the model.

nodes.label: Output Processors (processors/output/)
nodes.rationale: Files under processors/output/ run after the model responds, useful for filtering or transforming responses before they are returned.

nodes.label: Processor Precedence Rules
nodes.rationale: Function-valued config processors cannot be statically merged, so discovered processors of that type are ignored with a warning.

nodes.label: File-Based Agent Processors
nodes.rationale: Use config.ts for processors that need to be created at runtime or shared across agents; use file-based processors for static, per-agent processors that should be reviewed alongside the agent.

nodes.label: Skill Formats (module, SKILL.md package, flat markdown)
nodes.norm_label: skill formats (module, skill.md package, flat markdown)

nodes.label: File-Based Agent Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills are reusable procedures or reference material the agent can load when relevant, instead of putting every detail into the always-on prompt. They are bundled at build time so the deployed agent does not read them from disk.

nodes.label: instructions.md
nodes.rationale: Always-on identity, tone, or rules that the model should see every turn.

nodes.label: SKILL.md Package Format
nodes.rationale: Packaged skills require description in SKILL.md frontmatter; write when to use the skill, not only what it contains.

nodes.label: tools/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Callable actions with inputs and outputs, including operations that perform side effects.

nodes.label: config.ts
nodes.rationale: On a key collision, config.tools wins and a warning is logged; if config.tools is a function, discovered tools are ignored because function-valued tools cannot be statically merged.

nodes.label: File-based agent tools directory
nodes.rationale: Nested directories are not discovered as tools, so related tools should be grouped with clear filename prefixes instead of subfolders.

nodes.label: SerializedMemoryConfig
nodes.rationale: A JSON-serializable subset of Memory configuration stored on an agent record; the runtime hydrates it back into a Memory instance by resolving vector and embedder IDs against the Mastra instance.

nodes.label: SerializedMemoryOptions
nodes.rationale: Omits non-serializable fields like working memory and threads so the config can be persisted as JSON.

nodes.label: createTestMessage()
nodes.rationale: Replaces createUIMessage() and creates MastraDBMessage objects with the nested content structure, aligning test utilities with the new message format.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Scorer input/output types use MastraDBMessage[] instead of UIMessage to align scorers with the database-persisted message format.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Renamed from MastraMessageV2 to better describe the database message format; now the default return format everywhere.

nodes.label: InputProcessor
nodes.rationale: Deprecated input-processor exports removed; replace InputProcessor with Processor which implements a processInput function.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Processors and scorers now use the database message format and its types instead of MastraMessageV2.

nodes.label: Processor interface
nodes.rationale: Unified Processor interface consolidates processor types; processors now require an id field instead of name to align with other Mastra entities such as scorers and agents.

nodes.label: input (voice)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from listenProvider.

nodes.label: output (voice)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from speakProvider.

nodes.label: Voice Configuration
nodes.rationale: Properties renamed to match each property's role in voice input and output.

nodes.label: Realtime voice
nodes.rationale: Mastra hands the audio loop to LiveKit for voice activity and semantic turn detection plus barge-in, while the agent generates each reply with its own model, tools, and memory.

nodes.label: Detection Handling Strategies (block, warn, filter, rewrite)
nodes.norm_label: detection handling strategies (block, warn, filter, rewrite)
nodes.rationale: 'rewrite' attempts to neutralize the injection while preserving legitimate user intent; 'block' rejects with error, 'warn' logs but allows through, 'filter' removes flagged messages.

nodes.label: CachingPubSub
nodes.rationale: Overrides the replay methods to replay cached events, supporting resuming a stream after a disconnect.

nodes.label: EventEmitterPubSub
nodes.rationale: Default in-process implementation used by most applications; retains nothing per topic so clearTopic is a no-op.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: Abstract base class defining the contract every pub/sub backend implements, so the rest of Mastra can publish and subscribe to events without knowing which transport is in use. Default supportedModes is ['pull'] so custom implementations keep today's behavior unless they opt in to push delivery.

nodes.label: RedisStreamsPubSub
nodes.rationale: Persists messages, so it overrides clearTopic and trimTopic to delete retained stream entries and consumer groups.

nodes.label: createDatasetSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Pure format utilities: they don't export from storage, import a dataset, allocate portable identities, or change Studio's JSON importer.

nodes.label: purgeItem
nodes.rationale: Permanent purge intentionally overrides historical immutability for erasure while preserving item identity and the dataset version timeline.

nodes.label: Datasets
nodes.rationale: Each mutation creates a new version, so you can reproduce past experiments exactly.

nodes.label: nack (redelivery behavior)
nodes.rationale: On nack the event is republished with an incremented deliveryAttempt and the original is acknowledged; once maxDeliveryAttempts is reached the event is dropped instead of redelivered.

nodes.label: ValkeyStreamsPubSub
nodes.rationale: Use it for Valkey deployments; use RedisStreamsPubSub for Redis deployments that use the official redis client. Both integrations implement the same Mastra behavior with independent tests against Valkey and Redis.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: Good for teams already using PostgreSQL who want to minimize infrastructure complexity.

nodes.label: createTool()
nodes.rationale: renderOnly exists for display-only tools: Mastra streams the call and returns { acknowledged: true } so the agent can keep generating without a client round trip, but the acknowledgement means the call was emitted, not that the browser rendered it, so it must not be used for client actions whose outcome matters to the agent.

nodes.label: ToolAnnotations (MCP)
nodes.rationale: Annotations follow the MCP specification and are passed through when tools are listed via MCP so clients can decide how to present and confirm tool calls.

nodes.label: StandardJSONSchemaV1
nodes.rationale: Schemas may be defined with any library supporting Standard JSON Schema (Zod, Valibot, ArkType) so tool definitions are not tied to one validation library.

nodes.label: createVectorQueryTool()
nodes.rationale: Most fields can be set at creation as defaults and overridden at runtime via request context or input, so one tool can serve multiple environments and tenants; id and description are creation-only.

nodes.label: QueryResult
nodes.rationale: document is only populated by stores whose query() returns document content, so callers should read chunk text from sources[i].metadata.text for other stores.

nodes.label: VectorStoreResolver
nodes.rationale: A resolver function receives the request context and returns the tenant's vector store, enabling schema or database isolation for multi-tenant applications.

nodes.label: session.mode.switch()
nodes.rationale: Modes change the instructions and tools used by the shared backing agent without replacing the Session or thread.

nodes.label: session.respondToToolSuspension()
nodes.rationale: Interactive tools use resumable tool suspensions rather than approval gates so the run can continue with user-supplied data.

nodes.label: submit_plan tool
nodes.rationale: Takes a plan file path rather than plan text so the agent writes the plan to a file and the app reads it for approval; it therefore needs a writable filesystem.

nodes.label: KNOWLEDGE_ROUTES
nodes.rationale: The Knowledge routes are off by default and must be registered explicitly, because without auth they expose the whole instance to anyone who can reach the server.

nodes.label: Knowledge route access control
nodes.rationale: An authorize function replaces the server's rules and role checks for every route, so apps must keep their existing decision for other paths rather than returning true for everything.

nodes.label: onIterationComplete
nodes.rationale: Called after each parent loop iteration to monitor execution, inject feedback, or stop early.

nodes.label: Rubric scorer
nodes.rationale: An LLM-as-judge scorer that reviews output against a checklist each iteration; most effective for tasks with clear, verifiable success criteria.

nodes.label: Task completion scoring
nodes.rationale: Scorers validate whether the task is complete after each iteration; failed scorer feedback enters the conversation so the parent keeps iterating.

nodes.label: Subagent versioning
nodes.rationale: Version overrides set on the Mastra instance or per invocation propagate automatically through delegation.

nodes.label: Code Source
nodes.rationale: Active agent overrides are serialized as deterministic JSON under <codePath>/agents/<encodedAgentId>.json; Git versions are read-only in Studio.

nodes.label: Database Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The resource record stores activeVersionId while individual snapshots don't store a lifecycle status.

nodes.label: Editor Versioning
nodes.rationale: Database-backed resources use draft and publish operations; code-backed agent overrides use deterministic files and Git history.

nodes.label: createTrajectoryAccuracyScorerCode()
nodes.rationale: Deterministic, reproducible, fast and cost-free (no LLM calls); suited to known expected trajectories, exact step sequences, and CI/CD automated tests.

nodes.label: createTrajectoryAccuracyScorerLLM()
nodes.rationale: Used when the optimal trajectory isn't predetermined and semantic understanding, missing/redundant step detection, and explanations are needed; score weighted 60% necessity, 30% ordering, minus 10% missing penalty.

nodes.label: createTrajectoryScorerCode() (unified scorer)
nodes.rationale: Multi-dimensional single-pass evaluation; default weights accuracy 0.4, efficiency 0.3, tool failures 0.2, blacklist 0.1, normalized over active dimensions; blacklist violations override everything to 0.0; nested evaluations weighted 70% top-level / 30% nested average.

nodes.label: ExpectedStep
nodes.rationale: Mirrors TrajectoryStep so specifying stepType gives autocomplete, but all variant-specific fields are optional so you only assert against what you care about; omitting stepType matches any step by name only.

nodes.label: extractTrajectory()
nodes.rationale: Fallback used when storage isn't available; produces a flat list of tool calls and does not capture nested execution or non-tool-call spans.

nodes.label: extractTrajectoryFromTrace()
nodes.rationale: Preferred extraction strategy: produces a hierarchical trajectory with nested children capturing the complete execution tree, including nested agent runs, tool calls within workflow steps, and model generations.

nodes.label: extractWorkflowTrajectory()
nodes.rationale: Fallback used when storage isn't available; produces a flat list of workflow steps and does not capture nested execution or non-tool-call spans.

nodes.label: runEvals
nodes.rationale: Pipeline automatically extracts trajectories so scorers receive a Trajectory object directly; trajectory scorers are configured under the `trajectory` key.

nodes.label: TrajectoryExpectation
nodes.rationale: Nested expectation config lets each level of the hierarchy set its own ordering or comparison rules, overriding the parent config for that step's children.

nodes.label: Observability Storage
nodes.rationale: When configured on the target's Mastra instance, the full execution trace is fetched from the observability store, enabling hierarchical trace-based extraction instead of flat fallbacks.

nodes.label: Ordering Modes (strict, relaxed, unordered)
nodes.rationale: Strict requires an exact match for 1.0 with penalties for extra steps; relaxed (default) allows extra steps but requires correct relative order; unordered only checks presence and does not penalize extras.

nodes.label: createStep()
nodes.rationale: Steps are the building blocks of workflows; inputSchema and outputSchema define accepted and returned data using Standard JSON Schema.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Accesses request-specific values so step behavior can be conditionally adjusted based on the context of the request.

nodes.label: Workflow State
nodes.rationale: Lets you share values across steps without passing them through every step's inputSchema and outputSchema, for tracking progress, accumulating results, or sharing configuration.

nodes.label: Discord Webhook Route
nodes.rationale: Mastra generates the Discord webhook route from the agent ID and adapter key, so the interactions endpoint URL is derived rather than configured by hand.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: When storage is passed to the Mastra class, init() is called automatically before any storage operation.

nodes.label: MongoDBStore
nodes.rationale: disableInit is useful for CI/CD pipelines where migrations are run explicitly; skipDefaultIndexes is useful when indexes are managed separately or only custom indexes are used.

nodes.label: Arthur Task Routing
nodes.rationale: Traces are routed to tasks either by serviceName (Arthur Engine auto-creates a matching task) or by an explicit taskId; when both are provided, taskId takes precedence so callers can override automatic routing.

nodes.label: AcpAgent
nodes.rationale: persistSession defaults to true so the ACP process and session stay alive across generate(), stream(), getAvailableModels() and setModel() calls; set it to false when each prompt should run in a fresh ACP process.

nodes.label: getScorerById()
nodes.rationale: Searches by the scorer's id property with name as a fallback, useful when the registration key is unknown.

nodes.label: dataset.purgeItem()
nodes.rationale: Permanent purge intentionally overrides SCD-2 historical immutability for erasure while preserving item identity and the dataset version timeline; it doesn't create a new dataset version. Use deleteItem() instead when you only need to remove an item from the current dataset version. externalId remains unchanged because Mastra uses it as an identity key, so sensitive data must not be stored there.

nodes.label: dataset.runExperimentItem()
nodes.rationale: Built for caller-driven loops where a durable orchestrator (e.g. a Temporal workflow) fans out one call per item and owns retries and timeouts; each call executes the item exactly once with no internal retry loop, and a retried call converges on the same (experimentId, itemId, attempt) row. Scorers resolve with the same precedence as native runs: experiment scorers win over item scorerIds, which win over dataset scorerIds.

nodes.label: dataset.startExperiment()
nodes.rationale: agentModel lets you compare models without changing the agent: the model is passed with each call the experiment makes, so the registered agent and other experiments are unaffected, and the experiment's metadata and each run's trace metadata record it as agentModel. When scorers is provided (even as [] or an empty categorized config) it overrides item-level and dataset-level scorer IDs for every item; when omitted, item scorerIds are used then dataset scorer IDs, and sources aren't merged.

nodes.label: abortSignal
nodes.rationale: Moved to the top level of stream/generate options because execution control sits outside model-specific settings.

nodes.label: Agent id
nodes.rationale: Now required; used by mastra.getAgentById() and must be unique within a Mastra instance.

nodes.label: agent.voice
nodes.rationale: Groups the voice APIs together in a namespace.

nodes.label: @mastra/codemod
nodes.rationale: Automates the v1 API renames.

nodes.label: format parameter
nodes.rationale: Removed to improve tree-shaking by moving AI SDK-specific code to a dedicated package.

nodes.label: agent.getDefaultGenerateOptionsLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Method name now indicates which AI SDK version it targets (legacy = AI SDK v4).

nodes.label: mastra.listAgents()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getAgents to align with the convention that plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: agent.listInputProcessors()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from get* to list* to align with the convention that list* methods return collections.

nodes.label: agent.listOutputProcessors()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from get* to list* to align with the convention that list* methods return collections.

nodes.label: memory option
nodes.rationale: Provides a cleaner API for memory configuration, replacing top-level threadId and resourceId options.

nodes.label: prepareStep
nodes.rationale: Now receives MastraDBMessage format to unify with the processInputStep processor method.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: New name identifies the class as request-specific data and matches web framework conventions.

nodes.label: structuredOutput.schema
nodes.rationale: Consolidates on a single, stable API for structured output, replacing output and experimental_output.

nodes.label: TMetrics
nodes.rationale: Removed because metrics/scorers are now configured using the scorers API instead of the Agent type system.

nodes.label: toAISdkStream()
nodes.rationale: Replacement for the removed format parameter for AI SDK format conversion.

nodes.label: agent.toStep()
nodes.rationale: Removed because agents can now be added directly to workflow steps.

nodes.label: tripwire
nodes.rationale: Changed from separate tripwire and tripwireReason fields to a single object containing reason, retry, metadata, and processorId.

nodes.label: Zod
nodes.rationale: Both Zod v3 and v4 schemas remain supported in public agent APIs.

nodes.label: createClassifierScorer()
nodes.rationale: Adapts one constructor-configured Classifier question to the scorer pipeline without aggregating questions, applying boolean thresholds, inferring choice ordering, or calling a second judge model; the question option selects which answer becomes the score but does not limit which questions are sent to the model.

nodes.label: ScorerRunError
nodes.rationale: Run-time failures reject scorer.run() with failedStep set to 'analyze' and the original error preserved as cause, so classifier failures are attributable to the analyze step.

nodes.label: createKeywordCoverageScorer
nodes.rationale: Analyzes keyword presence while ignoring common words and stop words, with case-insensitive matching and word-form variation handling, so coverage reflects useful keywords rather than filler.

nodes.label: src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Code-registered storage wins over storage.ts; use code registration when setup depends on runtime wiring.

nodes.label: storage.ts
nodes.rationale: Mastra registers the store before file-based agents and workflows, so storage-dependent primitives bind to this store instead of the default in-memory store.

nodes.label: src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Code-registered Studio config wins over studio.ts; use code registration when auth depends on runtime wiring.

nodes.label: studio.ts
nodes.rationale: Studio opens without authentication in local development; add studio.ts when securing a shared or production deployment.

nodes.label: researcher subagent
nodes.rationale: A subagent's description is routing text for the parent model; the parent reads it when deciding whether to delegate.

nodes.label: new Mastra()
nodes.rationale: On a key collision, the code-registered workflow wins over the file-based workflow.

nodes.label: data-om-activation marker
nodes.rationale: Activation is an instant operation: no LLM call is involved, because buffered content was already computed in the background.

nodes.label: @mastra/core/processors
nodes.rationale: The @mastra/memory/processors import path was removed in favor of a single consolidated location.

nodes.label: TokenLimiter
nodes.rationale: Processors are configured at the Agent level where processor behavior is scoped to agent execution; TokenLimiter limits historical messages to fit the context window.

nodes.label: @mastra/core/processors
nodes.rationale: Consolidates all processor exports in a single location, replacing @mastra/memory/processors and the deprecated input-processors path.

nodes.label: @mastra/memory/processors
nodes.rationale: Removed so that all processors are exported from @mastra/core/processors.

nodes.label: SensitiveDataFilter
nodes.rationale: Auto-applied to every configured instance by default (sensitiveDataFilter defaults to true); not duplicated if a config already includes one in spanOutputProcessors, and pre-instantiated instances are not modified.

nodes.label: CyberRefusalHandler
nodes.rationale: Cybersecurity safeguards can refuse ordinary coding work partway through a long agent run; many refusals are false positives and asking the model to continue usually gets past them, so the step is retried once and a second refusal stands.

nodes.label: Agent class
nodes.rationale: The Agent class is the foundation for creating AI agents in Mastra; it provides methods for generating responses and streaming interactions and also handles voice capabilities.

nodes.label: cancelQueuedMessages(options)
nodes.rationale: Cancels pending input without aborting the active run.

nodes.label: queueMessage(message, options)
nodes.rationale: Queues a user message for the next turn: if the thread is active Mastra waits for the active run to finish, otherwise it starts a run immediately.

nodes.label: queueSignal(signal, options)
nodes.rationale: Behaves like queueMessage but accepts any signal input and preserves its type, tagName, and attributes for the queued run.

nodes.label: SendAgentSignalAccepted
nodes.rationale: Resolves at decision-time with action wake/deliver/persist/discard; it resolves for routing and rejects only when the message or signal could not be routed or started at all.

nodes.label: sendMessage(message, options)
nodes.rationale: Message APIs are for user-authored input; sendMessage delivers a user message into an active run or memory thread immediately.

nodes.label: sendSignal(signal, options)
nodes.rationale: sendSignal is the lower-level API for system-generated context, while message APIs are for user-authored input.

nodes.label: subscribeThreadEvents({ resourceId, threadId }, listener)
nodes.rationale: Used to observe locally pending messages on the shared thread; the listener currently receives only queue-count-changed events.

nodes.label: ifActive / ifIdle delivery behaviors
nodes.rationale: Controls what happens to a message or signal depending on whether the target thread is active (deliver/persist/discard, default deliver) or idle (wake/persist/discard, default wake).

nodes.label: Agent instructions
nodes.rationale: Instructions may be a string, a system message object, or an array of system messages, allowing mixed and dynamically composed prompts.

nodes.label: Model strings (provider/model)
nodes.rationale: Passing model as a provider/model string is the simplest setup: Mastra reads matching provider credentials from the environment, so no provider package or import is required.

nodes.label: providerOptions
nodes.rationale: Set on the instruction level to configure a different caching strategy per system instruction/prompt, plus reasoning configuration.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: For signalIds cancellation, Mastra publishes all requested IDs through PubSub so other processes subscribed to the thread cancel matching pending input; propagation is best-effort and asynchronous.

nodes.label: queueOwnerId
nodes.rationale: The owner ID is local metadata: it is neither serialized with the message nor an authorization mechanism; it groups local queued messages for observation and cancellation.

nodes.label: Thread signals
nodes.rationale: Agent signals send real-time input and context into a memory thread; message APIs are for user-authored input while sendSignal is the lower-level API for system-generated context.

nodes.label: Transient signals
nodes.rationale: Set transient: true to deliver the signal to the current model request without storing it; transient signals are never stored, state signals cannot be transient, and combining transient with a persist behavior discards the signal.

nodes.label: processToolResult
nodes.rationale: Symmetric with processOutputStep, which fires before tool execution; this fires after a tool returns and before the raw result is persisted or fed to the next LLM call, so security policies can be enforced on tool output.

nodes.label: MessageList.updateToolInvocation
nodes.rationale: Mutating the message list in place lets the runtime re-read the post-processor result and overwrite the downstream tool-result stream chunk, so streaming clients see the processed value.

nodes.label: SkillSearchProcessor
nodes.rationale: Gives the agent search_skills and load_skill meta-tools instead of injecting all skill metadata upfront, reducing context token usage when workspaces have many skills.

nodes.label: SkillsProcessor
nodes.rationale: Eager alternative that injects all skills upfront; best for few skills (< 10).

nodes.label: UnixSocketPubSub
nodes.rationale: Delivers events across processes on a single host over a Unix domain socket by electing one process as broker with automatic re-election if the broker exits; it is a push transport, so Mastra doesn't run a pull worker for it.

nodes.label: autoEmbed
nodes.rationale: MongoDB can generate embeddings itself with a Voyage AI model, so no embedding provider is needed in the application.

nodes.label: hybridQuery()
nodes.rationale: Combines vector similarity with BM25 full-text search server-side via $rankFusion to blend semantic and keyword retrieval.

nodes.label: MongoDBVector
nodes.rationale: Good for teams consolidating vector search, full-text search, and operational data in one database to minimize infrastructure complexity.

nodes.label: BedrockKBResult
nodes.rationale: Standard retrieval includes source and score when Bedrock provides them; agentic retrieval may omit those fields, so both are optional.

nodes.label: createBedrockKBTool()
nodes.rationale: Agentic retrieval is enabled by default because it decomposes complex queries, retrieves across multiple passes and applies managed reranking; it automatically falls back to standard managed retrieval when agentic retrieval fails (e.g. older SDK, permissions).

nodes.label: listTools()
nodes.rationale: Used for static tool configuration where a single connection to the MCP server serves the entire app.

nodes.label: listToolsets()
nodes.rationale: Used when a new MCP connection is needed per user; toolsets are passed to stream() or generate() instead of being bound at agent construction.

nodes.label: Server instructions
nodes.rationale: Forwarding server instructions into an agent's system prompt is opt-in because a malicious or compromised server could inject instructions treated as trusted system guidance.

nodes.label: Tool namespacing
nodes.rationale: Tool names are namespaced by server name (serverName_toolName) to prevent conflicts.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: CompositeVoice delegates speak() to the configured output provider, which may be a Mastra provider or an AI SDK speech model.

nodes.label: voice.speak()
nodes.rationale: Realtime providers emit a 'speaking' event with audio data instead of returning a stream, so callers must register a listener to receive audio chunks.

nodes.label: Sandbox tools
nodes.rationale: Added when a sandbox is configured; with a static sandbox, capability checks decide which tool variants are exposed, while with a runtime-defined sandbox all tools are registered and the runtime throws if a capability is missing.

nodes.label: ToolConfigWithArgsContext
nodes.rationale: Execution-time policies need the tool's args in addition to requestContext and workspace.

nodes.label: Read-before-write tracking
nodes.rationale: Read records live in the threadState storage domain so they survive suspend/resume, later turns and serverless restarts; a successful write clears the record so the next edit requires a fresh read.

nodes.label: Workspace tool hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks run after name remapping and inside the agent hook wrapper: agent beforeToolCall → workspace beforeToolCall → tool → workspace afterToolCall → agent afterToolCall.

nodes.label: BatchPartsProcessor
nodes.rationale: Combines multiple stream parts before emitting them to the client, reducing network overhead and the number of LLM classification calls made by heavier output guardrails.

nodes.label: LanguageDetector
nodes.rationale: Detects and translates user messages into a target language to enable multilingual support.

nodes.label: ModerationProcessor
nodes.rationale: Detects inappropriate or harmful content across categories like hate, harassment, and violence and can block or rewrite it.

nodes.label: PIIDetector
nodes.rationale: Detects and removes personally identifiable information such as emails, phone numbers, and credit cards.

nodes.label: PromptInjectionDetector
nodes.rationale: Scans user messages for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and system override patterns using an LLM classifier so risky input can be blocked or rewritten before reaching the model.

nodes.label: SystemPromptScrubber
nodes.rationale: Detects and redacts system prompts or internal instructions from model responses to prevent unintended disclosure of prompt content or configuration details.

nodes.label: TokenCostControl
nodes.rationale: Monitors cumulative estimated cost across the agentic loop and blocks or warns when a monetary limit is exceeded; cost checks are approximate because metrics are persisted asynchronously, so fast-running agents may briefly exceed the limit.

nodes.label: UnicodeNormalizer
nodes.rationale: Cleans and normalizes user input by unifying Unicode characters, standardizing whitespace, and removing problematic symbols.

nodes.label: maxProcessorRetries
nodes.rationale: Set maxProcessorRetries explicitly when a specific limit is needed; otherwise a default error-retry budget applies when error processors are configured.

nodes.label: processAPIError
nodes.rationale: An error processor may change the request or messages and request another provider attempt.

nodes.label: onViolation Callback
nodes.rationale: Fires when a policy violation aborts the run so side effects like alerting, external logging, or notifications can be performed; errors thrown by runner-invoked callbacks after abort() are silently caught to avoid interfering with the processor's main logic.

nodes.label: Processor Strategies
nodes.rationale: Most strategies allow the request to continue; the block strategy calls abort() to stop the request immediately and prevent subsequent processors from running.

nodes.label: Tripwire
nodes.rationale: Signals that a processor aborted the request; surfaced as a tripwire field on generate() results and as tripwire chunks in stream().

nodes.label: Workflow Processor
nodes.rationale: Guardrails that only block and never mutate messages are independent and can run in parallel via a workflow processor to reduce latency.

nodes.label: Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Built-in processors add security and safety controls that detect, transform, or block harmful content before it reaches the language model or the user.

nodes.label: Stream Data Redaction
nodes.rationale: When streaming responses over HTTP, Mastra redacts sensitive request data (system prompts, tool definitions, API keys) from stream chunks at the server level by default.

nodes.label: Splat Route (src/routes/api/$.ts)
nodes.rationale: Catch-all route passes all supported HTTP methods to the adapter; prefix option defaults to /api and must match the splat route's mount path.

nodes.label: session.displayState.restoreTasks(tasks)
nodes.rationale: Pure snapshot update that emits no event, so the UI must re-render explicitly after calling it.

nodes.label: AgentControllerDisplayState
nodes.rationale: Canonical snapshot a UI renders from, kept in sync with every session event by a reducer.

nodes.label: display_state_changed event
nodes.rationale: Emitted after every event with the latest snapshot so UIs can subscribe instead of polling.

nodes.label: Agent.getSkill()
nodes.rationale: Searches the merged set of agent-level and workspace skills, with agent-level skills taking precedence on name conflicts.

nodes.label: Agent.listSkills()
nodes.rationale: Returns the merged set of agent-level and workspace skills; agent-level skills take precedence on name conflicts.

nodes.label: withMastra()
nodes.rationale: Wraps an AI SDK model with Mastra processors and/or memory so plain AI SDK calls gain Mastra processing and persistence.

nodes.label: Mastra.addGateway()
nodes.rationale: If a gateway with the same key already exists the addition is skipped; in development mode (MASTRA_DEV=true) type generation for custom gateways is triggered automatically.

nodes.label: Mastra.getToolById()
nodes.rationale: Searches the Mastra-level registry for a matching intrinsic id first, then falls back to treating the value as a registration key.

nodes.label: beforeToolCall Hook
nodes.rationale: Used to verify that an approval fingerprint matches the tool name and input before allowing execution.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Used to estimate whether a tool call needs human review based on tool name and arguments; a refused question has no probability so it falls back to requiring approval.

nodes.label: declineToolCall
nodes.rationale: Accepts an optional reason that is returned to the model in place of the tool result so the model can adjust instead of retrying blindly, and is stored on the tool call's approval metadata.

nodes.label: delegatedToolCallId
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes two pauses from the same delegation, such as a question followed by an approval.

nodes.label: listSuspendedRuns()
nodes.rationale: Rediscover pending runs from storage so approvals survive page refreshes, server restarts, or a different server instance behind a load balancer.

nodes.label: requireApproval
nodes.rationale: Set on a createTool() definition to pause calls to that specific tool; a tool-level requireApproval function is authoritative and replaces the combined agent/tool result for that tool.

nodes.label: requireToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Set on stream()/generate() options to pause every tool call for that request; accepts a function for per-call decisions, but durable and stored agents accept only a boolean because functions can't be serialized.

nodes.label: sendToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Falls back to storage-backed discovery when memory contains no active run for the thread.

nodes.label: Action Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Binds approval to the exact tool name and arguments shown to the reviewer so the tool doesn't run under an old approval if arguments drift; in production the fingerprint should be a stable hash stored in durable storage scoped to user, run, tool call, and policy version.

nodes.label: Pre-execution Approval
nodes.rationale: Pauses a tool call before its execute function runs; the LLM still decides which tool to call and provides arguments, but execute doesn't run until explicitly approved.

nodes.label: Runtime Suspension
nodes.rationale: A tool pauses during execute() to request additional user input or confirmation before it can finish.

nodes.label: Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Minimal resume artifacts holding only what's needed to resume a suspended run and deleted once the run finishes; tracing is used for the execution record and memory for conversation history.

nodes.label: Supervisor agent
nodes.rationale: Coordinates subagents via .stream()/.generate(); approval and suspension requests bubble up through the delegation chain to the supervisor level.

nodes.label: tool-call-approval Chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitted in the stream when a tool call pauses for pre-execution approval; contains toolCallId, toolName, and args so approval can be bound to the exact reviewed arguments.

nodes.label: tool-call-resumed Chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitted with the same toolCallId before the tool-result when a suspended or approval-gated call resumes; use this signal to mark a question as answered rather than inferring it from the tool output shape, since a sub-agent delegation's output is the sub-agent's result.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop
nodes.rationale: Lets a tool call be suspended before it executes so a human can approve or decline it, or let tools suspend themselves to request additional context from the user; used for destructive, cost-heavy, or conditionally confirmed operations.

nodes.label: Storage Provider
nodes.rationale: Must be configured on the Mastra instance or human-in-the-loop fails with a "snapshot not found" error.

nodes.label: Scorer
nodes.rationale: Registration also makes a scorer resolvable by ID, which is required to persist its scores.

nodes.label: dataset.addItem()
nodes.rationale: scorerIds overrides dataset-attached scorers per item: an empty array runs no scorers, while omitting the field inherits the dataset scorer IDs.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.compareExperiments()
nodes.rationale: Duplicate experiment IDs are removed before the 2-ID minimum is checked, and an unknown baselineId now throws instead of being silently ignored, to make comparisons deterministic.

nodes.label: dataset.createExperiment()
nodes.rationale: The experiment pins the dataset version at creation time so submissions are validated against a stable set of items even if the dataset changes afterwards; a caller-supplied id makes creation idempotent for retried workflow activities.

nodes.label: dataset.updateExperiment()
nodes.rationale: Only name, description, and metadata are editable; status and result counters are managed by the experiment lifecycle and cannot be changed here.

nodes.label: dataset.updateItem()
nodes.rationale: Only provided fields are updated and updating an item creates a new version; scorerIds uses [] to run no scorers, null to remove the override and restore dataset inheritance, or omission to preserve the current value.

nodes.label: createAnswerRelevancyScorer
nodes.rationale: Evaluates relevancy through query-answer alignment, considering completeness and detail level, but not factual correctness.

nodes.label: createAnswerSimilarityScorer
nodes.rationale: Designed for CI/CD testing scenarios where expected answers exist and consistency over time must be ensured.

nodes.label: src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Code-registered observability wins over observability.ts.

nodes.label: observability.ts
nodes.rationale: Use observability.ts when one project-wide configuration is enough; use code registration when setup depends on runtime wiring in src/mastra/index.ts.

nodes.label: Scorer Sampling
nodes.rationale: Controls how often a scorer runs by default-exporting a { scorer, sampling } entry instead of a bare scorer.

nodes.label: Memory.settled()
nodes.rationale: Await before closing a storage connection you own; without it background statements can run against a closed connection. A scoped call can return while other threads still use the store, so call it unscoped before closing shared storage.

nodes.label: autoModels
nodes.rationale: Overrides the model automatic selection picks for a given provider.

nodes.label: blockAfter
nodes.rationale: Thresholds are activation thresholds rather than hard caps; at blockAfter (default 1.2) a synchronous observation runs if no buffered chunk activates.

nodes.label: bufferActivation
nodes.rationale: Determines how much recent history is retained when buffered observations activate (default 0.8 retains 20% of the threshold).

nodes.label: bufferTokens
nodes.rationale: Controls how often the Observer buffers observations in the background (default 0.2, roughly every 6k tokens) so a ready chunk can activate without blocking the agent.

nodes.label: resolveAutoModelId
nodes.rationale: Useful for showing the effective auto-selected model in a settings UI.

nodes.label: resolveModel
nodes.rationale: Creates the auto-picked model with your own credentials or routing.

nodes.label: skillResultRedactor()
nodes.rationale: Replaces skill tool results with a placeholder so the Observer does not re-observe full skill instructions or file contents every time a skill is used.

nodes.label: tokenx
nodes.rationale: Fast local token estimation used for thresholding work, with provider-aware heuristics for image parts.

nodes.label: Caller-supplied token estimates for file parts
nodes.norm_label: caller-supplied token estimates for file parts

nodes.label: Context Rot
nodes.rationale: The more raw message history an agent carries, the worse it performs; OM addresses this by compressing old context into dense observations.

nodes.label: Observational Memory (OM)
nodes.rationale: OM compresses old context into dense observations to solve context rot and context waste, and keeps a stable, append-only prompt prefix so it stays cacheable and cheaper.

nodes.label: Resource scope (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated because shared observations across all threads invalidate prompt caches for every thread, mix context between conversations, and process unobserved messages across all threads together, which is slow.

nodes.label: retainFullInput
nodes.rationale: Disables client-echoed history filtering when request input must be processed exactly as sent; history still loads underneath.

nodes.label: Thread scope
nodes.rationale: Requires a valid threadId, which prevents multiple threads from silently sharing a single observation record and causing database deadlocks; also well tested for long-horizon agentic use.

nodes.label: AgentNetwork
nodes.rationale: Replaced by Agent plus agent.network() as of @mastra/core v0.20.0.

nodes.label: Memory class
nodes.rationale: Memory is now required for the agent network to function properly.

nodes.label: NewAgentNetwork
nodes.rationale: Replaced by Agent plus agent.network() as of @mastra/core v0.20.0.

nodes.label: sendEvent
nodes.rationale: Removed; use the suspend/resume API instead.

nodes.label: setState
nodes.rationale: Now async and validates data against the step's stateSchema when validateInputs is enabled.

nodes.label: waitForEvent
nodes.rationale: Removed; use the suspend/resume API instead.

nodes.label: suspendPayload Validation
nodes.rationale: suspendPayload is now validated against suspendSchema when validateInputs is enabled.

nodes.label: validateInputs
nodes.rationale: Default flipped to true so workflow inputs are validated by default.

nodes.label: BatchDeleteTracesArgs
nodes.rationale: Scoped deletion (organizationId/resourceId) is only supported by ClickHouse vNext, PostgreSQL vNext, DuckDB and the in-memory store; other adapters throw OBSERVABILITY_STORAGE_BATCH_DELETE_TRACES_SCOPE_NOT_SUPPORTED rather than applying an unscoped delete. Capped at 1,000 trace IDs per call.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorage.batchDeleteTraces()
nodes.rationale: Deletes matching traces and spans then cascades to metrics, logs, scores and feedback linked by trace ID; signals without a trace ID are preserved. On ClickHouse vNext it records the deletion predicate and waits for lightweight delete masks before resolving; Mastra OSS has no background reconciler, so failed requests stay unapplied and must be retried.

nodes.label: GoogleCloudPubSub
nodes.rationale: Backed by Google Cloud Pub/Sub to deliver events across processes and hosts with ordered delivery and message acknowledgment; intended for distributed deployments on Google Cloud.

nodes.label: createGraphRAGTool()
nodes.rationale: GraphRAG is used when information is spread across multiple documents, documents reference each other, or relationships between concepts matter and simple vector similarity misses contextual relationships.

nodes.label: createVectorQueryTool()
nodes.rationale: Combining vector and graph tools gives the agent flexibility to choose the appropriate retrieval method per query.

nodes.label: graphOptions
nodes.rationale: threshold controls graph density: higher values create sparser graphs with stronger connections, lower values create denser graphs with more potential relationships; dimension must match the embedding model output dimension.

nodes.label: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
nodes.rationale: RAG incorporates relevant context from your own data sources to improve accuracy and ground LLM responses in real information.

nodes.label: background-task-cancelled chunk
nodes.rationale: Triggers a continuation turn when consumed by Agent.streamUntilIdle().

nodes.label: background-task-completed chunk
nodes.rationale: Triggers a continuation turn when consumed by Agent.streamUntilIdle().

nodes.label: background-task-failed chunk
nodes.rationale: Triggers a continuation turn when consumed by Agent.streamUntilIdle().

nodes.label: background-task-suspended chunk
nodes.rationale: When consumed by streamUntilIdle() the task is dropped from the wait set without queuing a continuation, so the agent's response ends and the resumed task's completion injects into the next user turn.

nodes.label: thread-history chunk
nodes.rationale: Arrives only when subscribeToThread() is called with withInitialHistory: true; still emitted with an empty messages array and hasMore false when there is no memory or no stored messages.

nodes.label: thread-run-status chunk
nodes.rationale: Reports a run's outcome independently of stored-message replay; emitted only when subscribeToThread() receives withRunStatus: true (defaults to false).

nodes.label: fastembed
nodes.rationale: Local embedding model; embeds at most 512 tokens per input, so long documents should be chunked (e.g. maxSize 1500) to fit the window.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Default storage db if omitted.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector
nodes.rationale: Default vector db if omitted.

nodes.label: ModelRouterEmbeddingModel
nodes.rationale: Recommended embedder path: provider/model strings with autocomplete and automatic API key detection from environment variables.

nodes.label: recall()
nodes.rationale: Adds semantic search on top of listMessages: use it when messages must be found by meaning rather than recency, via vectorSearchString.

nodes.label: store.deleteVectors()
nodes.rationale: Used to clean up stale vectors after a document is deleted or updated, or when re-indexing a document.

nodes.label: upsert()
nodes.rationale: The upsert method handles batching automatically, so batch operations are recommended for large insertions.

nodes.label: MongoDB Automated Embedding
nodes.rationale: Server-side embeddings keep the embedding provider out of the application: the database embeds each message on write and the search string on arrival, so model choice and vector size belong to the index. Newly written messages are embedded in the background, so a just-saved message may not be immediately recallable.

nodes.label: Embedder
nodes.rationale: Memory uses a single embedder for both storing and recalling messages, so one model must be chosen and used consistently.

nodes.label: embeddingDimension
nodes.rationale: Setting the dimension explicitly skips the probe embedding, so startup makes no embedding call and does not depend on the embedding provider being reachable; the index name is unchanged so existing indexes keep working.

nodes.label: HNSW Vector Index
nodes.rationale: HNSW typically performs better than the default IVFFlat, especially with OpenAI embeddings using inner product distance; PgVector uses the vector index for thread/resource-filtered searches only with HNSW on pgvector 0.8.0 or newer, while IVFFlat compares the query against every message in the thread or resource.

nodes.label: Metadata Filter
nodes.rationale: Filters match metadata stored on message embeddings when messages are saved; if thread metadata changes later, existing embeddings keep their previous metadata until re-saved or re-indexed.

nodes.label: Semantic Recall
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default because each call adds latency: new messages are embedded and used to query a vector database before the LLM receives them. Matching on meaning is used because users often remember the idea behind something rather than the exact words, so keyword search misses connections.

nodes.label: Vector Store Metadata
nodes.rationale: Metadata is stored with no fixed schema, so consistent field naming is required to avoid unexpected query results; without metadata there would be only numerical embeddings with no way to return the original text or filter results.

nodes.label: Cached tool definitions
nodes.rationale: Plain serializable definitions contain no functions or live client references, so they can be passed through JSON.stringify and cached in Redis or a database.

nodes.label: Per-server discovery errors
nodes.rationale: Per-server errors let callers distinguish slow servers from broken ones and retry only timed-out servers.

nodes.label: submitPlanTool
nodes.rationale: The agent writes the plan to a markdown file and passes only the path, so the host reads and presents the plan and the run suspends until the user approves or rejects it.

nodes.label: speaker option
nodes.rationale: Speaker selection provides voice diversity, quality, voice personality and multilingual support across providers.

nodes.label: speechModel configuration
nodes.rationale: All speechModel parameters are optional; provider defaults are used when omitted, so configuration can be simplified to a bare constructor call.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: CompositeVoice delegates on() to the configured real-time provider.

nodes.label: voice.on()
nodes.rationale: Event listeners should be registered before calling methods that might emit events; on providers without event support the method logs a debug message and does nothing.

nodes.label: Run.timeTravel()
nodes.rationale: Use it to debug failed workflows and test individual steps with different inputs; it can also recover from errors without re-running the entire workflow. Time travel requires storage to be configured since it relies on persisted workflow snapshots.

nodes.label: beforeToolCall
nodes.rationale: Returning { proceed: false, output } skips the tool call entirely and the agent receives output as the tool result, enabling policy-based blocking.

nodes.label: MastraJwtAuth
nodes.rationale: Lightweight authentication using JWTs verified against a shared secret.

nodes.label: deleteFile Tool
nodes.rationale: requireApproval: true makes the tool render as an interactive card and only execute after approval.

nodes.label: Channel Tool Approval
nodes.rationale: By default only the user who requested a tool call can approve or deny it; toolApprovers: 'anyone' bypasses only the requester check, and hidden mode suppresses approval buttons without turning a message into consent.

nodes.label: toAISdkStream()
nodes.rationale: Useful when building custom streaming endpoints outside Mastra's provided route helpers such as chatRoute() or workflowRoute().

nodes.label: workflowRoute()
nodes.rationale: Registers an HTTP POST endpoint that executes a workflow and streams the response in AI SDK-compatible format; use handleWorkflowStream() if a framework-agnostic handler is needed.

nodes.label: workflowSnapshotToStream()
nodes.rationale: Lets a completed or suspended workflow run be displayed with the same UI components that render live workflow streams.

nodes.label: MastraAuthAuth0
nodes.rationale: Verifies Auth0-issued JWT tokens (JWKS signature, expiration, audience, issuer) and integrates with the Mastra server via the auth option; constructor params can be omitted when AUTH0_DOMAIN and AUTH0_AUDIENCE env vars are set.

nodes.label: MastraAuthClerk
nodes.rationale: Setting both organizationId and organizationSlug throws at startup so login can't be granted to two different organizations.

nodes.label: MastraAuthFirebase
nodes.rationale: By default authorization checks for a document in the 'user_access' Firestore collection keyed by the user's UID.

nodes.label: activateAfterIdle setting
nodes.rationale: Lets the next request activate buffered observations first once a thread has been idle long enough for the prompt cache to expire, sending a smaller compressed context window.

nodes.label: activateOnProviderChange setting
nodes.rationale: Forces buffered observations to activate before a new provider runs, avoiding sending a large raw window to a provider that cannot reuse the previous prompt cache.

nodes.label: Prompt caching
nodes.rationale: OM's context is stable and observations append over time rather than being retrieved each turn, keeping the prompt prefix cacheable and reducing costs.

nodes.label: session.subagents.model.get({ agentType? })
nodes.rationale: Per-agentType value is preferred over the global subagent model.

nodes.label: withMastra()
nodes.rationale: Lets developers keep existing Vercel AI SDK code while adding Mastra processors and memory (input/output processing and conversation persistence) without switching to the full Mastra agent API.

nodes.label: MastraAuthWorkos
nodes.rationale: Acts as an authentication provider rather than a role gate by default. fetchMemberships defaults to false so Mastra skips the extra WorkOS listOrganizationMemberships() call on each authenticated request; enable it only when MastraFGAWorkos needs the organization membership ID.

nodes.label: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: The definition is fully validated before anything is mutated; adding an existing ID replaces both stored definition and live registration while in-flight runs keep the graph they started with.

nodes.label: Mastra.addDynamicWorkflows()
nodes.rationale: The whole bundle is validated up front and members are registered in dependency order so a helper is always in place before the workflow that nests it; a rejected bundle registers nothing and the in-memory registry is rolled back.

nodes.label: Mastra.getMCPServerById()
nodes.rationale: The server id is slugified during construction, and the optional version parameter disambiguates multiple servers sharing an id; without a version the first match is returned.

nodes.label: SimpleAuth
nodes.rationale: SimpleAuth works well for worker tokens because it maps tokens to a user identity and role.

nodes.label: Background Task Worker
nodes.rationale: Executes agent tool calls marked with background: { enabled: true } so the API doesn't block the response stream.

nodes.label: MASTRA_STEP_EXECUTION_URL
nodes.rationale: Without this variable the orchestration worker attempts to execute steps in its own process, which doesn't have access to the full Mastra runtime in a split deployment.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKER_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: Forwarded as an Authorization: Bearer credential so the API's auth provider can validate internal worker step-execution requests.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKERS
nodes.rationale: Controls which workers start in each process so the same build artifact can be run in multiple containers with different roles.

nodes.label: Orchestration Worker
nodes.rationale: Subscribes to workflow events on the PubSub bus and executes workflow steps; in a split deployment it delegates step execution back to the API over HTTP.

nodes.label: Scheduler Worker
nodes.rationale: Producer only: polls storage for due cron schedules and publishes workflow.start events. Must run as a single instance because multiple schedulers polling the same storage would fire duplicate events.

nodes.label: mastra.startWorkers()
nodes.rationale: Required after the server starts listening when using a server adapter instead of the generated server.

nodes.label: BackgroundTaskWorker
nodes.rationale: Supports multiple replicas because instances share the consumer group.

nodes.label: OrchestrationWorker
nodes.rationale: Requires a pull-capable PubSub such as @mastra/redis-streams or @mastra/google-cloud-pubsub configured with a pull subscription.

nodes.label: SchedulerWorker
nodes.rationale: Must run as exactly one instance to avoid duplicate fires.

nodes.label: Bearer Token Credential
nodes.rationale: The default credential format because it covers most setups.

nodes.label: Workflow Events Endpoint (POST /api/workflows/events)
nodes.rationale: Marked requiresAuth: true so push-mode brokers must present credentials the server's auth provider recognizes.

nodes.label: Pull-mode Workers
nodes.rationale: Pull-mode workers pull events from the broker themselves, a distinct integration path from push-mode brokers that POST to the API event endpoint.

nodes.label: Worker Auth Security Recommendations
nodes.rationale: Use different tokens per worker type so access to one worker can be revoked without affecting others; rotate tokens on a schedule; use TLS in production to protect tokens in transit; keep the internal step execution and event endpoints off the public internet.

nodes.label: Step Execution Endpoint (POST /api/workflows/:workflowId/runs/:runId/steps/execute)
nodes.rationale: Marked requiresAuth: true so that when an auth provider is configured only authenticated workers can execute steps; without a provider the route is publicly accessible.

nodes.label: Workers
nodes.rationale: Workers handle background processing outside the request-response cycle so workflow steps, cron scheduling, and long-running tool calls don't block API responses; they can be split into separate processes for independent scaling.

nodes.label: MASTRA_STEP_EXECUTION_URL
nodes.rationale: Required when the orchestration worker runs in a separate process from the API; HTTPS URLs should be used in production.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKER_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: Bearer token sent by the orchestration worker to the API's step execution endpoint; the API's configured auth provider must recognize it.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKERS
nodes.rationale: Setting MASTRA_WORKERS to any value, including "false", makes createWorkflow build workflows that declare schedule on the evented engine, so it must be set on every process in a split deployment.

nodes.label: mastra-projects Helm Chart
nodes.rationale: Renders the worker deployments on the same image and environment as the server, and refuses to install combinations that would run every worker twice.

nodes.label: IdGeneratorContext
nodes.rationale: Receives optional context such as idType, source, entityId and threadId to support context-aware ID formats.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: Central orchestrator and top-level registry where agents, workflows, tools and other components are registered so they are accessible throughout the application; typically a single instance is created.

nodes.label: MastraMemory
nodes.rationale: Registered memory instances can be referenced by stored agents and resolved at runtime.

nodes.label: MastraRecoveryConfig
nodes.rationale: Recovery re-issues LLM calls and re-executes tool calls, so tools must be idempotent.

nodes.label: MastraWorker
nodes.rationale: Passing false disables all event processing, which is useful when running standalone workers separately; custom workers are merged with auto-created defaults and replace a default of the same name.

nodes.label: MCPServerBase
nodes.rationale: Each MCPServer must have an id property; servers can be retrieved by registry key via getMCPServer() or by intrinsic id via getMCPServerById().

nodes.label: NotificationDispatchConfig
nodes.rationale: The dispatch schedule (and the workflow scheduler backing it) activates lazily on the first deferred or summarized notification, so apps that never defer notifications don't run a scheduler at all.

nodes.label: Mastra.recoverAllDurableAgents()
nodes.rationale: Called automatically on boot when recovery.durableAgents is 'auto', but exposed for manual or scheduled recovery; requires persistent storage since an in-memory store has nothing to recover after a process restart.

nodes.label: VersionOverrides
nodes.rationale: Global version overrides determine which stored version of a sub-agent a supervisor delegates to instead of the code-defined default; requires the editor package to be configured.

nodes.label: Mastra.listTools()
nodes.rationale: Lists only the Mastra-level registry; tools that exist only in a function-based Agent tools callback are not included.

nodes.label: GatewayLanguageModel
nodes.rationale: Union of LanguageModelV2 | LanguageModelV3 | LanguageModelV4 covering AI SDK v5, v6 and v7 models.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.list()
nodes.rationale: Filters are applied at the storage layer, so callers don't need to post-filter results.

nodes.label: CompositeVoice
nodes.rationale: Combine different voice providers for text-to-speech and speech-to-text so you can use the best provider for each operation (e.g. OpenAI for STT, PlayAI for TTS).

nodes.label: MastraVoice
nodes.rationale: Abstract base class defining the core interface for voice services; provides a consistent interface across different voice service providers and optional real-time speech-to-speech support.

nodes.label: MastraVoice.traced()
nodes.rationale: Wraps method calls with performance tracking and error monitoring so telemetry is automatically handled for all method calls.

nodes.label: Mastra Documentation
nodes.rationale: Mastra docs are the canonical, current reference; trust them over training data.

nodes.label: src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Code-registered logging wins over logger.ts; use code registration when setup depends on runtime wiring.

nodes.label: logger.ts
nodes.rationale: Use logger.ts when one project-wide logger is enough; use code registration when setup depends on runtime wiring.

nodes.label: config.ts
nodes.rationale: config.memory wins over memory.ts in the merge table.

nodes.label: memory.ts
nodes.rationale: Without memory.ts or config.memory the agent has no memory by default, so each generate() or stream() call starts without remembered conversation state.

nodes.label: outputValidation (strict/warn)
nodes.rationale: Previously outputSchema was only used for type inference and output was never validated; v1 validates return values at runtime by default (strict).

nodes.label: AgentsMDInjector
nodes.rationale: Injects at most one new instruction reminder per invocation as a persisted reactive signal, skipping already loaded paths; stream exclusions are not an instruction-trust boundary, so isEnabled and a trusted reader control whether checkout instructions load.

nodes.label: ReminderFileReader
nodes.rationale: Controls both file access and optional path identity so instruction files can live in a virtual filesystem or trusted git ref rather than the current checkout.

nodes.label: clearSandboxCache(cacheKey?)
nodes.rationale: The workspace doesn't own resolver-returned sandboxes; this method only drops workspace references, so the sandbox must be destroyed in the caller's own lifecycle code. It also does not clear the per-RequestContext weak cache, which is garbage-collection managed.

nodes.label: Workspace.getInfo()
nodes.rationale: Never invokes a sandbox resolver because resolving a sandbox can provision real infrastructure.

nodes.label: Workspace.getInstructions()
nodes.rationale: Combined filesystem and sandbox instructions are injected into the agent's system message to explain the execution context.

nodes.label: Workspace.getInstructionsAsync()
nodes.rationale: Needed for resolver-backed providers; dynamic sandbox contributes placeholder text unless instructions.dynamicSandbox is 'resolve'.

nodes.label: Workspace.hasFilesystemConfig()
nodes.rationale: Needed because a resolver-based workspace returns undefined from the filesystem property.

nodes.label: hasSandboxConfig()
nodes.rationale: Use this instead of checking workspace.sandbox directly, because a resolver-based workspace returns undefined from the sandbox property.

nodes.label: Workspace.setToolsConfig()
nodes.rationale: Performs a full replacement rather than a merge; changes take effect on the next createWorkspaceTools() call.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.rationale: Combines a filesystem and sandbox to give agents file storage and command execution, plus BM25/vector search over indexed content.

nodes.label: Dynamic sandbox instructions
nodes.rationale: Default 'placeholder' mode avoids provisioning a sandbox while workspace instructions are built.

nodes.label: Per-user filesystem and sandbox resolvers
nodes.rationale: Resolver functions receive requestContext and return a provider per request, enabling per-user or per-thread isolation.

nodes.label: Sandbox cache key
nodes.rationale: Memoizing resolved sandboxes per key instead of per RequestContext instance lets background-process tools reach the same sandbox across follow-up requests.

nodes.label: BatchPartsProcessor
nodes.rationale: Batches stream parts to reduce network overhead and consolidate small text chunks while controlling emissions to optimize streaming performance.

nodes.label: load_tool meta-tool
nodes.rationale: Activates a discovered tool on the next turn; not exposed when search.autoLoad collapses the two-step flow into a single search step.

nodes.label: search_tools meta-tool
nodes.rationale: Always available to the agent; returns BM25-ranked tool matches so tools can be discovered without occupying prompt space.

nodes.label: ToolSearchProcessor
nodes.rationale: Instead of providing all tools to the agent upfront, it gives the agent two meta-tools so it can find and load tools on demand, reducing context token usage when working with large tool libraries.

nodes.label: StreamErrorRetryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Handles statuses that ask to try again later (408, 409, 429, 503, 504) by resending the same request, file included, so UnsupportedFileHandler leaves those errors to it.

nodes.label: UnsupportedFileHandler
nodes.rationale: Keeps an agent working when the model rejects a file the user sent: it takes the file out of the prompt and calls the model again, uploading to the workspace sandbox when one exists. Added to every agent's errorProcessors by default because which file types a model reads varies by provider and changes over time, so the processor doesn't guess up front.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Provides the updateWorkingMemory tool that performs working memory updates, keeping mutation out of the WorkingMemory input processor.

nodes.label: WorkingMemory
nodes.rationale: Injects working memory data as a system message so the agent can maintain context about users across conversations; updates happen through the Memory class's updateWorkingMemory tool, not through this processor.

nodes.label: File-based Agents
nodes.rationale: Special folder convention allowing an agent to be defined by file convention instead of constructing it in code.

nodes.label: Mastra Default Project Structure
nodes.rationale: Mastra is mostly unopinionated about file organization; the CLI provides a sensible default structure that works for most projects, and consistency is what keeps code maintainable.

nodes.label: embedV4()
nodes.rationale: Mastra selects the matching AI SDK implementation from the model's specificationVersion; the model specification version and the AI SDK package version are different (AI SDK v4 uses spec v1, v5 uses v2, v6 uses v3, v7 uses v4).

nodes.label: MCP protocol revision negotiation
nodes.rationale: The client speaks 2026-07-28 and probes server/discover, falling back to the pre-2026 initialize handshake so tools, resources, and prompts keep working against either revision.

nodes.label: voice.addInstructions()
nodes.rationale: Instructions are most effective when clear, specific and relevant; they should be added before connect() because they guide the model during real-time interactions that maintain conversation context.

nodes.label: voice.addTools()
nodes.rationale: Tools must be added before connect() so the voice model can call them during the session; the provider automatically handles invocation when the model decides to use a tool.

nodes.label: getTask() / listTasks()
nodes.rationale: Read from storage rather than the pubsub stream, making them suitable for paginated lists and detail views.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Aggregate properties still resolve against the first turn's internal buffer, so an aggregate view across continuations requires consuming fullStream manually.

nodes.label: registerStaticExecutor()
nodes.rationale: Static executors registered in every process let any process run or recover a task, avoiding 'No executor registered' failures.

nodes.label: backgroundTaskManager.stream({ allResources: true })
nodes.rationale: Delivers task arguments and results for every user, so it must only be used in trusted server-side code, never to serve a single user's request.

nodes.label: backgroundTasks configuration
nodes.rationale: Background tasks are off by default; enabling the manager does not run anything in the background by itself.

nodes.label: expiresAt
nodes.rationale: Cleanup never deletes a pending, running, or suspended task, so expired work must be cancelled first.

nodes.label: Lifecycle callbacks
