nodes.rationale: Callbacks at each layer don't replace one another; success/failure hooks fire for their outcomes.

nodes.label: Non-agent owners
nodes.rationale: The task's agentId is its owner key; a namespaced key such as mcp-server:<serverId> avoids collision with a real agent ID (not enforced by Mastra).

nodes.label: Notification signal reporting task results
nodes.rationale: The signal names the tool call and task rather than copying the result into the prompt, so the agent reads the result from the tool call.

nodes.label: notifyAgentOnFinish
nodes.rationale: Set to false when the app sends its own completion signal so the agent isn't told twice.

nodes.label: pinToWorker
nodes.rationale: Used when work for a task is already in flight in this process; the pending task holds an execution lease so no other process starts the same work. Pinned work should be idempotent because a stalled worker can still be running when another worker retries.

nodes.label: untilIdle option
nodes.rationale: Keeps the stream open until every dispatched background task has completed and the LLM has responded to the result; the idle timer only runs between turns so a slow first token won't close the stream.

nodes.label: wokenRunsEndAfterTurn
nodes.rationale: Temporary option; in the next major release ending after the turn becomes the only behavior and the option is removed.

nodes.label: onStart lifecycle hook
nodes.rationale: Runs after the sandbox reaches running and before pending mounts are processed, so it can be used for once-per-VM setup; a thrown error is fatal so a caller never observes a running sandbox whose setup hook failed, while onStop/onDestroy stay non-fatal because teardown proceeds best-effort.

nodes.label: SandboxStartResult
nodes.rationale: Outcome is derived structurally from which branch ran (find→connect vs create) so providers don't have to report it manually.

nodes.label: setOnStart()
nodes.rationale: Composing via an updater that receives the current hook means a caller never discards a hook it didn't know about; without it every host constructing a sandbox would have to accept and pass a hook, and a host that forgets leaves setup unrun with no error.

nodes.label: start()
nodes.rationale: Concurrent start() calls coalesce onto a single in-flight attempt and joined callers share its result; the in-flight slot is cleared when the attempt settles so a failed start can be retried.

nodes.label: Skill tools
nodes.rationale: Added when skills are configured.

nodes.label: VersionedSkillSource
nodes.rationale: Serves published skill versions from a content-addressable blob store.

nodes.label: Skills discovery
nodes.rationale: Skills are read from skillSource when set, otherwise from the workspace filesystem (resolved per request), and only fall back to local disk when no filesystem is configured.

nodes.label: webSearchTool
nodes.rationale: Resolved at run time from the active model so the provider's native web search tool is passed to the model; fails with MastraError if the provider cannot be inferred.

nodes.label: createRoute
nodes.rationale: Route-level fga metadata keeps authorization policy next to the route.

nodes.label: mapAuthInfoToUser
nodes.rationale: Lets Mastra set requestContext user from OAuth authInfo before checking tools/list and tools/call.

nodes.label: Fine-Grained Authorization
nodes.rationale: Answers whether a user can do an action on a specific resource, unlike RBAC which is role-level.

nodes.label: SimpleAuth
nodes.rationale: Designed for simplicity, not production security: tokens in memory, no expiration, no cryptographic verification.

nodes.label: Subagent memory isolation
nodes.rationale: Subagents get full conversation context but only their delegation prompt and response are saved, with a fresh thread per invocation, so they have context without cluttering their memory.

nodes.label: pauseSchedule
nodes.rationale: Durable operational override written to the schedules table; declarative-config upsert never overwrites a user-set status.

nodes.label: resumeSchedule
nodes.rationale: Recomputes nextFireAt from now so a long-paused schedule does not fire backlogged runs.

nodes.label: createWorkflowStateReader()
nodes.rationale: Exposes suspended steps, resume labels, payloads and outputs without reading the raw snapshot shape.

nodes.label: dynamic skills resolver
nodes.rationale: Enables per-request skill resolution; runs once per RequestContext and also on metadata reads where no span exists, so it should stay fast and guard span usage.

nodes.label: LocalSkillSource
nodes.rationale: Reads SKILL.md files following the same format as workspace skills.

nodes.label: skill / skill_read / skill_search tools
nodes.rationale: Automatically provided so the agent can discover and load skills during conversations.

nodes.label: agent skills config
nodes.rationale: Agent-level skills belong to one agent and can be defined in code without a workspace, unlike workspace skills discovered from the filesystem.

nodes.label: createSkill()
nodes.rationale: Creates an inline skill usable without a filesystem or workspace, while implementing the same Skill interface as filesystem-discovered skills.

nodes.label: Agent Skills
nodes.rationale: Reusable instructions that teach agents how to perform specific tasks, following the Agent Skills specification.

nodes.label: Workspace skills
nodes.rationale: Filesystem-based skill discovery shared by every agent using that workspace.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: When storage is passed to the Mastra class, init() is called automatically before any storage operation.

nodes.label: MSSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Exposes the mssql connection pool as a public field for advanced low-level access; direct access bypasses MSSQLStore validation and makes the caller responsible for connection and transaction handling.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: When storage is registered with Mastra, init() is called automatically to create the core schema.

nodes.label: MySQLStore
nodes.rationale: disableInit disables automatic initialization so storage.init() can be called manually; skipDefaultIndexes is for cases where default storage indexes are not wanted.

nodes.label: Vite/Nitro Config (vite.config.ts)
nodes.rationale: optimizeDeps.exclude prevents Vite's dev optimizer from opening DuckDB's native .node binary as JavaScript and from pre-bundling execa; Nitro rollupConfig.external keeps DuckDB native packages out of the production bundle so Node.js can load them at runtime.

nodes.label: session.followUps
nodes.rationale: Holds the FIFO queue of messages submitted while a run is in progress.

nodes.label: buildBasePrompt()
nodes.rationale: Product-specific strings are parameterized through productName, coAuthorName, and coAuthorEmail so the prompt and commit trailer can be rebranded without forking.

nodes.label: Session.abort()
nodes.rationale: Also clears pending suspension display state.

nodes.label: SessionDisplayState
nodes.rationale: The canonical AgentControllerDisplayState snapshot a UI renders from.

nodes.label: Session.followUp()
nodes.rationale: Queues while a run is active, sends immediately while idle.

nodes.label: Session.grantCategory()
nodes.rationale: Grants are ephemeral: they reset when the session restarts and are never persisted.

nodes.label: Session.grantTool()
nodes.rationale: Grants are ephemeral: they reset when the session restarts and are never persisted.

nodes.label: Session.queueMessage()
nodes.rationale: Queues for the next run, or sends immediately while the session is idle.

nodes.label: Session.resolveToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Returns the effective policy after applying explicit tool rules, session grants, and category rules.

nodes.label: Session.respondToToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: toolCallId is required because it identifies the parked call; always_allow_category also grants the tool's whole category for the gate's thread.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: The isolated runtime registered under one session id; several sessions can share a resource that owns their stored threads and resource-scoped memory. Direct construction is not an application API — sessions are created through controller.createSession().

nodes.label: session.mode.switch({ modeId })
nodes.rationale: The active model stays the same unless switched separately, which is necessary when the host assigns different models to different modes.

nodes.label: Session.steer()
nodes.rationale: Aborts the active run first, then sends the new content as a message.

nodes.label: Session.subscribe()
nodes.rationale: Each session owns an isolated event bus; the method returns an unsubscribe function.

nodes.label: Mastra.getWorkflow()
nodes.rationale: Use the registration key rather than the id for full TypeScript type inference of input, output and step results.

nodes.label: Mastra.removeWorkspace()
nodes.rationale: When destroy is true and workspace.destroy() throws, the call rejects and the workspace remains registered so the caller can retry cleanup.

nodes.label: dataset.deleteItems()
nodes.rationale: Bulk operation that deletes multiple items in a single call rather than one at a time.

nodes.label: ErrorProcessor
nodes.rationale: Type alias requiring processAPIError; configured via the errorProcessors array.

nodes.label: InputProcessor
nodes.rationale: Type alias requiring at least one of processInput, processInputStep, processLLMRequest, or processLLMResponse.

nodes.label: processAPIError
nodes.rationale: Runs when the API call fails with a non-retryable error (such as a 400 or 422 status code), unlike processOutputStep which runs after successful responses.

nodes.label: processLLMRequest
nodes.rationale: Returned prompt changes are forwarded to the model for the current call only; they are not persisted back to MessageList, memory, UI history, or later provider calls.

nodes.label: processLLMResponse
nodes.rationale: Pairs with processLLMRequest: use processLLMRequest to stash state (such as a cache key) before the provider call, and processLLMResponse to act on the completed response (such as writing it to a cache).

nodes.label: dataset.getItemHistory()
nodes.rationale: Exposes the full SCD-2 (Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2) history of an item across all dataset versions, including deletion tombstones via isDeleted and supersession via validTo.

nodes.label: dataset.listExperimentResults()
nodes.rationale: Filters are applied at the storage layer; results carry traceId so item-level results can be joined to observability traces.

nodes.label: dataset.listExperiments()
nodes.rationale: Filters are applied at the storage layer so results are always scoped to the current dataset; agentVersion filtering supports baseline vs variant comparisons.

nodes.label: dataset.listItems()
nodes.rationale: The bare DatasetItem[] snapshot returned when only version is passed is retained for backwards compatibility and is deprecated; passing page/perPage (or search) always yields the paginated shape.

nodes.label: filterRun()
nodes.rationale: Provides declarative filtering for prepareRun; a custom prepareRun function should be written directly when imperative logic is needed that filterRun does not cover.

nodes.label: MastraPartType
nodes.rationale: Part type values are prefix-matched, so 'data-' matches all data part types.

nodes.label: File-Based Server Configuration
nodes.rationale: Code-registered server config wins over server.ts; routes added during startup, such as channel webhooks, are preserved when file-based server config is applied.

nodes.label: agent.getMemory()
nodes.rationale: Makes asynchronous memory access explicit.

nodes.label: createThread()
nodes.rationale: Allows injecting initial working memory via thread metadata so user data is available to the agent without passing it in every request.

nodes.label: mergeWorkingMemory()
nodes.rationale: Throws if working memory isn't schema-based and resource-scoped, or if the storage adapter doesn't support atomic merges; callers should check supportsAtomicWorkingMemoryMerge() to fall back.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: Currently the only adapter supporting atomic merges, running each merge inside a row-locked database transaction so concurrent updates to different fields from separate processes are all kept.

nodes.label: WorkingMemoryStateProcessor
nodes.rationale: Auto-attached by Memory when useStateSignals is enabled to emit working memory as a state signal instead of folding it into the system prompt; the write tool is renamed to setWorkingMemory so legacy strip filters don't remove tool-call parts and the next model step picks up the new value automatically.

nodes.label: Resource-Scoped Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Default scope: memory persists across all conversation threads for the same user (resourceId), enabling persistent user memory for assistants, support bots and educational apps.

nodes.label: Schema-Based Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Uses merge semantics so the agent only supplies fields to add or update: object fields are deep merged, null deletes a field, and arrays are replaced entirely. Chosen for structured, type-safe JSON data with validation and programmatic access; template and schema cannot both be set.

nodes.label: Template-Based Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Uses replace semantics: the agent must provide the complete memory content on each update, which suits free-form text blocks such as a user profile or scratchpad.

nodes.label: Thread-Scoped Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Isolates memory per conversation thread; thread-scoped and resource-scoped memory are completely separate, so switching scopes means the agent won't see memory from the other scope.

nodes.label: Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Serves as the agent's active scratchpad for persistent, always-relevant state about the user or task, complementing message history and semantic recall which cover conversational recall.

nodes.label: listWorkflows
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getWorkflows to align with the API convention where plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: BatchPartsProcessor
nodes.rationale: Batches stream chunks before passing them to the scrubber, reducing the number of LLM calls required for detection.

nodes.label: SystemPromptScrubber
nodes.rationale: Opt-in buffering (bufferSize) holds streamed text back and checks it in one LLM call at sentence boundaries, making far fewer LLM calls and catching content split across chunks; recommended for production streaming.

nodes.label: ModelRouterEmbeddingModel
nodes.rationale: The model router automatically handles API key detection from environment variables.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: The vector database index must be configured to match the embedding model's output size to avoid errors or data corruption from mismatched dimensions.

nodes.label: MCPEventsSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: The provider stores the cursor after it notifies the threads, so an occurrence notified right before a crash is replayed after the restart.

nodes.label: agent.getVoice()
nodes.rationale: The agent.voice getter has no request context, so it throws when voice is a resolver; getVoice({ requestContext }) must be used instead.

nodes.label: Per-session voice resolver
nodes.rationale: A static voice instance is shared across every request, but realtime providers store session state (WebSocket connection, tools, instructions, request context); a shared instance can let one session overwrite another's state, so a resolver returns a fresh instance per request context.

nodes.label: webFetchTool
nodes.rationale: Failures do not throw; the tool returns isError: true with the reason in content so the agent can retry or explain the problem.

nodes.label: CiSignals (example provider)
nodes.rationale: Exposes only what the application needs: wraps protected subscribe()/unsubscribe() in public watch()/unwatch() methods.

nodes.label: connect()
nodes.rationale: Override only when you need setup that depends on the connected agent; always call super.connect(agent) first.

nodes.label: handleWebhook()
nodes.rationale: Used when the source can call your app; verify the source's signature against the raw body before parsing where required.

nodes.label: notify()
nodes.rationale: Wraps the connected agent's sendNotificationSignal() and accepts the same fields; throws when the provider isn't connected and propagates storage errors.

nodes.label: poll()
nodes.rationale: Base class skips cycles with no subscriptions, never overlaps cycles, logs errors and waits for the next cycle, and unrefs the timer so polling alone doesn't keep the process alive.

nodes.label: SignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Use a provider when your application needs to manage which threads receive events from which sources; the base class tracks subscriptions, runs polling, and forwards notifications to the agent.

nodes.label: stop()
nodes.rationale: Synchronous; default implementation stops polling and clears every subscription index, so overrides must call super.stop() to release the registry.

nodes.label: TaskSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Bundles the task tools and the TaskStateProcessor behind one registration so the agent can maintain a task list across turns.

nodes.label: WebhookSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: For generic webhook sources, use this instead of writing a subclass; extractResourceId and buildNotification are configurable.

nodes.label: validateSkillContent()
nodes.rationale: Applies the same rules used when skills are loaded and returns structured results instead of throwing.

nodes.label: Tool approval propagation
nodes.rationale: Approval requests from subagent tools surface in the parent agent's stream so the delegation chain stays gated.

nodes.label: Control-flow entry labeling
nodes.rationale: These fields identify and describe the graph entry itself, separate from the steps inside it. They survive serialization and storage and appear in serializedStepGraph. They have no effect on execution.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext.ensurePartitions()
nodes.rationale: Creating a partition is DDL; if the app role cannot create tables or does not own the observability tables, writes fail, so ensurePartitions() must be scheduled with a role that can create tables and owns them.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Uses the event-sourced tracing strategy: one row written when a span starts and another when it ends, never updating in place, so writes stay append-only and traces appear in Studio while the run is still executing.

nodes.label: Agent.getLLM()
nodes.rationale: Accepts a request-scoped model override so callers can swap the model per request without mutating the agent's configured model.

nodes.label: extractTrajectoryFromTrace
nodes.rationale: Preferred extraction method when storage is available; produces richer trajectories than extractTrajectory or extractWorkflowTrajectory because it captures the full execution tree, including nested agent runs, tool calls, and model generations.

nodes.label: MastraJwtAuth
nodes.rationale: The resolved secret must be non-empty: the constructor throws if neither the option nor JWT_AUTH_SECRET is set, and an empty string does not fall back to the environment variable.

nodes.label: MastraAuthSupabase
nodes.rationale: By default authorizeUser checks the 'isAdmin' column in the 'users' table after token verification.

nodes.label: server.apiRoutes
nodes.rationale: Mastra automatically exposes registered agents and workflows via its server; this option adds custom HTTP routes for additional behavior.

nodes.label: server.build
nodes.rationale: Controls development tools like Swagger UI and request logging, enabled during local development but disabled in production by default.

nodes.label: server.auth
nodes.rationale: mapUserToResourceId maps the authenticated user to a resource ID for memory/thread scoping; when omitted, built-in routes fall back to the client-supplied resource ID so ownership checks trust the caller, and Mastra logs a startup warning.

nodes.label: server.mcpOptions
nodes.rationale: MCP requests are self-contained, so no session state is kept between them and routes run unchanged in serverless environments; serverless and sessionIdGenerator are accepted only for compatibility and have no effect.

nodes.label: Mastra.getAgentById()
nodes.rationale: Searches registered agents by agent.id first and falls back to treating the value as the agent registry key, so both ID and registry-key lookups work.

nodes.label: mastra-core Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill exists so that agents working with @mastra/core APIs, configuration, or implementation obtain domain-specific knowledge by reading individual reference documents.

nodes.label: MCPClient
nodes.rationale: Includes built-in memory leak prevention: creating multiple instances with identical configurations without an `id` throws, so callers must supply a unique `id` or call `disconnect()` before recreating. Process hooks (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/beforeExit) are installed by default but can be disabled with `registerProcessHooks: false` because they can interrupt an application's awaited cleanup.

nodes.label: allowedHosts
nodes.rationale: Restricts which hosts the client will contact to prevent server-side request forgery when HTTP server URLs come from untrusted configuration.

nodes.label: Custom fetch for runtime-defined authentication
nodes.rationale: A custom fetch should not throw when authentication is unavailable: a thrown fetch is reported like a non-2xx response but loses the server's status and body, and the long-lived subscriptions/listen POST is retried, so an unauthenticated stream can loop. Forwarding the request lets the server reject it.

nodes.label: 'needs-auth' state
nodes.rationale: The client records a 'needs-auth' state instead of failing outright when a server rejects a connection because authorization is required.

nodes.label: Subprocess environment isolation
nodes.rationale: Stdio subprocesses do not inherit the full parent process environment; sensitive variables such as API keys are not inherited unless explicitly passed.

nodes.label: Tool annotations
nodes.rationale: Clients MUST consider tool annotations untrusted unless they come from trusted servers; annotations are advisory hints and provide no security boundary.

nodes.label: Tool approval
nodes.rationale: Require human approval before executing tools from a server, integrating with the human-in-the-loop approval flow.

nodes.label: Trace context
nodes.rationale: Trace context is observability data and is never used for authorization.

nodes.label: Typed client contracts
nodes.rationale: Pass an explicit server-map type to check configured server names, discovered tool names, and direct-call arguments.

nodes.label: Type generation (typegen)
nodes.rationale: Generates concrete TypeScript interfaces from live tool input and output schemas.

nodes.label: Mastra.setLogger()
nodes.rationale: Sets the logger for all components (agents, workflows, etc.) in the Mastra instance.

nodes.label: DatasetsManager.delete()
nodes.rationale: Experiments that ran against the dataset are kept but detached (datasetId and datasetVersion set to null) so experiment history survives dataset deletion; a tenancy mismatch is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: convertMessages()
nodes.rationale: Provided for cases where messages must be manually converted between AI SDK and Mastra formats, e.g. when fetching messages directly from storage.

nodes.label: MessageList
nodes.rationale: Handles AI SDK v4 to v5 format conversion on the fly, so no database migrations are required.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Renamed from MastraStorage to better reflect its role as a composite storage implementation that routes different domains to different underlying stores, avoiding confusion with the general 'Mastra Storage' concept (the storage property on the Mastra instance).

nodes.label: Vector store API
nodes.rationale: Arguments-by-name makes each value's purpose visible at the call site and lets method signatures evolve without relying on argument order.

nodes.label: createRun
nodes.rationale: Renamed from createRunAsync, removing the redundant Async suffix since all run creation is asynchronous.

nodes.label: getInitData
nodes.rationale: Now returns unknown instead of any, requiring explicit typing.

nodes.label: listWorkflowRuns
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getWorkflowRuns to follow the convention that list* methods return collections.

nodes.label: events Property
nodes.rationale: After a reconnect or a resume, the server can resend an occurrence, and the client drops repeats by eventId within dedupWindow of recent ids.

nodes.label: Webhook Delivery
nodes.rationale: By default the client generates a fresh secret for each subscription, so one server can't sign deliveries for another server's subscriptions.

nodes.label: allowedUrls
nodes.rationale: URLs accepted by allowedUrls skip the verification challenge.

nodes.label: WebhookSubscriptionStore
nodes.rationale: Default keeps subscriptions in memory, so they are lost on restart until clients refresh.

nodes.label: webhook url policy
nodes.rationale: allowPrivate and allowInsecure are for local development only; the public-routability check prevents DNS rebinding.

nodes.label: retryCount
nodes.rationale: Replaces deprecated runCount; the new name identifies the value as the number of retries.

nodes.label: streamVNext / resumeStreamVNext / observeStreamVNext
nodes.rationale: Experimental methods removed; their implementation is now the standard stream/resumeStream/observeStream.

nodes.label: pipeThrough / pipeTo
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favor of using the fullStream property directly.

nodes.label: outputWriter
nodes.rationale: Replaces writableStream with an async callback receiving each workflow event chunk, simplifying the API.

nodes.label: MDocument.chunk()
nodes.rationale: Multiple chunking strategies are offered because they are optimized for different document types (recursive, character, token, markdown, semantic-markdown, html, json, latex, sentence).

nodes.label: errorStrategy
nodes.rationale: strict throws, warn logs and continues, fallback substitutes fallbackValue so a failed structuring call does not break the caller.

nodes.label: structuredOutput.instructions
nodes.rationale: Prompt injection embeds the serialized JSON schema in every model call, which can cost thousands of tokens per step on a large schema; compact instructions replace the injected schema while the response is still validated against it.

nodes.label: jsonPromptInjection
nodes.rationale: By default the schema is passed via the provider response_format parameter; 'auto' picks native structured output or inline prompt injection from model capability data, which is required for models like Gemini 2.5 that cannot combine response_format with function calling.

nodes.label: object-result chunk
nodes.rationale: Text stream chunks are still emitted during structured streaming but contain natural language text rather than structured data; the structured object arrives on the object-result chunk.

nodes.label: prepareStep
nodes.rationale: Workaround for models that cannot use tools and structured output in the same call: run tools in one step and structured output in a later step.

nodes.label: response.object
nodes.rationale: Holds the parsed, schema-validated value so callers do not parse or validate themselves; the exception is errorStrategy 'fallback', where it holds the unvalidated fallbackValue.

nodes.label: useAgent
nodes.rationale: Reuses the parent agent with the separate structuring model and attaches read-only memory context when a thread is available; leave unset to structure only from the current response.

nodes.label: usedFallbackValue
nodes.rationale: Lets callers tell a substituted fallback object from a real schema-validated answer.

nodes.label: Zod
nodes.rationale: Recommended because it provides TypeScript type inference and runtime validation.

nodes.label: Gemini 2.5 tools limitation
nodes.rationale: Gemini 2.5 models do not support combining response_format with function calling in the same API call, so jsonPromptInjection must be enabled when tools are present.

nodes.label: JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: Useful when a language-agnostic format is needed instead of a TypeScript-inferred schema library.

nodes.label: Separate structuring model
nodes.rationale: Uses a second agent to extract structured data from the main agent's natural language response; costs an extra LLM call and latency but improves accuracy for complex structuring tasks.

nodes.label: Structured output
nodes.rationale: Use structured output on an agent instead when the model must produce a data object with many interdependent fields.

nodes.label: Function-Based Steps
nodes.rationale: Ideal for algorithmic evaluations with clear criteria, performance-critical scenarios, library integration, and reproducible results.

nodes.label: Prompt Objects
nodes.rationale: Use deterministic functions for algorithmic checks and LLM judges for subjective, nuanced, or hard-to-code criteria; the two can be mixed within one scorer.

nodes.label: goal chunk
nodes.rationale: A goal with no judge model configured produces no goal chunk.

nodes.label: verifyToken
nodes.rationale: Validates the token's signature, issuer, audience, algorithm, expiration and required claims before passing user data to the tool.

nodes.label: processOutputStream()
nodes.rationale: By default it skips data-* chunks so it does not accidentally operate on tool telemetry or other processors' output.

nodes.label: placeOrderTool
nodes.rationale: Sets outputValidation: 'warn' because the side effect (order placement) has already happened by the time the result is produced; returning the real result unchanged keeps the model from retrying an order that was already placed.

nodes.label: showProductTool
nodes.rationale: Returns a short acknowledgement instead of echoing the input so model context and stored messages stay small while the client renders the tool part from its input.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Used when the tool needs a structured answer from the user, e.g. a confirmed cart write; the run resumes with the user's answer.

nodes.label: TaskSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Bundles all four task tools and the TaskStateProcessor in a single registration; the task list lives in thread-scoped threadState so it survives observational-memory truncation.

nodes.label: weatherTool
nodes.rationale: Direct imports are preferred when one tool is used by multiple agents: each agent imports the tool and adds it to its tools record, keeping dependencies explicit and each agent independently usable.

nodes.label: Client tools
nodes.rationale: A tool without an execute function cannot run on the server; the run ends with finishReason 'tool-calls' until the client supplies a result.

nodes.label: toModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Shapes the payload sent back to the model so rich structured tool results are reduced to a smaller or multimodal representation, keeping model context focused while preserving the full result in the app.

nodes.label: transform
nodes.rationale: Separate from toModelOutput: transform shapes tool input, output, errors, approval and suspension payloads for display and transcript targets, so browser-facing streams and user-visible transcripts get a smaller or safer shape. No fallback to the raw payload occurs if a configured transform fails.

nodes.label: Mastra evals, datasets, and experiments workshop
nodes.norm_label: mastra evals, datasets, and experiments workshop

nodes.label: Application authorization
nodes.rationale: Decides whether the caller may perform an operation on data; OAuth scopes do not replace permission and ownership checks.

nodes.label: Delegated access
nodes.rationale: An OAuth access token grants access to its intended resource and is not a general-purpose identity credential.

nodes.label: AuroraDSQLClient
nodes.rationale: Used to generate short-lived IAM auth tokens, so no database passwords are required.

nodes.label: DSQLStore.createIndex
nodes.rationale: Aurora DSQL doesn't allow ASC/DESC in CREATE INDEX ASYNC, so those modifiers are automatically stripped.

nodes.label: DSQLStore.init
nodes.rationale: If init() isn't called, tables won't be created and storage operations will fail silently or throw errors; Mastra calls it automatically when storage is passed to the Mastra class.

nodes.label: IAM-only authentication
nodes.rationale: Connections are authenticated with IAM, so no database passwords are required.

nodes.label: No PostgreSQL extensions
nodes.rationale: CREATE EXTENSION isn't supported (including pgvector), so vector storage must use a separate store such as @mastra/s3vectors.

nodes.label: Optimistic concurrency control
nodes.rationale: Aurora DSQL may return retriable OCC errors under contention and limits transaction duration and size, so large bulk operations should be split into smaller batches at the application level.

nodes.label: CA certificate bundle (PG_CA_CERT_PATH)
nodes.rationale: The CA certificate is unique to the instance and must be available to the deployed application; SSL query parameters are left out of DATABASE_URL because the ssl object configures certificate verification.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.consumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Useful when you only need the final promise-based results and want to trigger stream consumption.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.elementStream
nodes.rationale: Each array element is emitted as it is completed rather than waiting for the entire array.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.finishReason
nodes.rationale: Undefined if the stream hasn't finished.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.fullStream
nodes.rationale: Provides granular access to every aspect of the model's response.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.getFullOutput()
nodes.rationale: Convenient single method to access all stream results.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Provides both streaming and promise-based access to model outputs, supporting structured output generation, tool calls, reasoning, and detailed usage tracking.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.object
nodes.rationale: Validated against the schema before resolving; rejects if validation fails.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.objectStream
nodes.rationale: Emits partial objects as they are built up, allowing real-time visualization of structured data generation.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.reasoning
nodes.rationale: Returns empty string for models without reasoning capability.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.reasoningText
nodes.rationale: Alternative access to reasoning content; may be undefined for models that don't support reasoning, while reasoning returns empty string.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput.textStream
nodes.rationale: Filters out all metadata, tool calls, and control chunks to provide just the text being generated.

nodes.label: registerHttpLoggingMiddleware()
nodes.rationale: Return early when request logging isn't enabled; implement as a no-op if the framework has no way to log requests.

nodes.label: start()
nodes.rationale: Invoked without awaiting, so it must stay independent of the first poll cycle and handle its own errors; also the place to rehydrate persisted subscriptions.

nodes.label: gist index
nodes.rationale: Best for geometric data and full-text search, fast for nearest-neighbor queries.

nodes.label: hash index
nodes.rationale: Small storage, very fast for equality comparisons only.

nodes.label: FileStat
nodes.rationale: The built-in read_file tool uses mimeType to choose how to return a file; a custom filesystem that never sets mimeType returns images and PDFs as text.

nodes.label: getMimeType
nodes.rationale: Returns application/octet-stream for unknown extensions.

nodes.label: grep tool
nodes.rationale: Delegates to native grep instead of downloading every file to search host-side.

nodes.label: list_files tool
nodes.rationale: Uses native walk when implemented instead of one readdir round trip per directory, which matters for remote providers.

nodes.label: read_file tool
nodes.rationale: Files matching mediaTypes come back as native media parts up to maxMediaBytes; larger files return metadata only unless an encoding is passed.

nodes.label: UnsupportedGrepPatternError
nodes.rationale: Thrown when a pattern can't run natively so callers catch it and fall back to the host-side implementation.

nodes.label: WorkspaceFilesystem
nodes.rationale: Optional native walk and grep methods exist so remote providers avoid one round trip per directory or per file; failures fall back to host-side implementations.

nodes.label: CompositeFilesystem
nodes.rationale: When mounted through CompositeFilesystem, workspace-facing paths include the mount prefix.

nodes.label: LocalFilesystem
nodes.rationale: contained defaults to true to prevent path traversal attacks and symlink escapes; absolute paths and ~ are treated as host paths subject to containment. Absolute basePath is recommended because relative paths resolve from process.cwd(), which differs between mastra dev, mastra start and direct scripts.

nodes.label: StaleFileError
nodes.rationale: Used for optimistic concurrency control to detect external modifications between read and write.

nodes.label: spgist index
nodes.rationale: Small storage; suited to non-balanced data and text patterns.

nodes.label: Agent.getMetadata()
nodes.rationale: Metadata lets clients classify agents without encoding that data in the agent ID or name; it may be static or a function of request context.

nodes.label: bundler.externals
nodes.rationale: Useful when the internal Mastra bundler (Rollup) has trouble bundling packages; defaults to true so package.json dependencies are installed separately.

nodes.label: bundler.minify
nodes.rationale: Off by default so build output stays readable and stack traces stay usable; enable when bundle size matters, such as container images for on-prem deployments. mastra dev is never minified.

nodes.label: Agent.streamLegacy()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: only works with V1 models; V2 models must use the new .stream() method, which offers AI SDK v5+ compatibility, better structured-output handling and an improved callback system.

nodes.label: Agent.streamUntilIdle()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favor of stream() with the untilIdle option. Keeps a single stream open across the initial turn plus every continuation triggered by background task completion, so callers do not have to manually re-prompt the agent to process task results.

nodes.label: smoothStream()
nodes.rationale: Buffers text and reasoning deltas and re-emits them in consistent chunks so streamed responses appear at a steadier pace when a model emits uneven deltas; non-text chunks pass through unchanged and buffered content is flushed before tool, control or completion chunks.

nodes.label: Run.observeStream()
nodes.rationale: Opens a new ReadableStream onto an already-running workflow run so events can still be observed when the original stream is no longer available.

nodes.label: Run.resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Resumes a suspended workflow run with new data from a specific step while exposing the event stream; forEachIndex allows resuming a single iteration of a suspended .foreach() step while other iterations stay suspended.

nodes.label: Run.stream()
nodes.rationale: Returns a WorkflowRunOutput that is directly async-iterable and also exposes fullStream, result, status and usage; closeOnSuspend defaults to true so the stream closes when the workflow suspends.

nodes.label: Run.timeTravelStream()
nodes.rationale: Re-executes a workflow from any specific step with streaming events, giving real-time visibility into each step's progress during time travel; requires storage because it relies on persisted workflow snapshots.

nodes.label: askUserTool
nodes.rationale: Agent-agnostic built-in tool that pauses through the native tool suspension primitive (calls suspend() with the question payload) so the run can be resumed with the user's answer; returns a readable fallback string when executed outside an agent run where no suspend is available.

nodes.label: bundler.pnpmWorkspaceSettings
nodes.rationale: Lets deployment installs follow pnpm install-policy settings; explicit values override copied source settings, and omitting it preserves the existing workspace-copy behavior.

nodes.label: bundler.sourcemap
nodes.rationale: When enabled, mastra dev and mastra start run the server with Node's --enable-source-maps flag so stack traces point at source files.

nodes.label: bundler.transpilePackages
nodes.rationale: Only needed when importing uncompiled source code directly; already-compiled CJS/ESM packages do not need listing. Mastra auto-detects monorepo workspace packages.

nodes.label: server.bodySizeLimit
nodes.rationale: Defaults to 4.5 MB; increase when the application needs to handle larger payloads.

nodes.label: server.cors
nodes.rationale: Use for one policy across all routes; for a route-specific policy use the cors option in registerApiRoute().

nodes.label: server.host
nodes.rationale: The MASTRA_HOST environment variable takes precedence over the localhost default.

nodes.label: server.https
nodes.rationale: mastra dev --https automatically creates and manages certificates; this option is for custom certificate management.

nodes.label: server.onError
nodes.rationale: Supported by all server adapters; non-Hono adapters (Koa, Express, Fastify) get a shim with commonly used methods like c.json() and c.req.path.

nodes.label: server.onValidationError
nodes.rationale: Return { status, body } to override the default 400 response, or undefined to keep default behavior; a route-level hook set via createRoute() takes precedence over the server-level hook.

nodes.label: server.port
nodes.rationale: The PORT environment variable takes precedence over the 4111 default.

nodes.label: authenticateToken
nodes.rationale: Verify the token and return the user, or null if authentication fails.

nodes.label: authorizeUser
nodes.rationale: Return true to allow access, false to deny (403 Forbidden).

nodes.label: MastraAuthProvider
nodes.rationale: Base class to extend for identity systems not covered by built-in providers.

nodes.label: registerOptions
nodes.rationale: Registers custom options such as authorizeUser override and public/protected paths.

nodes.label: server.studioBase
nodes.rationale: Useful when integrating with existing applications or auth tools such as Cloudflare Zero Trust that benefit from shared domains, and for managing multiple services under one domain.

nodes.label: server.timeout
nodes.rationale: On serverless platforms this limit is independent of the platform's own function timeout, so long requests need both raised (e.g. Vercel maxDuration plus server.timeout).

nodes.label: Optional Branch Result Fields
nodes.rationale: Reflects runtime behavior where each branch only executes if its condition is truthy, so outputs may be undefined.

nodes.label: Legacy Workflows Export
nodes.rationale: The ./workflows/legacy export path was removed; no direct migration path exists.

nodes.label: Watch Events API
nodes.rationale: Legacy watch events removed and consolidated on the v2 events API.

nodes.label: ActorSignal
nodes.rationale: Marks autonomous/scheduled agent calls so FGA can distinguish them from user requests.

nodes.label: IFGAProvider
nodes.rationale: Interface to implement to use any FGA backend.

nodes.label: mapUserToResourceId
nodes.rationale: Sets MASTRA_RESOURCE_ID_KEY in request context after authentication for stored resource scoping.

nodes.label: requireActor
nodes.rationale: Optional method to enforce per-agent least privilege; providers that omit it preserve the trusted-actor bypass, keeping the addition backward compatible.

nodes.label: resolveRouteFGA
nodes.rationale: Use only when route metadata must be derived centrally; a route map scales better than string-prefix checks.

nodes.label: validatePermissions
nodes.rationale: Validates the full set of permissions Mastra may emit at startup when a provider requires explicit slugs.

nodes.label: storedResources scoping
nodes.rationale: FGA authorizes access but does not filter stored records in shared storage; scoping is needed for multi-tenant apps.

nodes.label: RedisStreamsPubSub
nodes.rationale: A shared pub/sub backed by Redis Streams lets leases and signals coordinate across serverless instances, preventing a follow-up message from starting a duplicate run on another instance.

nodes.label: InlineLinkEntry
nodes.rationale: Object entries force a mime type and skip the HEAD request for sites like YouTube where HEAD returns text/html but the model treats the URL as video.

nodes.label: inlineMedia
nodes.rationale: Default list matches formats supported by major vision models; non-matching types are described as text summaries so models that reject unsupported types don't crash.

nodes.label: onMessage
nodes.rationale: Opt-in handler; omitted or false leaves unmentioned messages ignored so the bot does not reply to every readable message.

nodes.label: resolveResourceId
nodes.rationale: Lets apps with shared identity (e.g. SSO) decide memory ownership separately from the platform sender, avoiding split memory across platforms.

nodes.label: resolveThreadId
nodes.rationale: Runs only for new threads so reused threads keep their stored id and existing conversations don't depend on the resolver being available.

nodes.label: Chat SDK
nodes.rationale: Mastra uses Chat SDK for the channel layer so any compatible Chat SDK adapter can be wired in with the same Mastra configuration pattern.

nodes.label: Mastra Connect
nodes.rationale: Manages channel credentials for you, simplifying setup and maintenance when you don't want to configure a bot per channel yourself.

nodes.label: Channel Multimodal Content (inlineMedia / inlineLinks)
nodes.rationale: Only images are sent inline by default; unsupported types are described as text summaries so the agent knows about the file without failing on models that reject them.

nodes.label: Other Chat SDK Adapters
nodes.rationale: Any Chat SDK adapter factory compatible with channels.adapters can be used, so the platform guides are not the full list of supported platforms.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: The default in-memory pub/sub can't cross instance boundaries, so serverless deployments need a distributed pub/sub.

nodes.label: Serverless Channel Deployment
nodes.rationale: Serverless functions freeze after responding, so channels need a way to keep the function alive while the agent responds and a shared pub/sub so instances can coordinate.

nodes.label: Per-message Signal Metadata
nodes.rationale: Use signalMetadata for context that must stay attached to one message (it may be stored in memory or sent over pub/sub and is not added to the model prompt); use requestContext for run-scoped configuration.

nodes.label: Thread Context Fetching
nodes.rationale: On the first mention in a thread the agent may lack prior context, so earlier messages are fetched and saved into memory; subsequent messages don't re-fetch.

nodes.label: Thread Run Lease
nodes.rationale: Each run acquires a lease on its thread so one run owns the conversation at a time.

nodes.label: waitUntil
nodes.rationale: Vercel and AWS Lambda freeze the function as soon as the response is sent, so waitUntil is required there; Cloudflare Workers and Netlify Functions are detected automatically.

nodes.label: Channel Webhook Route (/api/agents/<AGENT_ID>/channels/<PLATFORM>/webhook)
nodes.rationale: The webhook acknowledges the platform before the agent finishes responding, so a 200 means received, not answered.

nodes.label: Chat SDK Adapter Catalog
nodes.rationale: The canonical source for available adapters; the in-doc list is only a snapshot and may be out of date.

nodes.label: filterRun()
nodes.rationale: Agent conversations can contain hundreds of messages with tool calls and metadata; filtering reduces noise and keeps each scorer focused.

nodes.label: Agent Scorer Type
nodes.rationale: type: 'agent' provides type safety and compatibility with both live agent scoring and trace scoring.

nodes.label: UnicodeNormalizer
nodes.rationale: Normalizes Unicode text to ensure consistent formatting and remove potentially problematic characters before messages are sent to the language model; always normalizes to NFKC form, which is not configurable.

nodes.label: filterRun()
nodes.rationale: Eligibility filters decide whether a scorer runs; filterRun() filters which messages a scorer sees once it runs.

nodes.label: Mastra Class
nodes.rationale: Scorers passed directly to runEvals need the scorers option on the Mastra class so they are registered and their scores persist.

nodes.label: notScorable()
nodes.rationale: Returning notScorable() from a scorer step skips the remaining steps and stores no score, which is how eligibility can depend on what happened in the run.

nodes.label: Step Class
nodes.rationale: Step-level scorers receive that step's own input and output so quality can be measured at each step instead of only on the final answer.

nodes.label: Eligibility Filters
nodes.rationale: Filtering occurs before sampling so sampling.rate applies only to matching runs; filters are plain JSON so they are unaffected by durable agent state serialization.

nodes.label: Live Evaluations
nodes.rationale: Scorers run asynchronously in the background so agents and workflows stay responsive while quality is monitored continuously.

nodes.label: Sampling Rate
nodes.rationale: Sampling is deterministic per trace (derived from the trace ID, not random) so scorers at the same rate score the same traces and coverage is reproducible.

nodes.label: Score Persistence
nodes.rationale: Registration is what lets Mastra resolve a scorer's metadata before writing the score; the lookup compares only scorer IDs so a registered instance may use different configuration.

nodes.label: Scorers
nodes.rationale: AI outputs are non-deterministic, so scorers provide quantifiable metrics (typically 0-1) to objectively track agent quality and compare approaches.

nodes.label: Trace Evaluations
nodes.rationale: Scoring historical traces is useful for analyzing past performance, debugging, and batch evaluations.

nodes.label: InworldVoice
nodes.rationale: The per-call deliveryMode option is honored only by the inworld-tts-2 model.

nodes.label: authInfo
nodes.rationale: With the default bridge the authenticated user is available at authInfo.extra.user, but it must be populated from trusted authentication results.

nodes.label: createOAuthMiddleware
nodes.rationale: Serves protected-resource metadata and challenge requests without a bearer token; without a validator it accepts unvalidated tokens, which is development-only.

nodes.label: executeTool
nodes.rationale: Called directly by the REST execute route without a protocol client, so FGA enforcement must happen inside it.

nodes.label: mapAuthInfoToUser
nodes.rationale: Maps trusted MCP authentication information to the user consumed by FGA checks; mapping fields does not validate credentials.

nodes.label: MCPClient
nodes.rationale: Used when a Mastra application connects out to another MCP server; outgoing credentials serve a different boundary than incoming ones.

nodes.label: MCPOAuthClientProvider
nodes.rationale: One provider per MCP server keeps authorization session state from being shared across servers, but does not isolate users or issuers.

nodes.label: MCPServer
nodes.rationale: Used when a Mastra application exposes capabilities to third-party clients; the same app can be both client and server but the credentials serve different boundaries.

nodes.label: OAuthStorage
nodes.rationale: Default OAuth storage is in memory; custom storage controls persistence and must be scoped to the user and connection.

nodes.label: server.auth
nodes.rationale: Built-in authentication for MCP REST routes depends on it; without it requiresAuth:true does not enforce authentication.

nodes.label: server.mcpOptions.setRequestAuth
nodes.rationale: Used by the auth bridge when no existing req.auth is present, before falling back to building authInfo from request context.

nodes.label: MCP auth bridge
nodes.rationale: Preserves an existing req.auth, otherwise uses setRequestAuth or builds authInfo from request context.

nodes.label: Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD)
nodes.rationale: Recommended by the specification; clients supporting all registration options should prefer existing pre-registered information when available.

nodes.label: Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)
nodes.rationale: Remains optional for compatibility but is deprecated for new implementations; MCPOAuthClientProvider does not support it.

nodes.label: Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA) provider
nodes.rationale: Filters tools/list and enforces tools/call authorization, but does not authorize resources, prompts, or subscriptions.

nodes.label: MCP REST routes
nodes.rationale: Registered alongside the MCP transport for Studio; custom middleware that only guards /mcp or /sse leaves them open, so default-deny /api/mcp/*.

nodes.label: Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
nodes.rationale: Clients must implement it, verify the authorization server advertises support, and use S256 when technically capable.

nodes.label: Protected Resource Metadata
nodes.rationale: Required by the specification so clients can discover the authorization servers for an MCP server; advertising an issuer does not validate a token.

nodes.label: MastraPlatformExporter
nodes.rationale: Replaced CloudExporter; CloudExporter remains available for backward compatibility but is deprecated.

nodes.label: addFeedback()
nodes.rationale: Optional on the observability entrypoint; rehydrates the target trace/span from configured storage before emitting the feedback event, unless a live correlationContext is supplied.

nodes.label: chatRoute()
nodes.rationale: Passes the run's traceId to the messageMetadata callback so the client has it on the live message without a server lookup.

nodes.label: createFeedback()
nodes.rationale: Storage-level write, so a timestamp is required.

nodes.label: deleteFeedback()
nodes.rationale: Idempotent, max 1,000 ids per request; useful when a comment contains sensitive data. ClickHouse uses lightweight deletes, so open-source deployments must configure a retention period to physically purge rows.

nodes.label: getFeedbackAggregate()
nodes.rationale: OLAP queries operate only on numeric value fields.

nodes.label: MastraPlatformExporter
nodes.rationale: Forwards emitted feedback events to Mastra Platform because the hosted query API has no creation route.

nodes.label: MastraStorageExporter
nodes.rationale: Keeps the trace available so addFeedback() can rehydrate it when feedback is added after the traced execution finished.

nodes.label: PostHog Exporter
nodes.rationale: Sends feedback as native $ai_feedback events that appear on the linked trace in PostHog.

nodes.label: correlationContext
nodes.rationale: Lets feedback be emitted during a live traced execution without rehydrating the trace from storage.

nodes.label: Feedback Record
nodes.rationale: Feedback captures human-in-the-loop signals (thumbs, ratings, comments, corrections) attached to a trace or span, unlike metrics and scores which are usually machine-generated.

nodes.label: Observability Event Bus
nodes.rationale: Feedback flows through the event bus so any exporter that supports feedback forwards it automatically.

nodes.label: traceId
nodes.rationale: Assistant messages carry traceId in content.metadata so feedback collected at generation time and later against a stored message anchor to the same trace; messages produced while tracing is disabled have no traceId.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: PubSub backends can redeliver an event after a timeout, failed acknowledgement, or crash, so the runtime assumes at-least-once delivery and handlers should be idempotent.

nodes.label: Graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: Stop accepting new webhook or signal requests before shutdown so new requests don't arrive while the process exits.

nodes.label: Thread lease
nodes.rationale: The renewal interval is one-third of the lease TTL so the owner has time to recover from a missed renewal before its claim expires; if renewal fails and the local deadline passes the owner stops the run because continuing would mean two owners writing to one conversation.

nodes.label: Shared PubSub backend
nodes.rationale: A shared backend fixes delivery between processes: a second instance publishes on the thread topic and the owning instance consumes, instead of starting a competing run on the same thread.

nodes.label: Serverless execution
nodes.rationale: Serverless functions can freeze as soon as they return a response, so a function that starts a run must keep it alive via waitUntil and consume the output stream.

nodes.label: Thread ownership
nodes.rationale: Only the lease holder may run a thread; other processes route signals to it, which prevents competing runs writing to the same conversation.

nodes.label: AgentController Session
nodes.rationale: Session wraps the Agent methods and manages the thread subscription, so most applications can use the Agent methods directly.

nodes.label: accepted result (wake/deliver/persist/discard/blocked)
nodes.rationale: Every send returns an accepted promise that resolves when Mastra decides what to do, not when a run finishes, so callers can catch routing failures without blocking on the run.

nodes.label: ifActive / ifIdle behavior
nodes.rationale: Applications usually keep the defaults (active threads receive input, idle threads wake); overrides exist only for a different result such as persisting without starting a run.

nodes.label: Interruption window
nodes.rationale: Mastra can cancel and retry a model request with new input while the model produces only reasoning or metadata; the window closes once text, a tool call, or other content is produced so running tools are never cancelled or repeated.

nodes.label: mapAuthInfoToUser
nodes.rationale: Maps MCP transport auth data from extra.authInfo into the user value used by Mastra FGA checks, for OAuth-protected MCP servers registered with an FGA provider.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Already carries authInfo and the mapped user, so it can be passed straight through when a tool calls an agent.

nodes.label: requestState
nodes.rationale: Provides integrity protection for input_required continuation state via a shared HMAC key of at least 32 bytes; without a key the server generates one per process.

nodes.label: setRequestAuth
nodes.rationale: The hook replaces the default authInfo mapping when your own middleware performs verification; leaving req.auth unset inside the hook opts the request out of auth info entirely.

nodes.label: authInfo
nodes.rationale: Whatever is set on req.auth in HTTP middleware becomes available as authInfo in tools and as requestContext.get('authInfo') in resource and prompt callbacks.

nodes.label: fga.resourceMapping / fga.permissionMapping
nodes.rationale: Lets MCP clients use a different authorization scope than internal agent or workflow tool execution; applies only to tools/list and tools/call for this server.

nodes.label: sendNotification (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated because the protocol has no server-initiated requests; replaced by context.mcp.log(), context.mcp.progress() and context.suspend().

nodes.label: sendRequest (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated because the protocol has no server-initiated requests; replaced by context.mcp.log(), context.mcp.progress() and context.suspend().

nodes.label: NovaSonicVoice
nodes.rationale: Static credentials are optional; the default AWS credential provider chain is used when none are passed.

nodes.label: Speech-to-Speech (STS)
nodes.rationale: STS enables real-time interactions but comes at high cost.

nodes.label: ProcessHandle.closeStdin()
nodes.rationale: Signals EOF for commands that read until stdin closes; writer.end() also closes stdin but finishes without error on providers lacking a close primitive.

nodes.label: SandboxProcessManager.get()
nodes.rationale: Reading an exited process dismisses it by default; { release: false } lets one reader inspect output without taking it from another, such as the agent that started it.

nodes.label: SandboxProcessManager.list()
nodes.rationale: An exited process stays in the list until something reads it with get(pid), so a finished command's output can still be read.

nodes.label: MastraSandbox
nodes.rationale: When a process manager is provided, MastraSandbox automatically creates a default executeCommand implementation using spawn() + wait(), so providers don't need to implement both.

nodes.label: ProcessHandle
nodes.rationale: Exposes reader/writer streams so Node.js stream-based protocols like LSP or JSON-RPC can be layered on top of stdio.

nodes.label: SandboxProcessManager
nodes.rationale: Abstract base class so custom sandbox providers only implement spawn() and list(); the base class automatically wraps methods with ensureRunning() so the sandbox starts before any process operation.

nodes.label: SandboxProcessManager.spawn()
nodes.rationale: Returns a ProcessHandle immediately without waiting for the process to finish, enabling background processes.

nodes.label: ProcessHandle.wait()
nodes.rationale: Callbacks passed to wait() are automatically removed when it resolves.

nodes.label: LocalSandbox
nodes.rationale: Runs commands on the application host by default and isn't isolated or secure; enable native isolation or use a remote/container sandbox when running untrusted code.

nodes.label: SandboxFeatureNotSupportedError
nodes.rationale: Because a resolver-backed sandbox isn't known until request time, Mastra initially exposes every sandbox tool; calling one unsupported by the resolved backend fails with this error.

nodes.label: WORKSPACE_TOOLS
nodes.rationale: Configured capabilities determine which tools are available; tool configuration can then disable, rename, or add approval policies to those tools.

nodes.label: FileUploadProcessor
nodes.rationale: Only the prompt sent to the model changes; stored messages keep their files so the thread, clients such as Studio, and other agents still have the original file. Uploaded paths keep nothing of the original name but the extension, because a path that looks like the name invites the model to retype one from the other and ask the sandbox for a file that doesn't exist.

nodes.label: LanguageDetector
nodes.rationale: lastMessageOnly exists to keep LLM calls flat as conversation history grows; minTextLength exists because short text is often unreliable for language detection.

nodes.label: ModelSelectionProcessor
nodes.rationale: Intended for cost routing: keep a capable model as the agent's configured default and downgrade to a cheaper model when a decision model is confident. Routing fails open because the worst case is paying for the model already configured — the opposite of the fail-closed stance appropriate for tool approval. scope defaults to 'run' because the opening call is the cheapest one, so routing only it captures very little saving.

nodes.label: Background processes
nodes.rationale: By default background processes inherit the agent's abort signal and stop when the agent disconnects; set abortSignal to a custom signal or null/false when the process should continue after the request ends.

nodes.label: Filesystem
nodes.rationale: Sandboxes are often temporary, so a filesystem gives the agent a place to read, write, and search files that can outlive the sandbox; filesystems also work without a sandbox.

nodes.label: Native isolation
nodes.rationale: Restricts filesystem and network access at the operating-system level using Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) on macOS and Bubblewrap (bwrap) on Linux.

nodes.label: Network and credential safety
nodes.rationale: Mastra doesn't define one network policy for every backend and provides no backend-neutral credential broker, so block outbound access or allowlist only needed destinations at creation time and give each command only the credentials it needs.

nodes.label: Sandbox persistence
nodes.rationale: Persistence is backend-specific: files and processes aren't guaranteed to survive a stop or restart, and the sandbox id isn't a cross-backend persistence guarantee.

nodes.label: Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Gives an agent an isolated environment to run commands, execute code, install dependencies, and manage processes that would be risky, resource-intensive, or impractical to run directly inside the application.

nodes.label: Sandbox provider interface
nodes.rationale: Implement this interface to add a sandbox provider that Mastra doesn't support out of the box.

nodes.label: Sandbox resolver
nodes.rationale: A static sandbox is shared across every request and memory thread; use a resolver with sandboxCacheKey when each user, tenant, or thread needs a separate environment.

nodes.label: Extractor
nodes.rationale: Lets OM persist specific values alongside observations; adding a schema makes it run as a follow-up structured output request, while schema-less extractors are inline string extractors emitted directly in the Observer or Reflector response.

nodes.label: manageWorkingMemory
nodes.rationale: Lets the Observer manage working memory automatically so updates don't depend on the main agent remembering to make them, and keeps working memory prompt-cache friendly by moving it into state signals.

nodes.label: ModelByInputTokens
nodes.rationale: Selects a model tier at runtime from inclusive `upTo` token thresholds so cheaper models handle small inputs and stronger models handle large contexts.

nodes.label: observeAttachments
nodes.rationale: Drops attachments before they reach a text-only Observer while keeping readable placeholders so the Observer can still reason about what was shared without receiving the binary payload.

nodes.label: onExtracted
nodes.rationale: Lets applications normalize or react to custom extracted values before they're persisted.

nodes.label: observation.threadTitle
nodes.rationale: Opt-in: the Observer suggests a short thread title when the topic meaningfully changes, updating thread metadata for thread lists and status UI.

nodes.label: skillResultRedactor
nodes.rationale: Replaces skill tool results with a placeholder while keeping the tool call, so the Observer records which skill was used without ingesting the skill text.

nodes.label: bufferOnIdle
nodes.rationale: Runs background observation buffering when an agent turn ends and the agent becomes idle, so short turns are observed without waiting for the next turn or the messageTokens threshold; separate from bufferTokens (step-time async buffering).

nodes.label: Early Activation
nodes.rationale: Activates buffered observations before the token threshold is reached, useful when a prompt cache is likely to expire or when the agent changes model providers.

nodes.label: Observer
nodes.rationale: Creates concise observations once message history tokens exceed a threshold (default 30,000), replacing raw message history as it grows.

nodes.label: Reflector
nodes.rationale: Reorganizes, combines and condenses observations into long-term memory, mirroring how human reflection works.

nodes.label: Temporal Gap Markers
nodes.rationale: Insert a short reminder before a new user message when enough time has passed, helping the agent and UI see the conversation resumed after a useful pause; off by default.

nodes.label: Client SDK session.switchModel(modelId, { thinkingLevel })
nodes.rationale: Exposes the same operation as session.model.switch on the client side.

nodes.label: session.model.set({ modelId })
nodes.rationale: Sets the active model in memory only — no persistence, no model-use reporting, no model_changed event.

nodes.label: session.model.switch(modelId, options?)
nodes.rationale: Both live values (model and thinking level) are updated before events are emitted so listeners never observe a partially applied switch; omitting the option preserves the existing thinking-level override.

nodes.label: session.state
nodes.rationale: Updates are serialized and validated against the stateSchema; a queued write keeps its source thread so switching threads mid-write does not apply one thread's preferences to another.

nodes.label: session.state.update(updater)
nodes.rationale: Runs the updater atomically inside the write queue so read-modify-write changes always see the latest state.

nodes.label: model_changed event
nodes.rationale: Every model_changed event includes the current { modelId, thinkingLevel } even when the thinking level is unchanged, so listeners can rely on a complete payload.

nodes.label: Persistence boundaries
nodes.rationale: Configured storage persists threads, messages, token usage and thread settings, but arbitrary custom state, grants, follow-ups and the active stream require host-managed persistence; a cold restart can recover only persisted settings and controller defaults.

nodes.label: state_changed event
nodes.rationale: Emitted with the changed keys only for visible state changes.

nodes.label: stateSchema
nodes.rationale: Passed to the AgentController; all state writes are validated against it before state_changed is emitted.

nodes.label: Thinking level
nodes.rationale: Must be one of 'off', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max' and accepted by the controller's state schema; undefined when the session has no override.

nodes.label: MastraAuthGoogle
nodes.rationale: Authenticates in order: encrypted session cookie first, then Google ID token verified against Google's JWKS endpoint. hostedDomain is a login hint only and is not used for authorization; allowedDomains is validated against the verified hd claim.

nodes.label: MastraRBACGoogle
nodes.rationale: If user.groups is already an array, that value is used and the Directory API is not called; group lookups are LRU-cached. Requires a Mastra EE license in production.

nodes.label: MastraAuthNeon
nodes.rationale: Verifies bearer tokens as JWTs against the Neon Auth JWKS endpoint and falls back to validating Neon Auth session tokens through the session API. refreshSession does not force a remote refresh because Neon Auth refreshes sessions automatically at its configured update interval.

nodes.label: MastraRBACNeon
nodes.rationale: Role lookup cache defaults to 60,000 ms TTL and 1,000 entries. Requires a Mastra EE license in production.

nodes.label: MastraAuthOkta
nodes.rationale: Authenticates in order: encrypted session cookie first, then JWT fallback verified against Okta's JWKS endpoint with iss checked against issuer and aud against audience. The audience option does not affect the ID token verified during the SSO login flow, which always uses the client ID.

nodes.label: MastraRBACOkta
nodes.rationale: Requires an Okta API token to fetch user groups from the Okta API; group lookups are LRU-cached. Requires a Mastra EE license in production.

nodes.label: @mastra/codemod CLI
nodes.rationale: Automated codemods let users run all v1 codemods at once with npx @mastra/codemod@latest v1.

nodes.label: @mastra/observability
nodes.rationale: OTEL telemetry replaced with a dedicated observability package and exporters; telemetry: config must migrate to observability: or observability data stops flowing.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Renamed from RuntimeContext throughout the codebase.

nodes.label: Migration checklist
nodes.rationale: Ordered starting with high-impact changes that affect most applications.

nodes.label: Mastra v1
nodes.rationale: Released January 2026; new projects should start on v1 and existing projects should upgrade to continue receiving updates and support.

nodes.label: buildResponseCacheKey
nodes.rationale: Re-export it to override individual fields while preserving the rest of the standard key shape.

nodes.label: ResponseCache
nodes.rationale: The cache key is derived from the resolved LanguageModelV2Prompt after memory has loaded and earlier input processors have transformed it, so two users with different memory contexts produce different cache keys; each step in an agentic tool loop is independently cached.

nodes.label: ResponseCacheContextOptions
nodes.rationale: cache, ttl and agentId are intentionally not overridable per call: they're instance-level concerns that shouldn't vary per request.

nodes.label: SemanticRecall
nodes.rationale: Hybrid processor: performs semantic search over history on input and creates embeddings for new messages on output so future turns can retrieve them.

nodes.label: E2BSandbox
nodes.rationale: Always exposes filesystem.

nodes.label: getEnv()
nodes.rationale: Returns a copy so mutations don't change the sandbox; use setEnv() for updates.

nodes.label: getInstructions()
nodes.rationale: Injected into the agent's system message when the workspace is assigned to an agent.

nodes.label: PlatformSandbox
nodes.rationale: Uses a fused get-or-create start() override because decomposing it would add round-trips; filesystem is available only when the provider is e2b.

nodes.label: RailwaySandbox
nodes.rationale: Uses a fused get-or-create start() override because decomposing it would add round-trips.

nodes.label: SandboxComputer
nodes.rationale: Coordinates are pixels from the top-left of the display; providers normalize their SDK semantics (key names, scroll units) onto this surface and expose richer native APIs through their own accessors.

nodes.label: setEnv()
nodes.rationale: The runtime environment applies to commands executed through the sandbox rather than the VM's own environment, so it is never written into the VM and survives provider pause and resume; precedence is provider defaults, then sandbox runtime env, then per-call env.

nodes.label: WorkspaceFilesystem
nodes.rationale: Native file API takes one request per operation instead of a shell command per step; the provider owns containment, so filesystem does not confine paths or symlinks to a workspace root.

nodes.label: WorkspaceSandbox interface
nodes.rationale: Defines how workspaces execute commands and manage background processes; optional capabilities (processes, computer, filesystem) degrade gracefully so their tools are simply unavailable when unimplemented.

nodes.label: Computer-use tools (mastra_workspace_computer_*)
nodes.rationale: Registered automatically by the workspace tools factory when a statically configured sandbox exposes the computer property.

nodes.label: mastra_workspace_apply_patch
nodes.rationale: Opt-in: only added when tools[WORKSPACE_TOOLS.FILESYSTEM.APPLY_PATCH].enabled is set; the top-level tools.enabled doesn't enable it. It checks every hunk before writing and leaves all files unchanged if any hunk fails to match.

nodes.label: maxMediaBytes
nodes.rationale: Files larger than this fall back to metadata-only output rather than being fully base64-encoded into context and persisted in storage on rehydration.

nodes.label: mediaTypes
nodes.rationale: Defaults to the cross-provider-safe intersection of image formats plus PDF; only applies when the caller doesn't pass an explicit encoding.

nodes.label: WORKSPACE_TOOLS
nodes.rationale: Constants used as config keys for per-tool overrides; the key stays the original constant even when the exposed tool name is remapped.

nodes.label: Filesystem tools
nodes.rationale: Added when a filesystem is configured; with a static filesystem, write tools are excluded in read-only mode, while with a runtime-defined filesystem write tools are always included and read-only is enforced at runtime.

nodes.label: Search tools
nodes.rationale: Added when BM25 or vector search is configured.

nodes.label: Tool name remapping
nodes.rationale: Only the name exposed to the agent changes; the config key remains the original WORKSPACE_TOOLS constant. Names must be unique or an error is thrown.

nodes.label: createCodeMode()
nodes.rationale: Because code mode runs model-authored code, you must choose its execution boundary deliberately by passing sandbox or using a workspace that provides one.

nodes.label: IsolatedVmCodeModeTransport
nodes.rationale: Runs the program in an in-process V8 isolate, so no sandbox is required: the isolate has no filesystem, network, or process access.

nodes.label: LocalSandbox
nodes.rationale: Runs the function as a host node process with host privileges, so only use it for trusted or local development.

nodes.label: QuickJsCodeModeTransport
nodes.rationale: Gives the same in-process boundary using a QuickJS runtime compiled to WebAssembly, at the cost of slower execution.

nodes.label: Least-privilege tool scoping
nodes.rationale: Use this for least-privilege scoping and to keep each tool's prompt surface small.

nodes.label: Agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: The standard streaming API for agents; returns a MastraModelOutput exposing textStream plus promises that resolve when the stream finishes.

nodes.label: stream.fullStream
nodes.rationale: Exposes all emitted event chunks, not just text, so callers can inspect tool calls, steps, and lifecycle events.

nodes.label: Run.stream()
nodes.rationale: Workflow streaming returns structured lifecycle events rather than incremental text chunks, enabling real-time progress tracking.

nodes.label: stream.textStream
nodes.rationale: Breaks the response into chunks so output streams progressively instead of arriving all at once.

nodes.label: toAISdkMessages()
nodes.rationale: Converts stored messages for useChat()'s initialMessages.

nodes.label: toAISdkStream()
nodes.rationale: Converts Mastra streams to AI SDK-compatible formats; defaults to AI SDK v5 for backward compatibility, so pass the version matching the installed SDK.

nodes.label: writer API
nodes.rationale: Shared by tools and workflow steps so they can emit custom events, data, or values into the active stream.

nodes.label: writer.custom()
nodes.rationale: Emits top-level stream chunks, useful when integrating with UI frameworks.

nodes.label: writer.write()
nodes.rationale: Must be awaited or the stream locks and throws a WritableStream is locked error.

nodes.label: Transient data chunks
nodes.rationale: data-* chunks are persisted by default; transient:true skips storage for large or high-frequency live-only data, which is then unavailable after a page refresh.

nodes.label: Workflow stream events
nodes.rationale: Events include runId and from at the top level so a run can be identified without inspecting the payload.

nodes.label: cloneThread()
nodes.rationale: Useful for branching conversations, creating checkpoints before destructive operations, or testing variations of a conversation.

nodes.label: copyThread()
nodes.rationale: Never returns message payloads and copies rows inside the database on LibSQL and PostgreSQL, for forking long threads without needing the copied messages returned.

nodes.label: Message history
nodes.rationale: The most basic and important form of memory; gives the LLM a view of recent messages in the context window so the agent can reference earlier exchanges.

nodes.label: Threads and resources
nodes.rationale: Each message belongs to a thread (conversation) and a resource (owning user or entity), which Mastra uses to organize conversations.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
