nodes.rationale: Recommended for long-running conversations because it keeps the prompt prefix stable, unlike the sliding lastMessages window which invalidates the provider prompt cache.

nodes.label: CorrelationContext
nodes.rationale: Shared context snapshot attached to observability signals, carrying entity hierarchy, user/organization identifiers, run, session, thread, request, environment, source, service name, experiment and tags.

nodes.label: describeProcessorPipeline
nodes.rationale: Reads the attributes Mastra owns and keeps everything else apart in `rest`, so a reader can show known fields without repeating them beside a raw JSON view. Returns undefined when the phase is missing or unknown, but still describes the pipeline when the payload is empty.

nodes.label: describeSpanInput
nodes.rationale: Derives a payload tag at read time from spanType and the value's shape; nothing is stored. Returns the JSON fallback for a span with no recorded phase, an unknown newer phase, or an empty payload.

nodes.label: describeSpanOutput
nodes.rationale: Derives a payload tag at read time from spanType and the value's shape; nothing is stored. Returns the JSON fallback for a span with no recorded phase, an unknown newer phase, or an empty payload.

nodes.label: ExportedScore
nodes.rationale: New exporters should prefer scoreSource over the deprecated source field and correlationContext.experimentId over the deprecated top-level experimentId field; top-level traceId/spanId are preferred for the scored target.

nodes.label: ObservabilityDropEvent
nodes.rationale: Emitted when the exporter pipeline drops observability events so custom exporters or bridges can forward them to external metrics or alerting systems.

nodes.label: ObservabilityExporter
nodes.rationale: addScoreToTrace is deprecated and preserved only for backwards compatibility: eval scores now flow through the unified observability bus as ScoreEvents, so new exporters should implement onScoreEvent instead.

nodes.label: ScoreEvent
nodes.rationale: A small observability bus envelope wrapping a bounded payload (ExportedScore), like LogEvent, MetricEvent and FeedbackEvent.

nodes.label: SpanInputMap
nodes.rationale: Only lists span types whose input Mastra writes itself with a fixed shape; every other type keeps `any` because tool arguments and workflow data are caller-defined, MODEL_CHUNK carries several chunk shapes on one span type, and GENERIC is the escape hatch for custom spans. PROCESSOR_RUN is absent on purpose: three executors emit processor spans with different shapes, so payloads are narrowed at read time by recorded phase.

nodes.label: SpanOutputMap
nodes.rationale: Only lists span types whose output Mastra writes itself with a fixed shape; PROCESSOR_RUN is deliberately excluded because three executors emit processor spans with different shapes, narrowed at read time by phase instead.

nodes.label: SpanOutputProcessor
nodes.rationale: process() must mutate the span in place and return the same instance (or undefined to drop it): a copy such as { ...span } cannot be exported because exportSpan() and isValid are instance members of the live span, so returning one logs a processor error and drops the span.

nodes.label: SpanType
nodes.rationale: SKILL_RESOLUTION is deprecated in favour of SKILL_ACTION with operation 'resolve' and is no longer emitted, but is retained so stored traces keep resolving. PROCESSOR_RUN is the default processor span type; a processor may declare a different span type so its span names the subsystem it belongs to.

nodes.label: SpanTypeMap
nodes.rationale: Defines which attribute interface is used for each span type when creating or processing spans.

nodes.label: autoIndexPaths
nodes.rationale: Runs as part of workspace.init(); passing the workspace to new Mastra() registers it but doesn't initialize it or build the index, and it doesn't support a filesystem resolver because no provider is selected at init time.

nodes.label: MongoDBVector
nodes.rationale: MongoDB embeds new documents in the background, so content indexed moments ago may not show up in search results yet.

nodes.label: mastra_workspace_index tool
nodes.rationale: Because it can trigger embedding calls and vector-store writes, require approval when agents shouldn't mutate the index without review.

nodes.label: workspace.init()
nodes.rationale: Call once during startup before serving requests; calling it again rescans paths and clears the process-local BM25 index before rebuilding it.

nodes.label: Batch embedder
nodes.rationale: A single-text embedder makes a separate provider call for each document, so large indexes should use a provider batch API with batch: true and maxBatchSize.

nodes.label: BM25 keyword search
nodes.rationale: Scores documents by term frequency and document length and needs no external service or embedding model.

nodes.label: Hybrid search
nodes.rationale: Combines keyword and semantic results; used by default when both BM25 and vector search are configured and no mode is passed.

nodes.label: Search index
nodes.rationale: Queries read the index, not the live filesystem, so filesystem and index mutations are independent and content from databases or APIs can also be indexed.

nodes.label: Vector search
nodes.rationale: Uses embeddings to find semantically similar content, requiring a vector store and an embedder.

nodes.label: mapUserToResourceId
nodes.rationale: Easiest way to set MASTRA_RESOURCE_ID_KEY; when the resource ID is derived this way clients can omit memory.resource from request bodies because the server-derived value always takes precedence.

nodes.label: MASTRA_MESSAGE_AUTHOR_KEY
nodes.rationale: Names who sent a user message so a thread shared by several people can show who wrote what.

nodes.label: MASTRA_RESOURCE_ID_KEY
nodes.rationale: Forces all memory operations to use this resource ID; the server validates that accessed threads belong to this resource and returns 403 otherwise. Used to implement user isolation in multi-tenant applications.

nodes.label: MASTRA_SCOPES_KEY
nodes.rationale: Sets the scopes the agent run acts as; a resource: or thread: scope that conflicts with another resource or thread value returns a 400 error.

nodes.label: MASTRA_THREAD_ID_KEY
nodes.rationale: Forces thread operations to use this thread ID, overriding client-provided values.

nodes.label: promptRegistry
nodes.rationale: Fetching instructions from a prompt registry at runtime allows prompts to be updated without redeploying, running experiments with variants, and tracking prompt usage across agents.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Primarily used for passing data into specific requests; distinct from agent memory, which handles conversation history and state persistence across multiple calls.

nodes.label: requestContextSchema
nodes.rationale: Validates request context values at runtime, catching missing or invalid context values early, providing clear error messages and type inference within the component.

nodes.label: Studio
nodes.rationale: Request context presets add a dropdown to the request context editor in Studio so configurations can be switched without manually editing JSON each time.

nodes.label: Request context best practices
nodes.rationale: Defining the same required fields in the schema that middleware sets makes the contract between middleware and components explicit and validated.

nodes.label: Server middleware
nodes.rationale: Runtime server middleware can populate requestContext from the incoming request, e.g. setting temperature-unit from the CF-IPCountry header so responses match the user's locale.

nodes.label: DurableAgent.abortRunStream()
nodes.rationale: Only needs the runId, so a later request can stop a run it didn't start; requires a shared PubSub backend in multi-process deployments.

nodes.label: DurableAgent.abortThreadStream()
nodes.rationale: expectedRunId prevents aborting a successor run that became active before the request was handled.

nodes.label: createDurableAgent()
nodes.rationale: Recommended way to create a DurableAgent; prefer the factory unless subclassing.

nodes.label: createEventedAgent()
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget execution on the built-in evented workflow engine; events on PubSub drive execution independently of the caller.

nodes.label: DurableAgent
nodes.rationale: Wraps an Agent with durable execution and resumable streams so a client can disconnect and reconnect without missing events.

nodes.label: DurableAgent.listActiveRuns()
nodes.rationale: Lists runs left in running status after a crash so recoverActiveRuns() can re-drive them; requires persistent storage.

nodes.label: DurableAgent.prepare()
nodes.rationale: Registers the run and returns serialized workflow input so callers control when and how the workflow is triggered.

nodes.label: DurableAgent.recoverActiveRuns()
nodes.rationale: Re-drives a run from its last persisted snapshot; sub-agent delegation is one tool step, so tools must be idempotent to avoid repeating side effects.

nodes.label: shouldCache
nodes.rationale: Per-topic opt-out of the replay cache trades replay for minimum publish latency on hot topics when the cache is remote.

nodes.label: shouldPersistSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Default always persists pending, paused, and suspended (required for human-in-the-loop resume) and running only when recovery.durableAgents is 'auto'.

nodes.label: generate
nodes.rationale: Standard API with full AI SDK v5 and v2 model compatibility; internally calls stream() and awaits getFullOutput().

nodes.label: generateLegacy
nodes.rationale: Legacy API maintaining backward compatibility with AI SDK v4 and v1 models.

nodes.label: stream
nodes.rationale: Standard API with full AI SDK v5 and v2 model compatibility.

nodes.label: streamLegacy
nodes.rationale: Legacy API maintaining backward compatibility with AI SDK v4 and v1 models.

nodes.label: experimental_output
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favor of structuredOutput.

nodes.label: format option
nodes.rationale: Lets callers choose between 'mastra' (default) and 'aisdk' (AI SDK v5 compatible) output.

nodes.label: memory option
nodes.rationale: resourceId and threadId moved into the memory object.

nodes.label: modelSettings
nodes.rationale: Unifies temperature and other model settings.

nodes.label: output
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favor of structuredOutput.

nodes.label: structuredOutput
nodes.rationale: Enhanced structured output with model override and custom options; replacement for experimental_output and output.

nodes.label: excludeSpanTypes
nodes.rationale: Drops spans by type before processors and spanFilter run; use for broad, low-overhead filtering of whole span categories.

nodes.label: spanFilter
nodes.rationale: Use when filtering depends on attributes, metadata, timing, or entity identifiers; if spanFilter throws, Mastra keeps the span and logs the error to avoid silent data loss.

nodes.label: ExportedSpan
nodes.rationale: Lightweight version of Span without methods or circular references, used for tracing exporters.

nodes.label: NoOpSpan
nodes.rationale: Returned when tracing is disabled (sampling returns false) so span calls remain safe no-ops.

nodes.label: createIndex()
nodes.rationale: Index dimension must match the embedding model output and cannot be changed after creation, so a different model requires deleting and recreating the index.

nodes.label: LanceVectorStore
nodes.rationale: LanceDB is an embedded vector database built on the Lance columnar format, suitable for local development or cloud deployment.

nodes.label: UpstashVector
nodes.rationale: Upstash creates indexes (namespaces) automatically, so no createIndex call is needed.

nodes.label: Shared Vector Store Interface
nodes.rationale: A consistent interface across vector databases lets the same createIndex/upsert/query code work regardless of backend.

nodes.label: Run.cancel()
nodes.rationale: Cancellation triggers the abort signal and prevents subsequent steps; steps must actively check the abort signal to be canceled mid-execution.

nodes.label: Run.restart()
nodes.rationale: Restarts an active run that lost connection to the server, continuing from the last active step.

nodes.label: Run.resume()
nodes.rationale: resume() atomically claims the run by moving stored status from suspended to running so downstream steps and side effects run once per suspension.

nodes.label: Run.startAsync()
nodes.rationale: Use startAsync() for long-running workflows, scheduled triggers, and background processing; with Inngest workflows start() polls for completion which can fail and cause retries, while startAsync() avoids this issue.

nodes.label: WORKFLOW_RESUME_ALREADY_CLAIMED error
nodes.rationale: The claim is enforced atomically only by storage adapters that report supportsConcurrentUpdates(); adapters without atomic read-modify-write support can't enforce it.

nodes.label: ClaudeSDKAgent
nodes.rationale: Doesn't accept Mastra's tools option because the Claude SDK owns the agent loop; tools must be supplied as Claude SDK MCP servers via sdkOptions.mcpServers.

nodes.label: CursorSDKAgent
nodes.rationale: Cursor local agents require an explicit model set in sdkOptions.model.

nodes.label: OpenAISDKAgent
nodes.rationale: Creates the OpenAI SDK agent lazily on first use.

nodes.label: SDK agents
nodes.rationale: Register Claude, Cursor, or OpenAI SDK-backed agents while the provider SDK retains control of the runtime, tools, permissions, and agent loop.

nodes.label: MCP Servers (sdkOptions.mcpServers)
nodes.rationale: Claude Agent SDK custom tools are provided through Claude SDK MCP servers; a Mastra tool can't be passed directly to createSdkMcpServer().

nodes.label: CachingPubSub
nodes.rationale: Wraps EventEmitterPubSub to record published events per topic so a late or reconnecting subscriber can catch up before continuing with live events.

nodes.label: EventEmitterPubSub
nodes.rationale: Default backend; delivers events in process using a Node.js EventEmitter so it works without any external service, but events are not persisted and do not reach other processes.

nodes.label: GoogleCloudPubSub
nodes.rationale: Distributed pull-mode backend that persists events, but does not provide leases across hosts.

nodes.label: RedisStreamsPubSub
nodes.rationale: Distributed pull-mode backend that persists events for redelivery and provides leases across hosts.

nodes.label: UnixSocketPubSub
nodes.rationale: Used when several processes on the same machine need to share a stream; elects one process as broker and re-elects if the broker exits.

nodes.label: Inheriting background intent from subagent
nodes.rationale: Subagent-level configuration travels with the agent, keeping its background behavior the same under every supervisor, whereas supervisor-side opt-in centralizes tuning in one place.

nodes.label: Storage backend requirement
nodes.rationale: Tasks are persisted so they survive process restarts.

nodes.label: Subagents in the background
nodes.rationale: Opting each subagent in on the supervisor is clearer and lets timeoutMs be tuned per subagent in one place.

nodes.label: Agent Signals
nodes.rationale: Sending a signal to an active agent run publishes an event on a thread topic so a run executing in another process receives it.

nodes.label: Background Tasks
nodes.rationale: A task manager dispatches work to a worker group and fans task lifecycle updates out to subscribers, keeping background task streams live.

nodes.label: Consumer Groups
nodes.rationale: Members of the same group split events so each event is handled once; a subscriber without a group receives every event, fanning the stream out.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: Serves as Mastra's internal event bus; the backend is set once on the Mastra instance and applies to all built-in systems at once.

nodes.label: Workflow Execution
nodes.rationale: The scheduler publishes a workflow.start event and a long-lived worker consumes it to run the workflow.

nodes.label: Durable Agents
nodes.rationale: Claim each run through a lease when the workflows store doesn't support run fencing, so crash recovery can tell whether another process still drives the run.

nodes.label: cleanup()
nodes.rationale: Tears the run down: unsubscribes from PubSub, removes the run from the registry, and deletes cached events so nobody can replay it. Must be called from the process that started the run; an automatic timer fires cleanupTimeoutMs after the run ends if skipped.

nodes.label: createDurableAgent()
nodes.rationale: In-process factory: no external infrastructure required, returns a DurableAgentStreamResult you can await directly, making it the fastest way to get started.

nodes.label: createEventedAgent()
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget: the workflow starts in the background without blocking the caller, so the HTTP handler that triggered the run need not wait for completion.

nodes.label: createInngestAgent()
nodes.rationale: Production deployments: Inngest adds step memoization, retries, and a monitoring dashboard, and its own replay provides durability so only suspended snapshots are persisted.

nodes.label: createStoredAgent()
nodes.rationale: Agents created through the API opt in with a durable field so the server wraps them with createDurableAgent() on hydration, requiring no code deployment.

nodes.label: detach()
nodes.rationale: Stops observing a run from outside the loop (e.g. on client disconnect) without stopping the run itself.

nodes.label: observe(runId, options?)
nodes.rationale: Calling observe(runId) without an offset is the supported general reconnect flow: it replays all available cached events before delivering live events. Observing does not own the run, so the run keeps going for other watchers.

nodes.label: shouldCache option
nodes.rationale: Lets a topic publish straight through when the cache is remote and resumption of that topic is not needed, avoiding cache round-trip latency.

nodes.label: untilIdle option
nodes.rationale: Keeps the stream connection open across background-task continuations until the agent is idle; maxIdleMs customizes the idle timeout (default 5 minutes).

nodes.label: Durable Agent
nodes.rationale: Use a durable agent when the client may drop and reconnect mid-stream, the agentic loop may outlive a single HTTP request, you need an observe/reconnect API, or you want Inngest-powered execution; a regular Agent with stream()/generate() is simpler for short-lived, request-scoped calls where the client stays connected.

nodes.label: Resumable Streams
nodes.rationale: Let a client reconnect and replay missed events, which requires the backend to keep recent history.

nodes.label: Durable Agent
nodes.rationale: Wraps the same agent loop in a workflow so run state persists and events publish through PubSub.

nodes.label: getDefaultOptions()
nodes.rationale: generate() and stream() validate RequestContext before calling getDefaultOptions(), so a function-based default option cannot add a missing required value in time for validation.

nodes.label: maxSteps
nodes.rationale: Treat maxSteps as a bound on model steps rather than an application completion rule.

nodes.label: processInput
nodes.rationale: processInput remains useful for message transformation and state needed later in the loop, but it cannot change initial validation or completed skill and input-processor resolution.

nodes.label: processLLMRequest
nodes.rationale: Changes only the prompt sent for that provider call, for temporary provider-facing changes that should not alter stored conversation history.

nodes.label: processOutputResult
nodes.rationale: Runs once per request on the completed result and messages, whether the run completes normally or the provider throws.

nodes.label: processToolResult
nodes.rationale: Runs before a raw tool result enters the message list, allowing validation or redaction before later model steps or persistence.

nodes.label: stopWhen
nodes.rationale: Use stopWhen for application-specific completion rules evaluated against accumulated steps.

nodes.label: Agent Loop
nodes.rationale: Tool results often cause another model call because the model must use those results to produce its next response.

nodes.label: Durable Run
nodes.rationale: Durable execution persists run state and publishes events so supported runtimes can recover work and clients can reconnect; persistent production backends are required when state and event history must survive restarts.

nodes.label: Finalization
nodes.rationale: Finalization is separate from a model step: it operates on the result of the whole run rather than the response from one provider call.

nodes.label: Loop Iteration
nodes.rationale: An iteration commonly coincides with one model step, but that pairing is implementation behavior rather than a stable contract.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Auto-attached memory output processors run after configured output processors so message history can persist the final form.

nodes.label: Preparation Phase
nodes.rationale: Preparation turns the agent definition and current request into a runnable model interaction; its tasks do not all happen in one strict sequence.

nodes.label: Regular Run
nodes.rationale: A regular run keeps the loop in the current process; if that process ends, the in-memory execution ends with it.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: RequestContext carries trusted runtime data but its values are not automatically included in the model prompt; a context value can only affect work that has not happened yet, so it should be set at the earliest trusted boundary.

nodes.label: Run
nodes.rationale: A run spans all work from one generate()/stream() call through the final result or error, including pause and resume during durable execution.

nodes.label: chatRoute()
nodes.rationale: Forwards the incoming request's AbortSignal to agent.stream(), the right default when a browser disconnect should cancel the model call.

nodes.label: createRoute()
nodes.rationale: Used in apiRoutes to parse and validate path/query params and bodies with Zod; schemas also infer handler parameters and generate OpenAPI metadata.

nodes.label: Custom API routes
nodes.rationale: Mastra automatically exposes registered agents and workflows via its server; custom HTTP routes are defined for additional behavior.

nodes.label: D1Store
nodes.rationale: Serverless SQL storage on Cloudflare D1; does not support the observability domain and enforces a 1 MiB maximum row size.

nodes.label: LanceStorage
nodes.rationale: High-performance storage and vector operations; does not support the observability domain.

nodes.label: Composite storage
nodes.rationale: Used when domains have different operational needs and each should be routed to the right backend.

nodes.label: observability domain
nodes.rationale: Writes high-volume telemetry and often queries aggregations, so a dedicated observability or OLAP backend is recommended.

nodes.label: Apache Arrow
nodes.rationale: LanceDB uses Apache Arrow data types internally; Mastra schema types are mapped to them.

nodes.label: MastraModelGateway.buildUrl()
nodes.rationale: Provider URLs containing placeholders such as ${ACCOUNT_ID} must be resolved inside buildUrl() from envVars or process.env before returning the final URL.

nodes.label: GatewayAuthResult
nodes.rationale: May include apiKey, bearerToken, headers and an optional source field to trace where auth came from.

nodes.label: MastraModelGateway.getId()
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favour of the id property.

nodes.label: MastraModelGateway
nodes.rationale: Abstract base class handling provider-specific logic for accessing language models: provider configuration, authentication, URL construction and model instantiation.

nodes.label: MastraModelGatewayInterface
nodes.rationale: Use this interface when you want to provide a plain object gateway instead of extending the base class.

nodes.label: ModelsDevGateway
nodes.rationale: models.dev is a provider registry and doesn't use a gateway ID prefix.

nodes.label: ProviderConfig
nodes.rationale: Pricing is expressed in USD per 1 million tokens with the same keys as a models.dev cost; @mastra/observability uses them for cost metrics when models.dev has no price for the model.

nodes.label: MastraModelGateway.resolveAuth()
nodes.rationale: Optional hook to implement when a gateway owns authentication; if omitted, Mastra falls back to getApiKey().

nodes.label: Step class
nodes.rationale: Scorers can be attached per step so you can see which step degraded quality in multi-step and RAG workflows, instead of only scoring the workflow's final answer.

nodes.label: Workflow.agent()
nodes.rationale: Unlike wrapping an agent with createStep(), .agent() records a declarative entry in the workflow graph, making the workflow portable: the same graph can be serialized and persisted as a dynamic workflow.

nodes.label: Workflow.branch()
nodes.rationale: Every branch whose condition evaluates to true runs; conditions are evaluated independently, so mutually exclusive conditions are needed when only one branch should run.

nodes.label: Workflow.classifier()
nodes.rationale: The classifier evaluates the complete previous step output, so a .map() must be inserted before .classifier() to select or reshape its input.

nodes.label: Workflow.commit()
nodes.rationale: Creating a run on a workflow with uncommitted step changes throws an error, so the definition must be finalized before execution.

nodes.label: Workflow.createRun()
nodes.rationale: resourceId associates a run with a specific resource such as a user or tenant, useful for multi-tenant applications and tracking who initiated a workflow.

nodes.label: Workflow.dountil()
nodes.rationale: Always runs the step at least once before evaluating the condition; iterationCount is 1 on the first evaluation.

nodes.label: Workflow.dowhile()
nodes.rationale: Always runs the step at least once before evaluating the condition; iterationCount is 1 on the first evaluation.

nodes.label: FactorySandbox
nodes.rationale: Everything provider-specific stays inside the object: Factory only calls the contract and reads provider for display. Factory recognizes subclasses by a brand the base class sets, so a plain object with the same shape isn't accepted.

nodes.label: FactorySandboxBuild
nodes.rationale: unknown means the provider can't read the status of a build it didn't start in this process.

nodes.label: FactorySandboxBuilds
nodes.rationale: Its presence is the capability: declaring builds lets Factory build the environment template ahead of sessions.

nodes.label: FactorySandboxContext
nodes.rationale: Scope secrets by factoryId, not factoryName: names can be edited and two factories can share one.

nodes.label: LocalFactorySandbox
nodes.rationale: Without env, commands only see an allow-list of host variables that git and TLS need, plus PATH, so app secrets stay out of commands that run in repository checkouts. Factory doesn't offer recreate for LocalFactorySandbox because its destroy() keeps the session directory.

nodes.label: MastraFactory
nodes.rationale: An explicit sandbox option always takes precedence; under mastra dev or NODE_ENV=development it installs LocalFactorySandbox so development doesn't start remote machines.

nodes.label: PublicSchema
nodes.rationale: Keep schema changes additive: the stored document outlives the schema that wrote it, so undeclared keys are dropped and the update retried before refusing.

nodes.label: factory-environment-build workflow
nodes.rationale: Scheduled and push builds skip when the last build is ready, no repository head moved and no template input changed.

nodes.label: AcpAgent
nodes.rationale: Wraps an ACP agent as a Mastra subagent with generate() and stream() support; keeps a reusable process alive across calls by default (persistSession true).

nodes.label: createACPTool()
nodes.rationale: Used when the parent Mastra agent should decide when to call the ACP agent as a tool; sends a task string and returns an output string.

nodes.label: LocalFilesystem
nodes.rationale: Fallback workspace backing at cwd or process.cwd() when no workspace is available.

nodes.label: AcpAgent model selection (getAvailableModels/setModel)
nodes.rationale: ACP agents may expose selectable models; pass model in the configuration to select after session creation or manage models at runtime.

nodes.label: onPermissionRequest
nodes.rationale: By default @mastra/acp selects the first option returned by the ACP agent; pass this hook for custom permission behavior.

nodes.label: Mastra Workspace
nodes.rationale: ACP file reads and writes requested through the protocol go through the workspace abstraction; the workspace covers only those requests, so the agent process is not sandboxed or isolated.

nodes.label: ACP Client
nodes.rationale: The default client rejects unknown extension methods with a "Method not found" error, which can abort the agent's turn, so createClient lets callers extend or replace it.

nodes.label: createACPTool()
nodes.rationale: Each tool execution creates its own ACP connection and session; use AcpAgent instead when a reusable subagent instance with explicit session lifecycle control across calls is needed.

nodes.label: persistSession
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true so the child process stays alive across calls; set false when each prompt should run in an isolated process.

nodes.label: Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
nodes.rationale: Used to run compatible coding-agent processes as Mastra tools or subagents.

nodes.label: AgentController
nodes.rationale: Provides opinionated defaults for an ongoing session where the agent acts as a collaborator rather than a one-shot endpoint; use the Agent class directly for full control or request-response calls.

nodes.label: controller.init()
nodes.rationale: Initialize the shared controller host once and reuse it for many Sessions.

nodes.label: createCodingAgent()
nodes.rationale: Returns a standard Agent that already has a workspace, task tracking, and retries for transient model errors, which are the defaults Mastra Code runs on.

nodes.label: onSessionStart
nodes.rationale: Runs once per session after the session is bound to its mapped thread and before the first message; errors are logged and swallowed so a session that can't be configured still answers the message.

nodes.label: onStaleToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Approval gates live in memory, so every approval answered after a restart is stale; this hook settles the attempt the user answered instead of dropping it.

nodes.label: resolveResourceId
nodes.rationale: Only affects new threads; an existing thread keeps its stored resource ID.

nodes.label: subagent tool
nodes.rationale: Forked subagents preserve the parent prompt prefix and require memory on the controller, ignoring the definition's instructions, tools, allowlists, and default model.

nodes.label: Channels
nodes.rationale: Each external chat thread maps to one controller Session and Mastra thread.

nodes.label: goal config
nodes.rationale: The goal config auto-registers the state-signal projection, so the model always sees the current objective as <current-objective> without extra setup.

nodes.label: GoalEvaluationPayload
nodes.rationale: Emitted as a typed goal stream chunk each evaluation so a UI can show goal progress mid-run.

nodes.label: goal.judge
nodes.rationale: The judge model is the activation switch: if no judge resolves, the goal step performs no scoring or budget consumption and emits no goal chunk, and the gate covers every scorer including a custom goal.scorer.

nodes.label: goal.scorer
nodes.rationale: Replaces the built-in LLM-as-judge pipeline with a custom scorer; the custom scorer brings its own judging so prompt, tools, and maxSteps no longer apply.

nodes.label: isTaskComplete
nodes.rationale: Use isTaskComplete for a one-off completion check within a single stream() call; goals build on the same LLM-as-judge machinery but are durable and set through Agent methods.

nodes.label: goal.maxRuns
nodes.rationale: Bounds the loop: when runsUsed >= maxRuns the loop stops and the objective is marked paused; raise maxRuns and resume to continue. Defaults to 50.

nodes.label: updateObjectiveOptions()
nodes.rationale: Only provided fields are written; unset fields fall back to the agent's goal config, and per-objective values take precedence over that config.

nodes.label: Goal
nodes.rationale: A goal is durable and thread-scoped (stored in thread state, not passed per call) so the success criteria need not be re-supplied on every call and survive reloads and mid-run messages.

nodes.label: State-Signal Projection
nodes.rationale: Projects the persisted objective into the model's context as <current-objective>.

nodes.label: CompositeVersionedSkillSource
nodes.rationale: Mounts published skill versions from a content-addressable blob store under directories where Mastra can discover them.

nodes.label: skill_search tool
nodes.rationale: Without BM25 or vector search it falls back to case-insensitive text matching, keeping skill search available without a separate search configuration.

nodes.label: skillSource
nodes.rationale: An explicit skillSource doesn't fall back to the configured filesystem or local disk when a path is missing.

nodes.label: skill tool
nodes.rationale: Loading is stateless: instructions remain in the conversation as a tool result and the agent can call skill again if they leave context after compaction.

nodes.label: Agent skills (direct)
nodes.rationale: Use direct agent skills when a skill should be defined in one agent's code; a direct skill takes precedence over a filesystem-backed skill with the same name.

nodes.label: Dynamic skill paths
nodes.rationale: Mastra resolves the function for each execution and gives the agent the skill set for that request, so available skills can depend on request context.

nodes.label: Filesystem-backed skills
nodes.rationale: Directories of reusable instructions and supporting files discovered from configured paths and made available to every agent using that configuration.

nodes.label: SKILL.md
nodes.rationale: Keep the main workflow in SKILL.md and move detailed material to references/ so the agent only reads it when needed.

nodes.label: DuckDBConnection
nodes.rationale: Exported for sharing a single underlying database across multiple Mastra storage instances; most applications won't need it directly.

nodes.label: DuckDBStore
nodes.rationale: Embedded, file-based and starts instantly, so it is intended for local development of observability features; not recommended for production because it runs in-process, persists to a single local file, and fails on ephemeral filesystems.

nodes.label: prune()
nodes.rationale: Deletes in bounded, batched chunks (each batch its own transaction) so it never takes a long lock or bloats the transaction log; runs are resumable and cancellable, and it never runs a VACUUM.

nodes.label: RetentionConfig
nodes.rationale: Opt-in and age-based: unconfigured data is kept forever, so behavior doesn't change until you opt in.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Native TTL
nodes.rationale: ClickHouse applies its native time-to-live policy within the database instead of exposing prune().

nodes.label: MongoDB TTL Indexes
nodes.rationale: Simpler zero-maintenance automated deletion for fixed retention periods, at the cost of fine-grained control over deletion timing and rate.

nodes.label: DuckDBVector
nodes.rationale: Embedded high-performance vector search with no external server, using the VSS extension and HNSW indexing for lightweight local vector storage.

nodes.label: HNSW Index
nodes.rationale: Used for fast approximate nearest neighbor search in DuckDB vector collections.

nodes.label: Event-sourced Observability Strategy
nodes.rationale: Buffers spans in memory and writes completed events in batches, which is appropriate for development-scale traffic.

nodes.label: actionFingerprint
nodes.rationale: Fingerprints tool name and args so an approval is consumed once and only for the same canonical arguments that were reviewed; production should use a stable hash stored in durable storage scoped to user, run, tool call, and policy version.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Intended for conversational flows where users provide resume data in natural language, as opposed to programmatic control via resumeStream().

nodes.label: beforeToolCall hook
nodes.rationale: Binds approval to the exact tool name and arguments shown to the reviewer: if arguments drift before execution, the tool is blocked under the old approval.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Used to estimate whether a tool call needs human review when the decision depends on tool name and arguments; a refused question has no probability so it falls back to requiring approval.

nodes.label: declineToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Accepts an optional reason returned to the model in place of the tool result so the model can adjust instead of retrying blindly; the reason is also stored on the tool call's approval metadata.

nodes.label: delegatedToolCallId
nodes.rationale: Used to tell apart two pauses from the same delegation, such as a question followed by an approval.

nodes.label: delegatedToolName
nodes.rationale: Names the deepest subagent tool call that actually paused, across multiple levels of delegation.

nodes.label: listSuspendedRuns()
nodes.rationale: Lets a later request rediscover the pending run from storage, since in production the approval often arrives after a page refresh, a server restart, or on a different server instance behind a load balancer.

nodes.label: requireApproval
nodes.rationale: Tool-level flag that pauses calls to that specific tool before execute runs, giving fine-grained control so only sensitive tools pause while others execute immediately.

nodes.label: requireToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Request-level option that pauses every tool call for that request; accepts a boolean or a per-call function so approval can be gated at runtime (e.g. only tools matching a name pattern).

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: Required so the agent knows what data structure to extract from the user's message for automatic resumption.

nodes.label: resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Manual resumption path used for programmatic control, webhooks, button clicks and external triggers.

nodes.label: sendToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: Falls back to storage-backed discovery when memory contains no active run for the thread.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Used instead of a tool without execute when the tool needs a structured answer from the user and also runs inside a subagent: subagents can't run client tools, but suspension propagates through the supervisor. suspend() doesn't throw, so code after await suspend(...) still runs before the tool pauses.

nodes.label: GET /agents/:agentId/suspended-runs
nodes.rationale: Exposes the same storage-backed discovery over HTTP so browser-based approval UIs can rediscover pending runs directly.

nodes.label: tool-call-resumed chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitted only when a real suspension or approval request is cleared; use it to mark a question as answered rather than inferring from the shape of the tool output, since a sub-agent delegation returns the sub-agent's result.

nodes.label: Automatic Tool Resumption
nodes.rationale: Detects suspended tools from message history on the next user message, extracts resumeData from the tool's resumeSchema, and resumes automatically — avoiding explicit UI or API actions for conversational flows.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop
nodes.rationale: Used when tools handle sensitive operations: destructive or irreversible actions, cost-heavy third-party API calls, and conditional confirmation where a tool discovers mid-execution that it needs user input.

nodes.label: Resuming After a Restart
nodes.rationale: Holding on to stream.runId only works while the process stays alive; storage-backed rediscovery is needed for production approval flows.

nodes.label: Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Minimal resume artifacts holding only what's needed to resume a suspended run; deleted once the run finishes. Tracing is used for the execution record and memory for conversation history.

nodes.label: Storage Provider
nodes.rationale: Suspended runs only survive restarts when a persistent storage provider is configured; the default in-memory store loses snapshots when the process exits.

nodes.label: Supervisor Agent
nodes.rationale: Coordinates multiple subagents; approval and suspension requests propagate up through the delegation chain and surface at the supervisor level so the decision can be made in one place.

nodes.label: cloneThread()
nodes.rationale: Useful for branching conversations, creating checkpoints before a destructive operation, or testing variations of a conversation.

nodes.label: copyThread()
nodes.rationale: Never returns message payloads and copies rows inside the database on LibSQL and PostgreSQL, for when copied messages aren't needed (e.g. forking a long thread).

nodes.label: generateTitle option
nodes.rationale: Use when building a chat interface that renders conversation titles in a thread list or sidebar; generation runs asynchronously after the agent responds so it doesn't affect response time.

nodes.label: getMemory()
nodes.rationale: Access point for memory functions for querying, cloning, or deleting threads and messages.

nodes.label: lastMessages option
nodes.rationale: The default of 10 messages keeps agents grounded in the conversation; counts every stored message including tool calls, results and signals, and the window slides forward each turn which invalidates the provider prompt cache.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Stores data locally in a mastra.db file in the examples.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Message history requires a storage adapter to persist conversations.

nodes.label: messageHistory token budget option
nodes.rationale: Message count is a poor proxy for context size, so a token budget is used instead; removing history in chunks keeps the prompt prefix stable across turns and helps provider prompt caches stay warm.

nodes.label: recall()
nodes.rationale: Supports pagination, date filtering, metadata filtering and semantic search for custom memory retrieval logic or rendering conversation history in a UI.

nodes.label: retainFullInput option
nodes.rationale: Disables input filtering so a self-assembled request input is processed exactly as sent, while stored history still loads.

nodes.label: toAISdkV5Messages()
nodes.rationale: Message queries return MastraDBMessage[]; conversion is needed to display messages in a frontend UI library.

nodes.label: WorkingMemoryStateProcessor
nodes.rationale: Auto-attached by Memory when useStateSignals is enabled; emits current working memory as a state signal with stateId 'working-memory'.

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.rationale: Use when OM isn't an option or when a structured, deterministic participants list readable and writable every turn is needed; scope is set to thread so the list belongs to the document, not an individual user.

nodes.label: Merge Semantics
nodes.rationale: Object fields are deep merged, null deletes a field, and arrays are replaced entirely rather than merged element-by-element.

nodes.label: Read-only Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Useful for routing agents and sub agents that need context but shouldn't update user profiles.

nodes.label: Resource-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Default scope: memory persists across all conversation threads for the same user (resourceId), enabling persistent user memory.

nodes.label: Working Memory Schema
nodes.rationale: Schemas give structured, type-safe JSON data with validation and programmatic access, and use merge semantics so only changed fields need to be provided.

nodes.label: Working Memory Template
nodes.rationale: Templates use replace semantics: the agent must provide the complete memory content on each update.

nodes.label: Thread-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Isolates working memory to individual conversation threads; switching scopes means the agent won't see memory from the other scope.

nodes.label: approveNetworkToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Network approval uses snapshots to capture execution state, so a storage provider must be enabled.

nodes.label: .network()
nodes.rationale: Returns a stream of events that can be iterated over; memory is required because .network() uses it to store task history and determine when a task is complete.

nodes.label: resumeNetwork()
nodes.rationale: Used to provide the data requested by a suspended primitive and continue execution.

nodes.label: Agent Networks
nodes.rationale: Deprecated and will be removed in a future major release; supervisor agents provide the same multi-agent coordination through a simpler API that improves control and debugging.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Creates a conversational flow where users provide required information naturally; requires memory, the same thread/resource, and a resumeSchema on the tool.

nodes.label: Routing Agent
nodes.rationale: Uses an LLM to interpret a request and decide which primitives (subagents, workflows, or tools) to call, in what order, and with what data.

nodes.label: Structured Output (structuredOutput / objectStream)
nodes.rationale: Pass structuredOutput to get typed, validated results; objectStream yields partial objects as they generate.

nodes.label: AttachmentUploader
nodes.rationale: Uploads base64 attachments to external storage and replaces them with URL references before messages are persisted, because some storage providers enforce record size limits that base64-encoded attachments can exceed.

nodes.label: MemoryInputFilter
nodes.rationale: Runs first so MessageHistory, SemanticRecall, and Observational Memory receive only the new input they need; trims client-echoed history and strips provider item metadata that could refer to items not in storage.

nodes.label: MessageHistory
nodes.rationale: Fetches the last N messages from storage and prepends them on input, then persists new messages after the model responds.

nodes.label: SemanticRecall
nodes.rationale: Requires a vector store plus an embedder unless the vector store generates embeddings itself; performs vector similarity search on input and creates embeddings for new messages on output.

nodes.label: WorkingMemory
nodes.rationale: Input-only processor: retrieves working memory state for the current thread and prepends it; requires a storage adapter.

nodes.label: abort() / tripwire
nodes.rationale: A processor abort() skips memory processors and persists nothing, whereas a caller abortSignal still runs output processors and saves the partial assistant text the user already saw.

nodes.label: Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Output guardrails run before memory processors save messages, so an abort prevents inappropriate content from being persisted to memory.

nodes.label: Memory processors
nodes.rationale: Used when combined memory exceeds the model's context limit, to filter, trim, or prioritize content so the most relevant information is preserved.

nodes.label: agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: For a one-off request it starts a run and reads the response directly, but doesn't give a subscription that follows later runs on the same thread.

nodes.label: client.getAgent()
nodes.rationale: The client returns the subscription stream and leaves run ownership on the server.

nodes.label: subscribeToThread()
nodes.rationale: Subscribing first means the subscription is already open when the input starts a run.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: Signals let you send input to an agent's thread at any time, including while the agent is working; by default Mastra delivers it to the active run or starts a run when the thread is idle, so callers don't need to check whether the agent is running.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Single storage message shape; content.parts is the authoritative body while toolInvocations, reasoning and experimental_attachments are flat mirrors kept only for AI SDK v4 compatibility.

nodes.label: messageHistory token budget
nodes.rationale: Preferred over lastMessages because message count is a poor proxy for context size; oldest remembered messages are dropped until the prompt fits maxTokens minus atMaxRemoveTokens, while protected content and linked tool call/result pairs are preserved.

nodes.label: saveMessages()
nodes.rationale: Needed only when writing messages manually (seeding a thread, importing a transcript, storing externally originated messages); agent.generate() and agent.stream() persist messages automatically.

nodes.label: GithubSignals
nodes.rationale: Polls subscribed PRs and sends notification signals to the agent thread when relevant activity occurs.

nodes.label: startPollingForThread()
nodes.rationale: Called for each persisted thread subscription to resume polling after a process restart.

nodes.label: GitHub CLI (gh api)
nodes.rationale: Real `gh api` responses are used to check repository permissions and GitHub App ownership before notifying the agent.

nodes.label: gitcrawl
nodes.rationale: The provider runs `gitcrawl sync` and reads its SQLite database to observe PR activity.

nodes.label: DynamoDBStore
nodes.rationale: Uses a single-table design with ElectroDB because it is optimized for DynamoDB's key-value and query capabilities, often giving better performance and capacity than mimicking relational models; the table and GSIs are provisioned externally so the adapter focuses only on interacting with the existing structure.

nodes.label: MastraStorage interface
nodes.rationale: Adhering to the same MastraStorage interface as other adapters keeps storage interchangeable within the Mastra Memory component despite the different underlying model.

nodes.label: Single-table design pattern
nodes.rationale: Deliberate design choice optimized for DynamoDB, differing from relational adapters that use one table per entity; lowers cost, improves performance, simplifies administration and enables cross-entity transactions.

nodes.label: TTL (time to live) configuration
nodes.rationale: Supports cost optimization, data lifecycle/retention policies, preventing unbounded table growth, and privacy compliance by purging personal data.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Set the editor option on MastraCompositeStore to use a separate backend for Editor data while other domains use the default store.

nodes.label: editor.agent.update()
nodes.rationale: The method saves changed snapshot fields as a new version that starts as an inactive draft; the published agent keeps serving its previous version until explicitly published.

nodes.label: Editor
nodes.rationale: Use Editor when an agent is defined in code but the people responsible for its behavior shouldn't edit the codebase, and when instructions or tools change often and need testing before reaching users.

nodes.label: Prompt Blocks
nodes.rationale: A prompt block is a saved piece of instruction text shared by more than one agent, so a policy change is published once instead of editing every agent.

nodes.label: Editor Versioning
nodes.rationale: Saving creates a draft while the live agent continues using the published version, so changes can be tested before going live.

nodes.label: close()
nodes.rationale: Each store closes once even if it backs several domains, so connections are released without double-closing.

nodes.label: init()
nodes.rationale: MastraCompositeStore initializes each configured domain independently; init() is called automatically when passed to the Mastra class.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Compose storage domains from different providers so different databases can serve different purposes (e.g. LibSQL for memory, PostgreSQL for workflows).

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouse (legacy)
nodes.rationale: Legacy observability domain implementation, still exported and supported for projects that haven't migrated to the VNext class.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext
nodes.rationale: Current observability domain implementation; ClickHouse is recommended for production observability because it is optimized for high-volume, write-heavy analytics workloads.

nodes.label: applyRetention()
nodes.rationale: Lets deployments update ClickHouse TTL configuration without running the full initialization path.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext
nodes.rationale: Uses native ClickHouse table TTLs instead of prune(); init() applies TTLs to new and existing tables and skips ALTER TABLE when the configured TTL is already present.

nodes.label: prune()
nodes.rationale: Deletes in bounded, batched chunks (each batch its own transaction) so it never takes a long lock or bloats the transaction log on tables with millions of rows; runs are resumable and cancellable.

nodes.label: PruneOptions
nodes.rationale: maxBatches, maxRows, pauseMs and signal bound each run so a large backlog drains over several maintenance windows without starving live traffic.

nodes.label: PruneResult
nodes.rationale: done: false signals eligible rows remain so the caller re-invokes prune() on the next tick.

nodes.label: RetentionConfig
nodes.rationale: Fully typed per-domain, per-table age policies so unknown domains or non-retention-eligible tables produce compile errors.

nodes.label: TableRetentionPolicy
nodes.rationale: batchSize bounds lock duration and WAL growth on large tables by making each batch its own transaction.

nodes.label: MongoDB TTL indexes
nodes.rationale: Database-native, zero-maintenance automated deletion for fixed retention periods; prune() is preferred when fine-grained control, rate capping, or resumable cleanup is needed.

nodes.label: Age-based storage retention system
nodes.rationale: Storage grows without bound by default, so retention is opt-in: unconfigured data is kept forever and behavior doesn't change until you opt in.

nodes.label: review Subscription Mode
nodes.rationale: Use review mode when the thread only needs code revisions, authorized latest PR comments, and observable review-thread-state updates.

nodes.label: working Subscription Mode
nodes.rationale: Follows all actionable PR activity detected by the provider; it is the default when mode is omitted and for stored subscriptions without a valid mode.

nodes.label: Composite storage
nodes.rationale: Used to route observability data to a supported provider because DynamoDB does not support the observability domain.

nodes.label: ring_clip tool
nodes.rationale: visibleToModel defaults to false because few models accept video; video input also consumes context window per second of footage, so durationMs should be kept short.

nodes.label: ring_snapshot tool
nodes.rationale: visibleToModel defaults to true because most models accept images, so the agent can describe what it sees.

nodes.label: RingSignals
nodes.rationale: Ring events arrive in an agent thread as notification signals so the agent can react to doorbell presses and motion and fetch media to see who is at the door.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Creates the core storage tables automatically, including mastra_notifications for notification inbox records and delivery metadata.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: Passing storage to the Mastra class calls init() automatically to create the core schema.

nodes.label: Channels store
nodes.rationale: Linked Ring account tokens are saved in the channels store and refreshed before they expire.

nodes.label: Signed media links proxy
nodes.rationale: Ring gives no shareable media links and downloads need account tokens, so tools return a signed link to the Mastra server under <baseUrl>/ring/media/ which fetches the media on demand; nothing is stored beyond a few minutes of in-memory cache.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Suggested for production environments with higher trace volumes.

nodes.label: Turso
nodes.rationale: Recommended over file storage for serverless deployments because file storage does not work on ephemeral file systems.

nodes.label: CollabAgent
nodes.rationale: Instructions teach the agent to read the <turn> tag so it can address users by name and respect functional roles.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: The agent must have memory configured so it can be called with a thread and resource.

nodes.label: generateTitle
nodes.rationale: A top-level thread concern that isn't applied to inherited subagent threads.

nodes.label: Mastra
nodes.rationale: Adding the storage provider to the main Mastra instance enables memory across all configured agents.

nodes.label: MASTRA_SCOPES_KEY
nodes.rationale: Lets trusted server middleware set scopes directly via the request context.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Recommended for long-running conversations because it keeps the prompt prefix stable.

nodes.label: Threads and Resources
nodes.rationale: A thread is a conversation session; a resource is the entity that owns the thread, so conversations can be scoped to a user, organization, or domain entity.

nodes.label: Message history
nodes.rationale: For short conversations or when a verbatim record of who said what is needed, the user tags in history are enough and no extra memory layer is required.

nodes.label: Multi-user threads
nodes.rationale: Use when several people collaborate on the same subject through one agent, e.g. collaborative documents, group chats, or multi-stakeholder reviews.

nodes.label: Request Context
nodes.rationale: The speaker must be set from authenticated request context, never the request body, otherwise one user can impersonate another.

nodes.label: <turn> identity tag
nodes.rationale: The message body is the one place that survives into history and back into context, so speaker identity is carried there and stays attached when prior turns are recalled.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Use memory when the agent needs multi-turn conversations that reference prior exchanges or recall user preferences; skip it for single-turn independent requests.

nodes.label: Scopes
nodes.rationale: Scopes are the addresses a run acts as, written as <type>:<value>; memory reads the resource from a resource: scope and the thread from a thread: scope while other scopes pass to tools and processors.

nodes.label: Storage providers
nodes.rationale: Memory requires a storage provider to persist message history, including user messages and agent responses.

nodes.label: Subagent memory isolation
nodes.rationale: Each delegation creates a fresh threadId and a deterministic resourceId ({parentResourceId}-{agentName}) so subagents start with clean history but resource-scoped memory persists between calls; title generation is skipped for ephemeral subagent threads to avoid wasting an LLM call per delegation.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: libSQL is the fastest path for local development because it doesn't require running a separate database server.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Use composite storage when one database isn't the right fit for every domain, routing each domain to the right backend.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Agent-level storage is configured on a Memory instance to give an agent an isolated memory boundary or a different memory backend.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is a good default for most teams because it works well for transactional runtime state and is widely available as a managed service.

nodes.label: suspendSchema
nodes.rationale: Custom metadata attached when suspending is stored in the snapshot and made available when the workflow is resumed.

nodes.label: Storage Domains
nodes.rationale: A domain owns one type of runtime data, and a storage adapter implements one or more domains.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Configure a persistent storage adapter when state must survive restarts or be shared across processes; the default in-memory store loses data when the process exits.

nodes.label: Workflow Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are the key mechanism enabling Mastra's suspend and resume capabilities, capturing all information needed to resume a workflow from exactly where it left off.

nodes.label: GET /health
nodes.rationale: Returns 503 while startWorkers() is initializing and 200 after every selected worker starts successfully, so it can be used for deployment readiness checks.

nodes.label: MASTRA_STEP_EXECUTION_URL
nodes.rationale: Without this variable the orchestration worker attempts to execute steps in its own process, which doesn't have access to the full Mastra runtime in a split deployment.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKER_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: Forwarded as an Authorization: Bearer credential so the API's configured auth provider can validate worker-to-API step execution requests.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKERS
nodes.rationale: Controls which workers start in each process so the same build artifact can be run in multiple containers with different roles; any value switches workflows that declare schedule to the evented engine.

nodes.label: mastra.startWorkers()
nodes.rationale: Needed when using a server adapter instead of the generated server, so in-process workers start after the server begins listening.

nodes.label: mastra worker start
nodes.rationale: Sets MASTRA_WORKERS in the spawned process; without a worker name it doesn't set the variable, so a name must be passed or the variable set in the environment.

nodes.label: Background Task Worker
nodes.rationale: Executes agent tool calls marked with background: { enabled: true } so the API does not block the response stream; manages concurrency limits, task lifecycle, and result delivery through the PubSub bus.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Split Deployment
nodes.rationale: Runs PostgreSQL, Redis, the API, and one process for each worker type, all sharing infrastructure and using the worker artifact.

nodes.label: mastra-projects Helm Chart
nodes.rationale: Renders the worker deployments with workers on the same image and environment as the server, and refuses to install combinations that would run every worker twice.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Deployment
nodes.rationale: Separate Deployments for API, orchestration, scheduler, and background task workers using the same image and Secret, with only role-specific environment variables set per container.

nodes.label: Orchestration Worker
nodes.rationale: Subscribes to workflow events on the PubSub bus and executes workflow steps; in a split deployment it pulls events from a distributed PubSub backend and delegates step execution back to the API over HTTP.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: A distributed PubSub backend persists unacknowledged events, which lets orchestration and background task workers resume after a restart.

nodes.label: Scheduler Worker
nodes.rationale: Producer only: polls storage for due cron schedules and publishes workflow.start events. Only one instance should run because multiple schedulers polling the same storage would fire duplicate events for the same schedule.

nodes.label: Workers
nodes.rationale: Workers handle background processing outside the request-response cycle (workflow step execution, cron scheduling, long-running tool calls), keeping the API responsive. Beta: breaking changes may occur without a major version bump.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector.close()
nodes.rationale: Closes the underlying libSQL client and releases file handles; calling it more than once is a no-op.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector.deleteVectors()
nodes.rationale: Either ids or filter must be provided, but not both.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector
nodes.rationale: Provides a SQLite-compatible vector search on libSQL/Turso, offering a lightweight and efficient vector database solution with metadata filtering.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector.updateVector()
nodes.rationale: Either id or filter must be provided, but not both.

nodes.label: LibSQLVector.upsert()
nodes.rationale: Uses a transaction so all vectors are inserted atomically; if any insert fails the entire operation is rolled back.

nodes.label: withMastra()
nodes.rationale: Lets you wrap any AI SDK model with Mastra features (processors, memory) without switching to the full Mastra agent API, so existing AI SDK code can gain input/output processing and conversation persistence.

nodes.label: Mastra class
nodes.rationale: Central orchestrator and top-level registry where agents, workflows, tools, and other components are registered so they are accessible throughout the application.

nodes.label: Mastra.recoverAllDurableAgents()
nodes.rationale: Re-drives orphaned running durable-agent runs after a crash; requires persistent storage because an in-memory store has nothing to recover after a process restart.

nodes.label: memory.ts file convention
nodes.rationale: Without memory.ts or config.memory, the agent has no memory by default and each generate()/stream() call starts without remembered conversation state.

nodes.label: storage.ts file convention
nodes.rationale: Mastra registers the store before file-based agents and workflows, so storage-dependent primitives bind to this store instead of the default in-memory store.

nodes.label: FastEmbed
nodes.rationale: Local embedding model; embeds at most 512 tokens per input, so long documents must be chunked to fit the window.

nodes.label: ModelRouterEmbeddingModel
nodes.rationale: The model router automatically handles API key detection from environment variables.

nodes.label: recall()
nodes.rationale: recall() adds semantic search support on top of listMessages, which only retrieves by thread ID with basic pagination.

nodes.label: Semantic recall
nodes.rationale: Retrieves relevant past messages by semantic meaning rather than exact keywords; same-thread matches interleave with history by timestamp while cross-thread matches become a system message.

nodes.label: Embedder
nodes.rationale: Memory uses a single embedder for both storing and recalling messages, so one model must be used consistently.

nodes.label: embeddingDimension
nodes.rationale: Setting the dimension skips the probe embedding, so startup makes no embedding call and doesn't depend on the embedding provider being reachable.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Index Optimization
nodes.rationale: HNSW indexes typically provide better performance than the default IVFFlat, especially with OpenAI embeddings which use inner product distance.

nodes.label: Server-side Embeddings
nodes.rationale: The database embeds each message on write and the search string on arrival, keeping the embedding provider out of the application entirely.

nodes.label: createVectorQueryTool()
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent decide retrieval at runtime, combining semantic search with optional filtering and reranking based on its understanding of the user's needs.

nodes.label: MONGODB_PROMPT
nodes.rationale: Vector store prompts are required in agent instructions to specify the valid filter operators and syntax for each vector store implementation.

nodes.label: PGVECTOR_PROMPT
nodes.rationale: Vector store prompts are required in agent instructions to specify the valid filter operators and syntax for each vector store implementation.

nodes.label: rerankWithScorer()
nodes.rationale: Blends semantic, vector and position weights to combine vector similarity with semantic understanding and improve retrieval quality.

nodes.label: VoyageRelevanceScorer
nodes.rationale: Reads VOYAGE_API_KEY from the environment or accepts an apiKey in its config; Voyage rerank models allow up to 32,000 tokens per query+document and 600,000 tokens per request.

nodes.label: Metadata Filtering
nodes.rationale: Combining vector similarity with structured metadata filters (hybrid vector search) narrows the search space; declaring filterFields on a MongoDB index lets the filter run inside $vectorSearch and avoids the 16 MB BSON limit of the pre-filter fallback path.

nodes.label: Re-ranking
nodes.rationale: More computationally expensive than initial vector similarity search but more accurate: it considers word order and exact matches and applies cross-attention between query and documents.

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: A step whose resumeSchema can't be shown as a form, such as one with nested objects, leaves the task working.

nodes.label: run.cancel()
nodes.rationale: In the process executing the run, that handle is the executing run, so cancel() stops it there.

nodes.label: syncWindowMs
nodes.rationale: In 'auto' mode a run that fails within syncWindowMs answers synchronously without a task, while a run that suspends within it continues as a task so it can ask for input.

nodes.label: tasks/update
nodes.rationale: An answer sent with tasks/update is stored before it's acknowledged, so the task resumes even if the instance that took the answer stops before running it.

nodes.label: ttlMs
nodes.rationale: The server deletes a finished task's row about a minute after its ttlMs ends; a task with ttlMs: null keeps its row until deleted.

nodes.label: input_required Task State
nodes.rationale: The server asks for one suspended step at a time.

nodes.label: Mastra Storage
nodes.rationale: Needs a storage adapter that keeps a TTL per task; on an older adapter the server falls back to memory and logs a warning when registered.

nodes.label: Retained task caps
nodes.rationale: Finishing a task frees its open slot but not its memory, so a client running many short tasks could grow memory without bound; retained caps bound every task the store still holds.

nodes.label: Access to tasks
nodes.rationale: A task id is an unguessable bearer token bound to the caller that created it, so another caller or a refused caller gets the same -32602 error as for an unknown id.

nodes.label: Tracing
nodes.rationale: A standalone MCPServer with no mastra instance produces no spans.

nodes.label: Workflow Recovery
nodes.rationale: Requires recovery.workflows to be 'auto' (the default); with 'off' the task stays working until its TTL expires. The step that was running when the server stopped runs again, so steps must be safe to repeat.

nodes.label: Workflow Task (run_<key>)
nodes.rationale: The run starts once, under the tools/call that creates the task, with a run id of its own; the task id is never the run id.

nodes.label: ActorSignal
nodes.rationale: Autonomous and scheduled agents run without an end user, so an actor signal lets FGA distinguish them from user requests.

nodes.label: createRoute
nodes.rationale: Route-level fga metadata is preferred for custom routes because it keeps authorization policy next to the route.

nodes.label: FGARouteResolver
nodes.rationale: A route map scales better than string-prefix checks when route FGA metadata must be derived centrally.

nodes.label: IFGAProvider
nodes.rationale: Interface exists so any FGA backend can be plugged in by implementing check, require, and filterAccessible.

nodes.label: MastraAuthWorkos
nodes.rationale: fetchMemberships must be true when using MastraFGAWorkos because WorkOS FGA checks need the user's organization memberships to resolve the correct membership ID.

nodes.label: requireActor()
nodes.rationale: Optional provider method enabling per-agent least privilege; once implemented, errors from it stop execution with no fallback to organization-only authorization.

nodes.label: validatePermissions()
nodes.rationale: Used at startup when a provider requires every Mastra permission to have an explicit provider permission slug.

nodes.label: createOAuthMiddleware
nodes.rationale: Without a configured token validator the middleware accepts an unvalidated token; that behavior is intended for development and testing only and is not production protection.

nodes.label: Actor Propagation into Workflow Steps
nodes.rationale: Propagation is opt-in and deliberately narrow: the true shorthand never propagates and custom step execute functions are never covered, so a step acting on a user's behalf cannot silently inherit system trust.

nodes.label: Fine-Grained Authorization (FGA)
nodes.rationale: RBAC answers whether a role can do an action; FGA answers whether a specific user can do that action on a specific resource, which multi-tenant B2B products need because permissions are contextual (admin of Team A, member of Team B).

nodes.label: permissionMapping
nodes.rationale: Translates Mastra internal permission strings to provider permission slugs; unmapped permissions pass through unchanged.

nodes.label: resourceMapping
nodes.rationale: Tells Mastra how to resolve FGA resource types and IDs from request context; returning undefined from deriveId falls back to the original Mastra resource ID.

nodes.label: Route Policy Coverage
nodes.rationale: requireForProtectedRoutes and auditProtectedRoutes let operators deny or audit protected routes that do not resolve FGA metadata.

nodes.label: Stored Resource Scoping
nodes.rationale: FGA authorizes access to a resource but does not filter stored records in shared storage, so scoping must be enabled separately for multi-tenant stored resource APIs.

nodes.label: System Actors
nodes.rationale: Trusted actors skip the user-centric require() check after a tenant-scope check by default; requireActor is optional so providers that omit it preserve the trusted-actor bypass, keeping the addition backward compatible.

nodes.label: mastra-mcp Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill exists so agents obtain domain-specific knowledge whenever working with @mastra/mcp APIs, configuration, or implementation.

nodes.label: createTool
nodes.rationale: Uses the same suspend/resume vocabulary as agents and workflows so one createTool definition serves all three.

nodes.label: requestState
nodes.rationale: The continuation payload is signed, not encrypted, so it must stay small and non-secret (IDs and phase, not confidential data); a shared key must be set from the environment so any instance can answer a continuation.

nodes.label: startHTTP
nodes.rationale: Session and serverless flags are gone because every request is stateless; options now only carry request security.

nodes.label: authenticate()
nodes.rationale: Runs the interactive OAuth authorization-code flow via a local loopback callback server.

nodes.label: cancelAuthentication()
nodes.rationale: Prevents an abandoned browser authorization from leaving the client waiting indefinitely.

nodes.label: createOAuthCallbackServer
nodes.rationale: One-shot loopback server that validates the OAuth state parameter before resolving with the code; plain HTTP so it is only suitable for local loopback redirects.

nodes.label: createSimpleTokenProvider
nodes.rationale: For testing or when a valid access token is already available.

nodes.label: getCallbackUrlCandidates
nodes.rationale: Lists every URL the callback helper may bind so all of them can be pre-registered as redirect_uris.

nodes.label: MCPOAuthClientProvider
nodes.rationale: The provider never registers a client at runtime: give it either clientInformation for a client pre-registered with the authorization server, or a Client ID Metadata Document URL as clientMetadataUrl. Give each server its own MCPOAuthClientProvider instance because a provider holds per-server session and credential state during authorization, so sharing one instance across multiple servers lets their flows overwrite each other.

nodes.label: OAuthStorage
nodes.rationale: Key-value contract for persistent token storage across sessions; stores latest token set, per-issuer entries, discovery state and the PKCE verifier under string keys.

nodes.label: 'needs-auth' state
nodes.rationale: Recorded instead of failing outright when a server rejects a connection because authorization is required.

nodes.label: resources.subscribe()
nodes.rationale: Mastra adds the URI to a single managed subscriptions/listen stream per server. Subscribing to the same URI more than once has no effect while the stream is active. Mastra restores the stream after a reconnect and closes it when the client disconnects.

nodes.label: listToolDefinitionsWithErrors()
nodes.rationale: Use when caching a catalog so a partial manifest omitting a server that was down is not persisted.

nodes.label: listToolsetsWithErrors()
nodes.rationale: The promise resolves only after every server finishes, so onServerSettled exists to handle each server as soon as it settles.

nodes.label: listToolsWithErrors()
nodes.rationale: errors stays a string map for backward compatibility while errorDetails adds machine-readable httpStatus and transport code.

nodes.label: MCP_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_CODE
nodes.rationale: Marks errors produced by perServerTimeoutMs so a slow server can be told apart from a broken one.

nodes.label: onServerSettled callback
nodes.rationale: Errors thrown by the callback are logged and do not affect discovery, including async rejections.

nodes.label: perServerTimeoutMs
nodes.rationale: Limits how long discovery waits per server so one slow server does not block the whole result.

nodes.label: serverNames filter
nodes.rationale: Allows retrying only servers that timed out without starting every other server again.

nodes.label: allowNoExpiry
nodes.rationale: Only enable it with a durable store, because clients with no-expiry subscriptions don't need to refresh after a server restart.

nodes.label: backpressure
nodes.rationale: Keep backpressure at its default, 'queue'; with other values a full queue fails the call.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: A local file is only shared by instances on the same host; use a database every instance can reach.

nodes.label: perOwnerConcurrency
nodes.rationale: MCP tasks share the per-agent limit (5) unless their owner gets its own.

nodes.label: createOAuthMiddleware
nodes.rationale: Validators should return subject so the server can bind input_required continuations to a user, preventing users who share an OAuth client from sharing a continuation.

nodes.label: OAuthStorage
nodes.rationale: Default OAuth storage is in memory; custom storage controls persistence and must be scoped to the user and connection.

nodes.label: appResources option
nodes.rationale: Lets an MCP server serve interactive HTML UIs via the MCP Apps extension, rendered in a sandboxed iframe in Mastra Studio.

nodes.label: events option
nodes.rationale: Lets clients subscribe to server-side occurrences such as ticket creation or build completion.

nodes.label: mapAuthInfoToUser
nodes.rationale: When set, requestContext includes user, which authorize callbacks can use to restrict event access.

nodes.label: server.events.emit()
nodes.rationale: Publishes event occurrences; throws for event types that declare a poll source because those cannot be pushed.

nodes.label: verifyToken
nodes.rationale: Validates the token's signature, issuer, audience, algorithm, expiration, and required claims before passing user data to the tool.

nodes.label: authInfo
nodes.rationale: Populated from whatever is set on req.auth in middleware, letting tools read authenticated user data.

nodes.label: metadata.clientLabel
nodes.rationale: The label is for debugging only: the server matches callers on the hashed principal, never on the label.

nodes.label: SEP-3415
nodes.rationale: Draft MCP extension, so the wire format and events API may change in any release.

nodes.label: authInfo
