nodes.rationale: The bearer token is stripped from authInfo before the request context is stored, so a task store never keeps credentials it should not hold.

nodes.label: What a task run receives
nodes.rationale: Task runs are rebuilt from what the task stored at creation, which keeps a task store free to run them again after a restart.

nodes.label: Mastra instance (listMCPServers)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from getMCPServers to align with the API convention that plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: MCPClient (v1)
nodes.rationale: getTools/getToolsets renamed to listTools/listToolsets to align with the API convention that plural getter methods use the list prefix.

nodes.label: listTools()
nodes.rationale: Tool names are namespaced as serverName_toolName to prevent conflicts; result is intended to be passed to an Agent definition.

nodes.label: listToolsets()
nodes.rationale: Intended to be passed at runtime into the generate or stream method.

nodes.label: Tool namespacing
nodes.rationale: Prefixing with the server key prevents tool name conflicts across servers; clientInfo does not change these prefixes.

nodes.label: toMCPServerProxies()
nodes.rationale: Lets external non-Mastra MCP servers be registered in mcpServers and appear in Studio without wrapping them in a Mastra MCPServer.

nodes.label: MastraFetchLike
nodes.rationale: Custom fetch allows dynamic auth headers, forwarding request-scoped credentials, and per-request interception; when provided, requestInit and authProvider become optional.

nodes.label: MastraMCPServerDefinition
nodes.rationale: Transport type is detected from the provided parameters: command selects Stdio, url selects Streamable HTTP.

nodes.label: MCPClientCapabilities
nodes.rationale: Only elicitation and extensions are supported; roots and sampling are not.

nodes.label: MCPClientTasksOptions
nodes.rationale: Poll intervals are clamped between 100 ms and 1 hour regardless of what the server suggests.

nodes.label: MCPInputRequestHandler
nodes.rationale: Without a handler an input_required result surfaces as an error.

nodes.label: MCPTraceContext
nodes.rationale: Trace context is observability data and is never used for authorization.

nodes.label: tasks
nodes.rationale: A call that returned a task is never retried, because a retry would start a second task.

nodes.label: allowedHosts host allowlist
nodes.rationale: Prevents server-side request forgery when HTTP server URLs come from untrusted configuration; intentionally minimal (exact hosts, no wildcards or scheme checks).

nodes.label: Answering input requests
nodes.rationale: When a call ends as input_required the handler answers each embedded request and the client retries the call.

nodes.label: JSON Schema validation
nodes.rationale: Schemas are limited to 128 nested levels and 10,000 nodes to bound validation work from untrusted tool catalogs.

nodes.label: Server instructions forwarding
nodes.rationale: Forwarding is opt-in because instructions are injected verbatim into the agent's system prompt and a malicious server could use them for prompt injection.

nodes.label: Stdio subprocess environment isolation
nodes.rationale: Sensitive variables such as API keys are not inherited unless passed explicitly; inheritDefaultEnv false gives stricter isolation.

nodes.label: Tool annotations
nodes.rationale: Clients MUST consider annotations untrusted unless they come from trusted servers; they are advisory hints with no security boundary.

nodes.label: Tool approval
nodes.rationale: Requires human approval before executing tools from a server, integrating with the existing human-in-the-loop approval flow.

nodes.label: Trace context propagation
nodes.rationale: Called per request so it can read a request-local carrier; explicit _meta keys on a tool call take precedence.

nodes.label: context.mcp namespace
nodes.rationale: MCP-specific functionality is organized under a clear API surface on the tool context.

nodes.label: progress
nodes.rationale: Off by default: opt in so tool calls carry a progressToken.

nodes.label: @mastra/mcp package
nodes.rationale: Optional peer dependency of @mastra/editor; must be installed before stored MCP clients can load their tools at runtime.

nodes.label: MastraEditor
nodes.rationale: Tool records are merged in a fixed resolution order where later records replace earlier records with the same ID, so unique tool IDs across sources are recommended.

nodes.label: MCPClient (2.0)
nodes.rationale: The client always speaks 2026-07-28 and probes each server, falling back to the initialize handshake, so one client can reach upgraded and third-party servers alike.

nodes.label: MCPOAuthClientProvider (2.0)
nodes.rationale: No runtime dynamic client registration: exactly one client identity must be configured via clientInformation (pre-registered) or clientMetadataUrl (CIMD).

nodes.label: OAuthStorage (2.0)
nodes.rationale: A storage namespace must not be shared between providers; tokens are stored per authorization-server issuer.

nodes.label: DatadogExporter
nodes.rationale: Gives spans their own IDs, so a link between two Mastra spans does not resolve in this backend.

nodes.label: context.mcp.log()
nodes.rationale: Delivery is opted into per request via the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel metadata key; without opt-in nothing is delivered, and each round of a tool call must opt in again.

nodes.label: context.mcp.progress()
nodes.rationale: Progress is only sent when the caller includes a progressToken in the request _meta; otherwise the call is a no-op.

nodes.label: SentryExporter
nodes.rationale: Gives spans their own IDs, so a link between two Mastra spans does not resolve in this backend.

nodes.label: allowedHosts
nodes.rationale: Restricts outbound hosts when HTTP server URLs come from untrusted configuration; a custom fetch is validated only against its final response URL, so it must enforce its own redirect policy.

nodes.label: App (ext-apps)
nodes.rationale: Event handlers must be registered before calling connect().

nodes.label: authenticate()
nodes.rationale: Completes the browser-based OAuth authorization flow for OAuth-protected servers.

nodes.label: listTools()
nodes.rationale: Static tools suit shared, fixed configuration with credentials shared by all requests.

nodes.label: listToolsets()
nodes.rationale: Runtime toolsets exist for per-user or per-request configuration where credentials vary between requests.

nodes.label: MCPClient
nodes.rationale: Manages multiple MCP server connections and their tools in a Mastra application.

nodes.label: MCPEventsSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: Delivers occurrences to agent threads as notifications instead of requiring a hand-written subscription loop.

nodes.label: MCPServer
nodes.rationale: Exposes existing Mastra tools and agents as an MCP server; every request is self-contained so the same server runs unchanged on long-lived hosts and serverless platforms.

nodes.label: @mcp-ui/client
nodes.rationale: Loads app HTML through a sandbox proxy and communicates over JSON-RPC with postMessage; iframes cannot access the parent page's DOM, cookies, or storage.

nodes.label: requireToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Tool results are untrusted model input, so sensitive tools need approval; annotations from servers you do not control are untrusted hints.

nodes.label: startStdio()
nodes.rationale: Used when packaging a server for local execution through a command such as npx.

nodes.label: toMCPServerProxies()
nodes.rationale: Registers proxies for external MCP servers so Studio can resolve remote app resources.

nodes.label: typegen
nodes.rationale: Generating types from published tool schemas gives stable direct tool calls without redeclaring arguments and results, while leaving dynamic discovery unchanged.

nodes.label: MCP Apps
nodes.rationale: Lets MCP tools serve interactive HTML interfaces through ui:// resources, rendered by Studio in sandboxed iframes; the model sees content while the app receives structuredContent.

nodes.label: MCP Events
nodes.rationale: Lets a client react when something happens on a server instead of polling on a schedule; implements draft SEP-3415 so the wire format and API are experimental.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.rationale: Open standard for connecting AI agents to external tools and resources.

nodes.label: MCPServer
nodes.rationale: This API is specifically for exposing Mastra tools and agents to external MCP clients; if you only need to use tools or agents directly within your Mastra application, you don't necessarily need to create an MCP server.

nodes.label: requestState
nodes.rationale: The payload is signed, not encrypted, so keep it small and non-secret (IDs and phase, not confidential data). Set requestState.key from the environment so every instance that may answer a continuation shares the key.

nodes.label: toolActions
nodes.rationale: Named toolActions because tools() is the method that returns the registered tool registry.

nodes.label: getServerInfo()
nodes.rationale: Values come from the remote server and are not validated, so icon and website URLs must be treated as untrusted; not a connection check.

nodes.label: listToolDefinitions()
nodes.rationale: Returns plain serializable definitions with no functions or live client references so they can be JSON.stringify'd and cached.

nodes.label: MCPClient
nodes.rationale: Manages multiple MCP server connections and their tools, handling connection lifecycle and tool namespacing across all configured servers.

nodes.label: toolFromDefinition()
nodes.rationale: No connection is opened; the client connects lazily the first time the tool is executed.

nodes.label: toolsFromDefinitions()
nodes.rationale: Cached counterpart to listTools(); servers in the catalog but no longer configured are skipped so a stale manifest degrades gracefully.

nodes.label: Cached tool definitions
nodes.rationale: Serializable definitions can be cached in Redis or a database and rebuilt into executable tools without connecting.

nodes.label: Custom fetch for runtime-defined authentication
nodes.rationale: Useful when tokens must be refreshed per request or user credentials forwarded from the incoming request; when fetch is provided, requestInit and authProvider become optional.

nodes.label: MCPClient instance management
nodes.rationale: Built-in memory leak prevention: duplicate configurations without an id throw, so instances must be given unique ids or disconnected before recreation.

nodes.label: registerProcessHooks
nodes.rationale: Default SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/beforeExit hooks can interrupt the application's awaited cleanup such as draining HTTP requests, so they can be disabled to let the app own shutdown.

nodes.label: Protocol revision negotiation
nodes.rationale: Client probes with server/discover and falls back to the pre-2026 initialize handshake so tools, resources and prompts keep working against either revision.

nodes.label: requestContext
nodes.rationale: Provides request-scoped data (cookies, bearer tokens) set by middleware or passed during agent/tool execution; null during the initial connection handshake.

nodes.label: Process shutdown hooks
nodes.rationale: Set registerProcessHooks to false when the application handles shutdown itself and call disconnect() from that handler.

nodes.label: Typed client contracts
nodes.rationale: Contracts describe a schema snapshot; live servers can differ, so runtime discovery, validation and execution are unchanged and availability must be checked before calling.

nodes.label: Client type generation (typegen)
nodes.rationale: Construction only stores readonly metadata and does not generate files; generation is an explicit CLI step.

nodes.label: recover
nodes.rationale: Only turn it on for tools that are safe to repeat.

nodes.label: Agent Task (ask_<key>)
nodes.rationale: Runs the agent's generate() as the task's work, like a tool task.

nodes.label: MCPClientWebhookOptions
nodes.rationale: Experimental webhook delivery for MCP events.

nodes.label: MCPEventsSignalProvider
nodes.rationale: The notification summary labels the event as untrusted and wraps its data, together with the server-advertised event name, in an <untrusted-mcp-event-data> block that the content can't close.

nodes.label: Webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: Experimental; servers POST occurrences to webhook.url which must route to events.handleWebhook().

nodes.label: Mastra Memory Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill exists to supply domain-specific knowledge for @mastra/memory APIs, configuration, and implementation; individual reference documents are read on demand rather than inlined.

nodes.label: data-om-buffering-end
nodes.rationale: Content is stored but not yet activated in the main context.

nodes.label: data-om-status
nodes.rationale: Emitted once per agent loop step before model generation so clients can derive window usage percentages, post-activation estimates, and reflection compression ratios from raw values.

nodes.label: ObservationalMemory
nodes.rationale: The ObservationalMemory class is the engine; to attach it to an agent, wrap it in an ObservationalMemoryProcessor, which needs a Memory instance for loading and persisting messages.

nodes.label: ObservationalMemoryProcessor
nodes.rationale: Wraps the ObservationalMemory engine so it can be attached to an agent's input/output processors; requires a Memory instance for loading and persisting messages.

nodes.label: recall tool
nodes.rationale: Registered when retrieval is truthy so the agent can page through raw messages behind observation group ranges, list threads, and search cross-thread; reflected groups are marked _kind: reflection_ so the agent treats them as lossy summaries.

nodes.label: MastraMemory
nodes.rationale: settled() is declared on the base memory class, so it is also available on the MastraMemory instance returned by agent.getMemory(); the scope parameter is only on Memory from @mastra/memory.

nodes.label: Memory.settled()
nodes.rationale: Await this method before closing a storage connection you own; without it, background statements can run against a closed connection. A scoped call can return while other threads still use the store, so call settled() without a scope before closing shared storage.

nodes.label: Extractor
nodes.rationale: Extractors with a Zod schema run as a follow-up structured output call; schema-less extractors are extracted inline, and each extractor's onExtracted hook fires with the extracted value.

nodes.label: summarizeConversation()
nodes.rationale: Distills messages with the same Observer plumbing that powers Observational Memory, but without Observational Memory attached to an agent and without reading from or writing to storage, so the caller decides where the summary and extracted values go.

nodes.label: Memory.summarizeThread()
nodes.rationale: Messages load page-by-page starting from the newest, bounded by lastMessages and maxInputTokens, so summarizing a long thread doesn't read its entire history from storage; nothing is written back to memory.

nodes.label: Memory.updateThreadResourceId()
nodes.rationale: Transfers ownership of an existing thread to a different resource while preserving the original createdAt timestamp, useful for scenarios such as moving a private thread into a shared workspace.

nodes.label: activateAfterIdle
nodes.rationale: Forces buffered observations to activate after inactivity so that once a thread has been idle long enough for the prompt cache to expire, the next request sends a smaller compressed context window.

nodes.label: activateOnProviderChange
nodes.rationale: Changing models or providers mid-thread invalidates the prompt cache, so activating buffered observations first avoids sending a large raw window to a provider that can't reuse the previous cache.

nodes.label: Async Buffering
nodes.rationale: Without async buffering the Observer runs synchronously at the threshold and the agent pauses mid-conversation while the Observer LLM call completes; buffering pre-computes observations in the background so activation is instant.

nodes.label: Prompt Caching
nodes.rationale: OM's context is stable and observations append over time rather than being retrieved at runtime each turn. This keeps the prompt prefix cacheable, which reduces costs.

nodes.label: Continuation Hints
nodes.rationale: Agents that drive their own control flow generally want suggestedResponse disabled so memory does not compete for what the agent says next.

nodes.label: Provider Capabilities Registry
nodes.rationale: Used by observeAttachments 'auto' to decide whether the Observer model supports multimodal input, useful when the Observer model is text-only while the main agent uses a multimodal model.

nodes.label: OM Retrieval / Recall Tool
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent look up the raw message history behind its observations via durable pointers kept in observation groups.

nodes.label: shareTokenBudget
nodes.rationale: Maximizes context usage through flexible allocation: messages can use more space when observations are small, and vice versa.

nodes.label: OM Streaming Data Parts
nodes.rationale: Emitted during agent execution so clients can use real-time UI feedback alongside the agent's response.

nodes.label: Temporal Markers
nodes.rationale: Shown to the observer so it can anchor observations to when events occurred.

nodes.label: Token Estimate Metadata Cache
nodes.rationale: Persists token payload estimates so repeated counting can reuse prior token estimation work.

nodes.label: FGA provider
nodes.rationale: Thread ownership transfer bypasses normal per-resource ownership checks, so the HTTP endpoint is restricted to privileged, non-resource-scoped callers and rejects unscoped requests when server.auth is configured without an FGA provider.

nodes.label: recall()
nodes.rationale: recall() adds semantic search on top of listMessages, which only retrieves messages by thread ID with basic pagination.

nodes.label: Semantic Recall
nodes.rationale: Retrieves relevant past messages based on semantic meaning rather than exact keywords.

nodes.label: Embedder
nodes.rationale: Memory uses a single embedder for both storing and recalling messages, so one model must be picked and used consistently.

nodes.label: embeddingDimension
nodes.rationale: Setting the dimension skips the probe embedding, so startup makes no embedding call and doesn't depend on the embedding provider being reachable.

nodes.label: Vector Index Configuration (HNSW/IVFFlat)
nodes.rationale: HNSW indexes typically provide better performance than the default IVFFlat, especially with OpenAI embeddings which use inner product distance; PgVector only uses the vector index for thread/resource-filtered searches with HNSW on pgvector 0.8.0 or newer.

nodes.label: Metadata Filter
nodes.rationale: Filters match metadata stored on message embeddings when messages are saved, so existing embeddings keep their previous metadata until re-saved or re-indexed.

nodes.label: Server-side Embeddings
nodes.rationale: With a store that embeds server-side, the embedding provider stays out of the application entirely; the database embeds each message on write and the search string on arrival.

nodes.label: actionFingerprint()
nodes.rationale: In production a stable hash of the tool name and arguments should be used, stored in durable storage scoped to user, run, tool call and policy version.

nodes.label: agent.generate()
nodes.rationale: Non-streaming use case: returns immediately with finishReason 'suspended', a suspendPayload and a runId when a tool requires approval.

nodes.label: beforeToolCall hook
nodes.rationale: Binds approval to the exact tool name and arguments shown to the reviewer so the tool doesn't run under an old approval if arguments drift.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Used to estimate whether a tool call needs human review when the decision depends on the tool name and arguments.

nodes.label: declineToolCall()
nodes.rationale: Accepts an optional reason returned to the model in place of the tool result so the model can adjust instead of retrying blindly.

nodes.label: requireApproval
nodes.rationale: Set on a tool definition to pause calls to that specific tool before execution, giving fine-grained control so only specific tools pause while others execute immediately.

nodes.label: requireToolApproval
nodes.rationale: Pauses every tool call for that request; accepts a boolean or a per-call function so approval can be gated at runtime.

nodes.label: tool-call-approval chunk
nodes.rationale: Contains toolCallId, toolName and args so the approval can be bound to the exact arguments shown to the reviewer.

nodes.label: tool-call-resumed chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitted only when a real suspension or approval request is cleared; use this signal to mark a question as answered rather than inferring it from the tool output shape.

nodes.label: Durable agents
nodes.rationale: Persist their options, and a function can't be serialized, so they accept only a boolean for requireToolApproval.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop
nodes.rationale: Agents need the same human oversight used in workflows when calling tools that handle sensitive operations, like deleting resources or running long processes.

nodes.label: Stored agents
nodes.rationale: Persist their options, and a function can't be serialized, so they accept only a boolean for requireToolApproval.

nodes.label: bufferActivation option
nodes.rationale: Controls how aggressively to clear the message window on activation; lower values keep more message history.

nodes.label: bufferOnIdle
nodes.rationale: Runs background observation buffering when an agent turn ends and the agent becomes idle, so short turns are observed without waiting for the next turn or token threshold.

nodes.label: shareTokenBudget option
nodes.rationale: Pools the message-history and observation budgets so history can expand into unused observation space while the observation log is small.

nodes.label: observation.threadTitle option
nodes.rationale: Opt-in; updates thread metadata so apps can show the latest title in thread lists and status UI.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: The lastMessages window slides forward on every request, invalidating the provider prompt cache; for long-running conversations Observational Memory is recommended.

nodes.label: bufferTokens
nodes.rationale: Controls how often to buffer; setting it to false disables both observation and reflection async buffering.

nodes.label: Compression
nodes.rationale: Raw message history and tool results get compressed into a dense observation log. Smaller context means faster responses and longer coherent conversations.

nodes.label: Early Activation
nodes.rationale: Useful when a prompt cache is likely to expire, or when the agent changes model providers.

nodes.label: Lifecycle Hooks
nodes.rationale: Telemetry callbacks (onObservationStart/End, onReflectionStart/End) that never change what OM stores.

nodes.label: Zero Context Rot
nodes.rationale: The agent sees relevant information instead of noisy tool calls and irrelevant tokens, which keeps the agent on task over long sessions.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Recommended: background agents compress older messages into observations, reducing context used by message history while retaining information for later turns.

nodes.label: ring_clip Tool
nodes.rationale: visibleToModel defaults to false for ring_clip because most models accept images but few accept video.

nodes.label: Ring Server Routes (/ring/link, /ring/token, /ring/webhook, /ring/home)
nodes.rationale: The token route has no check of its own; it sends each code to Ring and Ring rejects codes it didn't issue, so rate limiting should be added in server middleware.

nodes.label: ring_snapshot Tool
nodes.rationale: visibleToModel defaults to true for ring_snapshot because most models accept images.

nodes.label: attachment / maxAttachmentBytes Options
nodes.rationale: Users can't see tool results in chat channels, so media is sent as file attachments on channel threads instead.

nodes.label: coalesce Option
nodes.rationale: coalesce merges repeats of an event into one pending notification so a delivery policy can act on how many arrived.

nodes.label: Media Links
nodes.rationale: Ring doesn't give out shareable links to its media and downloading needs the account's tokens, so when baseUrl is set the tools return a signed link to the user's own server that fetches the media from Ring.

nodes.label: Thread Routing
nodes.rationale: By default each Ring device gets its own thread, with threadId set to the device ID and resourceId set to the agent ID.

nodes.label: DSQLStore.createIndex()
nodes.rationale: Aurora DSQL doesn't allow ASC/DESC in CREATE INDEX ASYNC, so those modifiers are automatically stripped.

nodes.label: DSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Aurora DSQL doesn't support PostgreSQL extensions (CREATE EXTENSION), including pgvector, so vector storage must use a separate vector store such as @mastra/s3vectors.

nodes.label: DSQLStore.init()
nodes.rationale: If init() isn't called, tables won't be created and storage operations will fail silently or throw errors; Mastra calls it automatically when storage is passed to the Mastra class.

nodes.label: Connection Lifetime Limit
nodes.rationale: Individual connections are limited to about 60 minutes, so the default maxLifetimeSeconds of 3300 recycles connections before hitting the limit.

nodes.label: IAM Authentication
nodes.rationale: Connections are authenticated with IAM, so no database passwords are required; short-lived auth tokens are generated by the Aurora DSQL node postgres connector.

nodes.label: Index Management
nodes.rationale: Indexes are created asynchronously with CREATE INDEX ASYNC, so new indexes may not be immediately available after init().

nodes.label: Optimistic Concurrency Control
nodes.rationale: Aurora DSQL may return retriable OCC errors under contention and limits transaction duration and size, so large bulk operations should be split into smaller batches at the application level.

nodes.label: Schema Management
nodes.rationale: Each cluster exposes a single database 'postgres', so logical separation is done via schemas controlled by the schemaName option.

nodes.label: GoalEvaluationPayload
nodes.rationale: Typed goal stream chunk so a UI can show goal progress mid-run.

nodes.label: updateObjectiveOptions()
nodes.rationale: Only provided fields are written; unset fields fall back to the agent's goal config.

nodes.label: activeDurationMs
nodes.rationale: Measures agent execution rather than the goal's wall-clock age, and is checkpointed when the run ends or waits for tool approval.

nodes.label: Goal
nodes.rationale: A goal is durable (stored in thread state, not passed per call) and is set and updated through Agent methods rather than per-stream() options, so it survives reloads and is evaluated in-loop.

nodes.label: Goal step
nodes.rationale: Runs inside the agentic execution loop right after isTaskComplete and is a no-op for background-task, mid-tool-loop, and working-memory-only iterations.

nodes.label: goal.judge
nodes.rationale: The judge model is the activation switch: if no judge resolves, the goal step performs no scoring or budget consumption and emits no goal chunk, even for a custom scorer.

nodes.label: maxRuns
nodes.rationale: When the budget is exhausted the loop stops and the objective is marked paused; raising maxRuns and resuming continues the work.

nodes.label: goal.scorer
nodes.rationale: A custom scorer brings its own judging, so goal.prompt, goal.tools and goal.maxSteps no longer apply and the judge model is no longer resolved for judging.

nodes.label: State-signal projection
nodes.rationale: The goal config auto-registers the projection so the model always sees the current objective as <current-objective> without extra setup.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Memory is required because .network() uses it to store task history and determine when a task is complete.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Creates a conversational flow where users provide required information naturally; requires memory, same thread/resource, and a resumeSchema on the tool.

nodes.label: Routing Agent
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: replace with supervisor agents that use agent.stream() or agent.generate(), which provide the same multi-agent coordination through a simpler API that improves control and debugging.

nodes.label: PostgresStore.close()
nodes.rationale: Destroys the pool only if Mastra created it.

nodes.label: DbClient
nodes.rationale: Exposed for advanced low-level use; direct access bypasses PostgresStore's additional logic and validation, so the caller is responsible for connection and transaction handling.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext.ensurePartitions()
nodes.rationale: Needed when the app role cannot create tables or does not own the observability tables; must be scheduled at least once every futureDays days with a role that can create tables.

nodes.label: PostgresStore.init()
nodes.rationale: Called automatically when storage is passed to the Mastra class; must be called explicitly when storage is used directly, otherwise tables are not created and operations fail.

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: When a pool is provided, Mastra does not create its own pool and does not close it on store.close(); the caller manages the pool lifecycle.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Uses the event-sourced tracing strategy: writes one row when a span starts and another when it ends, never updating in place, so writes stay append-only and traces appear in Studio while the run is still executing.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Index Types and Use Cases
nodes.norm_label: postgresql index types and use cases

nodes.label: processLLMRequest
nodes.rationale: Runs after earlier prompt processors have transformed the prompt so only tokens that actually reach the model are counted; system messages are always preserved and tool call/result messages are grouped.

nodes.label: processOutputStream
nodes.rationale: Only text and object parts count against the limit and can be withheld; lifecycle, reasoning and tool parts always pass through so tool calls always reach the agentic loop and get executed.

nodes.label: TokenLimiterProcessor
nodes.rationale: Acts as a prompt processor, input processor and output processor depending on trimMode; trimming of the provider prompt is transient so stored messages are never modified.

nodes.label: tokenx
nodes.rationale: Token counts are estimated with tokenx, so no encoder is needed and the encoding option is deprecated.

nodes.label: ToolCallFilter
nodes.rationale: The limiter should be registered after prompt-shrinking processors such as ToolCallFilter so it counts the prompt the model actually receives.

nodes.label: TripWire
nodes.rationale: Thrown when trimming would leave no sendable messages: empty messages, system messages alone exceeding the limit, or no message fitting the remaining budget.

nodes.label: trimMode option
nodes.rationale: 'best-fit' keeps as many messages as possible (may create gaps), 'contiguous' keeps a continuous suffix of conversation history, and 'memory-only' trims stored history in processInput instead of the prompt.

nodes.label: AttachmentUploader
nodes.rationale: Uploads base64 attachments to external storage and replaces them with URL references before messages are persisted, to stay under provider record size limits.

nodes.label: MemoryInputFilter
nodes.rationale: Runs first by default so MessageHistory, SemanticRecall, and Observational Memory receive only the new input they need.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: Stores data locally in a memory.db file for the quickstart examples.

nodes.label: observation.manageWorkingMemory option
nodes.rationale: Lets the Observer manage working memory automatically so updates don't depend on the main agent remembering to make them.

nodes.label: retainFullInput
nodes.rationale: Disables client-echoed history filtering so request input is processed exactly as sent.

nodes.label: skillResultRedactor()
nodes.rationale: Agent skill results contain full instructions or file contents, so without redaction the Observer re-observes that text every time a skill is used; the tool call survives so the Observer still records which skill was used.

nodes.label: workingMemory.useStateSignals option
nodes.rationale: Working memory normally lives in the system prompt, so updates can invalidate the prompt cache; moving it into state signals keeps working memory prompt-cache friendly.

nodes.label: WorkingMemoryExtractor
nodes.rationale: Skips OM metadata persistence so the working memory payload isn't duplicated under OM extracted metadata.

nodes.label: afterObservation
nodes.rationale: Replaces only the observation text; it does not recompute or redact structured extractor results, so it is not a redaction boundary for all cycle data.

nodes.label: afterReflection
nodes.rationale: Reflection extraction and its callbacks run before afterReflection, so rewriting the reflection doesn't rerun those callbacks.

nodes.label: beforeObservation
nodes.rationale: Returning an empty messages array skips the Observer model call while still marking the filtered messages as observed.

nodes.label: Resource scope (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated: shared observations across all threads invalidate prompt caches for other threads, mix context between conversations, and process unobserved messages across all threads at once, which is slow.

nodes.label: Retrieval Mode
nodes.rationale: Normal OM compresses messages into observations and loses the original wording; retrieval mode keeps each observation group linked to the raw messages that produced it so the agent can recover exact wording and tool output.

nodes.label: Semantic search over observation groups
nodes.rationale: Reuses the vector store and embedder already configured on the Memory instance; new observation groups are indexed at buffer time and during synchronous observation, fire-and-forget and non-blocking.

nodes.label: Thread scope
nodes.rationale: Requires a valid threadId; this prevents multiple threads from silently sharing a single observation record, which can cause database deadlocks.

nodes.label: Transform Hooks
nodes.rationale: Intercept data flowing through an observation/reflection cycle so callers can redact or rewrite what the Observer/Reflector sees or what gets persisted; always awaited on every path.

nodes.label: Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Stores persistent, structured user data such as names, preferences, and goals; injected as a system message.

nodes.label: Read-only Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Useful for routing agents that need context but shouldn't update user profiles, and sub agents that should reference but not own the memory.

nodes.label: Resource-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Default scope: memory persists across all conversation threads for the same user (resourceId), enabling persistent user memory.

nodes.label: Working Memory Schema
nodes.rationale: Schemas use merge semantics: the agent only needs to include fields it wants to add or update, existing fields are preserved, and setting a field to null deletes it.

nodes.label: Storage Adapters
nodes.rationale: Resource-scoped working memory requires specific storage adapters that support the mastra_resources table; only @mastra/pg currently supports atomic merges via row-locked transactions, other adapters merge in the application and only serialize writers inside a single process.

nodes.label: Working Memory Template
nodes.rationale: Templates use replace semantics: the agent must provide the complete memory content on each update. Short, focused labels and consistent casing keep updates readable and less likely to be truncated.

nodes.label: Thread-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Thread-scoped memory isolates working memory to individual conversation threads, for separate topics, session-specific information, or ephemeral unrelated workflows.

nodes.label: useStateSignals
nodes.rationale: Opt-in experimental delivery of working memory as a state signal instead of folding it into the system prompt; storage is identical and the tool is exposed under a new name so legacy strip filters don't remove tool-call parts.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Renamed from MastraMessageV2 because the name better describes the purpose of this type as the database message format; it is now the default return format everywhere.

nodes.label: MastraMessageV3
nodes.rationale: Removed to simplify the architecture by removing an intermediary format; messages now convert directly between MastraDBMessage and AI SDK v5 formats.

nodes.label: Memory.recall()
nodes.rationale: Renamed from query() because the name better describes the action of retrieving messages from memory and the API was simplified to a single return format.

nodes.label: Memory.rememberMessages()
nodes.rationale: Removed because it performed the same function as query() (now recall()); consolidating to one method simplifies the API.

nodes.label: toAISdkV5Messages
nodes.rationale: AI SDK format conversion moved to dedicated utility functions in @mastra/ai-sdk/ui to improve tree-shaking by moving UI-specific conversion code to a separate package.

nodes.label: TokenLimiter
nodes.rationale: Processors are configured at the Agent level because processor behavior is scoped to agent execution.

nodes.label: Memory scope (thread vs resource)
nodes.rationale: The default scope changed from 'thread' to 'resource' to align with common use cases where applications want to remember user information across conversations.

nodes.label: semanticRecall option
nodes.rationale: Default settings were optimized based on RAG research: topK increased from 2 to 4 and messageRange changed to { before: 1, after: 1 }, providing better accuracy while only slightly increasing message count. semanticRecall is now disabled by default to improve performance and reduce unexpected LLM API calls.

nodes.label: workingMemory option
nodes.rationale: The text-stream mode was removed to simplify the working memory API by removing the less reliable streaming mode; only tool-call mode is supported.

nodes.label: observation.observeAttachments option
nodes.rationale: Drops binary attachments before they reach a text-only Observer while keeping readable placeholders so the Observer can still reason about what was shared.

nodes.label: data-om-buffering-start
nodes.rationale: Buffering pre-computes observations or reflections in the background before the main threshold is reached.

nodes.label: data-om-thread-update
nodes.rationale: Only emitted when observation.threadTitle is enabled.

nodes.label: skillResultRedactor
nodes.rationale: Replaces skill tool results with a placeholder while keeping the tool call, so the Observer still records which skill was used and with what arguments without seeing the skill text.

nodes.label: blockAfter
nodes.rationale: Between the activation threshold and blockAfter, buffering keeps running in the background so the next ready chunk activates without blocking the agent.

nodes.label: Observer
nodes.rationale: Background agent that watches conversations and writes observations to the log.

nodes.label: observation.previousObserverTokens
nodes.rationale: Observer context optimization for long-running conversations where observations grow large, reducing Observer input costs by tail-truncating previous observations.

nodes.label: Reflections
nodes.rationale: Each reflection rewrites the entire observation log rather than accumulating as a separate growing layer, so memory stays bounded around the reflection threshold no matter how long the conversation runs.

nodes.label: Temporal Gap Markers
nodes.rationale: Help the agent and UI see that the conversation resumed after a useful pause; inserted when the gap is at least 10 minutes.

nodes.label: gitcrawl
nodes.rationale: The provider runs `gitcrawl sync` and reads its SQLite database to observe PR activity.

nodes.label: GithubSignals
nodes.rationale: Polls subscribed pull requests and sends notification signals to the agent thread when relevant activity occurs.

nodes.label: startPollingForThread()
nodes.rationale: Must be called for each persisted thread subscription after a process restart to resume polling.

nodes.label: subscribeThreadToPR()
nodes.rationale: The provider syncs the PR immediately, stores the subscription in the thread's metadata, and starts polling every five minutes.

nodes.label: Subscription Modes (review/working)
nodes.rationale: `review` mode is for threads that only need code revisions, authorized latest PR comments, and observable review-thread-state updates; `working` follows all actionable PR activity and is the default.

nodes.label: RedisStore.init()
nodes.rationale: Called automatically when storage is passed to Mastra; must be called explicitly when storage is used directly.

nodes.label: Redis Cluster
nodes.rationale: Not supported: RedisStore accepts only a standalone client, and several operations read or write keys that hash to different slots, which Redis Cluster rejects with a CROSSSLOT error.

nodes.label: Redis Sentinel
nodes.rationale: Supported only through a pre-configured custom client for high-availability deployments.

nodes.label: UpstashStore
nodes.rationale: Serverless-friendly: no connection management, pay-per-request pricing, global replication, edge-compatible. A fixed pricing plan is strongly recommended because the pay-as-you-go model can produce unexpectedly high costs from the high volume of Redis commands generated during agent conversations.

nodes.label: data-om-activation
nodes.rationale: Activation is an instant operation: no LLM call is involved, buffered content is simply moved into the active context window.

nodes.label: data-om-observation-failed
nodes.rationale: On failure the system falls back to synchronous processing; the retrying flag marks non-final failures where reflection did not compress below target and OM retries at a higher compression level.

nodes.label: ModelByInputTokens
nodes.rationale: Selects the model for the smallest threshold that covers the actual input size; exceeding the largest threshold throws, and during an OM Observer or Reflector run OM aborts via TripWire.

nodes.label: failurePolicy
nodes.rationale: A provider outage usually takes out both stages, so set the policy on both if you want the turn to survive one.

nodes.label: Observation Log
nodes.rationale: Dense log of observations that replaces raw message history as it grows.

nodes.label: Reflector
nodes.rationale: Background agent that watches conversations and maintains the observation log alongside the Observer.

nodes.label: Inline Task
nodes.rationale: The inline task receives the item's metadata, so each row can drive its own thread without changing the agent or any scorer.

nodes.label: targetOptions
nodes.rationale: targetOptions is global per call and forwarded to agent.generate(); no per-item override on RunEvalsDataItem is available today.

nodes.label: asUserTurn()
nodes.rationale: Wraps each user message in a <turn> tag so identity survives into history and back into context.

nodes.label: config.ts
nodes.rationale: config.memory wins over memory.ts in the merge precedence.

nodes.label: Memory (file-based agent)
nodes.rationale: Without memory.ts or config.memory the agent has no memory by default; each generate()/stream() call starts without remembered conversation state unless prior context is passed.

nodes.label: memory.ts
nodes.rationale: Default-exports a Memory instance that becomes the agent's memory; memory data is stored in the storage provider configured on the main Mastra instance.

nodes.label: exportSchemas
nodes.rationale: Generates Oracle DDL without connecting to a database, useful when schema changes are reviewed or applied outside application startup.

nodes.label: OraclePoolManager
nodes.rationale: Allows OracleStore and OracleVector to share one Oracle connection lifecycle.

nodes.label: OracleStore
nodes.rationale: Implements Mastra's composite storage interface so one OracleStore instance can back memory, workflow snapshots, observability, scores, scorer definitions, MCP client metadata, and agent registry data.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: libSQL is the fastest path for local development because it doesn't require running a separate database server and persists state between restarts.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is a good production default for most teams because it works well for transactional runtime state and is widely available as a managed service.

nodes.label: backgroundTasks
nodes.rationale: Subagent invocations are dispatched as tool calls, so long-running delegations can run as background tasks without blocking the parent agent's response.

nodes.label: createRubricScorer
nodes.rationale: Works as an LLM-as-judge scorer: a separate grader model reviews output against a rubric after each iteration, which is most effective for tasks with clear, verifiable success criteria.

nodes.label: hookErrorStrategy
nodes.rationale: By default a throwing delegation hook lets the delegation continue; set 'throw' to fail the delegation instead.

nodes.label: isTaskComplete
nodes.rationale: Validates whether the task is complete after each iteration; failed scorer feedback is added to the conversation so subagents can see what was missing.

nodes.label: messageFilter
nodes.rationale: Controls what messages are shared with a subagent, for example to remove sensitive data or limit context size.

nodes.label: onDelegationComplete
nodes.rationale: Called after a delegation finishes to inspect results, provide feedback, replace the tool result text, or bail out of the parent loop.

nodes.label: onDelegationStart
nodes.rationale: Called before the parent agent delegates so callers can intercept, modify, or reject delegations.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Each delegation receives a request context shallowly copied from the parent run, so subagent changes don't affect the parent's context.

nodes.label: Agent.streamUntilIdle()
nodes.rationale: Use streamUntilIdle() instead of stream() so the stream stays open until background subagents complete and the parent agent has had a chance to respond to their results.

nodes.label: DynamoDBStore
nodes.rationale: Uses a single-table design pattern with ElectroDB, a deliberate choice optimized for DynamoDB's key-value and query capabilities, differing from relational database adapters that use multiple tables.

nodes.label: Storage Domains
nodes.rationale: A domain owns one type of runtime data and a storage adapter implements one or more domains, so backends can be chosen per access pattern.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.rationale: Observability writes high-volume telemetry and often queries aggregations, so it should use a dedicated observability store or an OLAP backend such as ClickHouse or DuckDB.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Storage is the persistence layer for the Mastra runtime; it keeps memory, workflow state, observability data, eval results, schedules, and long-running agent state available after a process restarts.

nodes.label: Workflows
nodes.rationale: Workflow snapshots must be available when a run resumes, so they need a reliable persistent database.

nodes.label: Composite Storage
nodes.rationale: Use composite storage when one database isn't the right fit for every domain, routing each domain to the right backend.

nodes.label: Single-Table Design Pattern
nodes.rationale: Optimized for DynamoDB's key-value and query capabilities, often leading to better performance and capacity compared to mimicking relational models; offers lower cost, better performance, simplified administration, and transaction support.

nodes.label: TTL Configuration
nodes.rationale: Enables cost optimization, data lifecycle management, performance, and privacy compliance by automatically expiring items.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Memory is now required for the agent network to function properly.

nodes.label: onExtracted hook
nodes.rationale: Lets applications normalize or react to custom extracted values before they are persisted.

nodes.label: ElasticSearchStore
nodes.rationale: Shares the same connection configuration as ElasticSearchVector so a single cluster and even a single client instance can serve both agent memory and semantic recall.

nodes.label: GlideClient
nodes.rationale: Injected clients must be connected by the caller, who remains responsible for closing them; close() does not close an injected GlideClient.

nodes.label: ValkeyStore
nodes.rationale: Use @mastra/redis for Redis deployments that use the official redis client; the packages are tested independently against their respective servers. Requires a standalone Valkey server.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Pre-seeding RequestContext with MastraMemory isn't supported because thread resolution reads args.memory.thread and RequestContext.MastraMemory is populated by prepare-memory-step after the agent has already resolved its thread.

nodes.label: Automatic Model Selection
nodes.rationale: An automatic Observer or Reflector follows the active main model provider, using a built-in low-cost model when configured.

nodes.label: Factory
nodes.rationale: Stores automatic intent separately from the effective model shown in settings.

nodes.label: autoResumeSuspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Automatic resumption applies only to data-bearing suspend() flows; it does not approve tools that use requireApproval, which remain suspended until an explicit approval or decline is submitted.

nodes.label: listSuspendedRuns()
nodes.rationale: In production the approval often arrives later, after a page refresh, a server restart, or on a different server instance behind a load balancer, so pending runs must be rediscovered from storage rather than held in memory.

nodes.label: resumeSchema
nodes.rationale: The tool must define a resumeSchema so the agent knows what data structure to extract from the user's message.

nodes.label: resumeStream()
nodes.rationale: Manual resumption is intended for programmatic control, webhooks, button clicks and external triggers, whereas automatic resumption suits conversational flows where users provide resume data in natural language.

nodes.label: sendToolApproval()
nodes.rationale: If memory contains no active run for the thread, it searches storage for a suspended run before failing; pass a toolCallId when several suspended runs match the thread.

nodes.label: suspend()
nodes.rationale: Use suspend() instead of a tool without execute when the tool needs a structured answer from the user and also runs inside a subagent: subagents can't run client tools, but suspension propagates through the supervisor.

nodes.label: delegatedToolCallId
nodes.rationale: Use it to tell apart two pauses from the same delegation, such as a question followed by an approval.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Use for the conversation history, since snapshots are deleted once the run finishes.

nodes.label: Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Minimal resume artifacts: they hold only what's needed to resume the suspended run and are deleted once the run finishes; use tracing for the execution record and memory for conversation history.

nodes.label: Storage provider
nodes.rationale: Must be configured on the Mastra instance or human-in-the-loop fails with a 'snapshot not found' error.

nodes.label: Supervisor Agent
nodes.rationale: The supervisor raises a subagent's pause on its own delegation call, so the toolCallId on the approval or suspended chunk is the supervisor's call to the subagent and must always be passed when approving, declining or resuming.

nodes.label: Tracing
nodes.rationale: Use for the execution record, since snapshots are deleted once the run finishes.

nodes.label: Subagent
nodes.rationale: Each delegation gets a fresh threadId and a deterministic resourceId ({parentResourceId}-{agentName}) so subagent memory is isolated by default while resource-scoped memory persists across delegations.

nodes.label: ModelByInputTokens
nodes.rationale: Lets cheaper/faster models handle small inputs while stronger models handle larger contexts, selected at runtime from inclusive upTo thresholds.

nodes.label: Token Counting Cache
nodes.rationale: Caches token estimates in message metadata to reduce repeat counting work during threshold checks and buffering decisions; only payload estimates are cached so counting semantics stay the same.

nodes.label: Caller-supplied tokenEstimate
nodes.rationale: Lets callers attach an authoritative token estimate to image/file parts so the Token Counter skips its own estimator for expensive payloads.

nodes.label: data-om-buffering-failed
nodes.rationale: The system falls back to synchronous processing when the threshold is reached.

nodes.label: MDocument.chunk()
nodes.rationale: FastEmbed models embed at most 512 tokens per input, so long documents must be chunked to fit the window or text past the limit cannot be found by semantic recall.

nodes.label: ModelRouterEmbeddingModel
nodes.rationale: The model router is the simplest way to configure an embedder, using a provider/model string with autocomplete and automatic API key detection from environment variables.

nodes.label: agent.stream()
nodes.rationale: For a one-off request agent.stream() starts a run and reads its response directly, but it doesn't give a subscription that follows later runs on the same thread.

nodes.label: subscribeToThread()
nodes.rationale: Subscribing first means the subscription is already open when the input starts a run.

nodes.label: Signals
nodes.rationale: Signals let you send input to an agent's thread at any time, including while the agent is working; by default Mastra delivers it to the active run or starts a run when the thread is idle, so you don't need to check whether the agent is running before sending.

nodes.label: AgentController Session
nodes.rationale: If you're already using Agent Controller, its Session manages the thread and subscription for you.

nodes.label: cloneThread()
nodes.rationale: Useful for branching conversations, creating checkpoints before destructive operations, or testing variations of a conversation.

nodes.label: copyThread()
nodes.rationale: Never returns message payloads and copies rows inside the database on LibSQL and PostgreSQL, for forking long threads.

nodes.label: generateTitle
nodes.rationale: Runs asynchronously after the agent responds so it doesn't affect response time; emitEvent makes the stream wait to deliver the title.

nodes.label: Threads and resources
nodes.rationale: A thread is a conversation session; a resource is the entity that owns the thread.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Gives an agent access to earlier messages and tool results so it can answer follow-up questions and recall information from previous interactions.

nodes.label: Memory Processors
nodes.rationale: Filter, trim, or prioritize content when combined memory exceeds the model's context limit so the most relevant information is preserved.

nodes.label: Message History
nodes.rationale: High-fidelity record of the current conversation; enabled by default.

nodes.label: Multi-user Threads
nodes.rationale: Lets several people share one thread.

nodes.label: Scopes
nodes.rationale: Addresses a run acts as, written as <type>:<value>; memory reads resource from a resource: scope and thread from a thread: scope, while other scopes pass through to tools and processors.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Recommended over working memory for multi-user threads when storage supports it: extracts facts automatically, scales to any number of participants, and needs no template upkeep.

nodes.label: Request Context
nodes.rationale: Set the speaker from authenticated request context, never from the request body, to prevent impersonation.

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.rationale: Use when OM isn't an option or when a structured, deterministic participants list is needed.

nodes.label: Tracing
nodes.rationale: Traces show exactly which messages and observations the agent included in its context for each request, helping verify memory retrieval works as expected.

nodes.label: messageFilter
nodes.rationale: By default Mastra forwards the parent's conversation to the subagent; messageFilter passes only the messages the specialist needs.

nodes.label: processInputStep()
nodes.rationale: Use processLLMRequest() when a rewrite should apply only to the current provider call and leave memory untouched; processInput()/processInputStep() changes may later be saved to memory.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Use RequestContext when instructions depend on data that changes per request; anything evaluated at construction is fixed for the life of the process.

nodes.label: toModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Use when application code needs the full result but the model needs a smaller representation; start here for verbose tool results.

nodes.label: TokenLimiter
nodes.rationale: Add as a final budget guard rather than relying on the model's maximum context window.

nodes.label: ToolCallFilter
nodes.rationale: Removes old tool arguments and results from the next model request without deleting those messages from storage, so the model gets a smaller prompt while the application can still display the full interaction.

nodes.label: Compaction
nodes.rationale: A blunt fallback: the compaction turn adds latency, a single summary must represent everything before, and repeated summaries can flatten chronology or lose details; Observational Memory is preferred.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.rationale: The goal isn't to provide as much as possible, but to keep the context relevant and current; too little context leaves the model without needed information, too much increases cost and reduces response quality.

nodes.label: Dynamic Skills
nodes.rationale: Lets an agent load task-specific instructions only when needed instead of carrying every procedure in its base instructions, keeping default context smaller.

nodes.label: Filesystems
nodes.rationale: Choose a filesystem when the source of truth is a set of files the agent may need to list, read, or update; choose standalone RAG when retrieval is the main requirement and content doesn't need to behave like files.

nodes.label: includeSubAgentToolResultsInModelContext
nodes.rationale: Leave disabled unless the parent must reason over nested tool call details.

nodes.label: Inline Context
nodes.rationale: Select and label the fields the model needs instead of serializing an entire database record, keeping the prompt smaller and meanings clear.

nodes.label: Instructions
nodes.rationale: Keep instructions focused on behavior that applies to most calls; adding current data or task-specific details makes the base prompt larger and harder to reuse.

nodes.label: Processors
nodes.rationale: Use them when information should remain in stored history or application output but doesn't need to be sent back to the model on every step.

nodes.label: RAG
nodes.rationale: Choose RAG when semantic search over unstructured content is the actual requirement; direct source-specific tools are often simpler and cheaper because they avoid a chunking, embedding, and vector-index pipeline.

nodes.label: Tools
nodes.rationale: Tools are the recommended way to fetch current data; the model decides when it needs data while the application controls the query and returned fields.

nodes.label: Delegation Cancellation
nodes.rationale: The parent's abortSignal is forwarded to delegated subagents so in-flight subagent runs cancel at their next step instead of running to completion.

nodes.label: Subagent Memory Isolation
nodes.rationale: Subagents receive full conversation context but only their delegation prompt and response are saved to their memory, so they have context without cluttering memory with the parent's conversation.

nodes.label: Subagent Result References
nodes.rationale: Lets a later delegation reuse an earlier subagent result verbatim, avoiding the token cost and detail loss of the parent restating it in the next prompt.

nodes.label: Subagents
nodes.rationale: Use subagents when a task requires agents with different specializations to work together; the parent agent decides when to delegate and synthesizes their results.

nodes.label: Agent-level backgroundTasks.tools
nodes.rationale: Opts in specific tools or overrides timeouts for individual tools; disabled: true short-circuits background dispatch for the agent entirely.

nodes.label: Agent.generate()
nodes.rationale: Foreground execution is simpler for tool calls that return quickly.

nodes.label: _background per-call override
nodes.rationale: Only modifies tools already opted in, keeping deterministic foreground-only tools (calculators, lookups, schema validators) from being silently dispatched as tasks.

nodes.label: backgroundTasks Configuration
nodes.rationale: Background tasks are off by default and must be enabled on the Mastra instance.

nodes.label: MastraModelOutput
nodes.rationale: Aggregate properties still resolve against the first turn's internal buffer, so a cross-continuation aggregate view requires consuming fullStream manually.

nodes.label: notifyAgentOnFinish
nodes.rationale: Set to false when the app sends its own completion signal so the agent isn't told twice.

nodes.label: Tool-level background config
nodes.rationale: Tools opted in at this layer are eligible for background execution when called by an agent that has the manager enabled.

nodes.label: untilIdleMaxIdleMs
nodes.rationale: Should be longer than the slowest background task so its completion still triggers a continuation turn.

nodes.label: untilIdle stream option
nodes.rationale: Keeps the stream open until every dispatched background task has completed and the LLM has had a chance to respond to the result.

nodes.label: wokenRunsEndAfterTurn
nodes.rationale: Temporary option; in the next major release ending after the turn becomes the only behavior and this option is removed.

nodes.label: Background Tasks
nodes.rationale: Lets an agent dispatch a long-running tool call without blocking the agentic loop: the tool returns an immediate acknowledgement while the LLM continues responding, and the result is written to memory when the task finishes.

nodes.label: Subagent Background Config Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Subagent-level configuration travels with the agent, keeping its background behavior the same under every supervisor, whereas supervisor-side opt-in centralizes tuning in one place.

nodes.label: Notification Signal (background-task tag)
nodes.rationale: Names the tool call and task and tells the agent the result is on the tool call without copying the result into the prompt; not sent when an untilIdle stream is open or was cancelled.

nodes.label: Background Dispatch Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Agent-level and tool-level settings determine eligibility and fallback values; LLM _background fields override per call; manager defaults fill unset timeout and retry values.

nodes.label: Background Task Stream Chunks
nodes.rationale: Agent stream and manager stream each cover a different set of chunk types; untilIdle pipes the seven manager chunks into the same fullStream.

nodes.label: Subagents in the Background
nodes.rationale: Subagent invocations are dispatched as tool calls under the hood, so the same background configuration applies.

nodes.label: Suspend and Resume
nodes.rationale: Lets a task pause mid-execution for human approvals, webhooks, or data that arrives later; suspending releases the concurrency slot so other tasks can run.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Tasks are persisted so they survive process restarts.

nodes.label: getTask()
nodes.rationale: Reads from storage rather than the pubsub stream, making it suitable for paginated lists and detail views.

nodes.label: registerStaticExecutor()
nodes.rationale: Static executors registered in every process let any process run or recover a task, avoiding 'No executor registered' failures.

nodes.label: registerTaskContext()
nodes.rationale: The manager keeps tool executors in process memory, so after a restart the caller of resume() must re-register the executor closure first.

nodes.label: POST /api/background-tasks/:backgroundTaskId/resume
nodes.rationale: Requires suspendedAt so a stale answer is rejected with 409 Conflict instead of being delivered.

nodes.label: allResources
nodes.rationale: Delivers task arguments and results for every user, so it is restricted to trusted server-side code and must never serve a single user's request.

nodes.label: expiresAt
nodes.rationale: Cleanup never deletes a pending, running, or suspended task, so expired work must be cancelled first.

nodes.label: Lifecycle callbacks (onTaskComplete / onTaskFailed)
nodes.rationale: Callbacks at tool, agent and manager level do not replace one another; success/failure hooks fire for their own outcomes.

nodes.label: Non-agent owners
nodes.rationale: A namespaced owner key such as mcp-server:<serverId> avoids collision with a real agent ID, though Mastra does not enforce it.

nodes.label: onNoSlot: 'queue'
nodes.rationale: The queue lives in the memory of the process that called resume(); to survive restarts the resume data must be persisted and resume() called again.

nodes.label: perOwnerConcurrency
nodes.rationale: Gives an owner its own concurrency limit instead of perAgentConcurrency, while its tasks still count toward globalConcurrency.

nodes.label: pinToWorker
nodes.rationale: Signals that work for the task is already in flight on this worker, so no other process starts the same work; pinned work should be idempotent because a lapsed lease does not prove the work stopped.

nodes.label: metadata.suspendedTools
nodes.rationale: Records the open request on the assistant message so a chat that reloads the thread can still show the request; removed when the task resumes or is cancelled.

nodes.label: LibSQLStore
nodes.rationale: libSQL with a file-backed database is the fastest path for local development because it doesn't require running a separate database server.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Routes domains to different backends when one database isn't the right fit for every domain.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is a good default for most teams in production because it works well for transactional runtime state and is widely available as a managed service.

nodes.label: close()
nodes.rationale: Releases connections for the stores used by a composite; each store closes once even if it backs several domains.

nodes.label: init()
nodes.rationale: MastraCompositeStore initializes each configured domain independently; init() is called automatically when passed to the Mastra class.

nodes.label: MastraCompositeStore
nodes.rationale: Composes storage domains from different providers, for use when you need different databases for different purposes (e.g. LibSQL for memory and PostgreSQL for workflows).

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouse
nodes.rationale: Legacy observability domain implementation, still exported and supported for projects that haven't migrated.

nodes.label: ObservabilityStorageClickhouseVNext
nodes.rationale: ClickHouse is recommended for production observability because it's optimized for high-volume, write-heavy analytics workloads.

nodes.label: Agent-Level Storage
nodes.rationale: Configured on a Memory instance and overrides instance-level storage for that agent's memory data only; use when an agent needs an isolated memory boundary or a different memory backend.

nodes.label: Composite Storage
nodes.rationale: Use when domains have different operational needs, e.g. routing high-volume observability to a dedicated analytics backend.

nodes.label: Instance-Level Storage
nodes.rationale: Shared by agents, workflows, observability, evals, schedules, and other runtime features registered on the same Mastra instance; use when most runtime domains can share the same database.

nodes.label: memory Domain
nodes.rationale: Reads and writes rows during every remembered agent call, so it should use a transactional database such as libSQL, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB.

nodes.label: observability Domain
nodes.rationale: Writes high-volume telemetry and often queries aggregations, so a dedicated observability store or OLAP backend such as ClickHouse or DuckDB is appropriate.

nodes.label: Storage Retention and prune()
nodes.rationale: Configure retention policies on the storage adapter or composite store, then call storage.prune() from a scheduler or maintenance job.

nodes.label: schedules Domain
nodes.rationale: Schedules require an adapter that implements the schedules domain.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Storage is the persistence layer for the Mastra runtime, keeping memory, workflow state, observability data, eval results, schedules, and long-running agent state available after a process restarts.

nodes.label: workflows Domain
nodes.rationale: Stores durable snapshots that must be available when a run resumes, so it needs a reliable persistent database.

nodes.label: agents Domain
nodes.rationale: Enables agents to be defined and updated at runtime without code deployments.

nodes.label: Storage Domains
nodes.rationale: Mastra organizes storage into domains, each handling a specific type of data and each backed by a different storage adapter.

nodes.label: Background task worker
nodes.rationale: Executes agent tool calls marked background: { enabled: true } so the API does not block the response stream.

nodes.label: Crash recovery
nodes.rationale: Distributed PubSub persists unacknowledged events so workers resume after restart; because events can be processed more than once, handlers should be idempotent.

nodes.label: Worker health checks
nodes.rationale: GET /health returns 503 while startWorkers() initializes and 200 after all selected workers start; used for readiness checks.

nodes.label: In-process mode
nodes.rationale: Default setup needs no external infrastructure beyond storage, but does not survive process crashes and cannot scale components individually.

nodes.label: MASTRA_STEP_EXECUTION_URL
nodes.rationale: Points the orchestration worker at the API's internal URL so it can delegate step execution; without it the worker tries to execute steps in its own process, which lacks the full Mastra runtime in a split deployment.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKER_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: Bearer token forwarded as an Authorization credential so the API auth provider can validate orchestration worker step-execution requests.

nodes.label: MASTRA_WORKERS
nodes.rationale: Environment variable controlling which workers start in each process; any value switches workflows declaring schedule to the evented engine, so every process must run those workflows on the same engine.

nodes.label: Orchestration worker
nodes.rationale: Subscribes to workflow events on the PubSub bus and executes workflow steps; in a split deployment it delegates step execution back to the API over HTTP.

nodes.label: PubSub
nodes.rationale: Distributed PubSub backend is required for split deployments; it carries workflow events, wake events, and background task dispatch between processes.

nodes.label: Scheduler worker
nodes.rationale: Producer only: polls storage for due cron schedules and publishes workflow.start events for the orchestration worker. Must run as a single instance to avoid duplicate fires.

nodes.label: Split processes
nodes.rationale: Runs workers in their own processes using a distributed PubSub backend and MASTRA_WORKERS to select which workers start in each process.

nodes.label: Workers
nodes.rationale: Workers handle background processing outside the request-response cycle so the API stays responsive; by default they run in the same process as the API, and can be split out for production scale.

nodes.label: neon.ts config
nodes.rationale: Lets branch settings be managed in the repository.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: Neon doesn't require a separate Mastra storage package; Mastra connects to Neon through PostgresStore, which uses the Node.js pg driver.

nodes.label: DbClient
nodes.rationale: Exposed via store.db for advanced low-level query and transaction access, bypassing PostgresStore validation.

nodes.label: ensurePartitions()
nodes.rationale: Needed when the app role cannot create tables: call it on a schedule at least once every futureDays days with a role that owns the observability tables. A larger futureDays gives the scheduled job more time between runs.

nodes.label: init()
nodes.rationale: If init() isn't called, tables won't be created and storage operations will fail silently or throw errors.

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: When a pool is provided, Mastra uses it but doesn't close it on store.close(); when Mastra creates the pool, Mastra owns and closes it.

nodes.label: PostgresStore
nodes.rationale: Production-ready storage solution using PostgreSQL databases; handles schema creation and updates automatically.

nodes.label: PostgresStoreVNext
nodes.rationale: Uses the event-sourced tracing strategy: writes one row when a span starts and another when it ends, never updating in place, so writes stay append-only and traces appear in Studio while the run is still executing.

nodes.label: Neon agent skills
nodes.rationale: The skills give compatible coding agents Neon setup instructions and Postgres-specific guidance.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Index Types
nodes.rationale: Different index types are optimized for specific scenarios (btree for range/sort, hash for equality, gin for JSONB/arrays, gist for geometric, spgist for non-balanced data, brin for large naturally ordered tables).

nodes.label: PgVector.buildIndex()
nodes.rationale: Will drop any existing index before creating the new one.

nodes.label: PgVector.describeIndex()
nodes.rationale: count is an exact SELECT COUNT(*) that scans the whole table, so avoid calling it on a hot path for a large index; reads and writes only use index metadata from the Postgres catalog.

nodes.label: fastembed
nodes.rationale: Used to generate local vector embeddings for memory's semanticRecall.

nodes.label: IndexConfig
nodes.rationale: The system automatically detects configuration changes and only rebuilds indexes when necessary, preventing performance issues from unnecessary index recreations.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: Provides reliable vector similarity search within an existing PostgreSQL database using the pgvector extension.

nodes.label: chunk()
nodes.rationale: Multiple chunking strategies exist because each is optimized for a different document type (structure-aware, sentence-aware, token-aware, etc.).

nodes.label: ModelRouterEmbeddingModel
nodes.rationale: The model router automatically handles API key detection from environment variables, so provider/model strings are the simplest embedding path.

nodes.label: Chunking Strategies
nodes.rationale: Chunking and embedding strategies are chosen for optimal retrieval.

nodes.label: RAG Observability
nodes.rationale: Observability tracks embedding and retrieval performance.

nodes.label: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
nodes.rationale: Incorporating relevant context from your own data sources improves accuracy and grounds LLM responses in real information.

nodes.label: Vector Stores
nodes.rationale: Multiple vector stores are supported for embedding persistence and similarity search.

nodes.label: createVectorQueryTool()
nodes.rationale: Most fields can be set at creation as defaults and overridden at runtime via request context or input; id and description can only be set at creation time.

nodes.label: DatabaseConfig
nodes.rationale: Allows database-specific features and optimizations to be applied automatically during query execution, and multiple configs let one tool serve dynamic stores.

nodes.label: QueryResult
nodes.rationale: document is only populated by stores whose query() returns document content; for others read chunk text from sources[i].metadata.text.

nodes.label: RerankConfig
nodes.rationale: Reranking improves result quality by combining semantic relevance, vector similarity, position bias and query analysis.

nodes.label: VectorStoreResolver
nodes.rationale: Enables multi-tenant schema or database isolation by resolving the vector store from request context at runtime.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Vector Store Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each tenant gets isolated data (e.g. separate PostgreSQL schemas) with cached per-tenant store instances, similar to how Agent.memory supports runtime-defined configuration.

nodes.label: ElectroDB
nodes.rationale: Provides a layer of abstraction and type safety over raw DynamoDB operations and manages the complexity of item types and access patterns on a single table.

nodes.label: MastraStorage Interface
nodes.rationale: Adhering to the same interface as other adapters ensures the DynamoDB adapter can be used interchangeably within the Mastra Memory component despite a different underlying storage model.

nodes.label: 400 KB Item Size Limit
nodes.rationale: DynamoDB enforces a 400 KB maximum item size, which can be exceeded when storing messages with base64-encoded attachments such as images.

nodes.label: Single-Table Design Pattern
nodes.rationale: A deliberate design choice optimized for DynamoDB's key-value and query capabilities, differing from relational adapters that use multiple tables per entity; it can lower cost, improve performance, simplify administration, and enable transactions across entity types.

nodes.label: TTL (Time To Live) Configuration
nodes.rationale: Supports cost optimization, data lifecycle management, performance (preventing unbounded table growth), and privacy compliance by automatically purging personal data.

nodes.label: mastra_% Storage Tables
nodes.rationale: Mastra initializes its storage tables when the application starts, so the database role must have permission to create those tables and indexes.

nodes.label: SSL CA Certificate Verification
nodes.rationale: The CA certificate is unique to the instance; SSL query parameters are left out of DATABASE_URL and certificate verification is configured through the ssl object instead.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: Setting disableInit: true prevents the runtime process from creating or changing the extension, tables and indexes.

nodes.label: recall()
nodes.rationale: Adds semantic search support over listMessages, letting callers find messages by meaning via vectorSearchString rather than recency.

nodes.label: waitForIndexReady()
nodes.rationale: createIndex() returns before the index finishes building, so queries must wait for readiness.

nodes.label: Embedder
nodes.rationale: Memory uses a single embedder for both storing and recalling messages, so one model must be chosen and used consistently.

nodes.label: embeddingDimension
nodes.rationale: Setting the dimension skips the startup probe embedding call, so startup does not depend on the embedding provider being reachable.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL index optimization
