nodes.rationale: HNSW indexes typically perform better than the default IVFFlat, especially with OpenAI embeddings using inner product distance; PgVector only uses the vector index for thread/resource-filtered searches with HNSW on pgvector 0.8.0+.

nodes.label: Semantic recall
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default because each call adds latency: new messages are embedded and used to query a vector database before the LLM receives them.

nodes.label: Server-side embeddings
nodes.rationale: With a store that embeds server-side, the embedding provider stays out of the application entirely and no embedder is required.

nodes.label: Hybrid Vector Search
nodes.rationale: Combining vector similarity search with metadata filters merges semantic search with structured filtering criteria.

nodes.label: Metadata Filtering
nodes.rationale: Useful when documents come from different sources, time periods, or have specific attributes.

nodes.label: MastraDBMessage
nodes.rationale: Storage uses a single message shape; content.parts is the part the agent actually reads, while toolInvocations/reasoning/experimental_attachments are flat mirrors kept only for AI SDK v4 compatibility.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: A storage provider is required for conversation history; semantic recall additionally requires a vector store and, unless the vector store self-embeds, an embedder. messageHistory is preferred over lastMessages because message count is a poor proxy for context size, and the lastMessages window slides forward on every request, invalidating the provider prompt cache on long threads.

nodes.label: saveMessages()
nodes.rationale: agent.generate() and agent.stream() persist messages automatically; saveMessages() is for seeding threads, importing transcripts, or storing messages that originated outside Mastra.

nodes.label: MessageHistory
nodes.rationale: Hybrid processor: fetches historical messages from storage on input and persists new messages on output, so retrieval and persistence share one configuration.

nodes.label: SemanticRecall
nodes.rationale: Hybrid processor: performs vector search over history on input and embeds new messages on output, using LRU caching to avoid redundant embedding API calls.

nodes.label: WorkingMemory
nodes.rationale: Input-only processor: it injects current working memory state as a system message, while updates happen through the updateWorkingMemory tool provided by the Memory class.

nodes.label: Observational Memory
nodes.rationale: Recommended for long-running conversations where the sliding lastMessages window would repeatedly invalidate the prompt cache.

nodes.label: createVectorQueryTool()
nodes.rationale: Tool name and description help the agent understand when and how to use the retrieval capabilities.

nodes.label: RequestContext
nodes.rationale: Allows databaseConfig to be overridden at runtime based on context.

nodes.label: rerankWithScorer()
nodes.rationale: Weights control how semantic, vector, and position factors influence the final ranking.

nodes.label: Vector Query Tool
nodes.rationale: Lets the agent be in charge of retrieval decisions, combining semantic search with optional filtering and reranking.

nodes.label: VoyageRelevanceScorer
nodes.rationale: Reads VOYAGE_API_KEY from the environment, or accepts an apiKey in its config.

nodes.label: databaseConfig
nodes.rationale: Query-time options like namespaces, performance tuning, and filtering are separated from database connection setup.

nodes.label: GraphRAG
nodes.rationale: Graph-based retrieval follows connections between chunks.

nodes.label: Re-ranking
nodes.rationale: More computationally expensive but more accurate: considers word order and exact matches, applies advanced relevance scoring, and uses cross-attention between query and documents.

nodes.label: Semantic Search
nodes.rationale: Uses vector similarity to find chunks semantically similar to the query.

nodes.label: Vector Store Prompts
nodes.rationale: When implementing filtering, these prompts are required in the agent's instructions to specify valid operators and syntax for each vector store implementation.

nodes.label: createIndex()
nodes.rationale: Indexes must be created before storing embeddings, and the dimension must match the embedding model's output dimension; index dimensions can't be changed after creation.

nodes.label: deleteVectors()
nodes.rationale: Used to clean up stale vectors after a document is deleted or updated, or when re-indexing.

nodes.label: hybridQuery()
nodes.rationale: Combines vector similarity with BM25 full-text search via server-side $rankFusion to blend semantic retrieval with keyword-based results.

nodes.label: LanceVectorStore
nodes.rationale: LanceDB is an embedded vector database built on the Lance columnar format, suitable for local development or cloud deployment.

nodes.label: MongoDBVector
nodes.rationale: MongoDB Vector Search is a good solution for teams who want to consolidate vector search, full-text search, and operational data in a single database to minimize infrastructure complexity.

nodes.label: OracleVector
nodes.rationale: Stores embeddings in native VECTOR columns and metadata in Oracle JSON; exact search is the default, with HNSW and IVF indexes configurable for tuned deployments.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension is a good solution for teams already using PostgreSQL who want to minimize infrastructure complexity.

nodes.label: upsert()
nodes.rationale: Upsert updates existing vectors sharing the same ID, creates new ones otherwise, and handles batching automatically for large datasets.

nodes.label: UpstashVector
nodes.rationale: Upstash creates indexes (known as namespaces) automatically, so no createIndex call is needed before upserting.

nodes.label: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed)
nodes.rationale: MongoDB can generate embeddings itself with a Voyage AI model, so no embedding provider is needed in the application.

nodes.label: Index Naming Rules
nodes.rationale: Each vector database enforces specific naming conventions for indexes and collections to ensure compatibility and prevent conflicts.

nodes.label: Vector Metadata
nodes.rationale: Without metadata you'd only have numerical embeddings with no way to return the original text or filter results, so at least the source text should always be stored.

nodes.label: Vector Store Interface
nodes.rationale: Mastra provides a consistent interface for storing and querying embeddings across vector databases, so all stores share the same createIndex/upsert/query surface.

nodes.label: memory.mergeWorkingMemory()
nodes.rationale: Lets application code merge a partial update; throws if working memory isn't schema-based and resource-scoped, or if the storage adapter doesn't support atomic merges.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Storage Adapter
nodes.rationale: Currently the only adapter supporting atomic merges, running each merge inside a row-locked database transaction.

nodes.label: memory.supportsAtomicWorkingMemoryMerge()
nodes.rationale: Check before calling mergeWorkingMemory if you need to fall back when the adapter lacks atomic merge support.

nodes.label: WorkingMemoryStateProcessor
nodes.rationale: Auto-attached by Memory when useStateSignals is enabled to emit current working memory as a state signal with stateId 'working-memory'.

nodes.label: mastra_resources Table
nodes.rationale: Resource-scoped working memory requires storage adapters that support this table.

nodes.label: Merge Semantics
nodes.rationale: Object fields are deep merged, setting a field to null deletes it, and arrays are replaced entirely rather than merged element-by-element.

nodes.label: Read-Only Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Useful for routing agents that need context but shouldn't update user profiles, and sub agents that should reference but not own the memory.

nodes.label: Resource-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Default scope: memory persists across all conversation threads for the same user (resourceId), enabling persistent user memory.

nodes.label: Schema-Based Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Structured, type-safe JSON data supporting validation and programmatic access; merge semantics preserve existing fields when the agent provides only the fields to update.

nodes.label: State Signals
nodes.rationale: Experimental delivery path (useStateSignals) that emits working memory as a state signal instead of folding it into the system prompt; storage is identical.

nodes.label: Template Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Markdown template maintained as a free-form text block; uses replace semantics, so the agent must provide the complete memory content on each update.

nodes.label: Thread-Scoped Memory
nodes.rationale: Isolates working memory to individual conversation threads; suited to separate topics, temporary/session-specific information, and ephemeral unrelated workflows.

nodes.label: Working Memory
nodes.rationale: Working memory is the agent's active scratchpad: key information it keeps available about the user or task, useful for maintaining ongoing state that is always relevant and should always be available to the agent.

nodes.label: Storing embeddings in a vector database
nodes.norm_label: storing embeddings in a vector database

nodes.label: applyRetention()
nodes.rationale: Lets deployments update TTL configuration without running the full initialization path.

nodes.label: prune()
nodes.rationale: Deletes in bounded, batched chunks (each batch its own transaction) so it never takes a long lock or bloats the transaction log; never runs VACUUM. Anchor-column indexes are created lazily on first prune() so deployments without retention pay no extra index write or disk overhead.

nodes.label: PruneOptions
nodes.rationale: maxBatches, maxRows, pauseMs and signal let each maintenance window bound its work and stop promptly.

nodes.label: PruneResult
nodes.rationale: done: false signals eligible rows remain so the caller re-invokes prune() on the next tick, letting a large backlog drain over several runs.

nodes.label: RetentionConfig
nodes.rationale: Fully typed: domain keys must exist and table keys must be retention-eligible, so unknown domains or tables produce compile errors.

nodes.label: TableRetentionPolicy
nodes.rationale: batchSize bounds lock duration and WAL growth on large tables because each batch is its own transaction.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Native TTL
nodes.rationale: Deletion requests are retained long enough to keep enforcing erasure after signal rows expire, so their TTL is the longest signal retention plus 30 days and stays unbounded if any signal is unbounded.

nodes.label: DuckDB Adapter
nodes.rationale: Uses built-in zone maps instead of creating retention indexes; file-backed stores need CHECKPOINT after pruning because VACUUM doesn't reclaim deleted rows.

nodes.label: Growth Tables
nodes.rationale: Retention covers only tables that accumulate rows unbounded as a side effect of normal operation; user-authored artifacts and config grow with user intent and are edited or deleted explicitly, so they're not valid retention keys.

nodes.label: MongoDB TTL Indexes
nodes.rationale: TTL is simpler and zero-maintenance for fixed retention periods; prune() gives more control (timing, rate capping, resumable/cancellable cleanup, composite storage). Both approaches are valid.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Adapter
nodes.rationale: vNext observability drops expired day partitions or TimescaleDB chunks instead of deleting rows, so effective level of detail is one day.

nodes.label: Reclaiming Disk
nodes.rationale: prune() deletes rows but doesn't shrink the database file; freed pages are reused by future writes, and returning space to the OS is a separate database-level maintenance concern Mastra doesn't manage.

nodes.label: Retention-Eligible Tables
nodes.rationale: Anchor columns are chosen so maxAge matches the meaning of the data: append-only logs use creation time, live state uses last activity, and jobs or runs use completion time so in-flight work isn't pruned.

nodes.label: Schedule Pruning
nodes.rationale: Run prune() from a scheduler or maintenance worker, not startup/shutdown hooks; prefer a single active scheduler for shared databases and lower-traffic periods for large tables.

nodes.label: Storage Retention
nodes.rationale: Storage grows without bound by default, so retention is opt-in and age-based; unconfigured data is kept forever so behavior doesn't change until you opt in.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Vectorize
nodes.rationale: Requires explicit metadata indexing before filtering can be used; vectors must be re-upserted after creating new metadata indexes.

nodes.label: Couchbase
nodes.rationale: Currently doesn't support metadata filters; filtering must be done client-side or via the Couchbase SDK Search capabilities.

nodes.label: createIndex() with filterFields
nodes.rationale: Declaring filter fields lets Mastra pass filters directly to $vectorSearch instead of falling back to a pre-filter pass limited by MongoDB's 16 MB BSON document limit.

nodes.label: createMetadataIndex()
nodes.rationale: Vectorize requires explicit metadata indexing before filtering can be used.

nodes.label: createPayloadIndex()
nodes.rationale: Qdrant payload fields must be indexed before filtering works on them.

nodes.label: libSQL
nodes.rationale: Metadata is stored in a JSONB column for efficient querying.

nodes.label: OracleDB Vector Store
nodes.rationale: User-provided metadata values are bound as parameters instead of interpolated into SQL.

nodes.label: PgVector
nodes.rationale: Metadata is stored in a JSONB column for efficient indexing; filters become PostgreSQL JSONB predicates.

nodes.label: Qdrant
nodes.rationale: Payload fields must be explicitly indexed before they can be filtered on.

nodes.label: filterFields
nodes.rationale: Filters referencing undeclared fields or unsupported operators take a fallback path that fails on large collections once the 16 MB BSON ID-set limit is exceeded, so filter fields should be declared for selective queries over large data sets.

nodes.label: Metadata Filters
nodes.rationale: A unified filtering syntax lets one query shape work across every vector store, with each store translating it into its native query format.

nodes.label: nonFilterableMetadataKeys
nodes.rationale: Keys listed here are stored but not filterable; the setting is immutable.
